situation: You are deciding where goodness toward others begins.
wise_response: "Filial piety and fraternal submission!-- are they not the root of all benevolent actions?" Good conduct starts with how you treat your own parents and siblings.
why_it_worked: Habits of respect learned at home grow into respect for everyone else. People who honor their family rarely stir up trouble.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating family carelessly while presenting a kind face to the wider world.

translation.original_text: 有子曰：「其爲人也孝弟，而好犯上者，鮮矣；不好犯上，而好作亂者，未之有也。君子務本，本立而道生；孝弟也者，其爲仁之本與？」

situation: Someone wins you over with smooth talk and a pleasing manner.
wise_response: "Fine words and an insinuating appearance are seldom associated with true virtue." Be wary of charm used to win favor.
why_it_worked: Polished flattery usually serves the speaker. Real goodness shows in conduct more than in pleasing words.
tempting_wrong_answer: Trusting whoever flatters best, or cultivating charm yourself in place of honest dealing.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「巧言令色，鮮矣仁。」

situation: You lead people and want their willing support.
wise_response: "Advance the upright and set aside the crooked, then the people will submit. Advance the crooked and set aside the upright, then the people will not submit."
why_it_worked: People accept authority when they see honesty rewarded. Promoting the crooked tells them the game is rigged.
tempting_wrong_answer: Promoting favorites and flatterers over honest people.

translation.original_text: 哀公問曰：「何爲則民服？」孔子對曰：「擧直錯諸枉，則民服；擧枉錯諸直，則民不服。」

situation: Someone suggests you are doing nothing worthwhile because you hold no public office.
wise_response: The Master answered that being filial and doing one's brotherly duties "are displayed in government." Good conduct at home is already public service.
why_it_worked: Order in a society grows out of order in households. Living well where you are counts.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking only a title or position makes your conduct matter.

translation.original_text: 或謂孔子曰：「子奚不爲政？」子曰：「，奚其爲爲政？」

situation: You are tempted to shade the truth to get ahead.
wise_response: "I do not know how a man without truthfulness is to get on. How can a large carriage be made to go without the cross-bar for yoking the oxen?"
why_it_worked: Truthfulness is what connects a person to others. Without it nothing can be pulled forward.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating honesty as optional when a lie seems useful.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「人而無信，不知其可也。大車無輗，小車無軏，其何以行之哉？」

situation: You perform the forms of courtesy and ceremony carefully.
wise_response: "If a man be without the virtues proper to humanity, what has he to do with the rites of propriety?"
why_it_worked: Forms without kindness behind them are empty. Ceremony is meant to express humane feeling.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping up polished manners while lacking care for people.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「人而不仁，如禮何？人而不仁，如樂何？」

situation: You are planning a ceremony, a celebration or a funeral.
wise_response: "In festive ceremonies, it is better to be sparing than extravagant. In the ceremonies of mourning, it is better that there be deep sorrow than a minute attention to observances."
why_it_worked: Display can crowd out meaning. Real feeling matters more than lavish or exact performance.
tempting_wrong_answer: Spending heavily for show and fussing over details while the heart is absent.

translation.original_text: 林放問禮之本。子曰：「大哉問！禮，與其奢也，寧儉；喪，與其易也，寧戚。」

situation: Someone advises you to court whoever actually holds power, whatever is right.
wise_response: "Not so. He who offends against Heaven has none to whom he can pray."
why_it_worked: Currying favor cannot protect someone who has done wrong. Doing right is the only real security.
tempting_wrong_answer: Flattering the powerful and assuming connections will cover your wrongs.

translation.original_text: 王孫賈問曰：「『與其媚於奧，寧媚於竈。』何謂也？」子曰：「不然。獲罪於天，無所禱也。」

situation: You are in an unfamiliar place and worry that asking questions will make you look ignorant.
wise_response: The Master asked about everything in the grand temple. When mocked, he said, "This is a rule of propriety."
why_it_worked: Asking when unsure shows respect and care to get things right. Pride that refuses to ask leads to mistakes.
tempting_wrong_answer: Pretending to know so no one thinks less of you.

translation.original_text: 子入太廟，每事問。或曰：「孰謂鄹人之子知禮乎？入太廟，每事問。」子聞之曰：「是禮也！」

situation: You manage people, or you serve someone above you.
wise_response: "A prince should employ his minister according to the rules of propriety; ministers should serve their prince with faithfulness."
why_it_worked: Respect flows down and loyalty flows up. Each side's duty supports the other's.
tempting_wrong_answer: A boss who treats staff without respect, or staff who serve without loyalty.

translation.original_text: 定公問：「君使臣，臣事君，如之何？」孔子對曰：「君使臣以禮，臣事君以忠。」

situation: You are choosing where to live and whom to live among.
wise_response: "It is virtuous manners which constitute the excellence of a neighborhood. If a man in selecting a residence, do not fix on one where such prevail, how can he be wise?"
why_it_worked: The people around you shape you. Good neighbors are worth more than other comforts.
tempting_wrong_answer: Choosing a place for status or convenience without regard for the character of the people.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「里仁爲美。擇不處仁，焉得知？」

situation: Wealth or honor is within reach, but only by an improper route.
wise_response: "Riches and honours are what men desire. If it cannot be obtained in the proper way, they should not be held." The superior man "does not, even for the space of a single meal, act contrary to virtue."
why_it_worked: Gain taken wrongly costs your integrity. Virtue has to hold in haste and danger too, or it is not virtue.
tempting_wrong_answer: Taking advantage you were not entitled to, or dropping principles when rushed or threatened.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「富與貴，是人之所欲也，不以其道得之，不處也。貧與賤，是人之所惡也；不以其道得之，不去也。君子去仁，惡乎成名？君子無終食之閒違仁，造次必於是，-{zh:顚;zh-hant:顛;zh-hans:颠}-沛必於是。」

situation: You think doing right is beyond your strength.
wise_response: "Is any one able for one day to apply his strength to virtue? I have not seen the case in which his strength would be insufficient."
why_it_worked: The obstacle is willingness. Anyone who truly tries has enough strength.
tempting_wrong_answer: Excusing yourself by saying goodness is too hard for you.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「我未見好仁者，惡不仁者。好仁者，無以尙之；惡不仁者，其爲仁矣。不使不仁者加乎其身。有能一日用其力於仁矣乎？我未見力不足者！蓋有之矣，我未之見也。」

wise_response: "A scholar, whose mind is set on truth, and who is ashamed of bad clothes and bad food, is not fit to be discoursed with."
why_it_worked: Shame over outward things shows where the heart really is.
tempting_wrong_answer: Claiming high ideals while chasing appearances.

situation: You come to a decision with a preference already fixed.
wise_response: "The superior man, in the world, does not set his mind either for anything, or against anything; what is right he will follow."
why_it_worked: Fixed preferences blind judgment. Following what is right in each case keeps you fair.
tempting_wrong_answer: Deciding by bias and then finding reasons.

wise_response: "He who acts with a constant view to his own advantage will be much murmured against."
why_it_worked: Self-interest pursued without restraint breeds resentment among those around you.

wise_response: "I am not concerned that I have no place, I am concerned how I may fit myself for one. I am not concerned that I am not known, I seek to be worthy to be known."
why_it_worked: Preparation is in your hands. Recognition follows worth more often than complaint.
tempting_wrong_answer: Resenting being overlooked instead of becoming capable.

situation: You want one principle to guide how you treat people.
wise_response: Tsang explained the Master's doctrine as "to be true to the principles of our nature and the benevolent exercise of them to others,-- this and nothing more."
why_it_worked: Being faithful to yourself and kind to others covers the whole of right conduct.
tempting_wrong_answer: Getting lost in rules while missing the basic duty of sincerity and kindness.

situation: You want to travel far while your parents are living.
wise_response: "While his parents are alive, the son may not go abroad to a distance. If he does go abroad, he must have a fixed place to which he goes."
why_it_worked: Parents need to know where you are. Keeping them informed spares them fear.
tempting_wrong_answer: Disappearing without word and leaving your parents to worry.

situation: You are about to make promises or bold statements.
wise_response: "The reason why the ancients did not readily give utterance to their words, was that they feared lest their actions should not come up to them."
why_it_worked: Saying less than you can do protects your word. Saying more than you can do makes you unreliable.
tempting_wrong_answer: Promising freely and then falling short.

wise_response: The Master said Kung-ye Ch'ang "might be wived; although he was put in bonds, he had not been guilty of any crime," and gave him his own daughter in marriage.
why_it_worked: A person's worth lies in what they actually did, not in the disgrace others put on them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Shunning someone because of an unjust record or public shame.

wise_response: "What is the good of being ready with the tongue? They who encounter men with smartnesses of speech for the most part procure themselves hatred."
why_it_worked: Quick, clever talk tends to wound and make enemies. It is no measure of goodness.
tempting_wrong_answer: Valuing wit and sharp replies over character.

situation: You admire someone who seems strong-willed and unbending.
wise_response: Of Shan Ch'ang the Master said, "Ch'ang is under the influence of his passions; how can he be pronounced firm and unbending?"
why_it_worked: Real firmness is mastery of your desires. Someone driven by appetite only looks strong.
tempting_wrong_answer: Mistaking stubbornness or appetite for strength of character.

situation: You believe you already live by the rule of not doing to others what you would not want done to you.
wise_response: Tsze-kung said, "What I do not wish men to do to me, I also wish not to do to men." The Master said, "Ts'ze, you have not attained to that."
why_it_worked: The rule is easy to state and hard to live. Claiming to have mastered it is itself a sign you have not.
tempting_wrong_answer: Assuming that knowing the golden rule means you practise it.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「吾未見剛者。」或對曰：「申棖。」子曰：「棖也慾！焉得剛？」

situation: A friendship has gone on for many years and has become casual.
wise_response: "Yen P'ing knew well how to maintain friendly intercourse. The acquaintance might be long, but he showed the same respect as at first."
why_it_worked: Familiarity wears respect away unless you guard it. Lasting friendship keeps the courtesy it began with.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting long acquaintance turn into carelessness or contempt.

translation.original_text: 子謂子產：「有君子之道四焉：其行己也恭，其事上也敬，其養民也惠，其使民也義。」

situation: You gain and lose positions of power.
wise_response: Tsze-wan thrice took office "and manifested no joy," thrice left it "and manifested no displeasure," and always briefed the new minister on how he had governed. The Master called him loyal.
why_it_worked: Serving the work more than your own standing lets you hand it on well, whether you rise or fall.
tempting_wrong_answer: Gloating over promotion, sulking at dismissal, and leaving your successor in the dark.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「臧文仲居蔡，山節藻梲。何如其知也？」

situation: People once wronged you, and you remember it.
wise_response: "Po-i and Shu-ch'i did not keep the former wickednesses of men in mind, and hence the resentments directed towards them were few."
why_it_worked: Letting old wrongs go keeps resentment from feeding back and forth.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping a list of grievances and letting it set the tone with others.

translation.original_text: 子在陳，曰：「歸與！歸與！吾黨之小子狂簡，斐然成章，不知所以裁之。」

situation: Someone asks you for something you do not have, and you want to look generous.
wise_response: Of Wei-shang Kao: "One begged some vinegar of him, and he begged it of a neighbor and gave it to the man." The Master would not call this upright.
why_it_worked: Uprightness means being straight about what you have. Passing off a borrowed favor as your own is a small deceit.
tempting_wrong_answer: Faking generosity to keep a reputation.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「伯夷、叔齊，不念舊惡，怨是用希。」

situation: You are asked what you most wish for in how you live with others.
wise_response: Tsze-lu wished to share his goods with friends without minding if they spoiled them. Yen Yuan wished not to boast. The Master wished "in regard to the aged, to give them rest; in regard to friends, to show them sincerity; in regard to the young, to treat them tenderly."
why_it_worked: Good wishes are about others: comfort for the old, faithfulness to friends, gentleness with the young.
tempting_wrong_answer: Wishing only for things for yourself.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「巧言、令色、足恭，左丘明恥之，丘亦恥之。匿怨而友其人，左丘明恥之，丘亦恥之。」

situation: You are angry, or you have made a mistake.
wise_response: Yen Hui "did not transfer his anger; he did not repeat a fault."
why_it_worked: Taking anger out on someone who did not cause it is unjust. Repeating a mistake means you did not learn from it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Snapping at whoever is near when you are angry, and making the same mistake twice.

translation.original_text: 哀公問：「弟子孰爲好學？」孔子對曰：「有顏回者，好學；不遷怒，不貳過，不幸短命死矣！今也則亡，未聞好學者也。」

situation: Someone's family or background counts against them.
wise_response: "If the calf of a brindled cow be red and horned, although men may not wish to use it, would the spirits of the mountains and rivers put it aside?"
why_it_worked: A person should be judged by their own qualities, not their parentage.
tempting_wrong_answer: Dismissing a capable person because of where they come from.

translation.original_text: 子謂仲弓曰：「犁牛之子，騂且角；雖欲勿用，山川其舍諸？」

situation: A friend or student is gravely ill.
wise_response: When Po-niu was sick, the Master went to him and "took hold of his hand through the window," grieving openly.
why_it_worked: Being present with the sick, even when nothing can be done, is an act of love.
tempting_wrong_answer: Staying away from someone dying because it is uncomfortable.

situation: You live with very little.
wise_response: Hui lived on a bamboo dish of rice and a gourd of drink in a mean lane, and "while others could not have endured the distress, he did not allow his joy to be affected by it."
why_it_worked: Joy that rests on character is not taken away by poverty.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting lack of money sour your spirit and define your worth.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「賢哉回也！一簞食，一瓢飮，在陋巷，人不堪其憂，回也不改其樂。賢哉回也！」

situation: You say the right path is too hard for you.
wise_response: "Those whose strength is insufficient give over in the middle of the way but now you limit yourself."
why_it_worked: Saying you cannot is often deciding not to try. Real limits show up only after real effort.
tempting_wrong_answer: Excusing yourself before you have even started.

situation: You did something brave and could take credit for it.
wise_response: Mang Chih-fan guarded the rear in a retreat and then said, "It is not that I dare to be last. My horse would not advance."
why_it_worked: Brushing off credit for courage keeps your deeds clean of vanity.
tempting_wrong_answer: Advertising your bravery to win praise.

situation: You are working on yourself and must balance substance with polish.
wise_response: "Where the solid qualities are in excess of accomplishments, we have rusticity; where the accomplishments are in excess of the solid qualities, we have the manners of a clerk. When the accomplishments and solid qualities are equally blended, we then have the man of virtue."
why_it_worked: Character without grace is rough; grace without character is hollow. Each needs the other.
tempting_wrong_answer: Cultivating either polish or plainness and neglecting the other.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「質勝文則野，文勝質則史。文質彬彬，然後君子。」

situation: You are tempted to get by on crookedness.
wise_response: "Man is born for uprightness. If a man lose his uprightness, and yet live, his escape from death is the effect of mere good fortune."
why_it_worked: Crooked living has no safe footing. Those who survive it are lucky, not wise.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking you can live dishonestly and stay safe.

situation: You are working toward something good and thinking about the reward.
wise_response: "The man of virtue makes the difficulty to be overcome his first business, and success only a subsequent consideration." Wisdom is giving yourself earnestly to the duties due to people.
why_it_worked: Doing the hard part first and leaving reward for later keeps you honest about your motives.
tempting_wrong_answer: Reaching for the payoff and avoiding the difficult work.

situation: You know a lot and are asked to teach.
wise_response: "The silent treasuring up of knowledge; learning without satiety; and instructing others without being wearied."
why_it_worked: Learning without end and teaching without tiring keeps knowledge alive and shared.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hoarding what you know, or growing impatient with those who ask.

wise_response: "From the man bringing his bundle of dried flesh for my teaching upwards, I have never refused instruction to any one."
why_it_worked: Teaching should be open to anyone who sincerely asks, whatever little they can offer.
tempting_wrong_answer: Reserving your knowledge for those who can pay well or bring status.

situation: You are teaching someone who will not make an effort.
wise_response: "I do not open up the truth to one who is not eager to get knowledge... When I have presented one corner of a subject to any one, and he cannot from it learn the other three, I do not repeat my lesson."
why_it_worked: Learning needs the student's own effort. Spoon-feeding someone who will not think does them no good.
tempting_wrong_answer: Doing all the work for a learner who puts in none.

wise_response: "When the Master was eating by the side of a mourner, he never ate to the full. He did not sing on the same day in which he had been weeping."
why_it_worked: Restraint in the presence of grief shows that you share it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Enjoying yourself openly beside someone in mourning.

situation: You are tempted to chase money at any cost.
wise_response: "If the search for riches is sure to be successful, though I should become a groom with whip in hand to get them, I will do so. As the search may not be successful, I will follow after that which I love."
why_it_worked: Wealth is uncertain. What is worth loving is a surer thing to spend your life on.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving your life to a chase for riches that may never come.

situation: You are asked whether people who gave up everything for principle regretted it.
wise_response: Of Po-i and Shu-ch'i the Master said, "They sought to act virtuously, and they did so; what was there for them to repine about?"
why_it_worked: If you sought to do right and did it, there is nothing left to regret, whatever it cost.
tempting_wrong_answer: Second-guessing a right choice because it was costly.

wise_response: "The superior man is satisfied and composed; the mean man is always full of distress."
why_it_worked: A clear conscience brings calm. Grasping and scheming bring constant worry.

wise_response: "When I walk along with two others, they may serve me as my teachers. I will select their good qualities and follow them, their bad qualities and avoid them."
why_it_worked: Anyone can teach you something, either by example or by warning.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking only great people have anything to teach you.

wise_response: "Having not and yet affecting to have, empty and yet affecting to be full, straitened and yet affecting to be at ease:-- it is difficult with such characteristics to have constancy."

tempting_wrong_answer: Putting on a show of wealth, knowledge or ease you do not have.

wise_response: "The Master angled,-- but did not use a net. He shot,-- but not at birds perching."
why_it_worked: Take what you need and give the creature a fair chance. Restraint shows respect for life.
tempting_wrong_answer: Taking all you can by the easiest means, with no thought for fairness.

situation: Goodness seems far away from you.
wise_response: "Is virtue a thing remote? I wish to be virtuous, and lo! virtue is at hand."
why_it_worked: Goodness begins the moment you truly want it.

situation: Someone points out your error in public.
wise_response: When criticized for his answer, the Master said, "I am fortunate! If I have any errors, people are sure to know them."
why_it_worked: Having faults pointed out is a gift that lets you correct them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Bristling and defending yourself when criticized.

translation.original_text: 陳司敗問：「昭公知禮乎？」孔子對曰：「知禮。」孔子退，揖巫馬期而進之，曰：「吾聞君子不黨，君子亦黨乎？君取於吳爲同姓，謂之吳孟子。君而知禮，孰不知禮？」巫馬期以吿。子曰：「丘也幸，苟有過，人必知之。」

situation: You are tempted to push someone you dislike into a corner.
wise_response: "The man who is fond of daring and is dissatisfied with poverty, will proceed to insubordination. So will the man who is not virtuous, when you carry your dislike of him to an extreme."
why_it_worked: Pressing too hard on a bad person drives them to worse. Restraint even toward wrongdoers prevents greater harm.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hounding someone without limit because they deserve disapproval.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「好勇疾貧，亂也。人而不仁，疾之已甚，亂也。」

situation: You are talented and know it.
wise_response: "Though a man have abilities as admirable as those of the Duke of Chau, yet if he be proud and niggardly, those other things are really not worth being looked at."
why_it_worked: Pride and stinginess cancel out talent. Ability is worth little without a generous, humble spirit.
tempting_wrong_answer: Relying on your gifts to excuse arrogance and meanness.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「如有周公之才之美，使驕且吝，其餘不足觀也已！」

situation: You have opinions about how someone else's job should be done.
wise_response: "He who is not in any particular office, has nothing to do with plans for the administration of its duties."
why_it_worked: Meddling in others' responsibilities causes confusion. Tend to your own.
tempting_wrong_answer: Interfering in matters that belong to someone else.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「不在其位，不謀其政。」

situation: You are zealous, or simple, and think that is enough.
wise_response: "Ardent and yet not upright; stupid and yet not attentive; simple and yet not sincere:-- such persons I do not understand."
why_it_worked: A weakness can at least come with a matching virtue. Zeal should come with honesty, and simplicity with sincerity.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being eager without being straight, or plain without being honest.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「狂而不直，侗而不愿，悾悾而不信，吾不知之矣！」

situation: You are learning something important.
wise_response: "Learn as if you could not reach your object, and were always fearing also lest you should lose it."
why_it_worked: Urgency to gain and care to keep what you have learned stop you from coasting.
tempting_wrong_answer: Learning casually and letting what you learned slip.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「學如不及，猶恐失之。」

situation: You have resources and must choose what to spend them on.
wise_response: Of Yu: "He used himself coarse food and drink... He lived in a low mean house, but expended all his strength on the ditches and water-channels."
why_it_worked: A leader who lives plainly and spends on public need serves the people.
tempting_wrong_answer: Living lavishly while neglecting what the community needs.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「禹，吾無間然矣！菲飮食，而致孝乎鬼神；惡衣服，而致美乎黻冕；卑宮室，而盡力乎溝洫。禹，吾無間然矣！」

situation: You see someone in mourning, someone of high office, or a blind person approaching.
wise_response: "Though they were younger than himself, he would rise up, and if he had to pass by them, he would do so hastily."
why_it_worked: Rising for the grieving and the blind shows respect for their condition, regardless of age.
tempting_wrong_answer: Ignoring the grief or disability of people you pass.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「鳳鳥不至，河不出圖，吾已矣夫！」

situation: You are drawn more to beauty than to goodness.
wise_response: "I have not seen one who loves virtue as he loves beauty."
why_it_worked: Attraction to looks comes easily. Wanting goodness that strongly takes deliberate effort.
tempting_wrong_answer: Pursuing beauty and appearance with zeal and goodness with indifference.

translation.original_text: 子在川上曰：「逝者如斯夫！不舍晝夜。」

situation: You meet a young person and are inclined to dismiss them.
wise_response: "A youth is to be regarded with respect. How do we know that his future will not be equal to our present?"
why_it_worked: The young may surpass us. Respect leaves room for that.
tempting_wrong_answer: Writing off young people because of their age.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「苗而不秀者，有矣夫！秀而不實者，有矣夫！」

situation: Someone with power tries to force your will.
wise_response: "The commander of the forces of a large state may be carried off, but the will of even a common man cannot be taken from him."
why_it_worked: Your resolve belongs to you. No force can take it unless you give it up.
tempting_wrong_answer: Surrendering your principles because you feel powerless.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「主忠信，毋友不如己者，過則勿憚改。」

situation: You stand in shabby clothes beside people dressed in fine furs.
wise_response: Of Tsze-lu: "Dressed himself in a tattered robe... standing by the side of men dressed in furs, and not ashamed." Yet when he kept repeating the praise, the Master said it was "by no means sufficient."
why_it_worked: Freedom from envy is good, but resting on one virtue and repeating your praise stops growth.
tempting_wrong_answer: Feeling shame over poverty, or growing smug over one good quality.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「三軍可奪帥也，匹夫不可奪志也。」

situation: Hard times come.
wise_response: "When the year becomes cold, then we know how the pine and the cypress are the last to lose their leaves."
why_it_worked: Character shows in adversity. Those who hold steady when it is hard are the ones to trust.
tempting_wrong_answer: Holding up only while times are easy.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「衣敝縕袍，與衣狐貉者立，而不恥者，其由也與！『不忮不求，何用不臧？』子路終身誦之。子曰：「是道也，何足以臧？」

situation: You say you would do the right thing but it is too far out of reach.
wise_response: On a poem lamenting a distant house, the Master said, "It is the want of thought about it. How is it distant?"
why_it_worked: What seems far away is often only neglected. Real desire closes the distance.
tempting_wrong_answer: Excusing yourself because the good seems remote.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「可與共學，未可與適道；可與適道，未可與立；可與立，未可與權。」

situation: Property is damaged in an accident.
wise_response: When the stable burned down, the Master returned and asked, "Has any man been hurt?" He did not ask about the horses.
why_it_worked: People come before property. The first concern after a disaster is for those who may be hurt.
tempting_wrong_answer: Asking first about the loss of goods.

wise_response: "When the villagers were drinking together, on those who carried staffs going out, he went out immediately after."
why_it_worked: Letting elders lead and leaving with them shows respect for age.
tempting_wrong_answer: Staying on and carrying on after your elders have gone.

situation: You wonder how to tell whether someone is truly good to their family.
wise_response: "Filial indeed is Min Tsze-ch'ien! Other people say nothing of him different from the report of his parents and brothers."
why_it_worked: Real goodness at home is visible to outsiders too. When neighbors and family agree, the praise is earned.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being praised by your family for show while outsiders see something else.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「孝哉，閔子騫！人不間於其父母昆弟之言。」

wise_response: "If I am not to mourn bitterly for this man, for whom should I mourn?"
why_it_worked: Deep grief for someone truly worthy is fitting. Love is shown in mourning.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hiding real grief to look composed.

translation.original_text: 顏淵死，子哭之慟。從者曰：「子慟矣！」曰：「有慟乎？非夫人之爲慟而誰爲？」

situation: People want to honor someone with more display than is fitting.
wise_response: The disciples gave Yen Yuan a grand funeral against the Master's wish. He said, "Hui behaved towards me as his father. I have not been able to treat him as my son. The fault is not mine."
why_it_worked: Honor that goes beyond what the person and their means warrant is not honor. Simple fittingness is the true respect.
tempting_wrong_answer: Staging a lavish display and calling it love.

translation.original_text: 顏淵死，門人欲厚葬之。子曰：「不可。」門人厚葬之。子曰：「回也，視予猶父也，予不得視猶子也；非我也，夫二三子也。」

situation: Someone proposes to tear down and rebuild something that only needs repair.
wise_response: Min Tsze-ch'ien said, "Suppose it were to be repaired after its old style;-- why must it be altered and made anew?" The Master said, "when he does, he is sure to hit the point."
why_it_worked: Needless rebuilding wastes people's labor and money. Speaking rarely gives your words weight.
tempting_wrong_answer: Pushing grand new projects for show at public expense.

situation: You work for someone already rich and are asked to squeeze more from the people for them.
wise_response: When Ch'iu collected heavier imposts to enrich the already wealthy Chi family, the Master said, "He is no disciple of mine. My little children, beat the drum and assail him."
why_it_worked: Helping the rich take more from the poor is a betrayal of the people, and serving well does not excuse it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Doing an unjust job efficiently because your employer asks.

translation.original_text: 季氏富於周公，而求也爲之聚斂而附益之。子曰：「非吾徒也！小子鳴鼓攻之，可也。」

situation: Someone talks seriously and sincerely, and you are ready to call them good.
wise_response: "If, because a man's discourse appears solid and sincere, we allow him to be a good man, is he really a superior man? or is his gravity only in appearance?"
why_it_worked: Serious talk can be a costume. Judge by conduct over time.
tempting_wrong_answer: Trusting someone because they sound earnest.

situation: You serve a leader who asks you to do wrong.
wise_response: "What is called a great minister, is one who serves his prince according to what is right, and when he finds he cannot do so, retires." Even ordinary ministers would not follow into parricide or regicide.
why_it_worked: Loyalty is to what is right. When service requires wrongdoing, the honorable course is to step away.
tempting_wrong_answer: Following a boss into wrongdoing because loyalty seems to demand it.

translation.original_text: 季子然問：「仲由、冉求可謂大臣與？」子曰：「吾以子爲異之問，曾由與求之問？所謂大臣者，以道事君，不可則止。今由與求也，可謂具臣矣。」曰：「然則從之者與？」子曰：「弒父與君，亦不從也。」

situation: You put someone unready into a responsible role, then defend it with clever words.
wise_response: When Tsze-lu appointed an untrained man governor and argued that books were unnecessary, the Master said, "You are injuring a man's son... It is on this account that I hate your glib-tongued people."
why_it_worked: Putting someone in a role before they are ready harms them and those they serve. Clever excuses make it worse.
tempting_wrong_answer: Defending a poor decision with smooth argument.

translation.original_text: 子路使子羔爲費宰。子曰：「賊夫人之子。」子路曰：「有民人焉，有社稷焉；何必讀書，然後爲學？」子曰：「是故惡夫佞者。」

situation: You want to know how to become good.
wise_response: "To subdue one's self and return to propriety, is perfect virtue... Look not at what is contrary to propriety; listen not to what is contrary to propriety; speak not what is contrary to propriety; make no movement which is contrary to propriety."
why_it_worked: Goodness comes from mastering yourself in what you watch, hear, say and do. It starts with you, not with others.
tempting_wrong_answer: Blaming circumstances or others while indulging every impulse.

translation.original_text: 顏淵問「仁」。子曰：「克己復禮爲仁。一日克己復禮，天下歸仁焉，爲仁由己，而由人乎哉？」顏淵曰：「請問其目。」子曰：「非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。」顏淵曰：「回雖不敏，請事斯語矣！」
translation.edition: Analects, Chinese text from Chinese Wikisource (論語), CC BY-SA 4.0 transcription; English tr. James Legge, public domain

situation: You see both strengths and faults in someone.
wise_response: "The superior man seeks to perfect the admirable qualities of men, and does not seek to perfect their bad qualities. The mean man does the opposite of this."
why_it_worked: Encouraging what is best in people helps them grow. Feeding their worst traits does harm.
tempting_wrong_answer: Egging people on in their faults or ignoring their virtues.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「君子成人之美，不成人之惡。小人反是。」

situation: You are tempted to speak quickly and promise easily.
wise_response: "The man of perfect virtue is cautious and slow in his speech... When a man feels the difficulty of doing, can he be other than cautious and slow in speaking?"
why_it_worked: Knowing how hard it is to do what you say makes you careful about saying it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Speaking glibly about things you have not done and may not do.

translation.original_text: 司馬牛問「仁」。子曰：「仁者，其言也訒。」曰：「其言也訒，斯謂之『仁』已乎？」子曰：「爲之難，言之得無訒乎！」

situation: You feel alone because you have no brothers or family.
wise_response: Tsze-hsia said, "Let the superior man never fail reverentially to order his own conduct, and let him be respectful to others and observant of propriety:-- then all within the four seas will be his brothers."
why_it_worked: Respect and good conduct make kin of strangers. Family can be found as well as born into.
tempting_wrong_answer: Brooding over what you lack instead of making new ties.

translation.original_text: 司馬牛憂曰：「人皆有兄弟，我獨亡！」子夏曰：「商聞之矣：『死生有命，富貴在天』君子敬而無失，與人恭而有禮，四海之內，皆兄弟也，君子何患乎無兄弟也！」

situation: You lead, and hard times force you to give something up.
wise_response: Of food, arms and the people's trust, give up arms first, then food: "From of old, death has been the lot of all men; but if the people have no faith in their rulers, there is no standing for the state."
why_it_worked: Trust is the last thing a leader can afford to lose. Without it, nothing else holds.
tempting_wrong_answer: Sacrificing honesty and trust to protect resources.

translation.original_text: 子貢問「政」。子曰：「足食，足兵，民信之矣。」子貢曰：「必不得已而去，於斯三者何先？」曰：「去兵。」子貢曰：「必不得已而去，於斯二者何先？」曰：「去食。自古皆有死，民無信不立。」

situation: Someone says only inner substance matters and outward refinement is useless.
wise_response: Tsze-kung said, "Four horses cannot overtake the tongue. Ornament is as substance; substance is as ornament. The hide of a tiger or a leopard stripped of its hair, is like the hide of a dog."
why_it_worked: Words once spoken cannot be recalled, so speak with care. Refinement is part of what makes character recognizable.
tempting_wrong_answer: Dismissing courtesy and form, and speaking rashly.

translation.original_text: 棘子成曰：「君子質而已矣，何以文爲？」子貢曰：「惜乎，夫子之說，君子也，駟不及舌！文猶質也，質猶文也；虎豹之鞹，猶犬羊之鞹。」

situation: Your feelings toward someone swing between love and hatred.
wise_response: "You love a man and wish him to live; you hate him and wish him to die. Having wished him to live, you also wish him to die. This is a case of delusion." Hold faithfulness and sincerity first.
why_it_worked: Feelings that swing to extremes cloud judgment. Steadiness rests on faithfulness.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting moods decide how you treat people.

translation.original_text: 子張問「崇德，辨惑。」子曰：「主忠信，徙義：崇德也。愛之欲其生，惡之欲其死；既欲其生，又欲其死：是惑也。」（誠不以富，亦祇以異。）

situation: You hold a role in your family or in public life.
wise_response: "There is government, when the prince is prince, and the minister is minister; when the father is father, and the son is son."
why_it_worked: Order depends on each person actually doing what their role requires.
tempting_wrong_answer: Holding a title while neglecting its duties.

translation.original_text: 齊景公問「政」於孔子。孔子對曰：「君君，臣臣，父父，子子。」公曰：「善哉！信如君不君，臣不臣，父不父，子不子，雖有粟，吾得而食諸？」

situation: You have made a promise.
wise_response: "Tsze-lu never slept over a promise."
why_it_worked: Keeping a promise promptly shows it was meant. Delay invites forgetting.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting promises sit until they are forgotten.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「片言可以折獄者，其由也與！」子路無宿諾。

situation: You are responsible for running things over a long time.
wise_response: "The art of governing is to keep its affairs before the mind without weariness, and to practise them with undeviating consistency."
why_it_worked: Steady, untiring attention matters more than bursts of effort.
tempting_wrong_answer: Losing interest and letting things slide.

translation.original_text: 子張問「政」。子曰：「居之無倦，行之以忠。」

situation: You want to grow in goodness and correct your faults.
wise_response: "To assail one's own wickedness and not assail that of others;-- is not this the way to correct cherished evil? For a morning's anger to disregard one's own life, and involve that of his parents;-- is not this a case of delusion?"
why_it_worked: Work on your own faults, not others'. Anger in a moment can ruin you and your family.
tempting_wrong_answer: Attacking others' faults and acting rashly in anger.

translation.original_text: 樊遲從遊於舞雩之下曰：「敢問崇德，脩慝，辨惑？」子曰：「善哉問！先事後得，非『崇德』與？攻其惡，無攻人之惡，非『脩慝』與？一朝之忿，忘其身以及其親，非『惑』與？」

situation: Your friend is going wrong.
wise_response: "Faithfully admonish your friend, and skillfully lead him on. If you find him impracticable, stop. Do not disgrace yourself."
why_it_worked: Honest, careful counsel is part of friendship, but pushing past the point of listening only harms both.
tempting_wrong_answer: Staying silent to keep the peace, or nagging until the friendship breaks.

translation.original_text: 子貢問「友」。子曰：「忠吿而善道之，不可則止，毋自辱焉。」

situation: You are choosing what friendship is for.
wise_response: "The superior man on grounds of culture meets with his friends, and by their friendship helps his virtue."
why_it_worked: Good friends help each other become better.
tempting_wrong_answer: Choosing friends for pleasure or advantage alone.

translation.original_text: 曾子曰：「君子以文會友，以友輔仁。」

situation: You are put in charge of people.
wise_response: "Go before the people with your example, and be laborious in their affairs." Asked for more, he said, "Be not weary."
why_it_worked: Leading by example and working hard for others earns their following. Tirelessness keeps it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving orders from a distance and tiring of the work.

situation: You are responsible for many people and wonder what to do for them.
wise_response: "Enrich them." And then? "Teach them."
why_it_worked: People's basic needs come first. Once those are met, they should be helped to grow.
tempting_wrong_answer: Preaching to people who are hungry, or feeding them and leaving them ignorant.

situation: You want to correct others.
wise_response: "If a minister make his own conduct correct, what difficulty will he have in assisting in government? If he cannot rectify himself, what has he to do with rectifying others?"
why_it_worked: You cannot set others straight until you are straight yourself.
tempting_wrong_answer: Correcting others while ignoring your own faults.

situation: You want to know whether you are leading well.
wise_response: "Good government obtains, when those who are near are made happy, and those who are far off are attracted."
why_it_worked: A good community is one where those inside are content and outsiders want to come.
tempting_wrong_answer: Measuring success by power while those close to you are miserable.

situation: You want quick results and small wins.
wise_response: "Do not be desirous to have things done quickly; do not look at small advantages. Desire to have things done quickly prevents their being done thoroughly. Looking at small advantages prevents great affairs from being accomplished."
why_it_worked: Haste ruins thoroughness, and petty gains distract from what matters.
tempting_wrong_answer: Rushing for fast results and grabbing every small advantage.

translation.original_text: 子夏爲莒父宰，問政。子曰：「無欲速，無見小利。欲速，則不達；見小利，則大事不成。」

situation: You live privately, work, and deal with people, some of them strangers.
wise_response: "It is, in retirement, to be sedately grave; in the management of business, to be reverently attentive; in intercourse with others, to be strictly sincere. Though a man go among rude, uncultivated tribes, these qualities may not be neglected."
why_it_worked: Good conduct does not change with the audience. It holds among strangers as at home.
tempting_wrong_answer: Behaving well only where you are known and dropping standards abroad.

translation.original_text: 樊遲問仁。子曰：「居處恭，執事敬，與人忠。雖之夷狄，不可棄也。」

situation: Your goodness comes and goes.
wise_response: "A man without constancy cannot be either a wizard or a doctor... Inconstant in his virtue, he will be visited with disgrace."
why_it_worked: Goodness that is not steady is not trusted. Constancy is part of virtue.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being good when it suits you and dropping it when it does not.

situation: You want to be friendly with people.
wise_response: "The superior man is affable, but not adulatory; the mean man is adulatory, but not affable."
why_it_worked: Real friendliness is honest warmth. Flattery is false and keeps people at a distance.
tempting_wrong_answer: Flattering people to win them instead of being genuinely kind.

situation: You judge someone by whether everyone likes or dislikes them.
wise_response: "It is better than either of these cases that the good in the neighborhood love him, and the bad hate him."
why_it_worked: Popularity proves little. Being liked by the good and disliked by the bad is a truer sign.
tempting_wrong_answer: Judging people by universal approval or universal dislike.

wise_response: "The superior man has a dignified ease without pride. The mean man has pride without a dignified ease."
why_it_worked: Inner steadiness needs no display. Pride is a sign of insecurity.
tempting_wrong_answer: Carrying yourself with arrogance and calling it confidence.

wise_response: "To govern means to rectify. If you lead on the people with correctness, who will dare not to be correct?"
why_it_worked: The leader's own correctness is the standard others follow.
tempting_wrong_answer: Demanding good conduct while behaving badly yourself.

wise_response: "If you, sir, were not covetous, although you should reward them to do it, they would not steal."
why_it_worked: Greed at the top teaches greed below. Fix your own covetousness first.
tempting_wrong_answer: Blaming others for crimes your own example encourages.

wise_response: The philosopher Tsang examined himself daily: had he been unfaithful in doing business for others, insincere with friends, or failed to practise what his teacher taught?
why_it_worked: Regular honest self-review catches small failures of loyalty and sincerity before they harden into habit.
tempting_wrong_answer: Never looking back at your own conduct and assuming you have been faithful.

situation: You could learn something from someone below you in rank.
wise_response: Kung-wan earned his honored title because "he was of an active nature and yet fond of learning, and he was not ashamed to ask and learn of his inferiors."
why_it_worked: Wisdom does not follow rank. Asking those beneath you shows true humility.
tempting_wrong_answer: Refusing to learn from juniors to protect your status.

situation: You are in charge of a state or an organization and its people.
wise_response: "There must be reverent attention to business, and sincerity; economy in expenditure, and love for men; and the employment of the people at the proper seasons."
why_it_worked: Leaders who are careful, sincere and thrifty, and who respect people's time and needs, keep their trust.
tempting_wrong_answer: Running things carelessly, spending freely, and calling on people whenever it suits you regardless of their burdens.

situation: A young person is working out what to put first in life.
wise_response: "A youth, when at home, should be filial, and, abroad, respectful to his elders. He should be earnest and truthful. He should overflow in love to all." Study comes after these.
why_it_worked: Character is the foundation. Learning built on a careless or unkind life is hollow.
tempting_wrong_answer: Chasing accomplishments and polish while neglecting honesty, respect and kindness.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「弟子入則孝，出則弟，謹而信，汎愛眾，而親仁。行有餘力，則以學文。」

situation: You lead others and are deciding how to hold their loyalty.
wise_response: "He who exercises government by means of his virtue may be compared to the north polar star, which keeps its place and all the stars turn towards it."
why_it_worked: People orient themselves around a leader whose character is steady. Example draws them without force.
tempting_wrong_answer: Relying on pressure and control because your own conduct gives no one a reason to follow.

situation: You are wondering what you owe your parents.
wise_response: Asked about filial piety, the Master said, "Parents are anxious lest their children should be sick." Take care of yourself so they need not worry.
why_it_worked: Part of honoring parents is not adding to their worry through your own carelessness.
tempting_wrong_answer: Living recklessly and leaving your parents to carry the fear.

situation: You provide for aging parents and think that is enough.
wise_response: "The filial piety of now-a-days means the support of one's parents. But dogs and horses likewise are able to do something in the way of support;-- without reverence, what is there to distinguish the one support given from the other?"
why_it_worked: Food and shelter without respect is mere upkeep. Reverence is what makes care honorable.
tempting_wrong_answer: Paying the bills for your parents while treating them with impatience or contempt.

translation.original_text: 子游問孝。子曰：「今之孝者，是謂能養。至於犬馬，皆能有養。不敬，何以別乎？」

wise_response: The superior man "acts before he speaks, and afterwards speaks according to his actions."
why_it_worked: Words that follow deeds can be trusted. Words that run ahead of them are boasts.
tempting_wrong_answer: Announcing big intentions and letting the talk stand in for the doing.

situation: You must keep order among people and are reaching for rules and penalties.
wise_response: "If the people be led by laws... and punishments, they will try to avoid the punishment, but have no sense of shame. If they be led by virtue... they will have the sense of shame, and moreover will become good."
why_it_worked: Punishment teaches people to dodge. Example and good custom teach them to care about doing right.
tempting_wrong_answer: Governing by threats alone and getting people who obey only when watched.

wise_response: "The difficulty is with the countenance." Doing the tasks is not enough; the manner in which you serve them matters.
why_it_worked: A grudging face tells your parents they are a burden. Warmth is the hard part of care.
tempting_wrong_answer: Doing your duty to elders with visible resentment and thinking the task is what counts.

wise_response: "See what a man does. Mark his motives. Examine in what things he rests. How can a man conceal his character?"
why_it_worked: Actions, the reasons behind them, and what a person finds contentment in together reveal who they are.
tempting_wrong_answer: Judging people by their words or a single impression.

situation: You need information from others and are tempted to pry or demand it.
wise_response: Tsze-kung said the Master was "benign, upright, courteous, temperate, and complaisant, and thus he gets his information."
why_it_worked: People open up to someone whose manner is gentle and upright. Good character does what pressure cannot.
tempting_wrong_answer: Pushing, prying or demanding what people would give freely to someone they trusted.

wise_response: "When you know a thing, to hold that you know it; and when you do not know a thing, to allow that you do not know it;-- this is knowledge."
why_it_worked: Admitting ignorance keeps you honest and open to learning. Pretending closes both.
tempting_wrong_answer: Bluffing to avoid looking uninformed.

why_it_worked: A promise is only worth keeping if it was right to make. Choosing good people to depend on keeps you from shame.
tempting_wrong_answer: Making promises you should not keep, or relying on people of poor character.

wise_response: "Things that are done, it is needless to speak about; things that have had their course, it is needless to remonstrate about; things that are past, it is needless to blame."
why_it_worked: Blame over what cannot be changed only sours things. Effort belongs to what can still be done.
tempting_wrong_answer: Rehashing and assigning blame for things that are over.

why_it_worked: Respect and loyalty are earned by a leader's own seriousness, kindness, and care for those who lag behind.
tempting_wrong_answer: Demanding respect while neglecting your own conduct and discarding the weak.

why_it_worked: Competing courteously keeps rivalry from turning into enmity. Your character does not pause during a contest.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating competition as license to be rude or ruthless.

wise_response: Tsze-ch'an had four marks of a superior man: "in his conduct of himself, he was humble; in serving his superiors, he was respectful; in nourishing the people, he was kind; in ordering the people, he was just."
why_it_worked: Each relationship asks for something different: humility for yourself, respect upward, kindness and fairness downward.
tempting_wrong_answer: Fawning upward while being harsh or unfair to those below.

wise_response: "T'ai-po may be said to have reached the highest point of virtuous action. Thrice he declined the kingdom, and the people in ignorance of his motives could not express their approbation of his conduct."
why_it_worked: The highest good is done for its own sake, even when no one knows enough to praise it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Doing good only where it will be seen and applauded.

why_it_worked: Meeting people as they come now gives them a chance to change.

wise_response: Tsze-hsia said that one who loves virtue more than beauty, serves his parents with all his strength, serves his prince devotedly, and keeps his word to friends has learned, "although men say that he has not learned."
why_it_worked: Learning is measured by how a person lives. Faithful conduct is the real proof of education.
tempting_wrong_answer: Judging people by credentials and book knowledge while ignoring how they treat others.

situation: You keep learning and working on yourself, but no one notices or credits you.
wise_response: "Is he not a man of complete virtue, who feels no discomposure though men may take no note of him?" Keep at the work and stay at ease when you go unrecognized.
why_it_worked: The worth of learning and good conduct does not depend on an audience. A person who needs notice is easily thrown off course.
tempting_wrong_answer: Growing bitter or showy when your effort goes unseen, or quitting because no one praises it.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「學而時習之，不亦說乎？有朋自遠方來，不亦樂乎？人不知而不慍，不亦君子乎？」
translation.edition: Analects, Chinese text from Chinese Wikisource (論語), CC BY-SA 4.0 transcription; English tr. James Legge, public domain

situation: You face long hardship, or long ease.
wise_response: "Those who are without virtue cannot abide long either in a condition of poverty and hardship, or in a condition of enjoyment. The virtuous rest in virtue."
why_it_worked: Character gives steadiness in both want and plenty. Without it, hardship corrupts and comfort spoils.
tempting_wrong_answer: Turning bitter or dishonest in hard times and indulgent in good ones.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「不仁者，不可以久處約，不可以長處樂。仁者安仁，知者利仁。」
translation.edition: Analects, Chinese text from Chinese Wikisource (論語), CC BY-SA 4.0 transcription; English tr. James Legge, public domain

source.author: James Legge (1861)

source.licence: Chinese text public domain; transcription from Chinese Wikisource (CC BY-SA 4.0). English tr. James Legge, public domain

situation: You have done something wrong.
wise_response: "I have not yet seen one who could perceive his faults, and inwardly accuse himself."
why_it_worked: Seeing your own fault and holding yourself to account is rare, and it is where change begins.
tempting_wrong_answer: Excusing yourself or blaming others whenever you fall short.

translation.original_text: 顏淵、季路侍。子曰：「盍各言爾志？」子路曰：「願，與朋友共，敝之而無憾。」顏淵曰：「願無伐善，無施勞。」子路曰：「願聞子之志。」子曰：「老者安之，朋友信之，少者懷之。」

situation: You are able and well supplied, and someone offends you.
wise_response: Tsang praised a friend who, "gifted with ability, and yet putting questions to those who were not so... full, and yet counting himself as empty; offended against, and yet entering into no altercation."
why_it_worked: Humility keeps you learning from anyone. Letting an offense pass without a quarrel keeps peace.
tempting_wrong_answer: Lording your ability over others and fighting back at every slight.

translation.original_text: 曾子曰：「以能問於不能，以多問於寡，有若無，實若虛，犯而不校。昔者吾友，嘗從事於斯矣。」

situation: You are weighing your duties in public and at home.
wise_response: "Abroad, to serve the high ministers and nobles; at home, to serve one's father and elder brothers... and not to be overcome of wine."
why_it_worked: Faithful service in both places and control over drink are basic, and still hard.
tempting_wrong_answer: Neglecting home duties or losing yourself in drink.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「吾自衞反魯，然後樂正，雅頌各得其所。」

situation: Times are hard and you are tempted to raise taxes on people who are already struggling.
wise_response: Yu Zo advised lowering the tax to a tithe: "If the people have plenty, their prince will not be left to want alone. If the people are in want, their prince cannot enjoy plenty alone."
why_it_worked: A leader's fortune is tied to the people's. Easing their burden in scarcity serves everyone.
tempting_wrong_answer: Squeezing more from those who have least when money is short.

translation.original_text: 哀公問於有若曰：「年饑，用不足，如之何？」有若對曰：「盍徹乎？」曰：「二，吾猶不足，如之何其徹也？」對曰：「百姓足，君孰與不足？百姓不足，君孰與足！」

situation: You want to be distinguished and well-known.
wise_response: "That is notoriety, not distinction. Now the man of distinction is solid and straightforward, and loves righteousness... He is anxious to humble himself to others." The notorious man "assumes the appearance of virtue, but his actions are opposed to it."
why_it_worked: Fame and true worth are different. Real distinction comes from honest, humble conduct.
tempting_wrong_answer: Chasing reputation while your actions contradict the image.

translation.original_text: 子張問：「士何如斯可謂之『達』矣？」子曰：「何哉，爾所謂『達』者？」子張對曰：「在邦必聞，在家必聞。」子曰：「是『聞』也，非『達』也。夫『達』也者，質直而好義，察言而觀色，慮以下人，在邦必達，在家必達。夫『聞』也者：色取仁而行違，居之不疑。在邦必聞，在家必聞。」
translation.edition: Analects, Chinese text from Chinese Wikisource (論語), CC BY-SA 4.0 transcription; English tr. James Legge, public domain

situation: You have discovered a fault in yourself.
wise_response: "Hold faithfulness and sincerity as first principles... When you have faults, do not fear to abandon them."
why_it_worked: A fault admitted and dropped does little harm. One defended out of pride keeps growing.
tempting_wrong_answer: Protecting your image by refusing to change once you see you were wrong.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「君子不重則不威，學則不固。主忠信，無友不如己者，過則勿憚改。」
translation.edition: Analects, Chinese text from Chinese Wikisource (論語), CC BY-SA 4.0 transcription; English tr. James Legge, public domain

situation: You want to advance in your career.
wise_response: "Hear much and put aside the points of which you stand in doubt, while you speak cautiously... See much and put aside the things which seem perilous." Few occasions for blame and few for regret lead to advancement.
why_it_worked: Care in speech and action builds a record people can trust. Advancement follows from that.
tempting_wrong_answer: Speaking on everything and acting rashly to get noticed.

translation.original_text: 子張學干祿。子曰：「多聞闕疑，愼言其餘，則寡尤；多見闕殆，愼行其餘，則寡悔。言寡尤，行寡悔，祿在其中矣。」

situation: You meet someone better than you, or someone worse.
wise_response: "When we see men of worth, we should think of equalling them; when we see men of a contrary character, we should turn inwards and examine ourselves."
why_it_worked: Others are mirrors. Good people show you what to aim for; bad ones show you what to check in yourself.
tempting_wrong_answer: Envying the good and sneering at the bad without looking at yourself.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「見賢思齊焉，見不賢而內自省也。」
translation.edition: Analects, Chinese text from Chinese Wikisource (論語), CC BY-SA 4.0 transcription; English tr. James Legge, public domain

situation: You keep correcting your boss or your friend.
wise_response: "In serving a prince, frequent remonstrances lead to disgrace. Between friends, frequent reproofs make the friendship distant."
why_it_worked: Correction has a limit. Pressing it too often damages the relationship and loses the hearing.
tempting_wrong_answer: Lecturing again and again until the other person stops listening.

translation.original_text: 子游曰：「事君數，斯辱矣。朋友數，斯疏矣。」 ===校勘記===

situation: You are deciding whom to give to.
wise_response: When a well-off disciple was sent on a mission, the Master gave little for his mother, saying, "a superior man helps the distressed, but does not add to the wealth of the rich." When a poor governor refused his salary, he said, "May you not give them away in the neighborhoods?"
why_it_worked: Giving should go where there is need. A surplus you do not need can still help your neighbors.
tempting_wrong_answer: Showering gifts on the comfortable while the needy go without, or refusing what you could pass on.

translation.original_text: 子華使於齊，冉子爲其母請粟。子曰：「與之釜。」請益，曰：「與之庾。」冉子與之粟五秉。子曰：「赤之適齊也，乘肥馬，衣輕裘；吾聞之也：君子周急不繼富。」原思爲之宰，與之粟九百，辭。子曰：「毋！以與爾鄰里鄉黨乎！」

situation: You have good qualities like respect, care, boldness or frankness, and you lean on them without limit.
wise_response: "Respectfulness, without the rules of propriety, becomes laborious bustle; carefulness... becomes timidity; boldness... becomes insubordination; straightforwardness... becomes rudeness." And leaders who do not neglect old friends keep the people from meanness.
why_it_worked: Every virtue needs measure or it turns into its own fault. Leaders who stay loyal to old friends teach loyalty by example.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking a good trait can be pushed without limit, or dropping old friends once you rise.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「恭而無禮則勞，愼而無禮則葸，勇而無禮則亂，直而無禮則絞。君子篤於親，則民興於仁。故舊不遺，則民不偷。」

situation: Others start to look down on a fellow student after a teacher's sharp remark.
wise_response: When the disciples stopped respecting Tsze-lu, the Master said, "Yu has ascended to the hall, though he has not yet passed into the inner apartments."
why_it_worked: A teacher's correction should not become a license for others to scorn. Give people credit for how far they have come.
tempting_wrong_answer: Piling on someone once an authority has criticized them.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「由之瑟，奚爲於丘之門？」門人不敬子路。子曰：「由也升堂矣，未入於室也！」

situation: You are following rules of courtesy and wonder whether ease or strict form matters more.
wise_response: "In practising the rules of propriety, a natural ease is to be prized." Yet ease that is not "regulated by the rules of propriety" should not be done either.
why_it_worked: Courtesy works best when it is natural, but naturalness without any standard slides into carelessness.
tempting_wrong_answer: Either going through stiff forms with no warmth, or dropping all standards in the name of being relaxed.

situation: Joy or grief is running strong in you.
wise_response: The Kwan Tsu ode "is expressive of enjoyment without being licentious, and of grief without being hurtfully excessive."
why_it_worked: Feeling deeply is right. Letting joy or sorrow run to excess does harm.
tempting_wrong_answer: Indulging pleasure without limit or sinking into grief that damages you.

wise_response: "If a man in the morning hear the right way, he may die in the evening without regret."
why_it_worked: Understanding the right way is worth more than anything else a life might gain.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating the search for right living as something for later.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣！」

situation: Your parents are doing something wrong and will not listen.
wise_response: "A son may remonstrate with them, but gently; when he sees that they do not incline to follow his advice, he shows an increased degree of reverence, but does not abandon his purpose; and should they punish him, he does not allow himself to murmur."
why_it_worked: Gentle, persistent honesty keeps both the truth and the relationship alive.
tempting_wrong_answer: Either keeping silent to avoid conflict or confronting parents harshly and resentfully.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「事父母幾諫；見志不從，又敬而不違，勞而不怨。」

situation: You are offered a post under people whose conduct you cannot support.
wise_response: Min Tsze-ch'ien said, "Decline the offer for me politely. If any one come again to me with a second invitation, I shall be obliged to go and live on the banks of the Wan."
why_it_worked: Refusing to serve wrongdoing keeps your integrity. Doing it politely keeps the refusal from becoming a quarrel.
tempting_wrong_answer: Taking a prestigious job under bad masters because it is offered.

translation.original_text: 季氏使閔子騫爲費宰。閔子騫曰：「善爲我辭焉。如有復我者，則吾必在汶上矣。」

situation: Unjust wealth or honor is available to you.
wise_response: "With coarse rice to eat, with water to drink, and my bended arm for a pillow;-- I have still joy in the midst of these things. Riches and honours acquired by unrighteousness, are to me as a floating cloud."
why_it_worked: Joy can live with simple means. Wrongful gain is insubstantial and passes.
tempting_wrong_answer: Taking dishonest wealth because poverty seems unbearable.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「飯疏食，飮水，曲肱而枕之，樂亦在其中矣。不義而富且貴，於我如浮雲。」

situation: The duty of living well feels heavy and endless.
wise_response: "The officer may not be without breadth of mind and vigorous endurance. His burden is heavy and his course is long... Only with death does his course stop."
why_it_worked: Goodness is a lifelong load. It takes breadth and stamina, not a single effort.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating virtue as a task you can finish and set down.

translation.original_text: 曾子曰：「士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠。仁以爲己任，不亦重乎；死而後已，不亦遠乎。」

situation: You approach a problem or a person.
wise_response: "He had no foregone conclusions, no arbitrary predeterminations, no obstinacy, and no egoism."
why_it_worked: An open mind, free of fixed ideas and self-importance, sees what is actually there.
tempting_wrong_answer: Deciding in advance, digging in, and making it about yourself.

translation.original_text: 子絕四：「毋意，毋必，毋固，毋我。」

situation: You are tempted to make comfort and good food your aim.
wise_response: One who aims at virtue "in his food does not seek to gratify his appetite, nor in his dwelling place does he seek the appliances of ease; he is earnest in what he is doing, and careful in his speech."
why_it_worked: Attention given to comfort is attention taken from the work and from becoming better.
tempting_wrong_answer: Organizing life around appetite and ease while speaking carelessly.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「君子食無求飽，居無求安，敏於事而愼於言，就有道而正焉：可謂好學。」

situation: You are weighing what to think about when you act.
wise_response: "The superior man thinks of virtue; the small man thinks of comfort. The superior man thinks of the sanctions of law; the small man thinks of favours which he may receive."
why_it_worked: Attention to right and to just limits makes a good person. Attention to comfort and favors makes a small one.
tempting_wrong_answer: Steering by comfort and by what favors you might get.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「君子懷德，小人懷土；君子懷刑，小人懷惠。」
translation.edition: Analects, Chinese text from Chinese Wikisource (論語), CC BY-SA 4.0 transcription; English tr. James Legge, public domain

situation: You must choose between spending lavishly and being stingy.
wise_response: "Extravagance leads to insubordination, and parsimony to meanness. It is better to be mean than to be insubordinate."
why_it_worked: Both extremes are faults, but extravagance does more harm to order and character.
tempting_wrong_answer: Spending beyond your place to impress.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「奢則不孫，儉則固；與其不孫也，甯固。」

situation: You must decide whether to seek office or wealth under a good or bad government.
wise_response: "When a country is well-governed, poverty and a mean condition are things to be ashamed of. When a country is ill-governed, riches and honour are things to be ashamed of."
why_it_worked: Under a just order, success comes from honest work. Under a corrupt one, wealth usually means complicity.
tempting_wrong_answer: Chasing riches and rank under any regime without asking how they are earned.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「篤信好學，守死善道。危邦不入，亂邦不居。天下有道則見，無道則隱。邦有道，貧且賤焉，恥也；邦無道，富且貴焉，恥也。」

situation: Your followers want to make you look more important than you are.
wise_response: When Tsze-lu arranged ministers for the sick Master, he said, "By pretending to have ministers when I have them not, whom should I impose upon? Should I impose upon Heaven?... Is it not better that I should die in the hands of you, my disciples?"
why_it_worked: Pretending to a status you lack is deceit. Being cared for by those who love you is better than empty honor.
tempting_wrong_answer: Accepting false honors to look grand.

translation.original_text: 顏淵喟然歎曰：「仰之彌高，鑽之彌堅，瞻之在前，忽焉在後！夫子循循然善誘人：博我以文，約我以禮。欲罷不能，既竭吾才，如有所立卓爾，雖欲從之，末由也已！」

situation: You hear slow, steady slander about someone, or a sudden shocking accusation.
wise_response: "He with whom neither slander that gradually soaks into the mind, nor statements that startle like a wound in the flesh, are successful, may be called intelligent indeed."
why_it_worked: Clear judgment resists both slow poison and sudden alarm. Weigh claims before believing them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting gossip or startling accusations shape your view of people.

translation.original_text: 子張問「明」。子曰：「浸潤之譖，膚受之愬，不行焉，可謂明也已矣。浸潤之譖，膚受之愬，不行焉，可謂遠也已矣。」

situation: You speak or act on matters where words and reality do not line up.
wise_response: "If names be not correct, language is not in accordance with the truth of things. If language be not in accordance with the truth of things, affairs cannot be carried on to success... What the superior man requires, is just that in his words there may be nothing incorrect." On what he does not know, he "shows a cautious reserve."
why_it_worked: Calling things by their right names is the start of honest dealing. When words lie, justice and order break down.
tempting_wrong_answer: Using vague or false words for things and speaking confidently about what you do not know.

translation.original_text: 子路曰：「衞君待子而爲政，子將奚先？」子曰：「必也正名乎！」子路曰：「有是哉？子之迂也！奚其正？」子曰：「野哉，由也！君子於其所不知，蓋闕如也。名不正，則言不順；言不順，則事不成；事不成，則禮樂不興；禮樂不興，則刑罰不中；刑罰不中，則民無所措手足。故君子名之必可言也，言之必可行也。君子於其言，無所苟而已矣。」

situation: You run a team and face mistakes and hiring choices.
wise_response: "Employ first the services of your various officers, pardon small faults, and raise to office men of virtue and talents... Raise to office those whom you know. As to those whom you do not know, will others neglect them?"
why_it_worked: Delegating, overlooking small errors, and promoting good people builds a strong team. Others will bring forward talent you have missed.
tempting_wrong_answer: Doing everything yourself, punishing every slip, and promoting only favorites.

translation.original_text: 仲弓爲季氏宰，問政。子曰：「先有司。赦小過。擧賢才。」曰：「焉知賢才而擧之？」曰：「擧爾所知。爾所不知，人其舍諸？」

situation: You are poor and tempted to flatter, or rich and tempted to be proud.
wise_response: Not flattering when poor and not being proud when rich "will do," but better is one "who, though poor, is yet cheerful, and... who, though rich, loves the rules of propriety."
why_it_worked: Avoiding the worst is a start. The fuller goal is gladness in hardship and good conduct in plenty.
tempting_wrong_answer: Fawning over the powerful when you are poor, or looking down on others when you are rich.

translation.original_text: 子貢曰：「貧而無諂，富而無驕，何如？」子曰：「可也。未若，富而好禮者也」。子貢曰：「《詩》云：『如切如磋，如琢如磨。』其斯之謂與？」子曰：「賜也，始可與言《詩》已矣！。」

situation: You hold high position, or perform ceremonies or mourning.
wise_response: "High station filled without indulgent generosity; ceremonies performed without reverence; mourning conducted without sorrow;-- wherewith should I contemplate such ways?"
why_it_worked: Each role has a heart: generosity for the powerful, reverence in rites, sorrow in grief. Without it, the role is hollow.
tempting_wrong_answer: Holding power without generosity, or going through rituals with no feeling.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「居上不寬，爲禮不敬，臨喪不哀，吾何以觀之哉！」

situation: You have just heard good advice.
wise_response: When Tsze-lu heard anything, "if he had not yet succeeded in carrying it into practice, he was only afraid lest he should hear something else."
why_it_worked: A lesson is wasted until it is put to use. Collecting more advice can be a way of avoiding action.
tempting_wrong_answer: Piling up good counsel without acting on any of it.

translation.original_text: 子貢曰：「夫子之文章，可得而聞也；夫子之言性與天道，不可得而聞也。」

situation: You are in charge and wonder how relaxed to be.
wise_response: Chung-kung said that ease in small matters is allowable if one holds "a reverential feeling of the necessity of attention to business," but easy in heart and easy in practice is excessive. The Master agreed.
why_it_worked: Leniency in details works only if you are serious underneath. Carelessness at both levels fails people.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being lax in attitude and in practice and calling it a light touch.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「雍也，可使南面。」仲弓問子桑伯子。子曰：「可也，簡。」仲弓曰：「居敬而行簡，以臨其民，不亦可乎？居簡而行簡，無乃大簡乎？」子曰：「雍之言然。」

wise_response: Tsze-yu praised Tan-t'ai Mieh-ming, "who never in walking takes a short cut, and never comes to my office, excepting on public business."
why_it_worked: Small habits of straightness and not seeking private favor show integrity.
tempting_wrong_answer: Cutting corners and courting influential people for private ends.

wise_response: The Master worried about "not being able to move towards righteousness of which a knowledge is gained; and not being able to change what is not good."
why_it_worked: The gap between knowing what is right and doing it is the real concern.
tempting_wrong_answer: Learning what is right and making no change in how you live.

wise_response: "Sell it! Sell it! But I would wait for one to offer the price."
why_it_worked: Your gifts should be used, but you need not cheapen yourself by peddling them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Either hoarding your talent or hawking it to anyone.

wise_response: "Though a man may be able to recite the three hundred odes, yet if, when intrusted with a governmental charge, he knows not how to act... of what practical use is it?"
why_it_worked: Learning is for use. Knowledge that cannot guide action is wasted.
tempting_wrong_answer: Piling up learning that you never apply.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「誦詩三百，授之以政，不達。使於四方，不能專對；雖多，亦奚以爲？」

wise_response: "When a prince's personal conduct is correct, his government is effective without the issuing of orders. If his personal conduct is not correct, he may issue orders, but they will not be followed."
why_it_worked: Authority rests on example. A leader's conduct speaks louder than commands.
tempting_wrong_answer: Issuing more orders instead of correcting your own conduct.

wise_response: "In archery it is not going through the leather which is the principal thing;-- because people's strength is not equal."
why_it_worked: Judge people by skill and effort, which they control, not by native strength, which they do not.
tempting_wrong_answer: Ranking people by raw power and dismissing those born with less.

why_it_worked: Their long life is cause for gladness, and their age a reminder that time with them is limited.
tempting_wrong_answer: Forgetting your parents' age and taking their presence for granted.

wise_response: "To conceal resentment against a person, and appear friendly with him;-- Tso Ch'iu-ming was ashamed of such conduct. I also am ashamed of it." So too with fine words and excessive respect.
why_it_worked: False warmth is a lie told with the face. It corrodes trust on both sides.
tempting_wrong_answer: Smiling at people you secretly resent, and flattering to win favor.

situation: You want to do good for others but think only great deeds count.
wise_response: "The man of perfect virtue, wishing to be established himself, seeks also to establish others; wishing to be enlarged himself, he seeks also to enlarge others. To be able to judge of others by what is nigh in ourselves;-- this may be called the art of virtue."
why_it_worked: Using your own wishes to understand what others need is the everyday practice of goodness.
tempting_wrong_answer: Seeking your own advancement while ignoring what others need to advance.

translation.original_text: 子貢曰：「如有博施於民，而能濟眾，何如？可謂仁乎？」子曰：「何事於仁，必也聖乎？堯舜其猶病諸！夫仁者，己欲立而立人，己欲達而達人。能近取譬，可謂仁之方也已。」

why_it_worked: Delighting in others' skill and joining in honors them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Ignoring or envying another's talent.

wise_response: "Do you think, my disciples, that I have any concealments? I conceal nothing from you... that is my way."
why_it_worked: Openness builds trust between teacher and students, leader and followers.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping secrets from people who depend on you to know.

situation: A grieving friend asks you to give up something improper to give, to honor their dead child.
wise_response: When Yen Lu asked for the Master's carriage to buy an outer coffin for Yen Yuan, he refused, noting his own son Li had no outer shell either, and his position required the carriage.
why_it_worked: Grief does not change what is fitting. The Master held to the same standard he applied to his own son.
tempting_wrong_answer: Making an exception out of sentiment that you would not make for your own family.

situation: Two people ask you the same question, but they have opposite temperaments.
wise_response: To bold Tsze-lu the Master said consult your elders first; to timid Ch'iu he said act at once. "Ch'iu is retiring and slow; therefore, I urged him forward. Yu has more than his own share of energy; therefore I kept him back."
why_it_worked: Good advice fits the person. The same words can help one and harm another.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving everyone identical advice without regard to who they are.

translation.original_text: 子路問：「聞斯行諸？」子曰：「有父兄在，如之何其聞斯行之？」冉有問：「聞斯行諸？」子曰：「聞斯行之。」公西華曰：「由也問：『聞斯行諸？』子曰：『有父兄在。』求也問：『聞斯行諸？』子曰：『聞斯行之。』赤也惑，敢問。」子曰：「求也退，故進之；由也兼人，故退之。」

situation: You are weighing what is right against what is profitable.
wise_response: "The mind of the superior man is conversant with righteousness; the mind of the mean man is conversant with gain."
why_it_worked: What you habitually think about shapes who you become.
tempting_wrong_answer: Asking first what you will get out of it.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「君子喻於義，小人喻於利。」

situation: You are tempted to deliberate endlessly before acting.
wise_response: Chi Wan thought thrice before acting. The Master said, "Twice may do."
why_it_worked: Thinking is needed, but too much of it turns into hesitation.
tempting_wrong_answer: Overthinking until the moment for action passes.

translation.original_text: 子張問曰：「令尹子文，三仕爲令尹，無喜色；三已之，無慍色。舊令尹之政，必以吿新令尹。何如？」子曰：「忠矣。」曰：「仁矣乎？」曰：「未知，焉得仁？」「崔子弒齊君，陳文子有馬十乘，棄而違之，至於他邦，則曰：『猶吾大夫崔子也！』違之，之一邦，則又曰：『猶吾大夫崔子也！』違之。何如？」子曰：「淸矣。」曰：「仁矣乎？」曰：「未知，焉得仁？」

situation: You know what is right.
wise_response: "They who know the truth are not equal to those who love it, and they who love it are not equal to those who delight in it."
why_it_worked: Knowing the good is a start. Loving it and taking joy in it are what carry you through.
tempting_wrong_answer: Holding goodness as knowledge only, and practising it as a chore.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「知之者，不如好之者，好之者，不如樂之者。」

situation: You are choosing someone to share a dangerous undertaking.
wise_response: "I would not have him to act with me, who will unarmed attack a tiger, or cross a river without a boat, dying without any regret. My associate must be the man who proceeds to action full of solicitude, who is fond of adjusting his plans."
why_it_worked: Courage without care gets people killed. Careful planning is part of real bravery.
tempting_wrong_answer: Admiring reckless daring and choosing partners for boldness alone.

translation.original_text: 子謂顏淵曰：「用之則行，舍之則藏。惟我與爾有是夫！」子路曰：「子行三軍，則誰與？」子曰：「暴虎馮河，死而無悔者，吾不與也。必也臨事而懼，好謀而成者也。」

situation: You hold rank and are thinking about what matters most in your own bearing.
wise_response: Tsang named three things: "in his deportment and manner he keep from violence and heedlessness; that in regulating his countenance he keep near to sincerity; and that in his words and tones he keep far from lowness and impropriety." The details of ritual vessels can be left to the proper officers.
why_it_worked: A leader's own manner, face and speech set the tone. Small technical matters belong to those whose job they are.
tempting_wrong_answer: Fussing over details while being rough, insincere or coarse in your own conduct.

translation.original_text: 曾子有疾，孟敬子問之。曾子言曰：「鳥之將死，其鳴也哀，人之將死，其言也善。君子所貴乎道者三：動容貌，斯遠暴慢矣；正顏色，斯近信矣；出辭氣，斯遠鄙倍矣；籩豆之事，則有司存。」

situation: Great trust is placed in you, and a crisis tests it.
wise_response: A superior man is one who "can be entrusted with the charge of a young orphan prince... and whom no emergency however great can drive from his principles."
why_it_worked: Trustworthiness shows when pressure is highest. Holding firm in crisis is the proof.
tempting_wrong_answer: Abandoning a trust when things get dangerous.

translation.original_text: 曾子曰：「可以託六尺之孤，可以寄百里之命，臨大節而不可奪也。君子人與？君子人也！」

situation: Common practice has drifted from what is right in some matter.
wise_response: The Master followed a new custom that was merely economical, but kept bowing below the hall because the new way "is arrogant. I continue to bow below the hall, though I oppose the common practice."
why_it_worked: Go along with harmless change, but hold to what is right when the crowd turns arrogant.
tempting_wrong_answer: Following every trend, or rejecting every change on principle.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「麻冕，禮也；今也純，儉，吾從眾。拜下，禮也；今拜乎上，泰也。雖違眾，吾從下。」

situation: You are close to finishing something, or barely starting.
wise_response: "If there want but one basket of earth to complete the work, and I stop, the stopping is my own work... Though but one basketful is thrown at a time, the advancing with it is my own going forward."
why_it_worked: Whether you finish or fail is your own doing. Each small step forward is real progress.
tempting_wrong_answer: Quitting just short of the goal, or never starting because the task is large.

translation.original_text: 子曰：「吾未見好德如好色者也。」

situation: Someone tells you what they will do, and you take their word for their conduct.
wise_response: "At first, my way with men was to hear their words, and give them credit for their conduct. Now my way is to hear their words, and look at their conduct."
why_it_worked: Words are easy. Conduct shows whether they were meant.
tempting_wrong_answer: Trusting promises without ever checking what was done.

translation.original_text: 子謂子貢曰：「女與回也孰愈？」對曰：「賜也何敢望回！回也聞一以知十，賜也聞一以知二。」子曰：「弗如也。吾與女，弗如也。」
