situation: A bedouin interrupted the Prophet's talk to ask when the Hour would come.
wise_response: The Prophet finished what he was saying, then asked, "Where is the one who asked about the Hour?" He told him: when trust is lost, wait for the Hour. Asked how it is lost, he said: when matters are entrusted to those not fit for them.
why_it_worked: He kept his talk in order and still came back to answer the man. His answer put the weight on trust: giving responsibility to the qualified.
tempting_wrong_answer: Handing posts and power to people for favor or kinship, with no regard for whether they are fit.

translation.original_text: وعنه قال‏:‏ بينما النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم  في مجلس يحدث القوم، جاءه أعرابي  فقال‏:‏ متى الساعة‏؟‏ فمضى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، يحدث، فقال بعض القوم‏:‏ سمع ما قال‏:‏ فكره ما قال، وقال بعضهم‏:‏ بل لم يسمع، حتى إذا قضى حديثه قال‏:‏ ‏"‏أين السائل عن الساعة‏؟‏ ‏"‏قال‏:‏ ها أنا يا رسول الله ‏.‏ قال‏:‏ ‏"‏إذا ضيعت الأمانة ، فانتظر الساعة‏"‏ قال‏:‏ كيف إضاعتها‏؟‏ قالك ‏"‏إذا وسد الأمر إلى غير أهله فانتظر الساعة‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.edition: riyad 1158 (The Book of Miscellaneous ahadith of Significant Values)
translation.ai_translation: While the Prophet was in a gathering speaking to the people, a bedouin came to him and said: "When is the Hour?" The Messenger of Allah went on speaking. Some of the people said: "He heard what he said and disliked it." Others said: "Rather, he did not hear." When he finished his talk he said: "Where is the one who asked about the Hour?" He said: "Here I am, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "When trust is lost, then wait for the Hour." He said: "How is it lost?" He said: "When the affair is entrusted to those not fit for it, then wait for the Hour."

key_terms.أمانة (amana): trust, faithful keeping of a responsibility

situation: A person loses any sense of shame about what he does.
wise_response: The Prophet said that among the words people have kept from the earliest prophecy is: if you feel no shame, then do as you wish.
why_it_worked: Modesty is the inner check on conduct. Without it, nothing holds a person back.
tempting_wrong_answer: Dropping all sense of shame and doing whatever one wants.

situation: Some people sin with no pressure that could excuse it.
wise_response: The Prophet named three whom Allah will not speak to, purify or look at: an old man who commits adultery, a king who lies, and a poor man who is arrogant.
why_it_worked: Each sins without the usual excuse: the old man has little desire to drive him, the king has no one to fear, and the poor man has nothing to be proud of.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving in to vice without need, lying from power, or acting proud with nothing behind it.

translation.original_text: وعنه رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ ‏"‏ثلاثة لا يكلمهم الله يوم القيامة، ولا يزكيهم، ولا ينظر إليهم ، ولهم عذاب أليم‏:‏ شيخ زان، وملك كذاب، وعائل مستكبر‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ (4)

situation: Aishah heard that her nephew Abdullah bin az-Zubair had threatened to restrict her spending. She vowed never to speak to him again, and the estrangement went on.
wise_response: Ibn az-Zubair had two men bring him to her. He went in, embraced her, wept and begged her. The two men reminded her that the Prophet forbade cutting off a brother for more than three nights. Weeping, she spoke to him, freed forty slaves as expiation for her vow, and wept whenever she remembered it.
why_it_worked: Mending family ties came before a vow made in anger. Ibn az-Zubair humbled himself, and Aishah forgave.
tempting_wrong_answer: Holding to an angry vow and letting a family rift last for good.

translation.original_text: وعن عوف بن مالك بن الطفيل أن عائشة رضي الله عنها حدثت أن عبد الله بن الزبير رضي الله عنهما قال في بيع أو عطاء أعطته عائشة رضي الله عنها‏:‏ والله لتنتهين عائشة، أو لأحجرن عليها، قالت أهو قال هذا ‏؟‏ قالو‏:‏ نعم، قالت‏:‏ هو لله علي نذر أن لا أكلم ابن الزبير أبدا، فاستشفع بن الزبير إليها حين طالت الهجرة، فقالت‏:‏ لا والله لا أشفع فيه أبداً، ولا أتحنث إلى نذري فلما طال ذلك على ابن الزبير كلم المسور ابن مخرمة، وعبد الرحمن بن الأسود بن عبد يغوث وقال لهما‏:‏ أنشدكما الله لما أدخلتماني على عائشة رضي الله عنها، فإنها لا يحل لها أن تنذر قطيعتى، فأقبل به المسور، وعبد الرحمن حتى استأذنا على عائشة، فقالا‏:‏ السلام عليك ورحمة الله وبركاته، أندخل‏؟‏ قالت عائشة‏:‏ ادخلوا، قالوا‏:‏ كلنا‏؟‏ قالت‏:‏ نعم ادخلوا كلكم، ولا تعلم أن معهما ابن الزبير، فلما دخلوا ، دخل ابن الزبير الحجاب، فاعتنق عائشة رضي الله عنها، وطفق يناشدها ويبكي، وطفق المسور، وعبد الرحمن يناشدانها إلا كلمته وقبلت منه، ويقولان ‏:‏ إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم  نها عما قد علمت من الهجرة، ولا يحل لمسلم أن يهجر أخاه فوق ثلاث ليال، فلما أكثروا على عائشة من التذكرة والتحريج، طفقت تذكرهما وتبكي ، وتقول‏:‏ إني نذرت والنذر شديد ، فلم يزالا بها حتى كلمت ابن الزبير، وأعتقت في نذرها ذلك أربعين رقبة، وكانت تذكر نذرها بعد ذلك فتبكي حتى تبل دموعها خمارها‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.edition: riyad 1180 (The Book of Miscellaneous ahadith of Significant Values)
translation.ai_translation: Aishah was told that Abdullah bin az-Zubair said about a sale or gift she had given: "By Allah, Aishah will stop, or I will put a restriction on her." She said: "Did he say this?" They said: "Yes." She said: "It is a vow upon me to Allah that I will never speak to Ibn az-Zubair." Ibn az-Zubair sought intercession with her when the estrangement grew long. She said: "No, by Allah, I will never accept intercession for him, nor break my vow." When it grew long for Ibn az-Zubair, he spoke to al-Miswar bin Makhramah and Abdur-Rahman bin al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth and said: "I adjure you by Allah to bring me in to Aishah, for it is not lawful for her to vow to cut me off." They brought him and asked permission: "Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. May we come in?" Aishah said: "Come in." They said: "All of us?" She said: "Yes, all of you," not knowing Ibn az-Zubair was with them. When they entered, Ibn az-Zubair went behind the screen, embraced Aishah, and began pleading with her and weeping. Al-Miswar and Abdur-Rahman pleaded with her to speak to him and accept from him, saying: "The Prophet forbade what you know of estrangement: it is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother beyond three nights." When they pressed her with reminders, she began reminding them and weeping, saying: "I made a vow, and a vow is grave." They kept on until she spoke to Ibn az-Zubair. She freed forty slaves for that vow, and afterwards she would remember her vow and weep until her tears wet her veil.

situation: A man resolved to give charity in secret. By night he gave it to a thief, then to a prostitute, then to a rich man, and each morning people mocked where it had gone.
wise_response: Each time he said, "O Allah, praise be to You," and resolved to give again. He was then told that his charity might lead the thief to stop stealing, the woman to give up her trade, and the rich man to learn from it and spend from what Allah gave him.
why_it_worked: He gave with a sincere heart and did not let mockery stop him. Charity can do good even when it lands where people think it does not belong.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving up on generosity after people laugh at you, or giving only where it wins praise.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي  هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم  قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏ قال رجل لأتصدقن بصدقة، فخرج بصدقته، فوضعها في يد سارق، فأصبحوا يتحدثون‏:‏ تصدق على سارق‏!‏ فقال‏:‏ اللهم لك الحمد لأتصدقن بصدقة، فخرج بصدقته، فوضعها في يد زانية‏؟‏‏!‏ فأصبحوا يتحدثون‏:‏ تصدق على زانية فقال‏:‏ اللهم لك الحمد على زانية، لأتصدقن بصدقة، فخرج بصدقته، فوضعها في يد غني‏,‏ فأصبحوا يتحدثون‏!‏ تصدق الليلة على غني‏,‏ فقال‏:‏ اللهم لك الحمد على سارق ، وعلى زانية، وعلى غني‏!‏ فأتى فقيل له‏:‏ أما صدقتك على سارق، فلعله أن يستعف عن سرقته، وأما الزانية فلعلها تستعف عن زناها، وأما الغني فلعله أن يعتبر، فينفق مما آتاه الله‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري بلفظه، ومسلم بمعناه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.edition: riyad 1186 (The Book of Miscellaneous ahadith of Significant Values)
translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of Allah said: "A man said: 'I will surely give a charity.' He went out with his charity and put it in the hand of a thief. In the morning they were saying: 'Charity was given to a thief!' He said: 'O Allah, to You is praise. I will surely give a charity.' He went out with his charity and put it in the hand of an adulteress. In the morning they were saying: 'Charity was given to an adulteress last night!' He said: 'O Allah, to You is praise, over an adulteress. I will surely give a charity.' He went out with his charity and put it in the hand of a rich man. In the morning they were saying: 'Charity was given to a rich man!' He said: 'O Allah, to You is praise, over a thief, an adulteress and a rich man.' Then someone came to him and it was said to him: 'As for your charity to the thief, perhaps he will refrain from his stealing. As for the adulteress, perhaps she will refrain from her adultery. As for the rich man, perhaps he will take a lesson and spend from what Allah has given him.'"

situation: Someone insults a person who is fasting or tries to pick a fight with him.
wise_response: The Prophet said the fasting person should not speak crudely or shout. If someone insults him or fights him, he should simply say, 'I am fasting.'
why_it_worked: The fast is meant to restrain the whole person, the tongue and temper included. Naming the fast is a way to step out of the quarrel without answering in kind.
tempting_wrong_answer: Shouting back, trading insults, and letting a hungry temper take over.

translation.original_text:
عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ ‏
"‏إذا كان يوم صوم أحدكم فلا يرفث ولا يصخب، فإن سابه أحد أو قاتله، فليقل‏:‏ إني صائم‏"‏
translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of God said: 'On a day when one of you is fasting, let him not speak obscenely or raise his voice. If anyone insults him or fights him, let him say: I am fasting.'

key_terms.صائم (sa'im): one who is fasting, holding back

why_it_worked: Going hungry has no worth if the person stays dishonest. The outward discipline is meant to serve inward truthfulness.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating the fast as a box to tick while lying and cheating as usual.

situation: A man of Bahila left the Prophet and returned a year later so worn down that the Prophet did not recognize him. He had eaten nothing but at night for a whole year.
wise_response: The Prophet told him, 'You have tormented yourself.' He set him a measured fast: the month of Ramadan and one day a month. When the man kept asking for more, the Prophet raised it a little at a time but kept a limit.
why_it_worked: Devotion that wrecks the body is not what is asked. The Prophet guided the man toward a steady, moderate practice he could sustain.
tempting_wrong_answer: Punishing oneself in the name of zeal and taking pride in how much one can endure.

translation.original_text: وعن مجيبة الباهلية عن أبيها أو عمها، أنه أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم انطلق فأتاه بعد سنة وقد تغيرت حاله وهيئته، فقال‏:‏ يا رسول الله أما تعرفني‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ ‏"‏ومن أنت‏؟‏‏"‏ قال‏:‏ أنا الباهلي الذي جئتك عام الأول‏.‏ قال‏:‏ ‏"‏فما غيرك، وقد كنت حسن الهيئة‏؟‏‏"‏ قال‏:‏ ما أكلت طعامًا منذ فارقتك إلا بليل‏.‏ فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏عذبت نفسك‏!‏‏"‏ ثم قال‏:‏ ‏"‏صم شهر الصبر، ويومًا من كل شهر‏"‏ قال‏:‏ زدني، فإن بي قوة، قال‏:‏ ‏"‏ صم يومين‏"‏ قال‏:‏ زذني، قال‏:‏ ‏"‏صم ثلاثة أيام‏"‏ قال‏:‏ زدني‏.‏ قال‏:‏ ‏"‏صم من الحرم واترك، صم من الحرم واترك، صم من الحرم واترك‏"‏ وقال بأصابعه الثلاث فضمها، ثم أرسلها‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه أبو داود‏.‏ ‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Mujiba al-Bahiliyya reported from her father or uncle that he came to the Messenger of God, then left, and came back a year later with his condition and appearance changed. He said: 'Messenger of God, do you not know me?' He said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'I am the Bahili who came to you last year.' He said: 'What changed you? You used to look well.' He said: 'I have not eaten food since I left you except at night.' The Messenger of God said: 'You have tormented yourself!' Then he said: 'Fast the month of patience and one day of every month.' He said: 'Give me more, for I have strength.' He said: 'Fast two days.' He said: 'Give me more.' He said: 'Fast three days.' He said: 'Give me more.' He said: 'Fast some of the sacred months and leave off; fast some of the sacred months and leave off; fast some of the sacred months and leave off,' and he gestured with three fingers, pressing them together and then releasing them.

situation: Someone has food to share at the time a fasting person breaks the fast.
wise_response: The Prophet said that whoever gives a fasting person something to break the fast with earns a reward like the faster's, with nothing taken from the faster's reward.
why_it_worked: Feeding another person shares in the good they do. Generosity here costs the giver little and takes nothing from the one fed.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping one's food to oneself and thinking another person's fast has nothing to do with you.

situation: The Prophet visited Sa'd ibn Ubada, who had only bread and olive oil to offer him.
wise_response: The Prophet ate the simple meal and then blessed his host: 'May the fasting break their fast with you, may the righteous eat your food, and may the angels pray for you.'
why_it_worked: The host gave what he had, and the guest answered plain hospitality with warm thanks and a prayer for him.
tempting_wrong_answer: A guest belittling a modest meal, or a host holding back because he has nothing grand to offer.

situation: A person is about to speak and is unsure whether what he will say is good.
wise_response: The Prophet said that whoever believes in God and the Last Day should say what is good or keep silent.
why_it_worked: Speech should be held to a simple test. If it is not good, silence does less harm.
tempting_wrong_answer: Saying whatever comes to mind, idle or hurtful, because it feels harmless in the moment.

wise_response: The Prophet answered: 'The one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.'

tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking oneself pious while wounding people with words or hands.

situation: A person faces the two strongest pulls on self-restraint: the tongue and sexual desire.
wise_response: The Prophet said: 'Whoever guarantees me what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I guarantee him Paradise.'
why_it_worked: Most harm to others and to oneself comes through speech and through desire. Guarding both is the core of self-governance.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving the tongue and appetites free rein and calling it freedom.

situation: A person says something without stopping to think whether it is good or bad.
wise_response: The Prophet warned that a person may speak one word without thinking it through and fall by it into the Fire farther than the distance between east and west.
why_it_worked: A single careless word can do great damage. Thinking before speaking is part of a person's responsibility.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating words as weightless and speaking first, thinking later.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول‏:‏ “إن العبد ليتكلم بالكلمة ما يتبين فيها يزل بها إلى النار أبعد مما بين المشرق والمغرب‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ ‏
‏ومعني‏:‏ ‏ ‏يتبين‏ ‏ يتفكر أنها خير أم لا.‏
translation.edition: riyad 835 (The Book of the Prohibited actions)
translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayra heard the Prophet say: 'A servant may speak a word whose meaning he does not consider, and by it he slips into the Fire farther than what is between the east and the west.'

situation: People speak small words every day, kind or cruel, without giving them much thought.
wise_response: The Prophet said a person may say a word that pleases God, not thinking much of it, and God raises him by degrees for it; and a person may say a word that angers God, not thinking much of it, and fall by it into Hell.
why_it_worked: Small words carry weight both ways. A passing kind word can count for much, and so can a passing cruel one.
tempting_wrong_answer: Assuming only big speeches matter and ignoring the everyday remark.

translation.original_text:
وعنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏إن العبد ليتكلم بالكلمة من رضوان الله تعالى ما يُلقي لها بالا يرفعه الله بها درجات، وإن العبد ليتكلم بالكلمة من سخط الله تعالى لا يُلقي لها بالا يَهوي بها في جهنم‏"‏‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.edition: riyad 836 (The Book of the Prohibited actions)
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet said: 'A servant may speak a word that pleases God, paying it no attention, and God raises him by it many degrees. And a servant may speak a word that angers God, paying it no attention, and by it he sinks into Hell.'

situation: Sufyan ibn Abdullah asked the Prophet for one thing to hold on to, and then asked what he feared most for him.
wise_response: The Prophet told him to say 'My Lord is God' and then stay upright. Asked what he feared most for him, he took hold of his own tongue and said, 'This.'
why_it_worked: Of all the dangers to a person's character, the Prophet pointed to the tongue first.
tempting_wrong_answer: Watching out for great outward sins while letting the tongue run unchecked.

translation.original_text:
وعن سفيان بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قلت يا رسول الله حدثني بأمر أعتصم به قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏ قل ربي الله ثم استقم‏"‏ قلت‏:‏ يا رسول الله ما أخوف ما تخاف علي‏؟‏ فأخذ بلسان نفسه، ثم قال‏:‏ “هذا”‏.‏ رواه الترمذي وقال حديث حسن صحيح‏.‏

situation: A person spends much of the day in idle talk.
wise_response: The Prophet said: do not talk much without remembrance of God, for much talk without it hardens the heart, and the farthest of people from God is the hard heart.
why_it_worked: Endless chatter dulls a person's inner softness. A hard heart is the real loss.
tempting_wrong_answer: Filling every silence with talk and never letting the heart settle.

translation.original_text:

"‏لا تكثروا الكلام بغير ذكر الله، فإن كثرة الكلام بغير ذكر الله تعالى قسوة للقلب‏!‏ وإن أبعد الناس من الله القلب القاسي‏"‏‏.‏ رواه الترمذي‏.‏

situation: Uqba ibn Amir asked the Prophet what brings a person to safety.
wise_response: The Prophet said: 'Hold your tongue, let your house be enough for you, and weep over your faults.'
why_it_worked: Safety comes from restraint in speech, contentment at home, and honest sorrow for one's own wrongs rather than other people's.
tempting_wrong_answer: Talking freely, chasing restlessly after more, and dwelling on others' faults instead of one's own.

translation.original_text:

"‏أمسك عليك لسانك، وليسعك بيتك، وابكِ على خطيئتك‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه الترمذي، وقال‏:‏ حديث حسن‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏

translation.ai_translation: Uqba ibn Amir said: I said, 'Messenger of God, what is salvation?' He said: 'Hold your tongue, let your house be roomy enough for you, and weep over your sin.'

situation: Each morning a person's whole body depends on how he will use his tongue that day.
wise_response: The Prophet said that every morning all the limbs humbly plead with the tongue: 'Fear God for our sake, for we go with you. If you are straight, we are straight; if you go crooked, we go crooked.'
why_it_worked: The tongue sets the course for the rest of a person's conduct. Keeping it straight keeps the whole person straight.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking speech is separate from action and that words do not lead anywhere.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ “إذا أصبح ابن آدم، فإن الأعضاء كلها تكفر اللسان، تقول‏:‏ اتقِ الله فينا، فإنما نحن بك‏:‏ فإن استقمت استقمنا وإن اعوججت اعوججنا”‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه الترمذي‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ ‏
'‏معني “تكفر اللسان” أي تذل وتخضع ل‏ه.‏
translation.edition: riyad 842 (The Book of the Prohibited actions)
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet said: 'When the son of Adam wakes in the morning, all the limbs humble themselves before the tongue and say: Fear God concerning us, for we are only through you. If you are upright, we are upright; and if you are crooked, we are crooked.'

situation: Mu'adh asked the Prophet for a deed that would bring him to Paradise. After naming the pillars of worship, the Prophet asked if he should tell him what holds it all together.
wise_response: The Prophet took hold of his own tongue and said, 'Restrain this.' When Mu'adh asked whether people are really held to account for what they say, he answered that what most throws people on their faces into the Fire is the harvest of their tongues.
why_it_worked: Worship and good deeds can be undone by speech. Control of the tongue is what keeps the rest intact.
tempting_wrong_answer: Doing all the visible acts of piety while speaking carelessly, cruelly or falsely.

translation.original_text: وعن معاذ رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قلت يا رسول الله‏:‏ أخبرني بعمل يدخلني الجنة، ويباعدني من النار‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ ‏"‏لقد سألت عن عظيم، وإنه ليسير على من يسره الله تعالى عليه‏:‏ تعبد الله لا تشرك به شيئًا، وتقيم الصلاة، وتؤتي الزكاة، وتصوم رمضان وتحج البيت إن استطعت إليه سبيلا ثم قال‏:‏ ألا أدلك على أبواب الخير‏؟‏ الصوم جُنة، والصدقة تطفئ الخطيئة كما يطفئ الماء النار، وصلاة الرجل من جوف الليل” ثم تلا‏:‏ ‏{‏تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع‏}‏ حتى بلغ‏:‏ ‏{‏يعملون‏}‏ ‏(‏‏(‏السجدة‏:‏ 16-17‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ ثم قال‏:‏ ‏"‏ألا أخبرك برأس الأمر وعموده وذِروة سنامه‏"‏ قلت‏"‏ بلى يا رسول الله، قال‏:‏ رأس الأمر الإسلام، وعموده الصلاة، وذِروة سنامه الجهاد” ثم قال‏:‏ “ألا أخبرك بملاك ذلك كله‏؟‏‏"‏ قلت‏:‏ بلى يا رسول الله، فأخذ بلسانه قال‏:‏ ‏"‏كف عليك هذا‏"‏ قلت‏:‏ يا رسول الله وإنا لمؤاخذون بما نتكلم به‏؟‏ فقال‏:‏ ثكلتك أمك‏!‏ وهل يُكب الناس في النار على وجوههم إلا حصائد ألسنتهم‏؟‏‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه الترمذي وقال‏:‏ حديث حسن صحيح، وقد سبق شرحه في باب قبل هذا‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.edition: riyad 843 (The Book of the Prohibited actions)
translation.ai_translation: Mu'adh said: I said, 'Messenger of God, tell me of a deed that will bring me into Paradise and keep me far from the Fire.' He said: 'You have asked about something great, yet it is easy for the one God makes it easy for: worship God and associate nothing with Him, establish prayer, give zakat, fast Ramadan, and make pilgrimage to the House if you are able.' Then he said: 'Shall I not show you the gates of good? Fasting is a shield, charity puts out sin as water puts out fire, and a man's prayer in the depth of the night.' Then he recited: 'Their sides forsake their beds' until he reached 'what they used to do.' Then he said: 'Shall I not tell you the head of the matter, its pillar and the peak of its hump?' I said: 'Yes, Messenger of God.' He said: 'The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is prayer, and the peak of its hump is jihad.' Then he said: 'Shall I not tell you what holds all of that together?' I said: 'Yes, Messenger of God.' He took hold of his tongue and said: 'Restrain this.' I said: 'Messenger of God, will we be held to account for what we say?' He said: 'May your mother lose you! Are people thrown on their faces into the Fire for anything but the harvests of their tongues?'

situation: The Prophet asked his companions whether they knew what backbiting is. One asked: what if the thing I say about my brother is true?
wise_response: The Prophet defined backbiting as 'mentioning your brother with what he dislikes.' If what you say is true, you have backbitten him. If it is not true, you have slandered him.
why_it_worked: Truth is no excuse for speaking about someone behind his back in a way he would hate. A person's dignity in his absence deserves the same care as in his presence.
tempting_wrong_answer: Justifying gossip because 'it's true' or 'I'm only saying what everyone knows.'

translation.original_text: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ “أتدرون ما الغيبة‏؟‏” قالوا‏:‏ الله ورسوله أعلم قال‏:‏ ‏"‏ذكرك أخاك بما يكره‏"‏ قيل‏:‏ أفرأيت إن كان في أخي ما أقول‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ ‏"‏إن كان فيه ما تقول، فقد اغتبته، وإن لم يكن فيه ما تقول فقد بهته”‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.edition: riyad 844 (The Book of the Prohibited actions)
translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of God said: 'Do you know what backbiting is?' They said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Your mentioning your brother with what he dislikes.' It was said: 'What if what I say is in my brother?' He said: 'If what you say is in him, you have backbitten him; and if it is not in him, you have slandered him.'

situation: During his farewell sermon at Mina, the Prophet addressed the whole gathering.
wise_response: He declared: 'Your blood, your property and your honour are sacred to one another, as sacred as this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours.' Then he asked, 'Have I conveyed it?'
why_it_worked: He tied the protection of people's lives, wealth and reputation to the holiest things his listeners knew, so no one could treat them lightly.
tempting_wrong_answer: Respecting holy days and places while thinking a neighbour's life, goods or good name are fair game.

translation.original_text: وعن أبي بكر رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال في خطبته يوم النحر بمنًى في حجة الوداع‏:‏ ‏"‏إن دماءكم، وأموالكم، وأعراضكم حرام عليكم كحرمة يومكم هذا، في شهركم هذا، في بلدكم هذا، ألا هل بلغت” ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.edition: riyad 845 (The Book of the Prohibited actions)

Have I not conveyed it?'

situation: Aisha made a remark to the Prophet mocking Safiyya's short stature, and on another occasion mimicked someone in front of him.
wise_response: The Prophet told her: 'You have said a word that, if mixed into the sea, would foul it.' Of the mimicry he said he would not like to imitate anyone even if he were paid a great deal.
why_it_worked: A small jab about someone's body or a mocking impression can be uglier than it seems. The Prophet corrected it at once, even from someone he loved.
tempting_wrong_answer: Laughing along with a remark about someone's looks, or imitating people for a cheap laugh.

translation.original_text:
وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها‏:‏ قالت قلت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حسبك من صفية كذا وكذا‏.‏ قال بعض الرواة‏:‏ تعني قصيرة، فقال‏:‏ ‏"‏لقد قلت كلمة لو مُزجت بماء البحر لمزجته‏!‏‏"‏ قالت‏:‏ وحكيت له إنسانًا فقال‏:‏ “ما أحب أني حكيت إنسانًا وإن لي كذا وكذا”‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه أبو داود والترمذي وقال حديث حسن صحيح‏.‏‏)‏‏)‏ 
ومعني‏:‏ ‏"‏مزجته‏"‏ خالطته مخالطة يتغير بها طعمه، أو ريحه لشدة نتنها وقبحها، وهذا الحديث من أبلغ الزواجر عن الغيبة، قال الله تعالى‏:‏ ‏{‏وما ينطق عن الهوى، إن هو إلا وحي يوحى‏}‏‏.‏
translation.edition: riyad 846 (The Book of the Prohibited actions)
translation.ai_translation: Aisha said: I said to the Prophet, 'Enough for you of Safiyya that she is such and such,' meaning short. He said: 'You have said a word that, were it mixed with the water of the sea, would pollute it.' She said: And I imitated a person to him, and he said: 'I would not like to imitate anyone even if I were given such and such.'

situation: The Prophet described a vision from his night journey.
wise_response: He said he passed people with copper nails scratching their own faces and chests. Jibril told him they were the ones who ate people's flesh and attacked their honour.
why_it_worked: Backbiting is pictured as tearing at others, and the harm returns on the one who does it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Feasting on other people's reputations in conversation.

translation.original_text: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ “لما عُرج بي مررت بقوم لهم أظفار من نُحاس يخمشون وجوههم وصدورهم، فقلت‏:‏ من هؤلاء يا جبريل‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ هؤلاء الذين يأكلون لحوم الناس، ويقعون في أعراضهم‏!‏”‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه أبو داود‏.‏‏)‏‏)‏

translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of God said: 'When I was taken up, I passed by people with nails of copper scratching their faces and chests. I said: Who are these, Jibril? He said: These are those who eat the flesh of people and assail their honour.'

situation: The Prophet asked where Malik ibn ad-Dukhshum was, and a man said, 'He is a hypocrite who does not love God and His Messenger.'
wise_response: The Prophet said, 'Do not say that. Do you not see that he has said there is no god but God, seeking God's face by it?'
why_it_worked: No one can see into another's heart. The Prophet refused to let a man be branded a hypocrite on a guess.
tempting_wrong_answer: Labelling someone a hypocrite or worse because he is absent or out of favour.

situation: At Tabuk the Prophet asked what had become of Ka'b ibn Malik. A man said Ka'b had been held back by his fine cloak and his admiration of himself.
wise_response: Mu'adh ibn Jabal answered the man: 'What a bad thing you have said. By God, Messenger of God, we know nothing of him but good.' The Prophet stayed silent.
why_it_worked: Mu'adh would not let an absent companion be mocked. He spoke from what he knew of Ka'b rather than from suspicion.
tempting_wrong_answer: Using someone's absence to hint at vanity or bad motives.

wise_response: The Prophet told her plainly: Mu'awiya was poor with no wealth, and Abu al-Jahm never put his stick down from his shoulder, which a version of the report explains as being hard on women.

situation: The Prophet said that any official who hides even a needle from what he handles has stolen and will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. A black man of the Ansar stood and asked to be released from his post.
wise_response: The Prophet did not soften the rule. He repeated it: whoever is given a post must bring in everything, little or much, take what he is given and leave what he is forbidden.
why_it_worked: Public office is a trust that must be fully accounted for. The man took the warning seriously enough to doubt himself, and the Prophet held the standard firm rather than lowering it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating small items that pass through your hands in a job as perks nobody will miss.

translation.original_text: وعن عدي ابن عميرة رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول‏:‏ “من استعملناه منكم على عمل، فكتمنا مخيطًا فما فوقه، كان غلولاً يأتي به يوم القيامة” فقام إليه رجل أسود من الأنصار، كأني أنظر إليه ، فقال‏:‏ يا رسول الله اقبل عني عملك، قال‏:‏ “ومالك‏؟‏” قال سمعتك تقول كذا وكذا، قال‏:‏ “وأنا أقوله الآن‏:‏ من استعملناه على عمل فليجئ بقليله وكثيره، فما أوتي منه أخذ، وما نهي عنه انتهى، ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whoever of you we appoint to a task and he hides from us a needle or anything above it, that is theft, and he will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. He said: I heard you say such and such. He said: And I say it now: whoever we appoint to a task, let him bring its little and its much. What he is given from it, he takes, and what he is forbidden, he leaves alone.

situation: The Prophet asked his companions who the bankrupt is. They said: the one with no money and no goods.
wise_response: He said the real bankrupt comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting and charity, but also having insulted one, slandered another, eaten someone's wealth, shed blood and beaten others. His good deeds are paid out to them, and when they run out their sins are loaded onto him.
why_it_worked: Devotion does not cancel what you owe to people you have harmed. Wrongs against others drain away the good you have done.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being careful with worship while being careless with how you treat people, as if one makes up for the other.

translation.original_text: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏"‏‏:‏أتدرون من المفلس‏؟‏‏"‏ قالوا ‏:‏ المفلس فينا من لا درهم له ولا متاع فقال‏:‏ ‏"‏إن المفلس من أمتي يأتي يوم القيامة بصلاة وصيام وزكاة، ويأتي قد شتم هذا، وقذف هذا وأكل مال هذا، وسفك دم هذا، وضرب هذا، فيعطى هذا من حسناته، وهذا من حسناته، فإن فنيت حسناته قبل أن يقضي ما عليه، أخذ من خطاياهم فطرحت عليه، ثم طرح في النار‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Do you know who the bankrupt is? They said: The bankrupt among us is the one who has no dirham and no goods. He said: The bankrupt of my community is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting and alms, and comes having cursed this one, slandered that one, eaten this one's wealth, shed that one's blood and beaten this one. So this one is given from his good deeds and that one from his good deeds. If his good deeds run out before what he owes is paid, some of their sins are taken and thrown onto him, and then he is thrown into the Fire.

wise_response: He said he was only human and judged by what he heard. If his ruling gave someone what was really his brother's right, he was only cutting off a piece of the Fire for him.
why_it_worked: A favorable verdict does not make a thing yours. Each party knows the truth of his own case and is answerable for it, whatever the judge decides.
tempting_wrong_answer: Winning a dispute through skillful argument and then keeping what you know is not yours because the ruling allowed it.

translation.ai_translation: I am only a human being, and you bring your disputes to me. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, and I judge for him according to what I hear. situation: People differ in character, and some show one face to one group and another face to the next.
wise_response: The Prophet said people are like mines of ore: the best of them before Islam are the best in it once they understand. The best in leadership are those who most dislike it. And the worst of people is the two-faced one who comes to these with one face and to those with another.
why_it_worked: Good character carries over. Shifting faces to please each side is a form of deceit that betrays everyone.
tempting_wrong_answer: Telling each group what it wants to hear to stay in favour with both.

translation.original_text: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ “تجدون الناس معادن‏:‏ خيارهم في الجاهلية خيارهم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا، وتجدون خيار الناس في هذا الشأن أشدهم له كراهية، وتجدون شر الناس ذا الوجهين، الذي يأتي هؤلاء بوجه، وهؤلاء بوجه‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏

translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of God said: 'You find people like mines. The best of them in the time of ignorance are the best of them in Islam if they understand. You find the best of people in this matter those who most dislike it. And you find the worst of people the two-faced one, who comes to these with one face and to those with another face.'

wise_response: The Prophet said: 'It is enough of a lie for a person to repeat everything he hears.'
why_it_worked: Passing on every report unchecked spreads falsehood, because much of what one hears is wrong.
tempting_wrong_answer: Forwarding every story and rumour without checking whether it is true.

wise_response: Ibn Umar answered: 'In the time of the Messenger of God we counted this as hypocrisy.'
why_it_worked: Saying one thing to a powerful person's face and another behind his back is dishonest whatever the excuse.
tempting_wrong_answer: Praising those in power to their faces and condemning them in private to stay safe and popular.

situation: A person decides, again and again, whether to tell the truth.
wise_response: The Prophet said truthfulness leads to goodness and goodness leads to Paradise, and a man keeps telling the truth until he is recorded with God as truthful. Lying leads to wickedness and wickedness to the Fire, and a man keeps lying until he is recorded as a liar.
why_it_worked: Each choice builds a habit and the habit becomes the person. Truth and lies both compound.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking one small lie does not matter and will not shape who you become.

translation.original_text:
وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ ‏
"‏ إن الصدق يهدي إلى البر، وإن البر يهدي إلى الجنة، وإن الرجل ليصدق حتى يكتب عند الله صديقًا، وإن الكذب يهدي إلى الفجور، وإن الفجور يهدي إلى النار، وإن الرجل ليكذب حتى يكتب عند الله كذابًا‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.edition: riyad 863 (The Book of the Prohibited actions)
translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of God said: 'Truthfulness guides to righteousness, and righteousness guides to Paradise. A man keeps being truthful until he is written with God as truthful. Lying guides to wickedness, and wickedness guides to the Fire. A man keeps lying until he is written with God as a liar.'

situation: A person is trusted with something, speaks, makes an agreement, or gets into a dispute.
wise_response: The Prophet named four traits of a pure hypocrite: when trusted, he betrays; when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a pledge, he breaks it; when he disputes, he becomes vicious. Whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he leaves it.
why_it_worked: Trust, truth, promises and fair conduct in conflict are what make a person reliable. Failing at any of them is a crack in character.
tempting_wrong_answer: Betraying trusts, lying, breaking agreements, and fighting dirty when a dispute arises.

translation.original_text:
وعن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏أربع من كن فيه كان منافقًا خالصًا، ومن كانت فيه خصلة منهن كانت فيه خصلة من نفاق حتى يدعها‏:‏ إذا أؤتمن خان، وإذا حدث كذب، وإذا عاهد غدر، وإذا خاصم فجر‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ 
وقد سبق بيانه مع حديث أبي هريرة بنحوه في باب الوفاء بالعهد‏.‏
translation.edition: riyad 864 (The Book of the Prohibited actions)
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet said: 'Four traits, whoever has them is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he leaves it: when he is trusted he betrays, when he speaks he lies, when he makes a pact he breaks it, and when he disputes he is wicked.'

situation: A person is tempted to make up a dream to impress others, or to listen in secretly on people's private talk.
wise_response: The Prophet warned that whoever claims a dream he did not see will be made to tie two barley grains together and will never manage it, and whoever listens to people's talk when they dislike it will have molten lead poured into his ears.
why_it_worked: Inventing experiences and prying into others' private words are both violations of trust, and the warnings fit the wrongs.
tempting_wrong_answer: Telling invented stories about oneself and eavesdropping on others.

translation.original_text:
وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏ من تحلم بحلم لم يره، كُلف أن يعقد بين شعيرتين ولن يفعل، ومن استمع إلى حديث قوم وهم له كارهون، صب في أذنيه الآنُك يوم القيامة، ومن صور صورة، عذب وكلف أن ينفخ فيها الروح وليس بنافخ‏"‏‏.‏رواه البخاري .
تحلم أي: قال أنه حلم في نومه ورأى كذا وكذا، وهو كاذب و الآنك بالمد وضم النون وتخفيف الكاف: وهو الرصاص المذاب .

translation.ai_translation: The Prophet said: 'Whoever claims a dream he did not see will be charged with tying a knot between two barley grains, and he will not do it. Whoever listens to a people's talk while they dislike it, molten lead will be poured into his ears on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever makes an image will be punished and charged with breathing a soul into it, and he will not breathe.'

situation: A woman with a co-wife asked whether she could pretend her husband had given her things he had not.
wise_response: The Prophet said: 'The one who shows off what he has not been given is like one who wears two garments of falsehood.'
why_it_worked: Pretending to have what you do not have is a lie, even if no one is directly robbed. It feeds rivalry and deceit.
tempting_wrong_answer: Inventing gifts or advantages to make a rival jealous.

translation.original_text:
وعن أسماء رضي الله عنها أن امرأة قالت‏:‏ يا رسول الله إن لي ضَّرة فهل علي جناح إن تشبعت من زوجي غير الذي يعطيني‏؟‏ فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ ‏
"‏المتشبع بما لم يعطَ كلابس ثوبي زور‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ المتشبع: هو الذي يظهر الشبع وليس بشبعان، ومعناها هنا أنه يظهر أنه حصل له فضيلة وليست حاصلة ولابس ثوبي زور أي: ذي زور وهو الذي يزور على الناس بأن يتزي بزي أهل الزهد أو العلم أو الثروة ليغتر به الناس وليس هو بتلك الصفة وقيل غير ذلك والله أعلم
translation.edition: riyad 870 (The Book of the Prohibited actions)
translation.ai_translation: A woman said: 'Messenger of God, I have a co-wife. Is there any harm on me if I pretend to be satisfied with something from my husband that he does not give me?' The Prophet said: 'The one who pretends to be satisfied with what he has not been given is like one who wears two garments of falsehood.'

situation: The Prophet asked his companions if he should tell them the greatest of the major sins.
wise_response: He named associating partners with God and disobedience to parents. Then he sat up from reclining and said, 'And false speech and false testimony,' repeating it until the companions wished he would stop.
why_it_worked: False testimony destroys justice and harms innocent people. He sat up and repeated it to show its weight.
tempting_wrong_answer: Lying in testimony or speech to win a case or protect someone.

translation.original_text: وعن أبي بكر رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ ‏"‏ألا أنبئكم بأكبر الكبائر‏؟‏‏"‏ قلنا‏:‏ بلى يا رسول الله‏.‏ قال‏:‏ ‏"‏الإشراك بالله، وعقوق الوالدين‏"‏ وكان متكئا فجلس، فقال‏:‏ ‏"‏ألا وقول الزور‏!‏‏"‏ فما زال يكررها حتى قلنا‏:‏ ليته سكت‏.‏ متفق عليه‏

situation: In anger a person curses someone or something.
wise_response: The Prophet said the curse rises to the sky and the gates are shut against it, falls to the earth and its gates are shut, turns right and left, and finding no way, returns to the one cursed if he deserved it, and otherwise returns to the one who said it.
why_it_worked: Cursing in anger is not harmless. An undeserved curse comes back on the speaker.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hurling curses freely at people, animals or things when frustrated.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ ‏
"‏إن العبد إذا لعن شيئًا، صعدت اللعنة إلى السماء، فتغلق أبواب السماء دونها، ثم تهبط إلى الأرض، فتغلق أبوابها دونها، ثم تأخذ يمينًا وشمالا، فإذا لم تجد مساغًا رجعت إلى الذي لُعن، فإن كان أهلا لذلك، وإلا رجعت إلى قائلها‏"‏‏.‏ رواه أبو داود.

Then it descends to the earth, and its gates are shut against it. Then it goes right and left, and if it finds no outlet, it returns to the one who was cursed if he deserved it; otherwise it returns to the one who said it.'

situation: On a journey, a woman of the Ansar riding a camel grew irritated and cursed the animal.
wise_response: The Prophet heard it and said, 'Take off what is on it and leave it, for it is cursed.' The narrator remembered seeing the camel walking among the people with no one touching it.
why_it_worked: The Prophet made the woman feel the cost of her curse. An animal that serves you should not be cursed in a passing fit of temper.
tempting_wrong_answer: Cursing a beast of burden out of frustration as though it were nothing.

translation.original_text:
وعن عمران بن الحصين رضي الله عنه الله عنهما قال‏:‏ بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض أسفاره، وامرأة من الأنصار على ناقة، فضجرت، فلعنتها، فسمع ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال‏:‏ ‏
"‏خذوا ما عليها ودعوها، فإنها ملعونة‏"‏ قال عمران‏:‏ فكأني أراها الآن تمشي في الناس ما يَعرض لها أحد‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏

The Messenger of God heard that and said: 'Take what is on it and leave it, for it is cursed.' Imran said: It is as if I see it now walking among the people, no one approaching it.

situation: People live among one another with chances to suspect, spy, envy and look down on each other.
wise_response: The Prophet said: beware of suspicion, for it is the most lying talk. Do not pry, do not spy, do not compete in rivalry, envy, hate or turn your backs. A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim: he does not wrong him, abandon him or hold him in contempt. Piety is here, he said, pointing to his chest. God does not look at your bodies or forms but at your hearts and deeds.
why_it_worked: Each of these habits eats at trust. Worth lies in the heart and in deeds, so there is no ground for contempt.
tempting_wrong_answer: Assuming the worst, digging into others' secrets, and looking down on people.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏"‏إياكم والظن، فإن الظن أكذب الحديث، ولا تحسسوا، ولا تجسسوا ولا تنافسوا، ولا تحاسدوا، ولا تباغضوا، ولا تدابروا، وكونوا عباد الله إخوانًا كما أمركم‏.‏ المسلم أخو المسلم، لا يظلمه، ولا يخذله ولا يحقره‏.‏ التقوى ههنا، ‏"‏ ويشير إلى صدره ‏"‏بحسب امرئ من الشر أن يحقر أخاه المسلم، كل المسلم على المسلم حرام‏:‏ دمه، وعرضه، وماله، إن الله لا ينظر إلى أجسادكم، ولا إلى صوركم، ولكن ينظر إلى قلوبكم وأعمالكم‏"‏‏.‏ وفي رواية‏:‏ ‏"‏لا تحاسدوا، ولا تباغضوا، ولا تجسسوا، ولا تحسسوا ولا تناجشوا وكونوا عباد الله إخوانًا‏"‏‏.‏ 
وفي رواية‏:‏ ‏"‏لا تقاطعوا، ولا تدابروا، ولا تباغضوا ولا تحاسدوا، وكونوا عباد الله إخوانًا‏"‏‏.‏ وفي رواية‏:‏ ‏"‏لا تهاجروا ولا يبع بعضكم على بيع بعض‏"‏‏.‏
‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم بكل هذه الروايات، وروى البخاري أكثرها‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.edition: riyad 891 (The Book of the Prohibited actions)
translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of God said: 'Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech. Do not seek out faults, do not spy, do not vie with one another, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and be servants of God, brothers, as He commanded you. A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim: he does not wrong him, does not forsake him, and does not despise him. Piety is here,' and he pointed to his chest. 'It is enough evil for a man to despise his Muslim brother. All of a Muslim is sacred to a Muslim: his blood, his honour and his wealth. God does not look at your bodies or your forms, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.'

wise_response: The Prophet said the poor man was better than an earthful of men like the first.
why_it_worked: Worth lies in a person's character, not in his rank or how others receive him.

situation: A black woman, or a young man, who swept the mosque died, and people buried her without telling the Prophet, thinking her of little importance. He noticed she was missing and asked about her.
wise_response: He asked why they had not told him, had them show him the grave, and prayed over her there.
why_it_worked: He treated the humblest member of the community as worth his full attention, even after death.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating the death of a lowly worker as too small to bother anyone important.

translation.ai_translation: A black woman used to sweep the mosque, or it was a young man. The Messenger of God missed her and asked about her, or him. They said: She died. He said: Why did you not let me know? It was as if they had thought her matter, or his, small. He said: Show me her grave. They showed him, and he prayed over her. Then he said: These graves are full of darkness for those in them, and God lights them for them through my prayer over them.

situation: Juraij, a devout man in his hermitage, was called by his mother while he was praying. He chose his prayer over her on two days, and she prayed that he would not die before seeing the faces of prostitutes. He was later falsely accused of fathering a child.
wise_response: Cleared when the infant named its real father, Juraij refused the people's offer to rebuild his hermitage in gold and asked for it in mud as before. The story also tells of an infant who chose to be like a slave woman falsely accused, not like a proud rider who was a tyrant.
why_it_worked: Ignoring a mother's call has a cost even for the pious. Humility in vindication and judging people by their truth, not their appearance, are the marks of the good.
tempting_wrong_answer: Putting your own devotions above your mother's call, or judging people by fine clothes and public accusations.

translation.original_text: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ “ لم يتكلم في المهد إلا ثلاثة‏:‏ عيسى ابن مريم، وصاحب جريج، وكان جريج رجلا عابدًا، فاتخذ صومعة فكان فيها، فأتته أمه وهو يصلي فقالت‏:‏ يا جريج، فأتته أمه وهو يصلي فقالت‏:‏ يا جريج، فقال‏:‏ يا رب أمي وصلاتي فأقبل على صلاته فانصرفت‏.‏ فلما كان من الغد أتته وهو يصلي، فقالت‏:‏ يا جريج، فقال‏:‏ أي رب أمي وصلاتي، فأقبل على صلاته، فقالت‏:‏ اللهم لاتمته حتى ينظر إلى وجوه المومسات‏.‏ فتذاكر بنو إسرائيل جريجًا وعبادته، وكانت امرأة بغي يتمثل بحسنها، فقالت‏:‏ إن شئتم لأفتننه، فتعرضت له، فلم يلتفت إليها، فأتت راعيًا كان يأوي إلى صومعته، فأمكنته من نفسها فوقع عليها‏.‏ فحملت، وجعلوا يضربونه، فقال‏:‏ ما شأنكم‏؟‏ قالوا‏:‏ زنيت بهذه البغي فولدت منك‏.‏ قال‏:‏ أين الصبي‏؟‏ فجاءوا به فقال‏:‏ دعوني حتى أصلي، فصلى، فلما انصرف أتى الصبي فطعن في بطنه وقال‏:‏ ياغلام من أبوك‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ فلان الراعي، فأقبلوا على جريج يقبلونه ويتمسحون به وقالوا‏:‏ نبني لك صومعتك من ذهب، قال‏:‏ لا، أعيدوها من طين كما كانت، ففعلوا‏.‏ وبينا صبي يرضع من أمه، فمر رجل راكب على دابة فارهة وشارة حسنة، فقالت‏:‏ “ اللهم اجعل ابني مثل هذا، فترك الثدي وأقبل إليه فنظر إليه فقال‏:‏ اللهم لا تجعلني مثله، ثم أقبل على ثديه فجعل يرتضع‏"‏ فكأني أنظر إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يحكي ارتضاعه بأصبعه السبابة في فيه، فجعل يمصها، قال‏:‏ ‏"‏ومروا بجارية وهم يضربونها، ويقولون‏:‏ زنيت سرقت، وهي تقول‏:‏ حسبي الله ونعم الوكيل‏.‏ فقالت أمه‏:‏ اللهم لا تجعل ابني مثلها، فترك الرضاع ونظر إليها فقال‏:‏ اللهم اجعلني مثلها، فهناك تراجعا الحديث فقالت‏:‏ مر رجل حسن الهيئة فقلت‏:‏ اللهم اجعل ابني مثله فقلت‏:‏ اللهم لا تجعلني مثله، ومروا بهذه الأمة وهم يضربونها ويقولون‏:‏ زنيت سرقت، فقلت‏:‏ اللهم لا تجعل ابني مثلها فقلت‏:‏ اللهم اجعلني مثلها‏؟‏‏!‏ قال‏:‏ إن ذلك الرجل كان جبارًا فقلت‏:‏ اللهم لا تجعلني مثله، وإن هذه يقولون لها زنيت، ولم تزن وسرقت، ولم تسرق، فقلت‏:‏ اللهم اجعلني مثلها‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ (25)
translation.ai_translation: No one spoke in the cradle except three: Jesus son of Mary, and the companion of Juraij. Juraij was a devout man who took a hermitage and stayed in it. His mother came to him while he was praying and said: Juraij! He said: My Lord, my mother or my prayer? And he turned to his prayer, and she went away. The next day she came while he was praying and said: Juraij! He said: My Lord, my mother or my prayer? And he turned to his prayer. She said: O God, do not let him die until he looks on the faces of prostitutes. The Children of Israel talked of Juraij and his devotion. There was a prostitute whose beauty was proverbial, and she said: If you like, I will tempt him. She offered herself to him, but he paid her no attention. So she went to a shepherd who used to shelter by his hermitage and gave herself to him, and she became pregnant. When she gave birth she said: It is from Juraij. They came, dragged him down, wrecked his hermitage and began beating him. He said: What is the matter with you? They said: You committed adultery with this prostitute and she bore your child. He said: Where is the child? They brought him. He said: Let me pray. He prayed, and when he finished he came to the child, poked him in the belly and said: Boy, who is your father? He said: So-and-so the shepherd. They turned to Juraij, kissing him and touching him for blessing, and said: We will build your hermitage of gold. He said: No, rebuild it of mud as it was. And they did. And while a child was nursing at his mother's breast, a man rode by on a fine mount, well dressed. She said: O God, make my son like this one. He left the breast, turned to look at him and said: O God, do not make me like him. Then he went back to the breast and nursed. (The narrator said: It is as if I can see the Messenger of God imitating his nursing, putting his forefinger in his mouth and sucking it.) Then they passed a slave girl whom people were beating, saying: You committed adultery, you stole, while she said: God is enough for me, and the best guardian. His mother said: O God, do not make my son like her. He left the breast, looked at her and said: O God, make me like her. Then they spoke back and forth. She said: A handsome man passed and I said, O God, make my son like him, and you said, O God, do not make me like him. They passed this slave girl being beaten and accused of adultery and theft, and I said, O God, do not make my son like her, and you said, O God, make me like her! He said: That man was a tyrant, so I said, O God, do not make me like him. And this girl, they say to her you committed adultery when she did not, and you stole when she did not, so I said, O God, make me like her.

situation: The leaders of the idolaters told the Prophet to drive away the poor companions sitting with him, such as Sa'd and Ibn Mas'ud, so that they would not presume upon the leaders. The Prophet considered it.
wise_response: A verse came down: do not drive away those who call on their Lord morning and evening seeking His face. The poor companions stayed.
why_it_worked: The sincere and poor are not to be pushed aside to please the powerful.
tempting_wrong_answer: Sidelining humble supporters to win the favor of influential people.

translation.original_text: وعن سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ كنا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ستة نفر، فقال المشركون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ اطرد هؤلاء لايجترئون علينا، وكنت أنا وابن مسعود ورجلان لست أسميهما، فوقع في نفس رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما شاء الله أن يقع، فحدث نفسه، فأنزل الله تعالى‏:‏ ‏{‏ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه‏}‏ ‏(‏‏(‏الأنعام‏:‏ 52‏:‏ رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Sa'd said: We were six men with the Prophet. The idolaters said to the Prophet: Drive these away so they will not be bold with us. They were I, Ibn Mas'ud, and two men I will not name. Something came into the Messenger of God's mind, as God willed, and he spoke to himself about it. Then God revealed: "Do not drive away those who call on their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face."

situation: Abu Sufyan, the old chief of Quraysh, passed Salman, Suhaib and Bilal, former slaves and poor men, and they spoke harshly of him. Abu Bakr rebuked them for speaking that way to the chief of Quraysh.
wise_response: The Prophet told Abu Bakr that if he had angered them he had angered his Lord. Abu Bakr went straight back and asked: 'My brothers, did I anger you?' They said: 'No, may God forgive you, brother.'
why_it_worked: Rank does not outweigh the dignity of humble believers. Abu Bakr apologized at once, without pride.
tempting_wrong_answer: Siding with the powerful man against the poor, and being too proud to apologize.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي هبيرة عائذ بن عمرو المزني وهو من أهل بيعة الرضوان رضي الله عنه، أن أبا سفيان أتى على سلمان وصهيب وبلال في نفر فقالوا‏:‏ ما أخذت سيوف الله من عدو الله مأخذها، فقال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه‏:‏ أتقولون هذا لشيخ قريش وسيدهم‏؟‏ فأتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فأخبره فقال‏:‏ ‏
"‏يا أبا بكر لعلك أغضبتهم‏؟‏ لئن كنت أغضبتهم لقد أغضبت ربك‏"‏ فأتاهم فقال‏:‏ ياإخوتاه أغضبتكم‏؟‏ قالوا‏:‏ لا، يغفر الله لك يا أخي‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Sufyan came upon Salman, Suhaib and Bilal among a group, and they said: The swords of God have not taken their due from the enemy of God. Abu Bakr said: Do you say this to the old man of Quraysh and their chief? Then he went to the Prophet and told him. He said: Abu Bakr, perhaps you angered them? If you angered them, you have angered your Lord. So he went to them and said: My brothers, did I anger you? They said: No. May God forgive you, my brother.

situation: An orphan has no one to provide for or raise them.
wise_response: The Prophet said: 'I and the one who takes care of an orphan will be in Paradise like this,' and held up his index and middle fingers with a little space between them.
why_it_worked: Raising a child who has lost a parent puts a person closest to the Prophet's own rank.
tempting_wrong_answer: Leaving orphans to fend for themselves because they are not your own.

situation: Widows and the poor need someone to work on their behalf.
wise_response: The Prophet said the one who works for the widow and the needy is like one who strives in God's path, and like one who prays all night without tiring and fasts without breaking.
why_it_worked: Practical work for the vulnerable ranks with the highest forms of devotion.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking piety lies only in personal worship while ignoring those who need help.

translation.ai_translation: The one who works for the widow and the needy is like one who strives in the path of God. And I think he said: And like one who stands in prayer without slackening, and like one who fasts without breaking his fast.

situation: A man holds a wedding feast and invites the rich while leaving out the poor.
wise_response: The Prophet called it the worst of food: kept from those who would come and offered to those who refuse. He also said whoever turns down an invitation has disobeyed.
why_it_worked: Hospitality is meant to share joy and food. A feast that shuts out the hungry and courts the wealthy defeats its purpose.
tempting_wrong_answer: Inviting only those whose presence raises your status and leaving out those who would most enjoy the meal.

translation.original_text:
وعنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏"‏ شر الطعام طعام الوليمة، يمنعها من يأتيها، ويدعى إليها من يأباها، ومن لم يجب الدعوة فقد عصى الله ورسوله‏"‏ ((رواه مسلم‏))‏.‏ 
وفي رواية في ‏"‏ الصحيحين‏"‏ عن أبي هريرة من قوله‏:‏ ‏"‏ بئس الطعام طعام الوليمة يدعى إليها الأغنياء ويترك الفقراء‏"‏‏‏‏(‏(متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The worst food is the food of a wedding feast: it is withheld from those who would come to it, and those who refuse it are invited to it. Whoever does not answer the invitation has disobeyed God and His Messenger. In a version in the two Sahihs, from Abu Huraira's own words: Evil is the food of the wedding feast to which the rich are invited and the poor are left out.

situation: A man has daughters to raise, in a culture that often valued sons more.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever supports two girls until they come of age will come on the Day of Resurrection with him like this, and he joined his fingers.
why_it_worked: Raising daughters with care is honored at the highest level.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating daughters as a burden and giving them less care than sons.

translation.original_text: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ “من عال جاريتين حتى تبلغا جاء يوم القيامة أنا وهو كهاتين‏"‏ وضم أصابعه‏.‏‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ ‏(29)
translation.ai_translation: Whoever supports two girls until they come of age, he and I will come on the Day of Resurrection like these two. And he joined his fingers.

situation: A poor woman carrying her two daughters came to Aisha, who gave her three dates. She gave each girl a date and lifted the third to her own mouth, but the girls asked for it.
wise_response: She split the date she meant to eat between them. When Aisha told the Prophet, he said God had made Paradise hers because of it.
why_it_worked: She gave her last mouthful to her children while hungry herself. Self-giving love in a small act is great.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping the last share for yourself because you are the one who earned it.

translation.original_text:
وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت‏:‏ جاءتني مسكينة تحمل ابنتين لها، فأطعمتها ثلاث تمرات، فأعطت كل واحدة منهما تمرة ورفعت إلى فيها تمرة لتأكلها ، فاستطعمتها ابنتاها، فشقت التمرة التي كانت تريد أن تأكلها بينهما، فأعجبني شأنها، فذكرت الذي صنعت لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال‏:‏ ‏
"‏إن الله قد أوجب لها بها الجنة، أو أعتقها بها من النار‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Aisha said: A poor woman came to me carrying two daughters of hers. I gave her three dates to eat. She gave each of them a date and raised a date to her mouth to eat it, but her two daughters asked her for it, so she split the date she had meant to eat between them. Her action amazed me, and I told the Messenger of God what she had done. He said: God has made Paradise binding for her because of it, or: He has freed her by it from the Fire.

situation: Sa'd felt he had more merit than the weaker men around him.
wise_response: The Prophet asked him: 'Are you given victory and provision except through your weak ones?'
why_it_worked: The strong owe their success to the whole community, including the poor and weak. Pride forgets this.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking your gains are your own doing and looking down on those beneath you.

وعن مصعب بن سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنهما قال‏:‏ رأى سعد أن له فضلا على من دونه، فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ ‏
"‏هل تنصرون وترزقون إلا بضعفائكم‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏ هكذا مرسلا، فإن مصعب بن سعد تابعي، ‏(‏‏(‏ورواه الحافظ أبو بكر البرقاني في صحيحه متصلا عن مصعب عن أبيه رضي الله عنه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏

source.author: Imam Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi
source.date_or_era: 13th century CE compilation of earlier hadith
source.citation: Arabic text via AhmedBaset/hadith-json (sunnah.com numbering); English translation cited, not stored

situation: A husband is frustrated that his wife does not behave exactly as he wants.
wise_response: The Prophet said to treat women well, and compared a woman to a rib: try to straighten it by force and you break it, and breaking her is divorcing her. Leave it and live with her as she is.
why_it_worked: Forcing another person into your mold breaks the relationship. Patience and kindness keep it whole.
tempting_wrong_answer: Trying to force a wife to change by harshness until the marriage breaks.

translation.original_text:
و عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ ‏"‏استوصوا بالنساء خيرًا، فإن المرأة خلقت من ضلع، وإن أعوج ما في الضلع أعلاه، فإن ذهبت تقيمه كسرته، وإن تركته، لم يزل أعوج، فاستوصوا بالنساء‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ 
وفي رواية في ‏(‏‏(‏الصحيحين‏)‏‏)‏ ‏:‏ ‏"‏المرأة كالضلع إن أقمتها كسرتها، وإن استمتعت بها، استمتعت وفيها عوج‏"‏‏.‏
وفي رواية لمسلم‏:‏ ‏"‏إن المرأة خلقت من ضلع ، لن تستقيم لك على طريقة، فإن استمعت بها وفيها عوج، وإن ذهبت تقيمها كسرتها ، وكسرها طلاقها‏"‏‏.
translation.ai_translation: Take my counsel to treat women well. Woman was created from a rib, and the most bent part of the rib is its top. If you set about straightening it, you will break it; and if you leave it, it will stay bent. So take my counsel to treat women well. In a version in the two Sahihs: Woman is like a rib. If you straighten her, you break her, and if you enjoy life with her, you enjoy it while there is a bend in her. In a version in Muslim: Woman was created from a rib; she will not stay straight for you on one course. If you enjoy life with her, you enjoy it with the bend in her, and if you set about straightening her, you break her, and breaking her is divorcing her.

wise_response: The Prophet named two practices among people that are acts of unbelief: attacking lineage and wailing over the dead.

tempting_wrong_answer: Insulting someone's ancestry or origins to put him down.

situation: In a sermon the Prophet spoke of men who beat their wives, and of people who laugh when someone breaks wind.
wise_response: He asked why a man would whip his wife like a slave and then lie with her at the end of the day, and why anyone laughs at something he does himself.
why_it_worked: Cruelty to the person you share your life with is self-contradiction. Mocking others for what everyone does is the same.
tempting_wrong_answer: Beating a wife, or mocking people for ordinary human things.

translation.original_text: وعن عبد الله بن زمعة رضي الله عنه ، أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يخطب، وذكر الناقة والذي عقرها، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ ‏(‏إذ انبعث أشقاها‏)‏ انبعث لها رجل عزيز، عارم منيع في رهطه‏"‏ ثم ذكر النساء، فوعظ فيهن، فقال ‏:‏ ‏"‏يعمد أحدكم فيجلد امرأته جلد العبد فلعله يضاجعها من آخر يومه‏"‏ ثم وعظهم في ضحكهم من الضرطة وقال‏:‏ ‏"‏لم يضحك أحدكم مما يفعل‏؟‏‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: He heard the Prophet give a sermon. He mentioned the she-camel and the one who hamstrung her, and the Messenger of God said: "When the most wretched of them rose up": a mighty man rose up for her, fierce and protected among his clan. Then he mentioned women and admonished about them, saying: One of you sets about whipping his wife as a slave is whipped, and then perhaps lies with her at the end of his day. Then he admonished them about laughing at breaking wind and said: Why does any of you laugh at what he himself does?

wise_response: The Prophet said a believing man should not hate a believing woman. If he dislikes one of her qualities, he will be pleased with another.

tempting_wrong_answer: Fixing on one fault until it turns into contempt for the whole person.

translation.ai_translation: Let no believing man hate a believing woman. If he dislikes one trait in her, he will be pleased with another.

situation: Mu'awiya ibn Haida asked the Prophet what a wife is owed by her husband.
wise_response: He said: feed her when you eat, clothe her when you clothe yourself, do not strike her face, do not insult her, and do not leave her except within the house.
why_it_worked: A wife shares her husband's standard of living and is owed basic dignity in word and deed.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping the best for yourself, insulting your wife, or walking out on her.

translation.original_text: وعن معاوية بن حيدة رضي الله عنه قال ‏:‏ قلت يا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما حق زوجة أحدنا عليه‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ ‏"‏أن تطعمها إذا طعمت ، وتكسوها إذا اكتسيت ولا تضرب الوجه، ولا تقبح، ولا تهجر إلا في البيت ‏"‏ حديث حسن رواه أبو داود وقال‏:‏ معنى ‏"‏لاتقبح‏"‏ أي ‏:‏ لا تقل قبحك الله‏.‏

situation: The Prophet forbade beating women. Umar complained that wives had grown bold, and permission was given. Then many women came to the Prophet's household complaining of their husbands.
wise_response: The Prophet said many women had come complaining of their husbands, and those men are not the best of you.
why_it_worked: What is tolerated is not what is good. Men who beat their wives fall short of the best.
tempting_wrong_answer: Using a permission as a license to hurt your wife.

translation.original_text: وعن إياس بن أبي ذباب رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ ‏"‏لاتضربوا إماء الله‏"‏ فجاء عمر رضي الله عنه إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فقال ‏:‏ ذئرن النساء على أزواجهن، فرخص في ضربهن، فأطاف بآل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نساء كثير يشكون أزواجهن، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ ‏"‏لقد أطاف بآل بيت محمد نساء كثير يشكون أزواجهن ليس أولئك بخياركم‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه أبو داود بإسناد صحيح‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of God said: Do not beat the female servants of God. Then Umar came to the Messenger of God and said: The women have become bold against their husbands. So he allowed beating them. Then many women came round to the family of the Messenger of God, complaining of their husbands. The Messenger of God said: Many women have come round to the family of Muhammad complaining of their husbands. Those are not the best of you.

situation: Everyone has some people in their care: a ruler, a husband, a wife, a parent.
wise_response: The Prophet said each of you is a shepherd and each is answerable for his flock: the ruler for his people, the man for his household, the woman for her husband's home and children.
why_it_worked: Responsibility comes with every role, however small, and each person will answer for those in their care.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating authority over others as privilege and forgetting the duty that comes with it.

وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏ كلكم راعٍ، وكلكم مسئول عن رعيته، والأمير راعٍ، والرجل راعٍ على أهل بيته؛ والمرأة راعية على بيت زوجها وولده، فكلكم راعٍ، وكلكم مسؤول عن رعيته‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock. The ruler is a shepherd, the man is a shepherd over his household, and the woman is a shepherd over her husband's house and his children. So each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock.

situation: A person does a good deed, such as leaving home for a better cause, but the motive behind it can be pure or self-serving.
wise_response: The Prophet said deeds are judged by intentions. Each person gets what he intended. Whoever moved for God and His Messenger has that. Whoever moved for some worldly gain or to marry a woman gets only what he moved for.
why_it_worked: The same outward act can be worth much or little. What gives it worth is the aim behind it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Doing good things for show, gain or advantage while letting people believe the motive is pure.

translation.original_text:
وعن أمير المؤمنين أبي حفص عمر بن الخطاب بن نفيل بن عبد العزى بن رياح بن قرط بن رزاح بن عدى بن لؤى ابن غالب القرشى العدوى‏.‏ رضي الله عنه، قال‏:‏ سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول‏:‏ ‏
"‏ إنما الأعمال بالنيات، وإنما لكل امرىء ما نوى فمن كانت هجرته إلى الله ورسوله فهجرته إلى الله ورسوله، ومن كانت هجرته لدنيا يصيبها، أو امرأة ينكحها فهجرته إلى ما هاجر إليه‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق على صحته‏.‏ رواه إماما المحدثين‏: أبو عبدالله محمد بن إسماعيل بن إبراهيم بن المغيرة بن بَرْدِزْبَهْ الجعفي البخاري، أبو الحسين مسلم بن الحجاج بن مسلم القشيرى النيسابورى رضي الله عنهما في صحيحهما اللذين هما أصح الكتب المصنفة‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Actions are only by intentions, and each person has only what he intended. So whoever's emigration was to God and His Messenger, his emigration is to God and His Messenger. And whoever's emigration was for some worldly thing he would gain, or a woman he would marry, his emigration is to what he emigrated for.

key_terms.نية (niyya): intention, the aim behind an act

situation: Yazid set aside some coins for charity and left them with a man in the mosque. His son Ma'n came and took them. Yazid objected that he had not meant them for his own son, and the two took the dispute to the Prophet.
wise_response: The Prophet told Yazid, "You have what you intended," and told Ma'n, "You have what you took." Both were treated fairly.
why_it_worked: Yazid's sincere intention to give was counted in full. The gift still reached someone in need, and the son was not wronged for accepting it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting a family quarrel over money turn bitter, or treating a gift as wasted because it did not land where the giver pictured.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي يزيد معن بن يزيد بن الأخنس رضي الله عنهم، وهو وأبوه وجده صحابيون، قال‏:‏ كان أبي يزيد أخرج دنانير يتصدق بها فوضعها عند رجل في  المسجد فجئت فأخذتها فأتيته بها، فقال‏:‏ والله ما إياك أردت، فخاصمته إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال‏:‏ ‏
"‏ لك ما نويت يا يزيد، ولك ما أخذت يامعن‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: My father Yazid had taken out some dinars to give in charity and placed them with a man in the mosque. I came and took them and brought them to him. He said: By God, it was not you I intended. So I took the dispute to the Messenger of God, and he said: "You have what you intended, Yazid, and you have what you took, Ma'n."

situation: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas fell gravely ill and thought he might die. He was wealthy with one daughter as heir, and asked the Prophet whether he could give two-thirds, then half, of his wealth to charity.
wise_response: The Prophet said no to two-thirds and to half, and allowed a third, adding that a third is a lot. He said it is better to leave your heirs rich than to leave them poor, holding out their hands to people. He told Sa'd that any spending done for God's sake is rewarded, even the bite of food he puts in his wife's mouth.
why_it_worked: Generosity to strangers should not leave your own family in need. Care for one's household is itself a good deed.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving away everything in a burst of piety and leaving dependants to beg, or thinking that only spending on outsiders counts as charity.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي إسحاق سعد بن أبي وقاص مالك بن أهيب بن عبد مناف بن زهرة بن كلاب بن مرة بن كعب بن لؤى القرش الزهرى رضي الله عنه، أحد العشرة المشهود لهم بالجنة، رضي الله عنهم، قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏ جاءنى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعودنى عام حجة الوداع من وجع اشتد بى فقلت‏:‏ يارسول الله  إني قد بلغ بى من الوجع ما ترى، وأنا ذو مال ولا يرثنى إلا ابنة لي، أفاتصدق بثلثى ما لي‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ لا، قلت‏:‏ فالشطر يارسول الله‏؟‏ فقال‏:‏ لا، قلت‏:‏ فالثلث يا رسول الله‏؟‏ قال الثلث والثلث كثير- أو كبير- إنك أن تذر ورثتك أغنياء خير من أن تذرهم عالة يتكففون الناس، وإنك لن تنفق نفقة تبتغى بها وجه الله إلا أجرت عليها حتى ما تجعل في  فيّ امرأتك قال‏:‏ فقلت‏:‏ يارسول الله أخلف بعد أصحابي‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ إنك لن تخلف فتعمل عملا تبتغي بهوجه الله إلا ازددت به درجة ورفعةً، ولعلك أن تخلف حتى ينتفع بك أقوام ويضرّ بك آخرون‏.‏ اللهم امض لآصحابى هجرتهم، ولا تردهم على أعقابهم، لكن البائس سعد بن خولة‏"‏ يرثى له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن مات بمكة‏.‏‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of God came to visit me in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage, during an illness that had grown severe. I said: Messenger of God, the pain has reached me as you see. I am a man of wealth, and none inherits from me but one daughter. Shall I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity? He said: No. I said: Then half, Messenger of God? He said: No. I said: Then a third? He said: A third, and a third is much (or: large). To leave your heirs rich is better than to leave them dependent, stretching out their hands to people. You will not spend anything seeking the face of God but you will be rewarded for it, even what you put in your wife's mouth. I said: Messenger of God, will I be left behind after my companions? He said: You will not be left behind and do a deed seeking the face of God except that you rise by it in degree and standing. Perhaps you will be left behind until some people benefit from you and others are harmed by you. O God, complete for my companions their emigration and do not turn them back on their heels. But the unfortunate one is Sa'd bin Khawla. The Messenger of God grieved for him because he died in Mecca.

situation: People judge each other by looks, bodies and appearance.
wise_response: The Prophet said God does not look at your bodies or your forms. He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
why_it_worked: Worth lies in character and conduct. Appearance says nothing about it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Judging people, or oneself, by beauty, build or dress.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي هريرة عبد الرحمن بن صخر رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏  
‏
"‏ إن الله لا ينظر إلى أجسامكم ، ولا إلى صوركم، ولكن ينظر إلى قلوبكم وأعمالكم‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: God does not look at your bodies or at your forms. He looks at your hearts and your deeds.

source.title: Riyad as-Salihin (Gardens of the Righteous)
source.author: Imam Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi
source.date_or_era: 13th century CE compilation of earlier hadith
source.citation: Arabic text via AhmedBaset/hadith-json (sunnah.com numbering); English translation cited, not stored

situation: A person feels the pull to do something wrong, or means to do some good but does not get to it.
wise_response: The Prophet reported that God records a good deed one intends but does not do as a full good deed, and one carried out as ten to seven hundred or more. An evil deed one intends but then holds back from is recorded as a full good deed. One carried out is recorded as a single bad deed.
why_it_worked: Holding back from a wrong you were tempted to do is itself counted as good. The account leans toward generosity.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating a passing urge as already acted on and giving in because "the thought was already there."

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي العباس عبد الله بن عباس بن عبد المطلب رضي الله عنهما، عن رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، فيما يروى عن ربه، تبارك وتعالى قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏ إن الله كتب الحسنات والسيئات ثم بين ذلك‏:‏ فمن همّ بحسنة فلم يعملها كتبها الله تبارك وتعالى عنده حسنة كاملة، وإن هم بها فعملها كتبها الله عشر حسنات إلى سبعمائه ضعف إلى أضعاف كثيرة، وإن هم بسيئة فلم يعملها كتبها الله عنده حسنة كاملة، وإن همّ بها فعملها كتبها الله سيئة واحدة ‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: God has written good deeds and bad deeds, then made it clear. Whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, God writes it with Him as one complete good deed. If he intends it and does it, God writes it as ten good deeds, up to seven hundred times, up to many times more. Whoever intends a bad deed and does not do it, God writes it with Him as one complete good deed. If he intends it and does it, God writes it as one bad deed.
