situation: A person wonders whether planting or farming is worth the effort when others may eat from it or even steal from it.
wise_response: The Prophet said that whenever a Muslim plants a tree, what is eaten from it is charity for him, what is stolen from it is charity for him, and whatever anyone takes from it is charity for him. In another narration: whatever person, animal or bird eats from it is charity for him.
why_it_worked: Work that feeds others keeps giving, whoever benefits. Even loss can be counted as giving.
tempting_wrong_answer: Refusing to plant or build because one might not get all the benefit oneself, or growing bitter over what others take.

translation.original_text:
التاسع عشر‏:‏ عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ ‏"‏ ما من مسلم يغرس غرساً إلا كان ما أكل منه له صدقة، وما سرق منه له صدقة، ولا يرزؤه أحد إلا كان له صدقة‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏.‏ ‏)‏‏)‏ وفي رواية له‏:‏ ‏"‏ فلا يغرس المسلم غرساً، فيأكل منه إنسان ولا دابة ولا طير إلا كان له صدقة إلى يوم القيامة‏"‏‏.‏ 
وفي رواية له‏:‏ ‏"‏ لا يغرس مسلم غرساً، ولا يزرع زرعاً، فيأكل منه إنسان ولا دابة ولا شىء إلا كانت له صدقة‏"‏ وروياه جميعاً من رواية أنس رضي الله عنه‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: No Muslim plants a plant except that what is eaten from it is a charity for him, what is stolen from it is a charity for him, and no one takes from it but it is a charity for him. In a narration of his: No Muslim plants a plant from which a person, an animal or a bird eats, except that it is a charity for him until the Day of Resurrection. In another narration: No Muslim plants a plant or sows a crop from which a person, animal or anything eats, except that it is a charity for him.

situation: A person who wants to do good looks for something practical to give.
wise_response: The Prophet named forty good traits, the highest of them lending a milk goat so another family can use its milk and then return it. Whoever does any of them hoping for its reward and trusting its promise will enter Paradise.
why_it_worked: Lending something productive lets a neighbour benefit without either side losing much. Simple acts of sharing count.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping one's goods idle when lending them would help a neighbour.

translation.original_text:
الثاني والعشرون‏:‏ عن أبي محمد عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ ‏
"‏أربعون خصلة أعلاها منيحة العنز، ما من عامل يعمل بخصلة منها رجاء ثوابها وتصديق موعودها إلا أدخله الله بها الجنة‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Forty traits, the highest of them is lending a she-goat for its milk. No one acts on one of these traits, hoping for its reward and believing what is promised for it, except that God admits him to Paradise by it.

key_terms.منيحة (maniha): a milk animal lent to someone for its milk

situation: A person feels he has too little to give to make any difference.
wise_response: The Prophet said: "Guard yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date." In another narration he added that whoever cannot find even that should give a kind word.
why_it_worked: Even the smallest gift matters, and a good word is itself a gift. No one is too poor to give.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving nothing because what one has seems too little, and withholding even kind words.

translation.original_text:
الثالث والعشرون‏:‏ عن عدي بن حاتم رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول‏:‏ ‏"‏ اتقوا النار ولو بشق تمرةٍ‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏ 
وفي رواية لهما عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ ‏"‏ ما منكم من أحد إلا سيكلمه ربه ليس بينه وبينه ترجمان فينظر أيمن منه فلا يرى إلا ما قدم، وينظر أشأم منه فلا يرى إلا ما قدم، ينظر بين يديه فلا يرى إلا النار تلقاء وجهه، فاتقوا النار ولو بشق تمرة، فمن لم يجد فبكلمة طيبةٍ‏"‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Guard yourselves against the Fire, even with half a date. In a narration of both: There is none of you but his Lord will speak to him with no interpreter between them. He will look to his right and see only what he sent ahead, look to his left and see only what he sent ahead, and look before him and see only the Fire facing him. So guard yourselves against the Fire, even with half a date, and whoever cannot find it, then with a good word.

situation: Three men asked the Prophet's wives about his worship and felt their own was small by comparison. One vowed to pray all night forever, one to fast every day, and one never to marry.
wise_response: The Prophet came to them and said that he feared God more than any of them, yet he fasted and broke his fast, prayed and slept, and married. "Whoever turns away from my way is not of me."
why_it_worked: Balance is part of goodness. Extreme vows that neglect the body, rest and family are not a higher path.
tempting_wrong_answer: Outdoing others in harsh self-denial and abandoning one's duties to family and self.

translation.original_text:
وعن أنس رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ جاء ثلاثة رهط إلى بيوت أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، يسألون عن عبادة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فلما أخبروا كأنهم تقالوها وقالوا‏:‏ أين نحن من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد غفر الله له تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر‏.‏ قال أحدهم‏:‏ أما أنا فأصلي الليل أبداً وقال الآخر‏:‏ وأنا أصوم الدهر أبداً ولا أفطر، وقال الآخر‏:‏ وأنا أعتزل النساء فلا أتزوج أبداً، فجاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إليهم فقال‏:‏ ‏
"‏أنتم الذين قلتم كذا وكذا‏؟‏‏!‏ أما والله إني لأخشاكم لله وأتقاكم له لكني أصوم وأفطر، وأصلي وأرقد، وأتزوج النساء، فمن رغب عن سنتي فليس مني‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Three men came to the houses of the Prophet's wives asking about the Prophet's worship. When they were told, it was as if they thought it little, and they said: Where are we compared with the Prophet, when God has forgiven him his past and later sins? One of them said: As for me, I will pray all night forever. Another said: And I will fast all my life and never break it. Another said: And I will keep away from women and never marry. The Messenger of God came to them and said: Are you the ones who said such and such? By God, I am the most fearful of God among you and the most mindful of Him, but I fast and I break my fast, I pray and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my way is not of me.

situation: Salman visited his brother-in-faith Abu al-Darda' and found Abu al-Darda's wife in shabby clothes. She said her husband had no interest in this world. Abu al-Darda' was fasting every day and praying all night.
wise_response: Salman refused to eat unless his host ate with him, and told him to sleep in the early night, waking him only toward dawn to pray together. He said, "Your Lord has a right over you, your self has a right over you, and your family has a right over you, so give each its due." The Prophet said, "Salman spoke the truth."
why_it_worked: Salman cared for his friend enough to correct him gently, by example and plain words. Devotion that neglects one's body and spouse is out of balance.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting a friend wear himself out and neglect his family for the sake of seeming piety, or keeping quiet to avoid an awkward talk.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي جحيفة وهب بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ آخى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بين سلمان وأبى الدرداء ، فزار سلمان أبا الدرداء، فرأى أم الدرداء متبذلة فقال‏:‏ ما شأنك قالت‏:‏ أخوك أبو الدرداء ليس له حاجة في الدنيا، فجاء أبو الدراداء فصنع له طعاماً، فقال له‏:‏ كل فإنى صائم، قال‏:‏ ما أنا بآكل حتى تأكل، فأكل، فلما كان الليل ذهب أبو الدرداء يقوم فقال له‏:‏ نم، فنام، ثم ذهب يقوم فقال له ‏:‏ نم، فلما كان من آخر الليل قال سلمان‏:‏ قم الآن‏:‏ فصليا جميعاً، فقال له سلمان‏:‏ إن لربك عليك حقاً، وإن لنفسك عليك حقاً، ولأهلك عليك حقاً، فأعط كل ذى حق حقه، فأتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر ذلك له، فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏
"‏صدق سلمان‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet made brotherhood between Salman and Abu al-Darda'. Salman visited Abu al-Darda' and saw Umm al-Darda' dressed in worn clothes. He said: What is the matter with you? She said: Your brother Abu al-Darda' has no need of this world. Abu al-Darda' came and made food for him and said: Eat, for I am fasting. He said: I will not eat until you eat. So he ate. When it was night Abu al-Darda' went to stand in prayer, and he said to him: Sleep. So he slept. Then he went to stand, and he said to him: Sleep. When it was the last part of the night Salman said: Get up now. And they both prayed. Then Salman said to him: Your Lord has a right over you, your self has a right over you, and your family has a right over you, so give everyone who has a right their right. He came to the Prophet and mentioned that to him, and the Prophet said: Salman spoke the truth.

situation: Hanzala felt that he became a different person away from the Prophet. In his presence he felt Paradise and Hell were before his eyes, but at home with his wife, children and work he forgot much. He feared this made him a hypocrite.
wise_response: He admitted it openly to Abu Bakr, who said he felt the same, and the two went to the Prophet and told him honestly. The Prophet said that if they stayed always in that state the angels would shake their hands in their beds and on the roads, "but Hanzala, an hour and an hour," repeating it three times.
why_it_worked: Hanzala was honest about his weakness instead of hiding it. The Prophet answered with realism: a person has times for devotion and times for family and work.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hiding one's doubts to look pious, or despairing because one cannot keep up a constant spiritual high.

translation.original_text: وعن أبي ربعي حنظلة بن الربيع الأسيدى الكاتب أحد كتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ لقيني أبو بكر رضي الله عنه فقال‏:‏ كيف أنت يا حنظلة‏؟‏ قلت‏:‏ نافق حنظلة‏؟‏ قلت‏:‏ نافق حنظلة ‍‍‏(‏ قال‏:‏ سبحان الله ما تقول‏؟‏ ‏(‏ قلت‏:‏ نكون عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يذكرنا بالجنة والنار كأنا رأي عين، فإذا خرجنا من عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عافسنا الأزواج والأولاد والضيعات نسينا كثيراً‏.‏ قال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه ‏:‏ فوالله إنا لنلقى مثل هذا، فانطلقت أنا وأبو بكر حتى دخلنا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ فقلت‏:‏ نافق حنظلة يا رسول الله ‏(‏ فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ ‏"‏وما ذاك‏؟‏‏"‏ قلت‏:‏ يا رسول الله نكون عندك تذكرنا بالنار والجنة كأنا رأي العين، فإذا خرجنا من عندك عافسنا الأزواج والأولاد والضيعات نسينا كثيراً‏.‏ فقال رسول الله 0‏:‏ ‏"‏والذي نفسي بيده لو تدومون على ما تكونون عندي وفي الذكر لصافحتكم الملائكة على فرشكم وفي طرقكم، ولكن يا حنظلة ساعة وساعة‏"‏ ثلاث مرات، ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Bakr met me and said: How are you, Hanzala? I said: Hanzala has become a hypocrite. He said: Glory be to God, what are you saying? I said: We are with the Messenger of God and he reminds us of Paradise and the Fire as if we saw them with our eyes. When we leave the Messenger of God, we busy ourselves with wives, children and our livelihoods and forget much. Abu Bakr said: By God, we meet the same thing. So Abu Bakr and I went until we entered upon the Messenger of God. I said: Hanzala has become a hypocrite, Messenger of God. The Messenger of God said: And what is that? I said: Messenger of God, we are with you and you remind us of the Fire and Paradise as if we saw them with our eyes. When we leave you, we busy ourselves with wives, children and livelihoods and forget much. The Messenger of God said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you remained as you are with me and in remembrance, the angels would shake your hands on your beds and in your streets. But, Hanzala, an hour and an hour. He said it three times.

situation: Early one morning a group from the tribe of Mudar came to the Prophet, nearly naked, in striped wool wraps, plainly starving. His face changed at the sight of their poverty.
wise_response: He led the prayer and spoke to the people, reciting verses about fearing God, kinship and looking to what one sends ahead for tomorrow. He urged them to give, from a dinar, a dirham, a garment, a measure of wheat or dates, "even half a date." A man of the Ansar brought a bag so heavy his hand could barely hold it, and others followed until there were two heaps of food and clothing. The Prophet's face shone. He said whoever starts a good practice has its reward and the reward of all who follow it.
why_it_worked: He was moved by others' hunger and acted on it at once. One man's generous lead drew the whole community to give.
tempting_wrong_answer: Seeing people in need and looking away, or waiting for someone else to give first.

translation.original_text:
عن أبي عمرو، جرير بن عبد الله، رضي الله عنه ، قال‏:‏ كنا  في صدر النهار عند رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، فجاءه قوم عراة مجتابي النمار، أو العباء، متقلدي السيوف، عامتهم من مضر، بل كلهم من مضر؛ فتمعر وجه رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، لما رأى بهم من الفاقة؛ فدخل ثم خرج، فأمر بلالاً فأذن وأقام، فصلى ثم خطب؛ فقال‏:‏ ‏{‏يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة‏}‏ إلى آخر الآية‏:‏ ‏{‏إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا‏}‏، والآية الأخرى التي في آخر الحشر‏:‏ ‏{‏يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد‏}‏ تصدق رجل من ديناره من درهمه من ثوبه من صاع بره من صاع تمره _حتى قال _ ولو بشق تمرة ‏,‏فجاء رجل من الأنصار بصرة كادت كفه تعجز عنها، بل قد عجزت، ثم تتابع الناس حتى رأيت كومين من طعام وثياب، حتى رأيت وجه رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، يتهلل كأنه مذهبة، فقال رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، ‏
"‏ من سن في الإسلام سنة حسنة فله أجرها، وأجر من عمل بها من بعده من غير أن يقنص من أجورهم شيء، ومن سن في الإسلام سنة سيئة كان عليه وزرها ووزر من عمل بها من بعده من غير أن ينقص من أوزارهم شيء‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: We were with the Messenger of God early in the day when a people came to him barefoot and nearly naked, wearing striped woollen wraps or cloaks, with swords hung on them. Most of them were from Mudar; indeed all of them were from Mudar. The face of the Messenger of God changed when he saw their need. He went in, then came out, and ordered Bilal, who gave the call to prayer and the call to stand. He prayed, then addressed them, saying: "O people, fear your Lord who created you from a single soul" to the end of the verse, "God is ever watchful over you," and the other verse at the end of al-Hashr: "O you who believe, fear God, and let every soul look to what it has sent ahead for tomorrow." Let a man give from his dinar, from his dirham, from his garment, from his measure of wheat, from his measure of dates, until he said: even half a date. Then a man of the Ansar came with a bag his hand could almost not hold, indeed could not. Then the people followed one after another, until I saw two heaps of food and clothing, and I saw the face of the Messenger of God glowing as if it were gilded. The Messenger of God said: Whoever begins a good practice in Islam has its reward and the reward of those who act on it after him, without anything being lessened from their rewards. And whoever begins a bad practice in Islam bears its burden and the burden of those who act on it after him, without anything being lessened from their burdens.

situation: A trusted treasurer or steward is told to pay out money on someone else's behalf.
wise_response: The Prophet said that the honest Muslim trustee who carries out what he is ordered, gives it in full without shortfall, with a willing heart, to the one he was told to give it to, is one of the two givers of charity.
why_it_worked: Handling another's money honestly and cheerfully is itself counted as giving. Faithful service shares in the good done.
tempting_wrong_answer: Skimming from what one is trusted to pay out, delaying it, or handing it over grudgingly.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏ الخازن المسلم الأمين الذي ينفذ ما أمر به، فيعطيه كاملاً موفراً، طيبة به نفسه فيدفعه إلى الذي أمر له به أحد المتصدقين‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The trustworthy Muslim treasurer who carries out what he is ordered, and gives it complete and in full, with a willing heart, handing it to the one it was ordered for, is one of the two who give charity.

situation: People relate to God, to leaders and to one another, and must decide whether to be sincere or to flatter and deceive.
wise_response: The Prophet said, "Religion is sincere counsel." Asked for whom, he said: for God, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims and their common people.
why_it_worked: Faith is lived as honest goodwill toward everyone, including telling leaders and ordinary people the truth for their good.
tempting_wrong_answer: Flattering the powerful, deceiving ordinary people, and keeping quiet when sincere advice is needed.

translation.original_text:
فالأول‏:‏ عن أبي رقية تميم بن أوس الداري رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏ الدين النصيحة‏"‏ قلنا‏:‏ لمن‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ لله ولكتابه ولرسوله ولأئمة المسلمين وعامتهم ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Religion is sincere goodwill. We said: To whom? He said: To God, to His Book, to His Messenger, and to the leaders of the Muslims and their common folk.

situation: A person sees something wrong being done and must decide whether to act.
wise_response: The Prophet said that whoever sees a wrong should change it with his hand. If he cannot, then with his tongue. If he cannot, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.
why_it_worked: Everyone has some duty in the face of wrong, matched to what he is able to do. At the least, one must not accept it inwardly.
tempting_wrong_answer: Looking away from wrongdoing, or approving it in one's heart to keep things comfortable.

translation.original_text:
فالأول‏:‏ عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول‏:‏ ‏
"‏من رأى منكم منكرًا فليغيره بيده ، فإن لم يستطع فبلسانه، فإن لم يستطع فبقلبه وذلك أضعف الإيمان‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whoever of you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand. If he cannot, then with his tongue. If he cannot, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.

key_terms.منكر (munkar): a wrong, what is recognised as evil

situation: The Prophet said cursing your own parents is a grave sin. People asked how anyone could curse his own parents.
wise_response: He said a man insults another man's father, and the other insults his father in return; he insults the other's mother, and the other insults his mother.
why_it_worked: Insults come back. Whoever starts the abuse is answerable for the abuse his own parents receive.
tempting_wrong_answer: Throwing insults at other people's families in a quarrel and thinking it does not touch your own.

translation.original_text:
وعنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏"‏من الكبائر شتم الرجل والديه‏!‏‏"‏ قالوا‏:‏ يا رسول الله وهل يشتم الرجل والديه‏؟‏ ‏!‏ قال‏:‏ ‏"‏نعم؛ يسب أبا الرجل، فيسب أباه، ويسب أمه، فيسب أمه‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏ 
وفي رواية ‏"‏إن من أكبر الكبائر أن يلعن الرجل والديه‏!‏‏"‏ قيل ‏:‏ يا رسول الله كيف يلعن الرجل والديه‏؟‏ ‏!‏ قال‏ "‏يسب أبا الرجل ، فيسب أباه، ويسب أمه، فيسب أمه‏"‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Among the major sins is a man reviling his own parents. They said: Messenger of God, would a man revile his own parents? He said: Yes. He reviles another man's father, and that man reviles his father; he reviles his mother, and that man reviles his mother. In another version: Among the greatest of the major sins is a man cursing his own parents. It was said: Messenger of God, how would a man curse his own parents? He said: He reviles another man's father, and that man reviles his father, and he reviles his mother, and that man reviles his mother.

situation: The Prophet listed habits that God forbids or dislikes.
wise_response: God has forbidden you to disobey mothers, to withhold what you owe while demanding what you are not owed, and to bury daughters alive. He dislikes idle gossip, excessive questioning, and wasting wealth.
why_it_worked: These are everyday ways of harming others and yourself: neglecting mothers, grasping, cruelty to girls, loose talk, and squandering.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being harsh to your mother, taking more than you give, trading in gossip and throwing money away.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي عيسى المغيرة بن شعبة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏إن الله تعالى حرم عليكم عقوق الأمهات، ومنعًا وهات، ووأد البنات، وكره لكم قيل وقال، وكثرة السؤال ، وإضاعة المال‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: God has forbidden you disobedience to mothers, withholding and demanding, and burying daughters alive. And He dislikes for you 'it was said' and 'he said', much asking, and wasting wealth.

situation: On the road to Mecca, Abdullah ibn Umar met a Bedouin whose father had been a friend of his own father, Umar. Ibn Umar gave him the donkey he rested on and the turban off his head. His companions said a Bedouin would be content with much less.
wise_response: Ibn Umar said the man's father had been dear to Umar, and he had heard the Prophet say the finest kindness is for a man to keep up ties with the people his father loved, after the father is gone.
why_it_worked: Honoring a parent continues after death through kindness to those the parent cared for.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving the least that will satisfy, and forgetting a parent's friendships once the parent has died.

translation.original_text:
وعن عبد الله بن دينار عن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن رجلاً من الأعراب لقيه بطريق مكة، فسلم عليه عبد الله بن عمر، وحمله على حمار كان يركبه، وأعطاه عمامة كانت على رأسه، قال ابن دينار‏:‏ فقلنا له‏:‏ أصلحك الله إنهم الأعراب وهم يرضون اليسير فقال عبد الله بن عمر‏:‏ إن أبا هذا كان ودًا لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول‏:‏ ‏"‏إن أبر البر صلة الرجل أهل ود أبيه‏"‏‏.‏ 
وفي رواية عن ابن دينار عن ابن عمر أنه كان إذا خرج إلى مكة كان له حمار يتروح عليه إذا مل ركوب الراحلة، وعمامة يشد بها رأسه، فبينا هو يومًا على ذلك الحمار إذ مر به أعرابي، فقال‏:‏ ألست ابن فلان بن فلان‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ بلى‏.‏ فأعطاه الحمار، فقال‏:‏ اركب هذا، وأعطاه العمامة وقال‏:‏ اشدد بها رأسك ، فقال له بعض أصحابه‏:‏ غفر الله لك أعطيت هذا الأعرابي حمارًا كنت تروح عليه، وعمامة كنت تشد بها رأسك‏؟‏ فقال‏:‏إني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول‏:‏ ‏"‏إن من أبر البر أن يصل الرجل أهل ود أبيه بعد أن يولي‏"‏ وإن أباه كان صديقًا لعمر رضي الله عنه ،
translation.ai_translation: Abdullah ibn Dinar reported that a Bedouin met Abdullah ibn Umar on the road to Mecca. Abdullah ibn Umar greeted him, mounted him on a donkey he had been riding, and gave him a turban that was on his head. Ibn Dinar said: We said to him: May God set you right, they are Bedouins and they are content with little. Abdullah ibn Umar said: This man's father was dear to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and I heard the Messenger of God say: The finest kindness is a man keeping ties with the people his father loved. In another version from Ibn Dinar: When Ibn Umar went out to Mecca he had a donkey he would rest on when tired of riding the camel, and a turban he tied round his head. One day while he was on that donkey a Bedouin passed him, and he said: Are you not the son of so-and-so son of so-and-so? He said: Yes. So he gave him the donkey and said: Ride this, and gave him the turban and said: Tie your head with it. One of his companions said to him: May God forgive you, you gave this Bedouin a donkey you rested on and a turban you tied your head with? He said: I heard the Messenger of God say: Among the finest kindness is that a man keeps ties with the people his father loved after he has passed. And his father was a friend of Umar.

situation: A man of Banu Salama asked whether there was any kindness left he could do for his parents after their death.
wise_response: The Prophet said yes: pray for them, ask forgiveness for them, carry out their promises after them, keep the family ties that exist only through them, and honor their friends.
why_it_worked: A child's duty to parents does not end at the grave. It continues in keeping their word and their bonds.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking duty to parents ends at death, letting their promises lapse and their friends be forgotten.

translation.original_text:
و عن أبي أُسَيد- بضم الهمزة وفتح السين- مالك بن ربيعة الساعدي رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ بينا نحن جلوس عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ جاءه رجل من بني سلمة فقال‏:‏ يا رسول الله هل بقي من بر أبوي شيء أبرهما به بعد موتهما‏؟‏ فقال‏:‏ ‏
"‏ نعم، الصلاة عليهما، والاستغفار لهما، وإنفاذ عهدهما من بعدهما، وصلة الرحم التي لا توصل إلا بهما، وإكرام صديقهما‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه أبو داود‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: While we were sitting with the Messenger of God, a man of Banu Salama came to him and said: Messenger of God, is there any kindness to my parents left that I can do for them after their death? He said: Yes: praying for them, asking forgiveness for them, carrying out their pledges after them, keeping the ties of kinship that are only kept through them, and honoring their friends.

situation: Years after his first wife Khadija died, the Prophet still spoke of her often. When he slaughtered a sheep, he would send portions to her women friends. Aisha, jealous, said it was as if Khadija were the only woman in the world.
wise_response: He answered that Khadija had been this and that, and that he had children by her. When her sister Hala asked to see him, he recognized Khadija's manner of asking and was moved.
why_it_worked: Faithfulness to a loved one continues after death through gratitude and kindness to the people they loved.
tempting_wrong_answer: Forgetting a spouse who stood by you once they are gone, and neglecting those who were close to them.

translation.original_text:
وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت‏:‏ ما غرت على أحد من نساء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما غرت على خديجة رضي الله عنها، وما رأيتها قط، ولكن كان يكثر ذكرها، وربما ذبح الشاة، ثم يقطعها أعضاء، ثم يبعثها في صدائق خديجة، فربما قلت له‏:‏ كأن لم يكن في الدنيا إلا خديجة‏!‏ فيقول‏:‏ ‏"‏إنها كانت وكانت وكان لي منها ولد‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏ 
وفي رواية وإن كان ليذبح الشاء، فيُهدي في خلائلها منها ما يسعهن‏.‏
وفي رواية كان إذا ذبح الشاة يقول‏:‏ ‏"‏أرسلوا بها إلى أصدقاء خديجة‏"‏‏.‏
وفي رواية قالت‏:‏ استأذنت هالة بنت خويلد أخت خديجة على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فعرف استئذان خديجة، فارتاح لذلك فقال‏:‏ اللهم هالة بنت خويلد‏"‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Aisha said: I was never as jealous of any of the Prophet's wives as I was of Khadija, though I never saw her. But he used to mention her often, and sometimes he would slaughter a sheep, cut it into parts and send them to Khadija's friends. Sometimes I said to him: It is as if there were no woman in the world but Khadija! And he would say: She was this and that, and I had children by her. In another version: He would slaughter sheep and send her friends as much as would suffice them. In another: When he slaughtered a sheep he would say: Send it to Khadija's friends. In another, she said: Hala bint Khuwailid, Khadija's sister, asked permission to come in to the Messenger of God, and he recognized Khadija's way of asking permission and was gladdened by it, and said: O God, Hala bint Khuwailid.

situation: Abdullah ibn Sahl was found murdered at Khaibar. His brother Abd al-Rahman, the youngest, came to the Prophet with his older cousins Huwaisa and Muhaisa, and began to speak first.
wise_response: The Prophet said: 'Let the elder speak, the elder.' Abd al-Rahman fell silent and the two older men presented the case.
why_it_worked: Even in grief and urgency, giving the elders the first word shows respect and keeps order.
tempting_wrong_answer: Pushing ahead of your elders because your stake feels greater.

translation.original_text: وعن أبي يحيى وقيل‏:‏ أبي محمد سهل بن أبي حَثْمة -بفتح الحاء المهملة وإسكان الثاء المثلثة -الأنصاري رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ انطلق عبد الله ابن سهل ومحيصة بن مسعود إلى خيبر وهي صلح، فتفرقا، فأتى محيصة إلى عبد الله بن سهل وهو يتشحط في دمه قتيلاً، فدفنه، ثم قدم المدينة فانطلق عبد الرحمن بن سهل ومحيصة وحويصة ابنا مسعود إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فذهب عبد الرحمن يتكلم فقال‏:‏ ‏"‏ كبر كبر‏"‏ وهو أحدث القوم، فسكت، فتكلما فقال‏:‏ ‏"‏أتحلفون وتستحقون قاتلكم‏؟‏ وذكر تمام الحديث‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abdullah ibn Sahl and Muhaisa ibn Mas'ud went to Khaibar during the truce and went their separate ways. Muhaisa came upon Abdullah ibn Sahl rolling in his blood, killed, and buried him. Then he came to Medina, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahl and Muhaisa and Huwaisa, the sons of Mas'ud, went to the Prophet. Abd al-Rahman began to speak, and he said: The elder, the elder. He was the youngest of them, so he fell silent, and the two spoke. He said: Will you swear and so claim your killer? And he mentioned the rest of the report.

wise_response: She cited the Prophet: 'Give people their due places.'

situation: Uyaina ibn Hisn got an audience with the caliph Umar through his nephew al-Hurr, then said to him: 'Son of al-Khattab, you do not give us much and you do not judge among us justly.' Umar grew so angry he was about to punish him.
wise_response: Al-Hurr recited the verse 'Take to forgiveness, command what is right, and turn away from the ignorant,' and said this man was one of the ignorant. Umar went no further; he always stopped at the Book of God.
why_it_worked: A timely reminder cooled a ruler's anger. Umar let a principle overrule his temper.
tempting_wrong_answer: Punishing an insult on the spot because you have the power to.

translation.original_text: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال‏:‏ قدم عيينة بن حصن، فنزل على ابن أخيه الحر بن قيس، وكان من النفر الذين يدنيهم عمر رضي الله عنه ، وكان القراء أصحاب مجلس عمر ومشاورته، كهولاً كانوا أو شبانًا ، فقال عيينة لابن أخيه‏:‏ يا ابن أخي لك وجه عند هذا الأمير، فاستأذن لي عليه، فاستأذن له، فأذن له عمر رضي الله عنه ، فلما دخل‏:‏ قال هي يا ابن الخطاب‏:‏ فوالله ما تعطينا الجزل، ولا تحكم فينا بالعدل، فغضب عمر رضي الله عنه حتى هم أن يوقع به، فقال له الحر‏:‏ يا أمير المؤمنين إن الله تعالى قال لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏{‏خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين‏}‏ وإن هذا من الجاهلين‏.‏ والله ما جاوزها عمر حين تلاها عليه، وكان وقافًا عند كتاب الله تعالى‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Uyaina ibn Hisn came and stayed with his nephew al-Hurr ibn Qais, who was one of the group Umar kept close; the reciters were the members of Umar's council and those he consulted, whether old or young. Uyaina said to his nephew: Nephew, you have standing with this ruler, so ask permission for me to see him. He asked permission for him, and Umar gave it. When he came in he said: Hey, son of al-Khattab! By God, you do not give us plenty, and you do not judge among us with justice. Umar became angry until he was about to strike him. situation: After the Prophet died, Abu Bakr suggested to Umar that they visit Umm Ayman, the Prophet's old nurse, as he used to visit her. When they arrived she wept.
wise_response: They reminded her that what is with God is better for the Prophet. She said she knew it; she wept because revelation from heaven had ended. Moved, they both wept with her.
why_it_worked: They kept up the Prophet's kindness to an old woman who had raised him, and they met her grief with shared grief.
tempting_wrong_answer: Dropping those your predecessor cared for once he is gone, or lecturing the grieving instead of sitting with them.

translation.original_text: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قال أبو بكر لعمر رضي الله عنهما بعد وفاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ انطلق بنا إلى أم أيمن رضي الله عنها نزورها كما كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يزورهان فلما انتهيا إليها، بكت، فقالا لها، ما يبكيك أما تعلمين أن ما عند الله خير لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏؟‏ فقالت‏:‏ إني لا أبكي إني لا أعلم أن ما عند الله تعالى خير لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، ولكن أبكي أن الوحي قد انقطع من السماء، فهيجتهما على البكاء، فجعلا يبكيان معها‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: After the Messenger of God died, Abu Bakr said to Umar: Come with us to Umm Ayman so we can visit her as the Messenger of God used to visit her. When they reached her she wept. They said to her: What makes you weep? Do you not know that what is with God is better for the Messenger of God? She said: I do not weep because I do not know that what is with God is better for the Messenger of God. I weep because revelation has been cut off from heaven. situation: A man set out to visit a brother in another village. An angel waiting on the road asked whether he had some favor from the man that he was going to tend.
wise_response: He said no; he loved him for God's sake. The angel told him God loved him as he loved his brother.
why_it_worked: Visiting a friend out of pure affection, with nothing to gain, is love at its cleanest.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping up friendships only where there is a favor to collect or protect.

situation: A person chooses whom to spend time with.
wise_response: The Prophet said a good companion is like a musk seller: he may give you some, you may buy from him, or at least you enjoy the scent. A bad companion is like a blacksmith working the bellows: he may burn your clothes, or at least you get the stench.
why_it_worked: Company rubs off on you. Good friends leave something good even when you do not try; bad ones leave harm.
tempting_wrong_answer: Spending time with people whose habits you know are harmful, thinking it will not touch you.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏إنما مثل الجليس الصالح وجليس السوء، كحامل المسك، ونافخ الكير، فحامل المسك، إما أن يحذيك، وإما أن تبتاع منه، وإما أن تجد منه ريحًا طيبة، ونافخ الكير، إما أن يحرق ثيابك ، وإما أن تجد منه ريحًا منتنة‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The likeness of the good companion and the bad companion is that of one carrying musk and one blowing a blacksmith's bellows. The one carrying musk will either give you some, or you will buy from him, or you will find a pleasant scent from him. The one blowing the bellows will either burn your clothes or you will find a foul smell from him.

situation: The Prophet had foretold that a man called Uwais would come from Yemen, a man devoted to his mother whose prayers God answers. When Umar found him among the Yemeni troops, he asked Uwais to pray for his forgiveness and offered to write to the governor of Kufa on his behalf.
wise_response: Uwais prayed for Umar but declined the letter, saying he preferred to be among the common, obscure people. When people later learned who he was, he left.
why_it_worked: His standing came from devotion to his mother and humility. He refused the favor of the powerful and fled fame.
tempting_wrong_answer: Using a moment of recognition from the powerful to win position and reputation.

translation.original_text:
وعن أُسَير بن عمرو ويقال‏"‏‏:‏ ابن جابر وهو ‏"‏بضم الهمزة وفتح السين المهملة‏"‏ قال‏:‏ كان عمر بن الخطاب إذا أتى عليه أمداد أهل اليمن سألهم‏:‏ أفيكم أويس بن عامر‏؟‏ حتى أتى على أويس رضي الله عنه ، فقال له‏:‏ أنت أويس بن عامر‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ نعم، قال‏:‏ من مراد ثم من قرن‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ نعم قال‏:‏ فكان بك برص، فبرأت منه إلا موضع درهم‏؟‏ قال نعم قال‏:‏ لك والدة‏؟‏ قال ‏:‏ نعم، قال ‏:‏ سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ‏"‏يأتي عليكم أويس بن عامر مع أمداد أهل اليمن من مراد، ثم من قرن كان به برص، فبرأ منه إلا موضع درهم، له والدة هو بها بر لو أقسم على الله لأبره، فإن استطعت أن يستغفر لك فافعل‏"‏ فاستغفر لي فاستغفر له، فقال له عمر‏:‏ أين تريد‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ الكوفة، قال‏:‏ ألا أكتب لك إلى عاملها‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ أكون في غبراء الناس أحب إلي، فلما كان من العام المقبل حج رجل من أشرافهم، فوافق عمر، فسأله عن أويس، فقال‏:‏ تركته رث البيت قليل المتاع، قال‏:‏ سمعت رسول الله يقول‏:‏ يأتي عليكم أويس بن عامر مع أمداد من أهل اليمن من مراد ، ثم من قرن، كان به برص فبرأ منه إلا موضع درهم، له والدة هو بها بر لو أقسم على الله لأبره، فإن استطعت أن يستغفر لك ‏:‏ فافعل، فأتى أويسًا، فقال استغفر لي قال‏:‏ أنت أحدث عهدًا بسفر صالح، فاستغفر لي‏.‏ قال‏:‏ لقيت عمر‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ نعم، فاستغفر له، ففطن له الناس، فانطلق على وجهه‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ 
وفي رواية لمسلم أيضًا عن أُسِير بن جابر رضي الله عنه أن أهل الكوفة وفدوا على عمر رضي الله عنه ، وفيهم رجل ممن كان يسخر بأويس، فقال عمر‏:‏ هل هاهنا أحد من القرنين‏؟‏ فجاء ذلك الرجل، فقال عمر‏:‏ إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قد قال‏:‏‏"‏إن رجلا يأتيكم من اليمن يقال له ‏:‏ أويس، لا يدع باليمن غير أم له، قد كان به بياض فدعا الله تعالى، فأذهبه إلا موضع الدينار أو الدرهم ، فمن لقيه منكم، فليستغفر لكم‏"‏‏.‏
وفي رواية له عن عمر رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ ‏"‏إنى سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول‏:‏ ‏"‏إن خير التابعين رجل يقال له‏:‏ أويس‏:‏ وله والدة وكان به بياض، فمروه، فليستغفر لكم‏"‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: When reinforcements from Yemen came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, he would ask them: Is Uwais ibn Amir among you? Until he came to Uwais and said: Are you Uwais ibn Amir? He said: Yes. He said: Of Murad, then of Qaran? He said: Yes. He said: You had leprosy and were cured of it except for the size of a dirham? He said: Yes. He said: You have a mother? He said: Yes. He said: I heard the Messenger of God say: Uwais ibn Amir will come to you with the reinforcements of the people of Yemen, of Murad, then of Qaran. He had leprosy and was cured of it except for the size of a dirham. He has a mother to whom he is devoted. If he swore by God, God would fulfil it. If you are able to have him ask forgiveness for you, do it. So ask forgiveness for me. And he asked forgiveness for him. Umar said to him: Where are you headed? He said: Kufa. He said: Shall I not write to its governor for you? He said: I prefer to be among the dusty, common people. The next year a man of their nobles went on pilgrimage and met Umar, who asked him about Uwais. He said: I left him with a shabby house and few belongings. Umar said: I heard the Messenger of God say: Uwais ibn Amir will come to you with the reinforcements from the people of Yemen, of Murad, then of Qaran. He had leprosy and was cured of it except for the size of a dirham. He has a mother to whom he is devoted. If he swore by God, God would fulfil it. If you are able to have him ask forgiveness for you, do it. So the man went to Uwais and said: Ask forgiveness for me. He said: You are fresher from a righteous journey, so ask forgiveness for me. He said: Did you meet Umar? He said: Yes. And he asked forgiveness for him. The people became aware of him, and he went off on his way. In another version in Muslim, from Usair ibn Jabir: The people of Kufa came in a delegation to Umar, and among them was a man who used to mock Uwais. Umar said: Is there anyone here from Qaran? That man came forward. Umar said: The Messenger of God said: A man will come to you from Yemen called Uwais. He leaves no one in Yemen but a mother of his. He had a white patch, and he prayed to God and He removed it except for the size of a dinar or a dirham. Whoever of you meets him, let him ask forgiveness for you. In another version from Umar: I heard the Messenger of God say: The best of the Followers is a man called Uwais. He has a mother, and he had a white patch. Tell him to ask forgiveness for you.

situation: Who will God shelter on the Day when there is no shade but His?
wise_response: The Prophet named seven: a just ruler; a youth raised in worship; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two who love each other for God, meeting and parting on that; a man invited by a beautiful woman of high standing who says 'I fear God'; one who gives charity so secretly his left hand does not know what his right gave; and one who remembers God alone and weeps.
why_it_worked: Most of the seven are about conduct toward others and mastery of self: fairness in power, refusing temptation, and giving without show.
tempting_wrong_answer: Ruling unjustly, giving in to temptation, and giving charity to be seen.

translation.original_text:
و عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏
"‏ سبعة يظلهم الله في ظله يوم لا ظل إلا ظله‏:‏ إما عادل، وشاب نشأ في عبادة الله عز وجل، ورجل قلبه معلق بالمساجد‏.‏ ورجلان تحابا في الله اجتمعا عليه ، وتفرقا عليه، ورجل دعته امرأة ذات حسن وجمال، فقال‏:‏ إني أخاف الله، ورجل تصدق بصدقة، فأخفاها حتى لا تعلم شماله ما تنفق يمينه، ورجل ذكر الله خاليًا ففاضت عيناه‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Seven God will shade in His shade on the day when there is no shade but His: a just ruler; a youth who grew up in the worship of God; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two men who love each other for God, coming together for that and parting for that; a man whom a woman of standing and beauty calls, and he says, I fear God; a man who gives charity and hides it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand spends; and a man who remembers God in private and his eyes overflow.

situation: While digging the trench at Medina, Jabir saw the Prophet with a stone tied over his stomach from hunger. Jabir went home, and he and his wife prepared their one small goat and a measure of barley, meaning to invite the Prophet and one or two others.
wise_response: Jabir and his wife gave everything they had to feed him. The Prophet then invited the whole company of diggers to share the meal and served them himself until all were full. He told Jabir's wife, 'Eat this and send some as gifts, for the people have been struck by hunger.'
why_it_worked: Jabir could not bear to see his leader hungry and gave all he had. The Prophet would not eat alone while his people starved. He shared the meal and sent the rest on to hungry neighbors.
tempting_wrong_answer: To keep a private meal for oneself and a favored few while others go hungry around you.

translation.original_text:
وعن جابر رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ إنا كنا يوم الخندق نحفر، فعرضت كدية شديدة، فجاؤوا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا‏:‏ هذه كدية عرضت في الخندق‏.‏ فقال‏:‏ ‏"‏أنا نازل‏"‏ ثم قام، وبطنه معصوب بحجر، ولبثنا ثلاثة أيام لا نذوق ذوقاً فأخذ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المعول، فضرب، فعاد كثيباً أهيل، أو أهيم، فقلت‏:‏ يا رسول الله ائذن لي إلى البيت، فقلت لامرأتي‏:‏ رأيت بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئاً ما في ذلك صبر فعندك شيء‏؟‏ فقالت‏:‏ عندي شعير وعناق، فذبحت العناق وطحنت الشعير حتى جعلنا اللحم في البرمة، ثم جئت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والعجين قد انكسر، والبرمة بين الأثاقي قد كادت تنضج، فقلت‏:‏ طعيم لي، فقم أنت يا رسول الله ورجل أو رجلان، قال‏:‏ ‏"‏كم هو‏؟‏‏"‏ فذكرت له فقال‏:‏ ‏"‏كثير طيب، قل لها لا تنزع البرمة، ولا الخبز من التنور حتى آتي” فقال‏:‏ “قوموا” فقام المهاجرون والأنصار، فدخلت عليها فقلت‏:‏ ويحك جاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمهاجرون والأنصار ومن معهم‏!‏ قالت‏:‏ هل سألك‏؟‏ قلت‏:‏ نعم، قال‏:‏ “ادخلوا ولا تضاغطوا فجعل يكسر الخبز، ويجعل عليه اللحم، ويخمر البرمة والتنور إذا أخذ منه، ويقرب إلى أصحابه ثم ينزع، فلم يزل يكسر ويغرف حتى شبعوا، وبقي منه، فقال‏:‏ كلي هذا وأهدي، فإن الناس أصابتهم مجاعة” ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ 

وفي رواية‏:‏ قال جابر‏:‏ لما حفر الخندق رأيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خمصاً، فانكفأت إلى امراتى فقلت‏:‏ هل عندك شيء؛ فإني رأيت برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خمصاً شديداً فأخرجت إلي جرابا فيه صاع من شعير، ولنا بهيمة داجن فذبحتها، وطحنت الشعير، ففرغت إلى فراغى، وقطعتها في برمتها، ثم وليت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت‏:‏ لا تفضحني برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن معه، فجئته وساررته فقلت‏:‏ يا رسول الله، ذبحنا بهيمة لنا، وطحنت صاعا من شعير، فتعال أنت ونفر معك، فصاح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال‏:‏ يا أهل الخندق إن جابراً قد صنع سؤراً فحيهلا بكم‏"‏ فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏ ‏"‏لا تنزلن برمتكم ولا تخبزن عجينكم حتى أجيء‏"‏ فجئت، وجاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقدم الناس، حتى جئت امرأتي فقالت‏:‏ بك وبك‏!‏ فقلت‏:‏ قد فعلت الذي قلت‏.‏ فأخرجت عجيناً، فبسق فيه وبارك، ثم عمد إلى برمتنا فبصق وبارك، ثم قال‏:‏ ‏"‏ادعي خابزة فلتخبز معك، واقدحي من برمتكم ولا تنزلوها‏"‏وهم ألف، فأقسم بالله لأكلوا حتى تركوه وانحرفوا، وإن برمتنا لتغط كما هي، وإن عجيننا ليخبز كما هو‏.‏

قوله‏:‏ ‏"‏عرضت كدية‏"‏ ‏:‏ بضم الكاف وإسكان الدال وبالياء المثناة تحت؛ وهي قطعة غليظة صلبة من الأرض لا يعمل فيها الفأس‏.‏ ‏"‏والكثيب‏"‏ أصله تل الرمل، والمراد هنا‏:‏ صارت تراباً ناعماً، وهو معنى “أهيل”‏.‏ ‏"‏الأثافي‏"‏ ‏:‏ الأحجار التى يكون عليها القدر‏.‏ و‏"‏تضاغطوا‏"‏ ‏:‏ تزاحموا‏.‏ و‏"‏المجاعة‏"‏ ‏:‏الجوع، وهو بفتح الميم‏.‏ و‏"‏الخمص‏"‏ بفتح الخاء المعجمة والميم‏:‏ الجوع‏.‏ و”انكفأت” ‏:‏ انقلبت ورجعت‏.‏ ‏"‏البهيمة‏"‏ بضم الباء‏:‏ تصغير بهمة، وهي العناق -بفتح العين-‏.‏ و‏"‏الداجن‏"‏‏:‏ هي التي ألفت البيت‏.‏ و‏"‏السؤر‏"‏ ‏:‏الطعام الذي يدعى الناس إليه، وهو بالفارسية‏.‏ و‏"‏حيهلا‏"‏ أي‏:‏ تعالوا‏.‏ وقولها‏:‏ ‏"‏بك وبك‏"‏ أي‏:‏ خاصمته وسبته، لأنها اعتقدت أن الذي عندها لا يكفيهم، فاستحيت وخفي عليها ما أكرم الله سبحانه وتعالى به نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم من هذه المعجزة الظاهرة والآية اباهرة‏.‏ “بسق‏"‏ أي ‏:‏بصق؛ ويقال أيضاً‏:‏ بزق -ثلاث لغات- و‏"‏عمد‏"‏ بفتح الميم‏:‏ أي قصد‏.‏ و‏"‏اقدحي” أي اغرفي؛ والمقدحة‏:‏ المغرفة‏.‏ و”تغط” أي‏:‏ لغليانها صوت، والله اعلم‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Jabir said: On the day of the Trench we were digging when a hard rock got in the way. They came to the Prophet and said, 'This rock has got in the way in the trench.' He said, 'I will go down.' He stood up, and his stomach was bound with a stone; we had gone three days without tasting anything. The Prophet took the pick and struck, and it turned to loose sand. I said, 'Messenger of God, give me leave to go home.' I said to my wife, 'I saw something in the Prophet that I cannot bear. Do you have anything?' She said, 'I have barley and a young goat.' I slaughtered the goat and she ground the barley, and we put the meat in the pot. Then I came to the Prophet when the dough had risen and the pot on the stones was nearly cooked. I said, 'I have a little food. Come, Messenger of God, you and a man or two.' He said, 'How much is it?' I told him. He said, 'Plenty and good. Tell her not to take the pot off or the bread out of the oven until I come.' Then he said, 'Get up,' and the Emigrants and the Ansar got up. I went in to my wife and said, 'Woe to you, the Prophet has come with the Emigrants and the Ansar and those with them.' She said, 'Did he ask you?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Come in and do not crowd.' He began breaking the bread and putting meat on it, covering the pot and the oven whenever he took from them, and handing it to his companions, then taking more. He kept breaking and ladling until they were full, and some was left. He said, 'Eat this and give it as gifts, for the people have been struck by hunger.'

key_terms.كلي هذا وأهدي (kuli hadha wa ahdi): eat this and give some as gifts

situation: A person believes that more possessions will finally make them feel rich.
wise_response: The Prophet said, 'Wealth is not having many possessions. Wealth is the richness of the soul.'
why_it_worked: Someone content inside is rich at any income. Someone grasping is poor at any income.
tempting_wrong_answer: To keep adding possessions in the hope that the next one will bring satisfaction.

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ ‏"‏ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض، ولكن الغنى غنى النفس‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏

translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet said, 'Richness is not an abundance of goods. Richness is richness of the soul.'

situation: Hakim bin Hizam asked the Prophet for money three times, and each time the Prophet gave to him.
wise_response: Then the Prophet told him that wealth is green and sweet. Whoever takes it with a generous spirit is blessed in it, and whoever takes it with greed is like one who eats and is never full. 'The upper hand is better than the lower hand.' Hakim swore he would take nothing from anyone again. He refused even his rightful share when Abu Bakr and later Umar offered it, and kept that oath until he died.
why_it_worked: The Prophet gave first and taught after, so the lesson came without shame. Hakim took it fully and kept his word for life.
tempting_wrong_answer: To keep asking because the giver keeps giving, as Hakim did before he was taught.

translation.original_text:
وعن حكيم بن حزام رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأعطاني، ثم سألته فأعطاني، ثم سألته فأعطاني ثم قال‏:‏ ‏"‏يا حكيم، إن هذا المال خضر حلو، فمن أخذه بسخاوة نفس بورك له فيه، ومن أخذه بإشراف نفس لم يبارك له فيه، وكان كالذي يأكل ولا يشبع، واليد العليا خير من اليد السفلى‏"‏ قال حكيم‏:‏ فقلت يا رسول الله والذي بعثك بالحق لا أرزأ أحداً بعدك شيئاً حتى أفارق الدنيا‏.‏ فكان أبو بكر رضي الله عنه يدعو حكيماً ليعطيه العطاء، فيأبى أن يقبل منه شيئاً ثم إن عمر رضي الله عنه دعاه ليعطيه، فأبى أن يقبله‏.‏ فقال‏:‏ يا معشر المسلمين، أشهدكم على حكيم أني أعرض عليه حقه الذي قسمه الله له في هذا الفيء فيأبى أن يأخذه فلم يرزأ حكيم أحداً بعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى توفي‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ 

‏"‏يرزأ‏"‏ براء ثم زاى ثم همزة، أي‏:‏ لم يأخذ من أحد شيئاً، وأصل الرزء‏:‏ النقصان، أي‏:‏ لم ينقص أحداً شيئاً بالأخذ منه‏.‏ و‏"‏إشراف النفس‏"‏‏:‏ تطلعها وطمعها بالشيء‏.‏ ‏"‏سخاوة النفس‏"‏‏:‏ هي عدم الإشراف إلى الشيء، والطمع فيه، والمبالاة به والشره‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Hakim bin Hizam said: I asked the Messenger of God and he gave to me, then I asked him and he gave to me, then I asked him and he gave to me. Then he said, 'Hakim, this wealth is green and sweet. Whoever takes it with a generous self is blessed in it, and whoever takes it with a craving self is not blessed in it, and is like one who eats and is not filled. The upper hand is better than the lower hand.' Hakim said: I said, 'Messenger of God, by Him who sent you with the truth, I will not take anything from anyone after you until I leave this world.' Abu Bakr used to call Hakim to give him his stipend, and he refused to accept anything from him. Then Umar called him to give to him, and he refused to accept it. Umar said, 'Muslims, I call you to witness about Hakim that I offer him his right that God has allotted him from this spoil, and he refuses to take it.' Hakim did not take anything from anyone after the Prophet until he died.

key_terms.إشراف نفس (ishraf nafs): craving, a self that strains after things

situation: Abu Musa told how, on a campaign, six men shared one camel and walked until their feet were torn and his toenails fell off, so they wrapped their feet in rags.
wise_response: After telling the story, Abu Musa regretted it and said, 'What need had I to mention it?' He disliked making known anything of his own good deeds.
why_it_worked: He did not want hardship he had borne for a good cause to become a way of winning praise.
tempting_wrong_answer: To retell one's sacrifices so that others will admire them.

translation.original_text: وعن أبي بردة عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزاة، ونحن ستة نفر بيننا بعير نعتقبه، فنقبت أقدامنا ونقبت قدمي، وسقطت أظافري، فكنا نلف على أرجلنا الخرق، فسميت غزوة ذات الرقاع لما كنا نعصب على أرجلنا من الخرق قال أبو بردة‏:‏ فحدث أبوموسى بهذا الحديث، ثم كره ذلك، وقال‏:‏ ما كنت أصنع بأن أذكره‏!‏ قال‏:‏ كأنه كره أن يكون شئياً من عمله أفشاه‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Burdah reported that Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: We went out with the Messenger of God on a campaign, six of us sharing one camel that we rode in turns. Our feet were worn through; my feet were worn through and my nails fell off, and we used to wrap rags around our feet, so it was called the campaign of Dhat al-Riqa' for the rags we bound on our feet. Abu Burdah said: Abu Musa told this, then disliked having done so, and said, 'What was I doing mentioning it?' It was as if he disliked having disclosed something of his own deeds.

situation: The Prophet divided some goods, giving to some men and leaving others out. Those left out were upset.
wise_response: He told them openly that he gave to those whose hearts he saw were anxious and impatient, and left others to the richness and goodness God had put in their hearts. He said the ones he left out were dearer to him, and named Amr bin Taghlib among them. Amr said he would not trade that word for a herd of red camels.
why_it_worked: He explained his decision instead of leaving resentment to fester. Fairness meant giving according to need and steadiness, and he honored those who could do without.
tempting_wrong_answer: To give only to those one favors, or to leave those passed over to stew without explanation.

translation.original_text:
وعن عمرو بن تغلب - بفتح التاء المثناة فوق وإسكان الغين المعجمة وكسر اللام - رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أتي بمال أو سبي فقسمه، فأعطى رجالا، وترك رجالا، فبلغه أن الذين ترك عتبوا ؛فحمد الله ثم أثنى عليه ثم قال، أما بعد فوالله إني لأعطي الرجل وأدع الرجل والذي أدع أحب إلي من الذي أعطي، ولكني إنما أعطي أقواماً لما أرى في قلوبهم من الجزع والهلع، وأكل أقواماً إلى ما جعل الله في قلوبهم من الغنى والخير، منهم عمرو بن تغلب” قال عمرو بن تغلب‏:‏ فوالله ما أحب أن لي بكلمة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حمر النعم ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ 

‏
"‏الهلع‏"‏‏:‏ هو أشد الجزع، وقيل‏:‏ الضجر‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Amr bin Taghlib reported that wealth or captives were brought to the Messenger of God and he divided them, giving to some men and leaving others. He heard that those he left were displeased. He praised God and glorified Him, then said: 'By God, I give to one man and leave another, and the one I leave is dearer to me than the one I give. I give to people because of the anxiety and restlessness I see in their hearts, and I leave others to the richness and good that God has placed in their hearts. Among them is Amr bin Taghlib.' Amr bin Taghlib said: By God, I would not want red camels in exchange for that word of the Messenger of God.

situation: The Prophet asked a small group of companions to renew their pledge to him.
wise_response: He asked them to worship God alone, pray, and obey, and then added quietly, 'And do not ask people for anything.' Afterwards some of those men, if a whip fell from their hand while riding, would not ask anyone to hand it to them.
why_it_worked: Not asking others for things preserves one's dignity and spares others a burden. The men kept the pledge even in the smallest matters.
tempting_wrong_answer: To lean on others for every small need when one can manage oneself.

translation.original_text: وعن أبي عبد الرحمن عوف بن مالك الأشجعي رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تسعة أو ثمانية أو سبعة فقال‏:‏ ‏"‏ألا تبايعون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏"‏ وكنا حديثي عهد ببيعة، فقلنا‏:‏ قد بايعناك يا رسول الله، فعلام نبايعك‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ ‏"‏على أن تعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئاً، والصلوات الخمس وتطيعوا‏"‏ وأسر كلمة خفية‏:‏ ‏"‏ولا تسألوا الناس شيئاً‏"‏ فلقد رأيت بعض أولئك النفر يسقط سوط أحدهم فما يسأل احداً يناوله اياه‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Abdur-Rahman Awf bin Malik al-Ashja'i said: We were with the Messenger of God, nine or eight or seven of us, and he said, 'Will you not pledge allegiance to the Messenger of God?' We had recently pledged, so we said, 'We have already pledged to you, Messenger of God. On what shall we pledge to you?' He said, 'That you worship God and associate nothing with Him, the five prayers, and that you obey,' and he added a word in a low voice: 'and that you do not ask people for anything.' I saw some of that group drop a whip and not ask anyone to hand it to him.

key_terms.لا تسألوا الناس شيئاً (la tas'alu al-nas: do not ask people for anything

situation: Qabisah had taken on a debt to make peace between two parties, and came to the Prophet for help paying it.
wise_response: The Prophet told him to wait until charity came in and he would be given from it. Then he explained that asking is allowed only for three: one who has taken on a debt for others, until it is paid; one whose property has been wiped out by disaster, until he can stand again; and one struck by poverty, if three sensible people of his community confirm it. Beyond that, what is gained by asking is unlawful.
why_it_worked: The community should help those who carry burdens for others or are ruined by misfortune. Asking without real need takes from those who have it.
tempting_wrong_answer: To ask for help without real need, or to refuse help to someone who took on a debt to make peace.

وعن أبي بشر قبيصة بن المخارق رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ تحملت حمالة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أسأله فيها، فقال‏:‏ ‏"‏أقم حتى تأتينا الصدقة فنأمر لك بها‏"‏ ثم قال‏:‏ ‏"‏يا قبيصة إن المسألة لا تحل إلا لأحد ثلاثة‏:‏ رجل تحمل حمالة، فحلت له المسألة حتى يصيبها، ثم يمسك‏.‏ ورجل أصابته جائحة اجتاحت ماله، فحلت له المسألة حتى يصيب قوماً من عيش، أو قال‏:‏ سداداً من عيش، ورجل أصابته فاقة، حتى يقول ثلاثة من ذوى الحجى من قومه‏:‏ لقد أصابت فلاناً فاقة، فحملت له المسألة حتى يصيب قواما من عيش، أو قال‏:‏ سداداً من عيش‏.‏ فما سواهن من المسألة يا قبيصة سحت، يأكلها صاحبها سحتاً‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ 

‏"‏الحمالة‏"‏ بفتح الحاء‏:‏ أن يقع قتال ونحوه بين فريقين، فيصلح إنسان بينهم على مال يتحمله ويلتزمه على نفسه‏.‏ و‏"‏الجائحة‏"‏ ‏:‏ الآفة تصيب مال الإنسان‏.‏ و‏"‏القوام‏"‏ بكسر القاف وفتحها‏:‏ هو ما يقوم به أمر الإنسان من مال ونحوه‏.‏ و‏"‏السداد‏"‏ بكسر السين‏:‏ ما يسد حاجة المعوز ويكفيه، و‏"‏الفاقة‏"‏ ‏:‏ الفقر‏.‏ و‏"‏الحجى‏"‏‏:‏ العقل‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Bishr Qabisah bin al-Mukhariq said: I took on a payment to settle a dispute and came to the Messenger of God to ask him about it. He said, 'Stay until the charity reaches us and we will order it for you.' Then he said, 'Qabisah, asking is lawful only for one of three. A man who has taken on a payment to settle between people; asking is lawful for him until he obtains it, then he stops. A man struck by a disaster that has swept away his property; asking is lawful for him until he obtains enough to live on. And a man struck by poverty, until three people of sound judgment from his people say, So-and-so has been struck by poverty; asking is lawful for him until he obtains enough to live on. Any other asking, Qabisah, is unlawful gain that its owner consumes unlawfully.'

key_terms.حمالة (hamala): a payment taken on to make peace between parties

situation: The Prophet would give Umar a stipend, and Umar would say, 'Give it to someone who needs it more than I do.'
wise_response: The Prophet told him to take what came to him when he had not been craving it or asking for it. He could keep it or give it away in charity. What did not come, he should not chase after. Umar's son Abdullah later never asked anyone for anything and never refused what was given him.
why_it_worked: Refusing a gift can be a show of its own. The sound course was to accept what came unsought, give from it freely, and not let the heart chase what did not come.
tempting_wrong_answer: To crave and chase money, or else make a show of refusing what is rightly given.

translation.ai_translation: Salim bin Abdullah bin Umar reported from his father Abdullah bin Umar, from Umar, who said: The Messenger of God used to give me a stipend, and I would say, 'Give it to someone poorer than me.' situation: The Prophet swore to three truths and then described four kinds of people in the world.
wise_response: He said charity does not lessen wealth, one who bears an injustice patiently is given more honor, and one who opens a door of begging has a door of poverty opened on him. Then he described the person with wealth and knowledge who fears God, keeps ties with kin and honors the rights in it; the one with knowledge but no wealth who sincerely wishes to do the same; the one with wealth but no knowledge who squanders it and neglects his kin; and the one with neither who wishes he could squander like him.
why_it_worked: What one intends with one's means matters as much as the means. Patience under wrong and generosity to kin are honored.
tempting_wrong_answer: To waste wealth heedlessly, cut off one's relatives, and envy those who do the same.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي كبشة عمرو بن سعد الأنمارى رضي الله عنه أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم  يقول‏:‏ ‏"‏ثلاثة أقسم عليهن وأحدثكم حديثاً فاحفظوه‏:‏ ما نقص مال عبد من صدقة،ولا ظلم عبد مظلمة صبر عليها إلا زاده الله عزاً، ولا فتح عبد باب مسألة إلا فتح الله عليه باب فقر، أو كلمة نحوها وأحدثكم حديثاً فاحفظوه قال‏:‏ إنما الدنيا لأربعة نفر‏:‏ 
عبد رزقه الله مالاً وعلماً، فهو يتقى فيه ربه، ويصل فيه رحمه، ويعلم لله فيه حقاً فهذا بأفضل المنازل‏.‏
وعبد رزقه الله علماً، ولم يرزقه مالاً فهو صادق النية يقول‏:‏ لو أن لى مالاً لعملت بعمل فلان، فهو بنيته فأجرهما سواء‏.‏
وعبد رزقه الله مالاً، ولم يرزقه علماً، فهو يخبط فى ماله بغير علم، لا يتقى فيه ربه ولا يصل فيه رحمه، ولا يعلم لله فيه حقاً، فهذا بأخبث المنازل‏.‏
وعبد لم يرزقه الله مالاً ولا علماً، فهو يقول‏:‏ لو أن لى مالاً لعملت فيه بعمل فلان، فهو بنيته، فوزرهما سواء” ‏(‏‏(‏رواه الترمذى وقال‏:‏ حديث حسن صحيح‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Kabshah Amr bin Sa'd al-Anmari heard the Messenger of God say, 'Three things I swear to, and I will tell you something, so remember it. A servant's wealth is not decreased by charity. No servant is wronged and bears it patiently but God increases him in honor. No servant opens a door of asking but God opens a door of poverty on him,' or a word like it. 'And I will tell you something, so remember it. The world is for four kinds of people. A servant whom God has given wealth and knowledge, and he is mindful of his Lord in it, keeps ties with his kin through it, and knows God's right in it; he is in the best station. A servant whom God has given knowledge but not wealth, and he is true in intention and says, If I had wealth I would do as so-and-so does; he has his intention, and their reward is equal. A servant whom God has given wealth but not knowledge, and he flails about in his wealth without knowledge, is not mindful of his Lord in it, does not keep ties with his kin through it, and does not know God's right in it; he is in the worst station. And a servant whom God has given neither wealth nor knowledge, and he says, If I had wealth I would do in it as so-and-so does; he has his intention, and their burden is equal.'

situation: The Prophet compared a generous person and a miser.
wise_response: He said they are like two men wearing iron coats of mail from chest to collarbone. Whenever the generous one gives, his coat spreads out and lengthens until it covers his fingertips and hides his footprints. Whenever the miser means to give, every ring clamps in place, and he tries to loosen it but it will not widen.
why_it_worked: Giving makes a person freer and more at ease. Stinginess tightens around the one who holds it.
tempting_wrong_answer: To clutch what one has, and so grow more cramped and anxious with every chance to give.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم  يقول‏:‏ “مثل البخيل والمنفق، كمثل رجلين عليهما جنتان من حديد من ثديهما إلى ترا قيهما، فأما المنفق، فلا ينفق إلا سبغت، أو وفرت على جلده حتى تخفى بنانه، وتعفو أثره، وأما البخيل، فلا يريد أن ينفق شيئاً إلا لزقت كل حلقةْ مكانها، فهو يوسعها فلا تتسع” ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏ 

و”الجنة” الدرع، ومعناه‏:‏ أن المنفق كلما أنفق سبغت، وطالت حتى تجر وارءه، وتخفى رجليه وأثر مشيه وخطواته‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayrah heard the Messenger of God say, 'The likeness of the miser and the one who spends is that of two men wearing coats of iron from their chests to their collarbones. As for the spender, he does not spend but that it spreads and covers his skin until it hides his fingertips and wipes out his tracks. As for the miser, he does not want to spend anything but every ring sticks in its place, and he tries to widen it and it does not widen.'

situation: A traveler heard a voice in a cloud say, 'Water the garden of so-and-so.' He followed the water to a man working his garden, and asked him what he did with it to deserve this.
wise_response: The owner said he looked at what the garden produced, gave a third in charity, ate a third with his family, and put a third back into the garden.
why_it_worked: He gave, provided for his family, and reinvested, all in measure. Steady, balanced use of what he had was blessed.
tempting_wrong_answer: To consume everything oneself, or to neglect the source that feeds the family and the poor alike.

translation.original_text:
وعنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم  قال‏:‏ “بينما رجل يمشى بفلاة من الأرض، فسمع صوتاً فى سحابة‏:‏ إسق حديقة فلان، فتنحى ذلك السحاب فأفرغ ماءه فى حرة، فإذا شرجة من تلك الشراح قد استوعبت ذلك الماء كله، فتتبع الماء، فإذا رجل قائم فى حديقته يحول الماء بمسحاته، فقال له‏:‏ يا عبد الله ما اسمك ، قال‏:‏ فلان للاسم الذى سمع فى السحابة، فقال له‏:‏ يا عبد الله لم تسألني عن اسمي ‏؟‏ فقال‏:‏ إنى سمعت صوتاً فى السحاب الذى هذا ماؤه يقول‏:‏ اسق حديقة فلان لإسمك، فما تصنع فيها‏؟‏ فقال‏:‏ أما إذا قلت هذا فإنى أنظر إلى ما يخرج منها، فأتصدق بثلثه، وآكل أنا وعيالى ثلثاً، وأرد فيها ثلثه ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏ 

“الحرة” الأرض الملبسة حجارة سوداء‏.‏ “والشرجة” بفتح الشين المعجمة وإسكان الراء وبالجيم‏:‏ هى مسيل الماء‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet said, 'While a man was walking in a barren land, he heard a voice in a cloud: Water the garden of so-and-so. That cloud moved aside and emptied its water onto stony ground, and one of the channels there took up all that water. He followed the water and found a man standing in his garden turning the water with his spade. He said to him, Servant of God, what is your name? He said, So-and-so, the name he had heard in the cloud. He said to him, Servant of God, why do you ask my name? He said, I heard a voice in the cloud whose water this is say, Water the garden of so-and-so, with your name. What do you do with it? He said, Since you say this, I look at what comes out of it, give a third of it in charity, eat a third with my family, and put a third back into it.'

key_terms.أتصدق بثلثه (atasaddaqu bi-thuluthihi): I give a third of it in charity

situation: People are tempted to wrong others and to hold tight to what they have.
wise_response: The Prophet said, 'Beware of oppression, for oppression will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection. And beware of greedy stinginess, for it destroyed those before you. It drove them to shed one another's blood and treat what was sacred as lawful.'
why_it_worked: Wronging others and grasping greed feed each other. Greed has led whole peoples to violence and to break every limit.
tempting_wrong_answer: To grab and hoard, and to trample others to get more.

translation.original_text: وعن جابر رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ اتقوا الظلم فإن الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة واتقوا الشح فإن الشح أهلك من كان قبلكم حملهم على أن سفكوا دماءهم واستحلوا محارمهم” ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Jabir reported that the Messenger of God said, 'Beware of injustice, for injustice is darkness upon darkness on the Day of Resurrection. situation: A starving man came to the Prophet. Each of his wives sent word that she had nothing but water. The Prophet asked who would host the man for the night. A man of the Ansar took him home, but his wife had only enough food for their children.
wise_response: The Ansari told her to soothe the children and put them to sleep, then put out the lamp when the guest came in, so he would think they were eating with him. The guest ate, and the couple went to bed hungry. In the morning the Prophet told him, 'God marveled at what you two did with your guest last night.'
why_it_worked: They gave a stranger their own supper and hid it so he would not feel ashamed to eat.
tempting_wrong_answer: To turn the hungry stranger away because there is barely enough at home, or to feed him in a way that makes him feel he is taking their food.

translation.original_text:
وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال‏:‏ إنى مجهود، فأرسل إلى بعض نسائه، فقالت‏:‏ والذى بعثك بالحق ما عندى إلا ماء، ثم أرسل إلى أخرى، فقالت مثل ذلك، حتى قلن كلهن مثل ذلك‏:‏ لا والذى بعثك بالحق ما عندى إلا ماء‏.‏ فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم “ من يضيفه هذا الليلة‏؟‏” فقال رجل من الأنصار‏:‏ أنا يا رسول الله، فانطلق به إلى رحله ، فقال لامرأته‏:‏ أكرمي ضيف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم  
وفى رواية قال لامرأته ‏:‏ هل عندك شئ‏؟‏ قالت‏:‏ لا، إلا قوت صبيانى‏.‏ قال‏:‏ فعلليهن بشئ‏.‏وإذا أرادوا العشاء فنوميهم‏.‏ وإذا دخل ضيفنا فأطفئ السراج وأريه أنا نأكل، فقعدوا وأكل الضيف وبات طاويين، فلما أصبح ، غدا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال‏:‏ “لقد عجب الله من صنيعكما بضيفكما الليلة” ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayrah said: A man came to the Prophet and said, 'I am worn out with hunger.' He sent to one of his wives, and she said, 'By Him who sent you with the truth, I have nothing but water.' Then he sent to another, and she said the same, until all of them said the same: 'No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I have nothing but water.' The Prophet said, 'Who will host this man tonight?' A man of the Ansar said, 'I will, Messenger of God.' He took him to his home and said to his wife, 'Honor the guest of the Messenger of God.' In another version he said to his wife, 'Do you have anything?' She said, 'No, only my children's food.' He said, 'Distract them with something, and when they want supper, put them to sleep. When our guest comes in, put out the lamp and let him think we are eating.' They sat, the guest ate, and they spent the night hungry. In the morning he went to the Prophet, who said, 'God marveled at what you two did with your guest tonight.'

key_terms.باتا طاويين (bata tawiyayn): the two spent the night hungry

situation: A household with food for two hesitates to invite a third person to the table.
wise_response: The Prophet said, 'Food for two is enough for three, and food for three is enough for four.' In another version: food for one is enough for two, food for two enough for four, and food for four enough for eight.
why_it_worked: There is almost always room for one more when people share. Fear of running short is usually larger than the real shortage.
tempting_wrong_answer: To keep a guest away because the meal was planned for fewer.

"‏ طعام الاثنين كافي الثلاثة، وطعام الثلاثة كافي الأربعة‏"‏ ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏ 

وفى رواية لمسلم عن جابر رضي الله عنه ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ طعام الواحد يكفي الاثنين وطعام الاثنين يكفي الأربعة، وطعام الأربعة يكفي الثمانية‏.‏

situation: On a journey, a man rode up and kept looking right and left, plainly in need.
wise_response: The Prophet said, 'Whoever has a spare mount, let him offer it to one who has none. Whoever has spare provisions, let him offer them to one who has none.' He went on through kinds of property until the companions felt none of them had any right to a surplus.
why_it_worked: On the road, what one does not need belongs to the one who needs it. The Prophet saw the man's need before he had to ask.
tempting_wrong_answer: To ride past a stranded traveler while keeping a spare mount and spare food.

translation.original_text: عن أبي سعيد الخدرى قال‏:‏ بينما نحن فى سفر مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ جاء رجل على راحلة له ، فجعل يصرف بصره يمينا وشمالاً فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏:‏” من كان معه فضل ظهر فليعد به على من لا ظهر له، ومن كان له فضل من زاد فليعد به على من لا زاد له” فذكر من أصناف المال ما ذكر حتى رأينا أنه لا حق لأحد منا فى فضل‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏

He mentioned kinds of wealth until we thought none of us had any right to a surplus.

situation: A woman wove a cloak for the Prophet, and he wore it because he needed it. A man saw it and asked him for it. The Prophet went home, folded it and sent it to him. The others scolded the man for asking for something the Prophet needed, knowing he never refused anyone.
wise_response: The Prophet gave the cloak he needed without hesitation. The man explained he had not asked in order to wear it but so it could be his burial shroud, and it was.
why_it_worked: The Prophet's generosity did not wait for his own need to be met. The man's request, which looked selfish, came from a sincere wish.
tempting_wrong_answer: To refuse a request because one needs the thing oneself, or to judge the asker before knowing why he asked.

translation.original_text: وعن سهل بن سعد رضي الله عنه، أن امرأة جاءت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ببردة منسوجة فقالت‏:‏ نسجتها لأكسوكها، فأخذها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم محتاجاً إليها ، فخرج إلينا وإنها إزاره، فقال فلان، اكسونيها ما أحسنها‏!‏ فقال‏:‏” نعم” فجلس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فى المجلس ثم رجع فطواها ثم أرسل به إليه‏:‏ فقال له القوم‏:‏ ما أحسنت‏!‏ لبسها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم  محتاجاً إليها ثم سألته وعلمت أنه لا يرد سائلاً ، فقال‏:‏ إنى والله ما سألته لألبسها وإنما سألته لتكون كفني، قال سهل‏:‏ فكانت كفنه‏.‏ ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏
translation.ai_translation: Sahl bin Sa'd said that a woman brought the Messenger of God a woven cloak and said, 'I wove it to clothe you with it.' The Prophet took it, being in need of it, and came out to us wearing it as his waist-wrap. A man said, 'Clothe me with it. How beautiful it is!' He said, 'Yes.' The Prophet sat in the gathering, then went back, folded it and sent it to him. The people said to him, 'You did not do well. The Prophet wore it needing it, then you asked him for it, knowing that he never turns away one who asks.' He said, 'By God, I did not ask him for it to wear it. I asked for it so that it would be my shroud.' Sahl said: And it was his shroud.

situation: The Ash'ari tribe would sometimes run short of food, on campaign or at home in Medina.
wise_response: The Prophet said that when this happened they gathered everything they had on one cloth and divided it equally among themselves in one vessel. 'They are of me and I am of them.'
why_it_worked: In hard times they shared out what they had equally, so no one went hungry while another had plenty.
tempting_wrong_answer: For each family to guard its own food when supplies run low.

situation: The Prophet was given a drink. A boy sat on his right, who by custom had the right to drink next, and elderly men sat on his left.
wise_response: The Prophet asked the boy, 'Will you allow me to give it to these men?' The boy said, 'No, by God, Messenger of God. I will not give up my share from you to anyone.' The Prophet placed the cup in the boy's hand.
why_it_worked: The Prophet honored the elders by asking, but he did not override the boy's right. When the boy declined, he respected it.
tempting_wrong_answer: To pass over a young person's rightful turn without asking, simply because others are older and more important.

situation: A person struck by illness or hardship wishes they were dead.
wise_response: The Prophet said no one should wish for death because of a harm that has struck him. If he must, let him say, 'O God, keep me alive as long as life is better for me, and take me when death is better for me.'
why_it_worked: Hardship passes, and life still holds good to be done. Leaving the outcome to God keeps despair from deciding.
tempting_wrong_answer: To give in to despair in a hard time and wish for one's own death.

translation.original_text: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه قال‏:‏ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ “لا يتمنين أحدكم الموت لضر أصابه فإن كان لابد فاعلاً، فليقل‏:‏ اللهم أحينى ما كانت الحياة خيراً لى، وتوفنى إذا كانت الوفاة خيراً لى” ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Anas said: The Messenger of God said, 'Let none of you wish for death because of a harm that has befallen him. If he must do so, let him say: O God, keep me alive as long as life is good for me, and take me when death is good for me.'

situation: Some things are clearly allowed, some clearly forbidden, and between them lie doubtful matters most people cannot judge.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever avoids the doubtful keeps his religion and honor clean. Whoever falls into it falls into the forbidden, like a shepherd grazing near a fenced pasture who soon strays in. He added that the heart is the piece of flesh that sets the whole body right or wrong.
why_it_worked: Keeping a margin from wrong protects a person from drifting into it. Conduct follows the state of the heart.
tempting_wrong_answer: Living right at the edge of what is allowed and telling oneself it is fine.

translation.original_text: وعن النعمان بن بشير رضي الله عنهما قال‏:‏ سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول‏:‏ “إن الحلال بين، وإن الحرام بين، وبينهما مشتبهات لا يعلمهن كثير من الناس، فمن اتقى الشبهات، استبرأ لدينه وعرضه، ومن وقع فى الشبهات، وقع فى الحرام، كالراعى يرعى حول الحمى يوشك أن يرتع فيه ألا وإن لكل ملك حمى، ألا وإن حمى الله محارمه، ألا وإن فى الجسد مضغة إذا صلحت صلح الجسد كله، وإذا فسدت فسد الجسد كله‏:‏ ألا وهى القلب” ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏.‏ وروياه من طرق بألفاظ متقاربة‏)‏‏)‏
translation.ai_translation: What is lawful is clear and what is forbidden is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know. Whoever guards against the doubtful matters has kept his religion and his honor free of blame. Whoever falls into the doubtful matters falls into the forbidden, like a shepherd grazing around a protected pasture who is about to graze in it. Every king has a protected pasture, and the protected pasture of Allah is what He has forbidden. In the body there is a lump of flesh: if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. It is the heart.

translation.ai_translation: Righteousness is good character, and sin is what stirs uneasily in your soul and you dislike that people should come to know of it.

situation: Abu Bakr ate food his servant brought. The servant then told him it was payment for fortune-telling he had once faked to deceive a man.
wise_response: Abu Bakr put his hand in his mouth and vomited up everything in his stomach.
why_it_worked: He would not keep in his body anything gained by deception, even when he had eaten it unknowingly.
tempting_wrong_answer: Shrugging and keeping what was gained dishonestly since it is already done.

translation.original_text: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت‏:‏ كان لأبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه غلام يخرج له الخراج وكان أبو بكر يأكل من خراجه فجاء يوماً بشئ، فأكل منه أبو بكر، فقال له الغلام‏:‏ تدرى ما هذا‏؟‏ فقال أبو بكر‏:‏ ما هو‏؟‏ قال‏:‏ كنت تكهنت لإنسان فى الجاهلية وما أحسن الكهانة إلا أني خدعته فلقيني، فأعطاني بذلك هذا الذى أكلت منه، فأدخل أبو بكر يده فقاء كل شئ فى بطنه” ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq had a servant who paid him a share of his earnings, and Abu Bakr ate from it. One day he brought something and Abu Bakr ate some of it. The servant said, "Do you know what this is?" Abu Bakr said, "What is it?" He said, "In the time of ignorance I told a man's fortune, though I was not good at fortune-telling. I just deceived him. He met me and gave me this for it, which is what you ate." Abu Bakr put his hand in and vomited up everything in his stomach.

situation: 'Umar set stipends of four thousand for each of the first emigrants, but only three thousand five hundred for his own son. People objected that his son was also an emigrant.
wise_response: 'Umar said his son had emigrated because his father took him, and was not like one who emigrated by his own choice.
why_it_worked: A leader must be strict with his own family so no one can say he favored them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving one's own children the top rate because one holds the purse.

translation.original_text: وعن نافع أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه كان فرض للمهاجرين الأولين أربعة آلاف وفرض لابنه ثلاثة آلاف وخمسمائة، فقيل له‏:‏ هو من المهاجرين فلم نقصته‏؟‏ فقال‏:‏ إنما هاجر به أبوه، يقول‏:‏ ليس هو كمن هاجر بنفسه” ‏(‏‏(‏رواه البخاري‏)‏‏)‏
translation.ai_translation: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab fixed four thousand for each of the first emigrants and fixed three thousand five hundred for his son. It was said to him, "He is one of the emigrants. Why did you give him less?" He said, "His father emigrated with him." He meant: he is not like one who emigrated by himself.

tempting_wrong_answer: Dominating conversations with showy talk to prove oneself above others.
