translation.original_text: وعنها أن قريشاً أهمهم شأن المرأة المخزومية التى سرقت فقالوا‏:‏ من يكلم فيها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏؟‏ فقالوا‏:‏ من يجترئ عليه إلا أسامة بن زيد حب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏؟‏ فكلمة أسامة، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ “أتشفع في حد من حدود الله تعالى‏؟‏‏!‏” ثم قام فاختطب ثم قال‏:‏ “إنما أهلك من قبلكم أنهم كانوا إذا سرق فيهم الشريف تركوه، وإذا سرق فيهم الضعيف أقاموا عليه الحد‏!‏ وايم الله، لو أن فاطمة بنت محمد سرقت لقطعت يدها” ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏ ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Quraysh were troubled by the matter of the Makhzumi woman who had stolen. They said, "Who will speak to the Messenger of Allah about her?" They said, "Who would dare but Usama ibn Zayd, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah?" Usama spoke to him, and the Messenger of Allah said, "Do you intercede concerning one of the set penalties of Allah the Exalted?" Then he stood and addressed the people and said, "Those before you were destroyed only because when a noble among them stole they let him be, and when a weak one among them stole they carried out the penalty on him. By Allah, if Fatima the daughter of Muhammad stole, I would cut off her hand."

situation: People hold different roles: ruler, husband, wife, servant.
wise_response: The Prophet said each of you is a shepherd and each is responsible for his flock: the ruler for his people, the man for his family, the woman for her husband's home, the servant for his master's property.
why_it_worked: Everyone has some trust in his care and will answer for it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking responsibility belongs only to those at the top.

translation.original_text: وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال‏:‏ سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول‏:‏ “كلكم راع، وكلكم مسئول عن رعيته‏:‏ الإمام راع ومسؤول عن رعيته، والرجل راع في أهله ومسؤول عن رعيته، والمرأة راعية في بيت زوجها ومسؤولة عن رعيتها، والخادم راع في مال سيده ومسؤول عن رعيته وكلكم راع ومسؤول عن رعيته” ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏
translation.ai_translation: Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock. The leader is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock. A man is a shepherd over his family and is responsible for his flock. A woman is a shepherd in her husband's house and is responsible for her flock. A servant is a shepherd over his master's property and is responsible for his flock. Each of you is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock.

wise_response: The Prophet said any servant whom Allah puts in charge of people and who dies cheating them, Allah forbids the Garden to him. In another wording, one who does not care for them sincerely will not smell the Garden.
why_it_worked: Authority is a trust held for the people under it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Using power for oneself and deceiving those one leads.

translation.original_text:

translation.ai_translation: There is no servant whom Allah puts in charge of a flock, who dies on the day he dies while cheating his flock, but Allah forbids the Garden to him. situation: People wonder which deeds are most precious.
wise_response: The Prophet named seven whom Allah shades on the Day when there is no shade but His. Among them are a just ruler, a man tempted by a woman of rank and beauty who says "I fear Allah," and a man who gives charity so secretly his left hand does not know what his right gave.
why_it_worked: Justice in power, chastity under temptation, and giving without show are deeds done for their own sake.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving charity for praise, and yielding to temptation when it comes with status.

translation.original_text: وعن أبى هريرة رضي الله عنه، عن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم قال‏:‏ “سبعة يظلهم الله في ظله يوم لا ظل إلا ظله‏:‏ إمام عادل، وشاب نشأ في عبادة الله تعالى، ورجل قلبه معلق بالمساجد، ورجلان تحابا في الله اجتمعا عليه وتفرقا عليه، ورجل دعته امرأة ذات منصب وجمال، فقال‏:‏ إنى أخاف الله، ورجل تصدق بصدقة فأخفاها حتى لا تعلم شماله ما تنفق يمينه، ورجل ذكر الله خالياً ففاضت عيناه” ‏(‏‏(‏متفق عليه‏)‏‏)‏
translation.ai_translation: Seven Allah will shade in His shade on the day when there is no shade but His: a just leader; a young man who grew up in the worship of Allah; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two men who love each other for Allah, meeting for that and parting for that; a man called by a woman of rank and beauty who says, "I fear Allah"; a man who gives charity and hides it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand spends; and a man who remembered Allah in solitude and his eyes overflowed.

situation: On a journey the Prophet gathered his companions and warned of hard trials to come.
wise_response: He said whoever wants to be kept from the Fire and enter the Garden should die believing in Allah and the Last Day, "and let him treat people as he would love to be treated."
why_it_worked: Treating others the way you want to be treated is set beside faith itself as the way through trials.
tempting_wrong_answer: Demanding fair treatment for oneself while dealing unfairly with others.

translation.original_text:
وعن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما قال‏:‏ كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم  في سفر، فنزلنا منزلاً، فمنا من يصلح خباءه، ومنا من ينتضل، ومنا من هو في جشره، إذ نادى منادي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم  الصلاة جامعة‏.‏ فاجتمعنا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم  فقال‏:‏ “إنه لم يكن نبي قبلي إلا كان حقاً عليه أن يدل أمته على خير ما يعلمه لهم، وينذرهم شر ما يعلمه لهم، وإن أمتكم هذه جعل عاقبتها في أولها، وسيصيب آخرها بلاء وأمور تنكرونها، وتجئ فتن يرقق بعضها بعضاً، وتجئ الفتنة فيقول المؤمن ‏:‏ هذه مهلكتي، ثم تنكشف؛ وتجئ الفتنة فيقول المؤمن‏:‏ هذه هذه، فمن أحب أن يزحزح عن النار، ويدخل الجنة، فلتأته منيته وهو يؤمن بالله واليوم الأخر، وليأت إلى الناس الذى يحب أن يؤتى إليه‏.‏ 

ومن بايع إماماً فأعطاه صفقة يده، وثمرة قلبه، فليطعه إن استطاع، فإن جاء آخر ينازعه، فاضربوا عنق الآخر” ‏(‏‏(‏رواه مسلم‏)‏‏)‏‏.‏‏.‏

قوله‏:‏ “ينتضل” أى ‏:‏ يسابق بالرمي بالنبل والنشاب‏.‏ “والجشر” بفتح الجيم والشين المعجمة وبالراء‏:‏ وهى الدواب التى ترعى وتبيت مكانها‏.‏ وقوله‏:‏ “يرقق بعضها بعضاً” أى‏:‏ يصير بعضها بعضا رقيقاً، أى ‏:‏خفيفاً لعظم ما بعده، فالثانى يرقق الأول‏.‏ وقيل‏:‏ معناه، يشوق بعضها إلى بعض بتحسينها وتسويليها، وقيل‏:‏ يشبه بعضها بعضاً‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: We were with the Messenger of Allah on a journey and stopped at a place. Some of us were fixing our tents, some competing at archery, some with their grazing animals, when the Messenger of Allah's caller called: Prayer in congregation. We gathered to the Messenger of Allah and he said, "There was no prophet before me but it was his duty to guide his people to the best he knew for them and warn them of the worst he knew for them. This community of yours has had its well-being placed in its beginning, and its last part will be struck by trials and things you will reject. Trials will come, each making the one before it seem light. A trial will come and the believer will say: This will be my ruin. Then it will clear. Then a trial will come and the believer will say: This is it, this is it. Whoever loves to be moved away from the Fire and brought into the Garden, let his death come to him while he believes in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people the way he would love to be treated. Whoever pledges allegiance to a leader, giving him the clasp of his hand and the fruit of his heart, let him obey him if he can. If another comes to dispute with him, strike the neck of the other."

wise_response: When asked what to do, he said: "Give the right that is owed by you, and ask Allah for what is owed to you."

translation.ai_translation: "After me there will be favoritism and things you will reject." They said, "Messenger of Allah, what do you command those of us who live to see that?" He said, "Fulfill the right that is upon you, and ask Allah for what is yours."

situation: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Samura might seek a position of authority, or might swear an oath and then see something better to do.
wise_response: The Prophet told him not to ask for authority: given unasked, he would be helped in it; given because he asked, he would be left to it alone. If he swore an oath and saw something better, he should do the better thing and make expiation for the oath.
why_it_worked: Chasing power is a sign one should not hold it. An oath should not lock a person into the worse course.
tempting_wrong_answer: Campaigning for office, or holding to a bad oath out of stubbornness.

translation.ai_translation: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Samura, do not ask for leadership. If you are given it without asking, you will be helped with it. tempting_wrong_answer: Surrounding oneself with yes-men who stay quiet when the leader errs.

translation.ai_translation: When Allah wants good for a leader, He gives him a truthful minister who reminds him if he forgets and helps him if he remembers. When He wants otherwise for him, He gives him a bad minister who does not remind him if he forgets and does not help him if he remembers.

situation: Someone has food or a gift to share and several neighbours. They must decide who to give to first.
wise_response: Abu Hurayra said not to begin with the farther neighbour before the nearer one. Start with the nearest and work outward.
why_it_worked: The neighbour closest to your door sees your life and shares its burdens most. Their claim on your kindness comes first.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving to distant people you want to impress while the family next door goes without.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا عِكْرِمَةُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَلْقَمَةُ بْنُ بَجَالَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ وَلاَ يَبْدَأُ بِجَارِهِ الأَقْصَى قَبْلَ الأَدْنَى، وَلَكِنْ يَبْدَأُ بِالأَدْنَى قَبْلَ الأَقْصَى‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: He should not begin with his farther neighbour before the nearer one. Rather, he begins with the nearer before the farther.

situation: Ibn Umar saw people come to love their money more than their brothers. He recalled what the Prophet said about neighbours who shut others out.
wise_response: He reported the Prophet's words: on the Day of Resurrection many a neighbour will cling to his neighbour and say, "Lord, this man shut his door on me and held back his kindness."
why_it_worked: Ordinary kindness to a neighbour is owed. Withholding it is a wrong the neighbour can bring as a complaint.
tempting_wrong_answer: Closing the door and keeping one's money and help to oneself.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مَالِكُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ السَّلاَمِ، عَنْ لَيْثٍ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ‏:‏ لَقَدْ أَتَى عَلَيْنَا زَمَانٌ، أَوْ قَالَ‏:‏ حِينٌ، وَمَا أَحَدٌ أَحَقُّ بِدِينَارِهِ وَدِرْهَمِهِ مِنْ أَخِيهِ الْمُسْلِمِ، ثُمَّ الْآنَ الدِّينَارُ وَالدِّرْهَمُ أَحَبُّ إِلَى أَحَدِنَا مِنْ أَخِيهِ الْمُسْلِمِ، سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ كَمْ مِنْ جَارٍ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِجَارِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَقُولُ‏:‏ يَا رَبِّ، هَذَا أَغْلَقَ بَابَهُ دُونِي، فَمَنَعَ مَعْرُوفَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A time came upon us, or he said a period, when no one thought himself more entitled to his dinar and his dirham than his Muslim brother. Now the dinar and the dirham are dearer to one of us than his Muslim brother. I heard the Prophet, peace be upon him, say: How many a neighbour will hold on to his neighbour on the Day of Resurrection, saying: My Lord, this man shut his door against me and withheld his kindness.

situation: A person has plenty to eat while the family next door is hungry.
wise_response: The Prophet said the believer is not one who eats his fill while his neighbour goes hungry.
why_it_worked: Faith shows in how you treat those near you. A full stomach beside a hungry neighbour proves it is missing.
tempting_wrong_answer: Eating well and ignoring the hunger next door because it is not your problem.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ كَثِيرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ أَبِي بَشِيرٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ الْمُسَاوِرِ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ يُخْبِرُ ابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ يَقُولُ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ لَيْسَ الْمُؤْمِنُ الَّذِي يَشْبَعُ وَجَارُهُ جَائِعٌ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The believer is not the one who eats his fill while his neighbour is hungry.

situation: Abu Dharr had little to spare. The Prophet gave him three pieces of advice, one about everyday cooking.
wise_response: He told him: when you make a stew, add plenty of water, then look to a household among your neighbours and give them a fair share of it.
why_it_worked: Even a small pot can be stretched to feed others. Generosity does not wait for wealth.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking you have too little to share and keeping the whole pot for yourself.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ أَبِي عِمْرَانَ الْجَوْنِيِّ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ الصَّامِتِ، عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ قَالَ‏:‏ أَوْصَانِي خَلِيلِي صلى الله عليه وسلم بِثَلاَثٍ‏:‏ أَسْمَعُ وَأُطِيعُ وَلَوْ لِعَبْدٍ مُجَدَّعِ الأَطْرَافِ، وَإِذَا صَنَعْتَ مَرَقَةً فَأَكْثِرْ مَاءَهَا، ثُمَّ انْظُرْ أَهْلَ بَيْتٍ مِنْ جِيرَانِكَ، فَأَصِبْهُمْ مِنْهُ بِمَعْرُوفٍ، وَصَلِّ الصَّلاَةَ لِوَقْتِهَا، فَإِنْ وَجَدْتَ الإِمَامَ قَدْ صَلَّى، فَقَدْ أَحْرَزْتَ صَلاَتَكَ، وَإِلاَّ فَهِيَ نَافِلَةٌ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: My dear friend, peace be upon him, charged me with three things: listen and obey, even if it is to a slave with maimed limbs. When you make a broth, put plenty of water in it, then look for a household among your neighbours and give them some of it in kindness. And pray the prayer at its time. If you find the imam has already prayed, you have safeguarded your prayer, and if not, it is a voluntary prayer.

situation: People wonder what makes someone a good friend or a good neighbour.
wise_response: The Prophet said the best of companions with God is the one who is best to his companion, and the best of neighbours is the one who is best to his neighbour.
why_it_worked: Goodness is measured by how you treat the person beside you, not by status or private piety.
tempting_wrong_answer: Seeking a good name through public deeds while being careless with the people closest to you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَيْوَةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا شُرَحْبِيلُ بْنُ شَرِيكٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ الْحُبُلِيَّ يُحَدِّثُ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، عَنْ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ‏:‏ خَيْرُ الأَصْحَابِ عِنْدَ اللهِ تَعَالَى خَيْرُهُمْ لِصَاحِبِهِ، وَخَيْرُ الْجِيرَانِ عِنْدَ اللهِ تَعَالَى خَيْرُهُمْ لِجَارِهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The best of companions in the sight of God the Exalted is the best of them to his companion, and the best of neighbours in the sight of God the Exalted is the best of them to his neighbour.

situation: The Prophet was told of a woman who prayed at night, fasted by day and gave charity, but hurt her neighbours with her tongue. Another woman did only the required prayers, gave small bits of curd, and harmed no one.
wise_response: He said there was no good in the first woman and she was among the people of the Fire. He said the second was among the people of the Garden.
why_it_worked: Devotion does not cancel harm done to people. A modest life that hurts no one ranks above showy worship joined to a cruel tongue.
tempting_wrong_answer: Piling up acts of worship while insulting and wounding the people next door.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَاحِدِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو يَحْيَى مَوْلَى جَعْدَةَ بْنِ هُبَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ يَقُولُ‏:‏ قِيلَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، إِنَّ فُلاَنَةً تَقُومُ اللَّيْلَ وَتَصُومُ النَّهَارَ، وَتَفْعَلُ، وَتَصَّدَّقُ، وَتُؤْذِي جِيرَانَهَا بِلِسَانِهَا‏؟‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ لاَ خَيْرَ فِيهَا، هِيَ مِنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ، قَالُوا‏:‏ وَفُلاَنَةٌ تُصَلِّي الْمَكْتُوبَةَ، وَتَصَّدَّقُ بِأَثْوَارٍ، وَلاَ تُؤْذِي أَحَدًا‏؟‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ هِيَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: It was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him: Messenger of God, a certain woman stands in prayer at night, fasts by day, does good and gives charity, but she hurts her neighbours with her tongue. The Messenger of God said: There is no good in her. She is among the people of the Fire. They said: And a certain woman prays the obligatory prayers, gives pieces of dried curd in charity, and hurts no one. The Messenger of God said: She is among the people of the Garden.

situation: A'isha had baked a barley loaf for the Prophet. While he slept, a neighbour's pet sheep walked in, took the loaf and ran off, and she chased it to the door.
wise_response: The Prophet said, "Take what you can save of your loaf, and do not hurt your neighbour over his sheep."
why_it_worked: A small loss is not worth harming a neighbour's property or the peace between households.
tempting_wrong_answer: Striking or injuring the neighbour's animal to get even for the stolen bread.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ زِيَادٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي عُمَارَةُ بْنُ غُرَابٍ، أَنَّ عَمَّةً لَهُ حَدَّثَتْهُ، أَنَّهَا سَأَلَتْ عَائِشَةَ أُمَّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا، فَقَالَتْ‏:‏ إِنَّ زَوْجَ إِحْدَانَا يُرِيدُهَا فَتَمْنَعُهُ نَفْسَهَا، إِمَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ غَضَبَى أَوْ لَمْ تَكُنْ نَشِيطَةً، فَهَلْ عَلَيْنَا فِي ذَلِكَ مِنْ حَرَجٍ‏؟‏ قَالَتْ‏:‏ نَعَمْ، إِنَّ مِنْ حَقِّهِ عَلَيْكِ أَنْ لَوْ أَرَادَكِ وَأَنْتِ عَلَى قَتَبٍ لَمْ تَمْنَعِيهِ، قَالَتْ‏:‏ قُلْتُ لَهَا‏:‏ إِحْدَانَا تَحِيضُ، وَلَيْسَ لَهَا وَلِزَوْجِهَا إِلاَّ فِرَاشٌ وَاحِدٌ أَوْ لِحَافٌ وَاحِدٌ، فَكَيْفَ تَصْنَعُ‏؟‏ قَالَتْ‏:‏ لِتَشُدَّ عَلَيْهَا إِزَارَهَا ثُمَّ تَنَامُ مَعَهُ، فَلَهُ مَا فَوْقَ ذَلِكَ، مَعَ أَنِّي سَوْفَ أُخْبِرُكِ مَا صَنَعَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ إِنَّهُ كَانَ لَيْلَتِي مِنْهُ، فَطَحَنْتُ شَيْئًا مِنْ شَعِيرٍ، فَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ قُرْصًا، فَدَخَلَ فَرَدَّ الْبَابَ، وَدَخَلَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ، وَكَانَ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَنَامَ أَغْلَقَ الْبَابَ، وَأَوْكَأَ الْقِرْبَةَ، وَأَكْفَأَ الْقَدَحَ، وَأطْفَأَ الْمِصْبَاحَ، فَانْتَظَرْتُهُ أَنْ يَنْصَرِفَ فَأُطْعِمُهُ الْقُرْصَ، فَلَمْ يَنْصَرِفْ، حَتَّى غَلَبَنِي النَّوْمُ، وَأَوْجَعَهُ الْبَرْدُ، فَأَتَانِي فَأَقَامَنِي ثُمَّ قَالَ‏:‏ أَدْفِئِينِي أَدْفِئِينِي، فَقُلْتُ لَهُ‏:‏ إِنِّي حَائِضٌ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ وَإِنْ، اكْشِفِي عَنْ فَخِذَيْكِ، فَكَشَفْتُ لَهُ عَنْ فَخِذَيَّ، فَوَضَعَ خَدَّهُ وَرَأْسَهُ عَلَى فَخِذَيَّ حَتَّى دَفِئَ‏.‏ فَأَقْبَلَتْ شَاةٌ لِجَارِنَا دَاجِنَةٌ فَدَخَلَتْ، ثُمَّ عَمَدَتْ إِلَى الْقُرْصِ فَأَخَذَتْهُ، ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَتْ بِهِ‏.‏ قَالَتْ‏:‏ وَقَلِقْتُ عَنْهُ، وَاسْتَيْقَظَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَبَادَرْتُهَا إِلَى الْبَابِ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ خُذِي مَا أَدْرَكْتِ مِنْ قُرْصِكِ، وَلاَ تُؤْذِي جَارَكِ فِي شَاتِهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: His aunt told him that she asked A'isha, Mother of the Believers: When the husband of one of us wants her and she refuses herself to him, because she is angry or not in the mood, is there any wrong in that for us? She said: Yes. Part of his right over you is that if he wanted you while you were on a camel saddle, you would not refuse him. She said: I said to her: One of us menstruates, and she and her husband have only one bed or one cover. What should she do? She said: Let her tie her wrapper firmly and then sleep beside him; he has what is above that. And I will tell you what the Prophet, peace be upon him, did. It was my night with him. I ground some barley and made him a round loaf. He came in, pushed the door to, and went into the mosque. When he wanted to sleep he would shut the door, tie up the waterskin, turn the cup over and put out the lamp. I waited for him to come back so I could feed him the loaf, but he did not come until sleep overcame me. The cold pained him, and he came and woke me and said: Warm me, warm me. I said: I am menstruating. He said: Even so. Uncover your thighs. So I uncovered my thighs and he laid his cheek and head on them until he was warm. Then a tame sheep belonging to our neighbour came in, went for the loaf, took it and made off with it. I was troubled by it, and the Prophet woke, and I raced the sheep to the door. The Prophet said: Take what you can save of your loaf, and do not hurt your neighbour over his sheep.

situation: A person's neighbours live in fear of what he might do to them.
wise_response: The Prophet said that one whose neighbour is not safe from his harm will not enter the Garden.
why_it_worked: Neighbours should be able to rest easy beside you. Making them afraid is a serious wrong.
tempting_wrong_answer: Bullying, cheating or threatening the people next door because they cannot easily move away.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ أَبُو الرَّبِيعِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الْعَلاَءُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ مَنْ لاَ يَأْمَنُ جَارُهُ بَوَائِقَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: He will not enter the Garden whose neighbour is not safe from his harms.

situation: A woman has only something small and poor to give her neighbour, or receives such a gift.
wise_response: The Prophet told the women not to look down on a gift between neighbours, even a burnt sheep's trotter.
why_it_worked: Small gifts keep neighbours bound together. Scorning them, given or received, cuts the bond.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving nothing because the gift seems too poor, or sneering at a humble gift.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبِي أُوَيْسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ مُعَاذٍ الأَشْهَلِيِّ، عَنْ جَدَّتِهِ، أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ‏:‏ قَالَ لِي رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ يَا نِسَاءَ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ، لاَ تَحْقِرَنَّ امْرَأَةٌ مِنْكُنَّ لِجَارَتِهَا، وَلَوْ كُرَاعُ شَاةٍ مُحَرَّقٍ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: O believing women, let none of you belittle a gift for her neighbour, even if it is a burnt sheep's trotter.

situation: A man complained to the Prophet that his neighbour kept harming him.
wise_response: The Prophet told him to carry his belongings out into the road. Passers-by asked why, heard the story, and began cursing the neighbour. The neighbour came and said, "Go back home. By God, I will not harm you."
why_it_worked: The man made the wrong public without striking back. Shame before the community moved the neighbour to stop.
tempting_wrong_answer: Taking revenge on the neighbour, or suffering in silence while the harm continued.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا صَفْوَانُ بْنُ عِيسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَجْلاَنَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ رَجُلٌ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، إِنَّ لِي جَارًا يُؤْذِينِي، فَقَالَ‏:‏ انْطَلِقْ فَأَخْرِجْ مَتَاعَكَ إِلَى الطَّرِيقِ، فَانْطَلَقَ فَأَخْرِجَ مَتَاعَهُ، فَاجْتَمَعَ النَّاسُ عَلَيْهِ، فَقَالُوا‏:‏ مَا شَأْنُكَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لِي جَارٌ يُؤْذِينِي، فَذَكَرْتُ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَ‏:‏ انْطَلِقْ فَأَخْرِجْ مَتَاعَكَ إِلَى الطَّرِيقِ، فَجَعَلُوا يَقُولُونَ‏:‏ اللَّهُمَّ الْعَنْهُ، اللَّهُمَّ أَخْزِهِ‏.‏ فَبَلَغَهُ، فَأَتَاهُ فَقَالَ‏:‏ ارْجِعْ إِلَى مَنْزِلِكَ، فَوَاللَّهِ لاَ أُؤْذِيكَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man said: Messenger of God, I have a neighbour who harms me. He said: Go and take your belongings out into the road. He went and took his belongings out, and people gathered round him and said: What is the matter with you? He said: I have a neighbour who harms me. I told the Prophet, peace be upon him, and he said: Go and take your belongings out into the road. So they began to say: O God, curse him. O God, disgrace him. That reached the neighbour, and he came to him and said: Go back to your home. By God, I will not harm you.

situation: A man came to the Prophet to complain about his neighbour. He saw the Prophet standing with a man in white and asked who it was.
wise_response: The Prophet said it was Jibril, and that Jibril kept urging him about the neighbour until he thought the neighbour would be given a share of inheritance.
why_it_worked: The neighbour's rights are so weighty they come close to the rights of family.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating the neighbour as a stranger with no claim on you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مَخْلَدُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو زُهَيْرٍ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ مَغْرَاءَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الْفَضْلُ يَعْنِي ابْنَ مُبَشِّرٍ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ جَابِرًا يَقُولُ‏:‏ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَسْتَعْدِيهِ عَلَى جَارِهِ، فَبَيْنَا هُوَ قَاعِدٌ بَيْنَ الرُّكْنِ وَالْمَقَامِ إِذْ أَقْبَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَرَآهُ الرَّجُلُ وَهُوَ مُقَاوِمٌ رَجُلاً عَلَيْهِ ثِيَابٌ بَيَاضٌ عِنْدَ الْمَقَامِ حَيْثُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى الْجَنَائِزِ، فَأَقْبَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ‏:‏ بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، مَنِ الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي رَأَيْتُ مَعَكَ مُقَاوِمَكَ عَلَيْهِ ثِيَابٌ بِيضٌ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ أَقَدْ رَأَيْتَهُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ نَعَمْ، قَالَ‏:‏ رَأَيْتَ خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا، ذَاكَ جِبْرِيلُ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَسُولُ رَبِّي، مَا زَالَ يُوصِينِي بِالْجَارِ حَتَّى ظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهُ جَاعِلٌ لَهُ مِيرَاثًا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, seeking his help against his neighbour. While he was sitting between the Corner and the Station, the Prophet came, and the man saw him standing with a man dressed in white at the Station, where they pray over the dead. The Prophet came over, and the man said: May my father and mother be your ransom, Messenger of God, who was the man I saw standing with you dressed in white? He said: Did you see him? He said: Yes. He said: You have seen great good. That was Jibril, the messenger of my Lord. He kept urging me about the neighbour until I thought he would give him a share of inheritance.

situation: Two people stop speaking to each other, or one neighbour oppresses another until he leaves his home.
wise_response: Thawban said that two men who cut each other off for more than three days and die that way are both ruined, and a neighbour who wrongs his neighbour until he drives him out is ruined.
why_it_worked: Estrangement left to harden and pressure that drives a family from its home are serious wrongs.
tempting_wrong_answer: Nursing a grudge indefinitely, or making life miserable for a neighbour until he gives up and moves.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عِصَامُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَرْطَاةُ بْنُ الْمُنْذِرِ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ، يَعْنِي أَبَا عَامِرٍ الْحِمْصِيَّ، قَالَ‏:‏ كَانَ ثَوْبَانُ يَقُولُ‏:‏ مَا مِنْ رَجُلَيْنِ يَتَصَارَمَانِ فَوْقَ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ، فَيَهْلِكُ أَحَدُهُمَا، فَمَاتَا وَهُمَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْمُصَارَمَةِ، إِلاَّ هَلَكَا جَمِيعًا، وَمَا مِنْ جَارٍ يَظْلِمُ جَارَهُ وَيَقْهَرُهُ، حَتَّى يَحْمِلَهُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى أَنْ يَخْرُجَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ، إِلاَّ هَلَكَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: No two men cut each other off for more than three days, and one of them perishes, so that both die still estranged, except that both are ruined. And no neighbour wrongs his neighbour and oppresses him until it drives him to leave his home, except that he is ruined.

situation: Abdullah ibn Amr's servant was skinning a sheep. Abdullah told him to start the sharing with their Jewish neighbour, and a man objected.
wise_response: Abdullah said, "Boy, when you finish, begin with our Jewish neighbour," and explained that the Prophet urged care for the neighbour so much they thought he would make him an heir.
why_it_worked: The neighbour's right does not depend on his religion. A neighbour is a neighbour.
tempting_wrong_answer: Passing over the neighbour of another faith and giving only to one's own.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو نُعَيْمٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا بَشِيرُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ قَالَ‏:‏ كُنْتُ عِنْدَ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، وَغُلاَمُهُ يَسْلُخُ شَاةً، فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا غُلاَمُ، إِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَابْدَأْ بِجَارِنَا الْيَهُودِيِّ، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ‏:‏ الْيَهُودِيُّ أَصْلَحَكَ اللَّهُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُوصِي بِالْجَارِ، حَتَّى خَشِينَا أَوْ رُئِينَا أَنَّهُ سَيُوَرِّثُهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I was with Abdullah ibn Amr while his servant was skinning a sheep. He said: Boy, when you finish, begin with our Jewish neighbour. A man among the people said: The Jew? May God set you right! He said: I heard the Prophet, peace be upon him, urge us about the neighbour until we feared, or we thought, that he would make him an heir.

situation: Someone has been treated kindly by a person they consider wicked, and wonders whether they still owe kindness in return.
wise_response: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya said of the verse "Is the reward of goodness anything but goodness?" that it holds without condition, for the righteous and the wicked alike.
why_it_worked: Repaying good with good is owed to anyone who does it. It does not depend on the doer's character.
tempting_wrong_answer: Refusing to return a favour because the giver is a sinner or an enemy.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا الْحُمَيْدِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سَالِمُ بْنُ أَبِي حَفْصَةَ، عَنْ مُنْذِرٍ الثَّوْرِيِّ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحَنَفِيَّةِ‏:‏ ‏{‏هَلْ جَزَاءُ الإِحْسَانِ إِلاَّ الإِحْسَانُ‏}‏، قَالَ‏:‏ هِيَ مُسَجَّلَةٌ لِلْبَرِّ وَالْفَاجِرِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: About "Is the reward of goodness anything but goodness?" he said: It is unconditional, for the righteous and the wicked.

situation: A person spends their days working for widows and the poor.
wise_response: The Prophet said such a person is like one who strives in the path of God, and like one who fasts every day and prays every night.
why_it_worked: Labouring for the weak is counted as high a devotion as the hardest worship.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking only formal worship counts and treating care for the needy as lesser work.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ ثَوْرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الْغَيْثِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ السَّاعِي عَلَى الأَرْمَلَةِ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ كَالْمُجَاهِدِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ، وَكَالَّذِي يَصُومُ النَّهَارَ وَيَقُومُ اللَّيْلَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The one who works on behalf of the widow and the poor is like the one who strives in the path of God, and like the one who fasts by day and stands in prayer by night.

situation: A poor woman with two daughters asked A'isha for food. A'isha had only one date and gave it. The mother split it between her daughters and ate nothing.
wise_response: When A'isha told the Prophet, he said whoever is responsible for daughters and treats them well, they will be a screen for him from the Fire.
why_it_worked: Caring well for daughters, even at cost to oneself, is honoured as a great good.
tempting_wrong_answer: Taking the date for oneself, or treating daughters as a burden.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْيَمَانِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا شُعَيْبٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، أَنَّ عُرْوَةَ بْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ أَخْبَرَهُ، أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ زَوْجَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَتْ‏:‏ جَاءَتْنِي امْرَأَةٌ مَعَهَا ابْنَتَانِ لَهَا، فَسَأَلَتْنِي فَلَمْ تَجِدْ عِنْدِي إِلاَّ تَمْرَةً وَاحِدَةً، فَأَعْطَيْتُهَا، فَقَسَمَتْهَا بَيْنَ ابْنَتَيْهَا، ثُمَّ قَامَتْ فَخَرَجَتْ، فَدَخَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَحَدَّثْتُهُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ يَلِي مِنْ هَذِهِ الْبَنَاتِ شَيْئًا، فَأَحْسَنَ إِلَيْهِنَّ، كُنَّ لَهُ سِتْرًا مِنَ النَّارِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A woman came to me with two of her daughters and asked me for something. She found nothing with me but a single date, so I gave it to her. She divided it between her two daughters, then got up and left. The Prophet, peace be upon him, came in and I told him. He said: Whoever is responsible for any of these daughters and treats them well, they will be a screen for him from the Fire.

situation: A person takes on the care of an orphan.
wise_response: The Prophet said, "I and the one who looks after an orphan will be in the Garden like these two," holding up two fingers side by side.
why_it_worked: Raising a child who has lost a parent places a person close to the Prophet.
tempting_wrong_answer: Leaving orphans to fend for themselves because they are someone else's responsibility.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنْ صَفْوَانَ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَتْنِي أُنَيْسَةُ، عَنْ أُمِّ سَعِيدٍ بِنْتِ مُرَّةَ الْفِهْرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِيهَا، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ أَنَا وَكَافِلُ الْيَتِيمِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ كَهَاتَيْنِ، أَوْ كَهَذِهِ مِنْ هَذِهِ‏.‏ شَكَّ سُفْيَانُ فِي الْوُسْطَى وَالَّتِي تَلِي الإِبْهَامَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I and the one who takes care of an orphan will be in the Garden like these two, or like this one to this one. Sufyan was unsure whether it was the middle finger and the one next to the thumb.

situation: An orphan regularly ate with Ibn Umar. One day he arrived late, after the meal was finished and no food was left.
wise_response: Ibn Umar had sawiq and honey brought for him and said, "Take this. By God, you have not been short-changed."
why_it_worked: He kept his place at the table for the orphan and gave him something better rather than send him away hungry.
tempting_wrong_answer: Telling the boy he came too late and there is nothing left.

situation: A household takes in an orphan. The way they treat the child is up to them.
wise_response: The Prophet said the best house is one where an orphan is treated well and the worst house is one where an orphan is treated badly.

situation: Dawud gave advice on how to treat orphans and friends.
wise_response: He said: be to the orphan like a merciful father. You will reap what you sow. When you promise your friend something, carry it out, or enmity will grow between you.
why_it_worked: Mercy to the weak and kept promises to friends return to the one who gives them. Broken promises breed hostility.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating an orphan coldly, or promising a friend something and letting it drop.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ أَبْزَى قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ دَاوُدُ‏:‏ كُنَّ لِلْيَتِيمِ كَالأَبِ الرَّحِيمِ، وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّكَ كَمَا تَزْرَعُ كَذَلِكَ تَحْصُدُ، مَا أَقْبَحَ الْفَقْرَ بَعْدَ الْغِنَى، وَأَكْثَرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ، أَوْ أَقْبَحُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ، الضَّلاَلَةُ بَعْدَ الْهُدَى، وَإِذَا وَعَدْتَ صَاحِبَكَ فَأَنْجِزْ لَهُ مَا وَعَدْتَهُ، فَإِنْ لاَ تَفْعَلْ يُورِثُ بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ عَدَاوَةٌ، وَتَعَوَّذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ صَاحِبٍ إِنْ ذَكَرْتَ لَمْ يُعِنْكَ، وَإِنْ نَسِيتَ لَمْ يُذَكِّرْكَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Dawud said: Be to the orphan like a merciful father. Know that as you sow, so you will reap. How ugly is poverty after wealth, and more than that, or uglier than that, is going astray after guidance. When you make a promise to your companion, fulfil what you promised him. If you do not, it leaves enmity between you and him. And seek refuge in God from a companion who does not help you when you remember, and does not remind you when you forget.

translation.ai_translation: I knew the Muslims when a man among them would wake in the morning and say: O my family, O my family, your orphan, your orphan! situation: Abu'd-Darda' told people he could tell the good among them from the bad.
wise_response: He said the best is the one whose good is hoped for and whose harm others are safe from. The worst is the one from whom no good is hoped and no one is safe.
why_it_worked: People judge us by whether they can count on our help and feel safe around us.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being someone others neither rely on nor trust to leave them unharmed.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ نُفَيْرٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ، أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ لِلنَّاسِ‏:‏ نَحْنُ أَعْرَفُ بِكُمْ مِنَ الْبَيَاطِرَةِ بِالدَّوَابِّ، قَدْ عَرَفْنَا خِيَارَكُمْ مِنْ شِرَارِكُمْ‏.‏ أَمَّا خِيَارُكُمُ‏:‏ الَّذِي يُرْجَى خَيْرُهُ، وَيُؤْمَنُ شَرُّهُ‏.‏ وَأَمَّا شِرَارُكُمْ‏:‏ فَالَّذِي لاَ يُرْجَى خَيْرُهُ، وَلاَ يُؤْمَنُ شَرُّهُ، وَلاَ يُعْتَقُ مُحَرَّرُهُ‏.‏

wise_response: Umar saw the burn on his face and set the servant free.

why_it_worked: He took the instruction to its fullest meaning. The best treatment he could give was freedom.
tempting_wrong_answer: Doing the minimum while keeping full control over the person.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادٌ، هُوَ ابْنُ سَلَمَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو غَالِبٍ، عَنْ أَبِي أُمَامَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَقْبَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَعَهُ غُلامَانِ، فَوَهَبَ أَحَدُهُمَا لِعَلِيٍّ صَلَوَاتُ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ، وَقَالَ‏:‏ لاَ تَضْرِبْهُ، فَإِنِّي نُهِيتُ عَنْ ضَرْبِ أَهْلِ الصَّلاَةِ، وَإِنِّي رَأَيْتُهُ يُصَلِّي مُنْذُ أَقْبَلْنَا، وَأَعْطَى أَبَا ذَرٍّ غُلاَمًا، وَقَالَ‏:‏ اسْتَوْصِ بِهِ مَعْرُوفًا فَأَعْتَقَهُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ مَا فَعَلَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ أَمَرْتَنِي أَنْ أَسْتَوْصِي بِهِ خَيْرًا فَأَعْتَقْتُهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, peace be upon him, came with two servants. He gave one of them to Ali and said: Do not beat him, for I have been forbidden to beat the people of prayer, and I have seen him praying since we set out. He gave Abu Dharr a servant and said: Take good care of him. Abu Dharr freed him. The Prophet said: What did he do? He said: You told me to take good care of him, so I freed him.

situation: Anas served the Prophet as a boy for about ten years, at home and on journeys.
wise_response: Anas said the Prophet never once asked him why he had done something a certain way, or why he had failed to do something.
why_it_worked: Patience with a young servant's mistakes kept his dignity whole and earned his lifelong devotion.
tempting_wrong_answer: Scolding a servant or child over every error or task left undone.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مَعْمَرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ قَدِمَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمَدِينَةَ وَلَيْسَ لَهُ خَادِمٌ، فَأَخَذَ أَبُو طَلْحَةَ بِيَدِي، فَانْطَلَقَ بِي حَتَّى أَدْخَلَنِي عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا نَبِيَّ اللهِ، إِنَّ أَنَسًا غُلاَمٌ كَيِّسٌ لَبِيبٌ، فَلْيَخْدُمْكَ‏.‏ قَالَ‏:‏ فَخَدَمْتُهُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَالْحَضَرِ، مَقْدَمَهُ الْمَدِينَةَ حَتَّى تُوُفِّيَ صلى الله عليه وسلم، مَا قَالَ لِي لِشَيْءٍ صَنَعْتُ‏:‏ لِمَ صَنَعْتَ هَذَا هَكَذَا‏؟‏ وَلاَ قَالَ لِي لِشَيْءٍ لَمْ أَصْنَعْهُ‏:‏ أَلاَ صَنَعْتَ هَذَا هَكَذَا‏؟‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, peace be upon him, came to Madina and had no servant. Abu Talha took me by the hand and brought me in to the Prophet and said: Prophet of God, Anas is a bright, sensible boy, so let him serve you. I served him at home and on journeys from his arrival in Madina until he died. He never said to me about anything I did: Why did you do it this way? Nor about anything I did not do: Why did you not do it this way?

situation: A household keeps food and goods that servants handle every day.
wise_response: Abu'l-Aliya said they were told to seal, measure and count what was in the servant's charge, so servants would not fall into bad habits and masters would not fall into suspecting them.
why_it_worked: Clear accounts protect both sides. No one is tempted and no one is wrongly suspected.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping no track, then accusing the servant when something seems missing.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو خَلْدَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي الْعَالِيَةِ قَالَ‏:‏ كُنَّا نُؤْمَرُ أَنْ نَخْتِمَ عَلَى الْخَادِمِ، وَنَكِيلَ، وَنَعُدَّهَا، كَرَاهِيَةَ أَنْ يَتَعَوَّدُوا خُلُقَ سُوءٍ، أَوْ يَظُنَّ أَحَدُنَا ظَنَّ سُوءٍ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: We used to be told to seal things against the servant, and to measure and count, out of dislike that they should grow used to bad character, or that one of us should think badly of them.

situation: Abu Mas'ud was beating his servant when he heard a voice behind him. It was the Prophet.
wise_response: The Prophet said, "Know, Abu Mas'ud, God has more power over you than you have over him." Abu Mas'ud at once freed the servant for God's sake.
why_it_worked: Remembering that he too stood under a greater power made him see his cruelty and set it right.
tempting_wrong_answer: Using power over the weak freely because no one can stop you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَلاَمٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ التَّيْمِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ‏:‏ كُنْتُ أَضْرِبُ غُلاَمًا لِي، فَسَمِعْتُ مِنْ خَلْفِي صَوْتًا‏:‏ اعْلَمْ أَبَا مَسْعُودٍ، لَلَّهُ أَقْدَرُ عَلَيْكَ مِنْكَ عَلَيْهِ، فَالْتَفَتُّ فَإِذَا هُوَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، قُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، فَهُوَ حُرٌّ لِوَجْهِ اللهِ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَمَا لَوْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ لَمَسَّتْكَ النَّارُ أَوْ لَلَفَحَتْكَ النَّارُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I was beating a servant of mine when I heard a voice behind me: Know, Abu Mas'ud, God has more power over you than you have over him. I turned, and it was the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. I said: Messenger of God, he is free for the sake of God. He said: Had you not done so, the Fire would have touched you, or scorched you.

situation: Ibn Mas'ud asked the Prophet which deeds Allah loves most, and kept asking for the next one.
wise_response: The Prophet named prayer at its proper time first, then devotion to parents, then striving in Allah's way.
why_it_worked: Kindness to parents ranks just after worship itself. It is placed among the highest deeds, ahead of going out to fight.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating care for one's parents as a lesser duty that can wait behind more visible acts of devotion.

translation.original_text: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو نَصْرٍ أَحْمَدُ بْن مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ حَامِدِ بْنِ هَارُونَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الجْبَّارِ البُخَارِيُّ المَعْرُوفُ بِابْنِ النَّيَازِكِيِّ قِرَاءَةً عَلَيْهِ فَأَقْرَّ بِهِ قَدِمَ عَلَيْنَا حَاجًا فِي صَفَرَ سَنَةَ سَبْعِينَ وَثَلاثِمِئَةٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَناَ أَبُو الْخَيْرِ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ الجَلِيلِ بْنِ خَالِدِ بْنِ حُرَيْثٍ البُخَارِيُّ الْكِرْمَانِيُّ الْعَبْقَسِيُّ البَزَّارُ سَنَة اثْنَتَيْنِ وَعِشْرِينَ وَثَلاَثِمِئَةٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اللهِ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ المُغَيرَةِ بْنِ الأَحْنَفِ الْجُعْفِيُّ البُخَاِرُّي قال‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْوَلِيدِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ قَالَ‏:‏ الْوَلِيدُ بْنُ الْعَيْزَارِ أَخْبَرَنِي قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَمْرٍو الشَّيْبَانِيَّ يَقُولُ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا صَاحِبُ هَذِهِ الدَّارِ، وَأَوْمَأَ بِيَدِهِ إِلَى دَارِ عَبْدِ اللهِ قَالَ‏:‏ سَأَلْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ أَيُّ الْعَمَلِ أَحَبُّ إِلَى اللهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ الصَّلاَةُ عَلَى وَقْتِهَا، قُلْتُ‏:‏ ثُمَّ أَيٌّ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ ثُمَّ بِرُّ الْوَالِدَيْنِ، قُلْتُ‏:‏ ثُمَّ أَيٌّ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ ثُمَّ الْجِهَادُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي بِهِنَّ، وَلَوِ اسْتَزَدْتُهُ لَزَادَنِي‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The owner of this house (and he pointed to the house of 'Abdullah) told us: I asked the Prophet, peace be upon him, which deed is most beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said, "Prayer at its time." I said, "Then which?" He said, "Then devotion to parents." I said, "Then which?" He said, "Then striving in the path of Allah." He said: He told me these, and if I had asked him for more he would have told me more.

situation: A grown child wonders whether he has paid back what his father gave him.
wise_response: The Prophet said a child cannot repay his father unless he finds him enslaved, buys him, and sets him free.
why_it_worked: What a parent gives is so large that only giving back freedom itself comes close to it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking a few favors have settled the debt owed to a parent.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا قَبِيصَةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ سُهَيْلِ بْنِ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ يَجْزِي وَلَدٌ وَالِدَهُ، إِلاَّ أَنْ يَجِدَهُ مَمْلُوكًا فَيَشْتَرِيَهُ فَيُعْتِقَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A child cannot repay his father unless he finds him a slave, buys him, and sets him free.

situation: A man asked the Prophet who most deserves his devotion.
wise_response: The Prophet said "Your mother" three times. On the fourth asking he said "Your father," then the nearest relatives in order.
why_it_worked: The mother carries the heaviest burden in raising a child, so her claim is repeated three times before the father's.
tempting_wrong_answer: Taking a mother's care for granted, or ranking relatives by who is useful to you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَاصِمٍ، عَنْ بَهْزِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ، قُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، مَنْ أَبَرُّ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ أُمَّكَ، قُلْتُ‏:‏ مَنْ أَبَرُّ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ أُمَّكَ، قُلْتُ‏:‏ مَنْ أَبَرُّ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ أُمَّكَ، قُلْتُ‏:‏ مَنْ أَبَرُّ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ أَبَاكَ، ثُمَّ الأَقْرَبَ فَالأَقْرَبَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I said, "Messenger of Allah, to whom should I be most dutiful?" He said, "Your mother." I said, "To whom should I be most dutiful?" He said, "Your mother." I said, "To whom should I be most dutiful?" He said, "Your mother." I said, "To whom should I be most dutiful?" He said, "Your father, then the nearest, and then the next nearest."

situation: A man told Ibn 'Abbas he had killed a woman out of jealousy after she chose another man, and asked if he could still repent. Ibn 'Abbas first asked whether his mother was alive.
wise_response: When he said no, Ibn 'Abbas told him to repent to Allah and draw near to Him as much as he could. Asked later why he had asked about the mother, he said he knew no deed nearer to Allah than devotion to one's mother.
why_it_worked: Ibn 'Abbas held that serving one's mother is the surest way back to Allah, even for someone who has done great wrong.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting jealousy turn to violence, or treating a living mother's care as a small thing when it is the deed closest to Allah.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي مَرْيَمَ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي زَيْدُ بْنُ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، أَنَّهُ أَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ‏:‏ إِنِّي خَطَبْتُ امْرَأَةً، فَأَبَتْ أَنْ تَنْكِحَنِي، وَخَطَبَهَا غَيْرِي، فَأَحَبَّتْ أَنْ تَنْكِحَهُ، فَغِرْتُ عَلَيْهَا فَقَتَلْتُهَا، فَهَلْ لِي مِنْ تَوْبَةٍ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ أُمُّكَ حَيَّةٌ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، قَالَ‏:‏ تُبْ إِلَى اللهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَتَقَرَّبْ إِلَيْهِ مَا اسْتَطَعْتَ‏.‏ فَذَهَبْتُ فَسَأَلْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ‏:‏ لِمَ سَأَلْتَهُ عَنْ حَيَاةِ أُمِّهِ‏؟‏ فَقَالَ‏:‏ إِنِّي لاَ أَعْلَمُ عَمَلاً أَقْرَبَ إِلَى اللهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ مِنْ بِرِّ الْوَالِدَةِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man came to him and said, "I asked a woman to marry me and she refused. Someone else asked her and she wanted to marry him. I was jealous over her and killed her. Is there any repentance for me?" He said, "Is your mother alive?" He said, "No." He said, "Repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and draw near to Him as much as you can." ['Ata' said:] So I went and asked Ibn 'Abbas, "Why did you ask him whether his mother was alive?" He said, "I know of no deed that brings one nearer to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than devotion to one's mother."

situation: A child has a parent who is angry with him, perhaps unfairly.
wise_response: Ibn 'Abbas said that whoever serves his parents seeking reward has two gates of the Garden opened, and that Allah is not pleased with a child until an angry parent is pleased. Asked "Even if they wrong him?" he answered, "Even if they wrong him."
why_it_worked: The duty to win back a parent's goodwill does not depend on the parent being in the right.
tempting_wrong_answer: Withholding kindness from a parent until the parent admits fault.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادٌ هُوَ ابْنُ سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ التَّيْمِيِّ، عَنْ سَعِيدٍ الْقَيْسِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ لَهُ وَالِدَانِ مُسْلِمَانِ يُصْبِحُ إِلَيْهِمَا مُحْتَسِبًا، إِلاَّ فَتْحَ لَهُ اللَّهُ بَابَيْنِ يَعْنِي‏:‏ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ وَإِنْ كَانَ وَاحِدًا فَوَاحِدٌ، وَإِنْ أَغْضَبَ أَحَدَهُمَا لَمْ يَرْضَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ حَتَّى يَرْضَى عَنْهُ، قِيلَ‏:‏ وَإِنْ ظَلَمَاهُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ وَإِنْ ظَلَمَاهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: There is no Muslim with two Muslim parents who goes to them each morning hoping for reward except that Allah opens two gates for him, meaning of the Garden. If there is one, then one. If he angers one of them, Allah is not pleased with him until that parent is pleased with him. Someone asked, "Even if they wrong him?" He said, "Even if they wrong him."

situation: Taysala feared he had committed major sins and asked Ibn 'Umar how to escape the Fire.
wise_response: Ibn 'Umar listed the nine major sins, including making one's parents weep through undutifulness. Then he asked if Taysala's parents were alive. Told his mother was, he said: "If you speak gently to her and feed her, you will enter the Garden, as long as you avoid the major sins."
why_it_worked: Gentle words and food for an aging mother are counted among the deeds that save a person.
tempting_wrong_answer: Looking for some grand act of atonement while neglecting the plain daily care of a parent at home.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا زِيَادُ بْنُ مِخْرَاقٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي طَيْسَلَةُ بْنُ مَيَّاسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ كُنْتُ مَعَ النَّجَدَاتِ، فَأَصَبْتُ ذُنُوبًا لاَ أَرَاهَا إِلاَّ مِنَ الْكَبَائِرِ، فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِابْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ‏:‏ مَا هِيَ‏؟‏ قُلْتُ‏:‏ كَذَا وَكَذَا، قَالَ‏:‏ لَيْسَتْ هَذِهِ مِنَ الْكَبَائِرِ، هُنَّ تِسْعٌ‏:‏ الإِشْرَاكُ بِاللَّهِ، وَقَتْلُ نَسَمَةٍ، وَالْفِرَارُ مِنَ الزَّحْفِ، وَقَذْفُ الْمُحْصَنَةِ، وَأَكْلُ الرِّبَا، وَأَكْلُ مَالِ الْيَتِيمِ، وَإِلْحَادٌ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ، وَالَّذِي يَسْتَسْخِرُ، وَبُكَاءُ الْوَالِدَيْنِ مِنَ الْعُقُوقِ‏.‏ قَالَ لِي ابْنُ عُمَرَ‏:‏ أَتَفْرَقُ النَّارَ، وَتُحِبُّ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ‏؟‏ قُلْتُ‏:‏ إِي وَاللَّهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَحَيٌّ وَالِدُكَ‏؟‏ قُلْتُ‏:‏ عِنْدِي أُمِّي، قَالَ‏:‏ فَوَاللَّهِ لَوْ أَلَنْتَ لَهَا الْكَلاَمَ، وَأَطْعَمْتَهَا الطَّعَامَ، لَتَدْخُلَنَّ الْجَنَّةَ مَا اجْتَنَبْتَ الْكَبَائِرَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I was with the Najdat and committed sins I could only think were among the major ones. I mentioned that to Ibn 'Umar. He said, "What are they?" I said, "Such and such." He said, "These are not among the major sins. They are nine: associating partners with Allah, killing a soul, fleeing from the advancing army, slandering a chaste woman, consuming usury, consuming an orphan's wealth, profaning the Mosque, mocking others, and the weeping of parents caused by undutifulness." Then Ibn 'Umar said to me, "Do you fear the Fire and want to enter the Garden?" I said, "Yes, by Allah." He said, "Is your father alive?" I said, "I have my mother." He said, "By Allah, if you speak softly to her and feed her, you will surely enter the Garden as long as you avoid the major sins."

key_terms.عقوق (uquq): undutifulness, breaking faith with one's parents

situation: A parent wants something the child would rather not give.
wise_response: 'Urwa explained the verse "lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy" as: "Do not hold back from them anything they love."
why_it_worked: Humility toward parents is shown in small daily yielding to what they want.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو نُعَيْمٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ‏:‏ ‏{‏وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ‏}‏، قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ تَمْتَنِعْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ أَحَبَّاهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: About {And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy}, he said: "Do not refuse them anything they love."

situation: A Yemeni man carried his mother on his back around the Ka'ba and asked Ibn 'Umar whether he had now repaid her.
wise_response: Ibn 'Umar said: "No, not even for a single groan" of the pain she bore for him.
why_it_worked: A mother's sacrifice in bearing a child cannot be paid off, even by great effort. The right posture is lasting gratitude.
tempting_wrong_answer: Believing a hard act of service has cleared one's debt to a parent.

translation.original_text:
حَدَّثَنَا آدَمُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي بُرْدَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَبِي يُحَدِّثُ، أَنَّهُ شَهِدَ ابْنَ عُمَرَ وَرَجُلٌ يَمَانِيٌّ يَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ، حَمَلَ أُمَّهُ وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ، يَقُولُ‏:‏
إِنِّي لَهَا بَعِيرُهَا الْمُذَلَّلُ إِنْ أُذْعِرَتْ رِكَابُهَا لَمْ أُذْعَرِ
ثُمَّ قَالَ‏:‏ يَا ابْنَ عُمَرَ أَتُرَانِي جَزَيْتُهَا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، وَلاَ بِزَفْرَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ، ثُمَّ طَافَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ، فَأَتَى الْمَقَامَ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ‏:‏ يَا ابْنَ أَبِي مُوسَى، إِنَّ كُلَّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ تُكَفِّرَانِ مَا أَمَامَهُمَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: He saw Ibn 'Umar while a Yemeni man was circling the House carrying his mother on his back, saying, "I am her tamed camel. If her mounts take fright, I do not." Then he said, "Ibn 'Umar, do you think I have repaid her?" He said, "No, not even for one groan." Then Ibn 'Umar circled the House, came to the Station, prayed two rak'as, and said, "Son of Abu Musa, every two rak'as wipe out what came before them."

situation: Abu Hurayra lived in a house next to his mother's and came and went each day.
wise_response: Each time he left or returned he stood at her door, greeted her, and said, "May Allah have mercy on you as you raised me when I was small." She answered, "May Allah have mercy on you as you were dutiful to me when I was old."
why_it_worked: A small daily ritual of greeting and thanks kept love and gratitude alive on both sides.
tempting_wrong_answer: Passing a parent's door without a word because one is busy or important.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي اللَّيْثُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي خَالِدُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ أَبِي هِلاَلٍ، عَنْ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي مُرَّةَ مَوْلَى عَقِيلٍ، أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ كَانَ يَسْتَخْلِفُهُ مَرْوَانُ، وَكَانَ يَكُونُ بِذِي الْحُلَيْفَةِ، فَكَانَتْ أُمُّهُ فِي بَيْتٍ وَهُوَ فِي آخَرَ‏.‏ قَالَ‏:‏ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ وَقَفَ عَلَى بَابِهَا فَقَالَ‏:‏ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكِ يَا أُمَّتَاهُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، فَتَقُولُ‏:‏ وَعَلَيْكَ السَّلاَمُ يَا بُنَيَّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، فَيَقُولُ‏:‏ رَحِمَكِ اللَّهُ كَمَا رَبَّيْتِنِي صَغِيرًا، فَتَقُولُ‏:‏ رَحِمَكَ اللَّهُ كَمَا بَرَرْتَنِي كَبِيرًا، ثُمَّ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ صَنَعَ مِثْلَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Marwan used to leave Abu Hurayra in charge in his place, and he would be at Dhu'l-Hulayfa. His mother was in one house and he in another. When he wanted to go out, he would stand at her door and say, "Peace be upon you, mother, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings." She would say, "And upon you be peace, my son, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings." He would say, "May Allah have mercy on you as you raised me when I was small." She would say, "May Allah have mercy on you as you were good to me when I was old." Then when he wanted to come in, he did the same.

situation: A man came to pledge to emigrate with the Prophet, having left his parents in tears.
wise_response: The Prophet told him: "Go back to them and make them laugh as you made them weep."
why_it_worked: A good cause pursued by breaking one's parents' hearts is not accepted. Repair at home comes first.
tempting_wrong_answer: Chasing a noble goal while ignoring the grief it causes the people who raised you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو نُعَيْمٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ السَّائِبِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قَالَ‏:‏ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُبَايِعُهُ عَلَى الْهِجْرَةِ، وَتَرَكَ أَبَوَيْهِ يَبْكِيَانِ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ ارْجِعْ إِلَيْهِمَا، وَأَضْحِكْهُمَا كَمَا أَبْكَيْتَهُمَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, to pledge to him to emigrate, and he had left his parents weeping. He said, "Go back to them and make them laugh as you made them weep."

situation: The Prophet asked his companions whether they wanted to hear the worst of the major sins.
wise_response: He named associating partners with Allah and undutifulness to parents. Then he sat up from reclining and said, "and false speech," and kept repeating it until Abu Bakra wished he would stop.
why_it_worked: Lying and false witness are placed beside the gravest wrongs. The Prophet's urgency shows how easily people slide into them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating a lie or false testimony as a minor slip.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ الْفَضْلِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الْجُرَيْرِيُّ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ أَلاَ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِأَكْبَرِ الْكَبَائِرِ‏؟‏ ثَلاَثًا، قَالُوا‏:‏ بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ الإِشْرَاكُ بِاللَّهِ، وَعُقُوقُ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَجَلَسَ وَكَانَ مُتَّكِئًا أَلاَ وَقَوْلُ الزُّورِ، مَا زَالَ يُكَرِّرُهَا حَتَّى قُلْتُ‏:‏ لَيْتَهُ سَكَتَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: "Shall I not tell you the greatest of the major sins?" He said it three times. They said, "Yes, Messenger of Allah." He said, "Associating partners with Allah, and undutifulness to parents." He had been reclining, and he sat up and said, "And false speech." He kept repeating it until I said, "I wish he would fall silent."

situation: Mu'awiya asked al-Mughira to write down something he had heard from the Prophet.
wise_response: Al-Mughira dictated: the Prophet forbade asking too many questions, wasting wealth, and idle talk of "it was said, and he said."
why_it_worked: Restraint in speech and in spending protects a person and those around him.
tempting_wrong_answer: Spreading rumor, prying with endless questions, and squandering money.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَلاَمٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا جَرِيرٌ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ وَرَّادٍ، كَاتِبِ الْمُغِيرَةِ بْنِ شُعْبَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ كَتَبَ مُعَاوِيَةُ إِلَى الْمُغِيرَةِ‏:‏ اكْتُبْ إِلَيَّ بِمَا سَمِعْتَ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَ وَرَّادٌ‏:‏ فَأَمْلَى عَلَيَّ وَكَتَبْتُ بِيَدَيَّ‏:‏ إِنِّي سَمِعْتُهُ يَنْهَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ السُّؤَالِ، وَإِضَاعَةِ الْمَالِ، وَعَنْ قِيلَ وَقَالَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Mu'awiya wrote to al-Mughira: "Write to me what you heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him." Warrad said: He dictated to me and I wrote with my own hand: "I heard him forbid asking much, wasting wealth, and 'it was said' and 'he said.'"

situation: 'Ali was asked whether the Prophet had given his family any special teaching.
wise_response: He said no, except a sheet in his sword sheath. It read that Allah curses whoever sacrifices to other than Allah, whoever steals the boundary markers of land, whoever curses his parents, and whoever shelters a wrongdoer.
why_it_worked: Moving a neighbor's boundary stone, cursing one's own parents, and protecting criminals all break the trust a community runs on.
tempting_wrong_answer: Quietly shifting land markers to gain ground, speaking abuse at one's parents, or hiding someone who has done wrong.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ مَرْزُوقٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ أَبِي بَزَّةَ، عَنْ أَبِي الطُّفَيْلِ قَالَ‏:‏ سُئِلَ عَلِيٌّ‏:‏ هَلْ خَصَّكُمُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِشَيْءٍ لَمْ يَخُصَّ بِهِ النَّاسَ كَافَّةً‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ مَا خَصَّنَا رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِشَيْءٍ لَمْ يَخُصَّ بِهِ النَّاسَ، إِلاَّ مَا فِي قِرَابِ سَيْفِي، ثُمَّ أَخْرَجَ صَحِيفَةً، فَإِذَا فِيهَا مَكْتُوبٌ‏:‏ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ ذَبَحَ لِغَيْرِ اللهِ، لَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ سَرَقَ مَنَارَ الأَرْضِ، لَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ لَعَنَ وَالِدَيْهِ، لَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ آوَى مُحْدِثًا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: 'Ali was asked, "Did the Prophet, peace be upon him, single you out for anything he did not give to people in general?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, did not single us out for anything he did not give to people, except what is in the sheath of my sword." Then he took out a sheet, and on it was written: "Allah curses whoever sacrifices to other than Allah. Allah curses whoever steals the boundary markers of land. Allah curses whoever curses his parents. Allah curses whoever shelters a wrongdoer."

situation: A man came to the Prophet wanting to go and fight in jihad.
wise_response: The Prophet asked if his parents were alive. When he said yes, the Prophet said: "Then strive in serving them."
why_it_worked: Caring for living parents is itself a form of striving, and it comes before leaving them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Seeking glory far from home while parents go without care.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْجَعْدِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ حَبِيبِ بْنِ أَبِي ثَابِتٍ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْعَبَّاسِ الأَعْمَى، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قَالَ‏:‏ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُرِيدُ الْجِهَادَ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَحَيٌّ وَالِدَاكَ‏؟‏ فَقَالَ‏:‏ نَعَمْ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ فَفِيهِمَا فَجَاهِدْ
translation.ai_translation: A man came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, wanting to go on jihad. He said, "Are your parents alive?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Then strive in them."

situation: A person lives to see one or both parents grow old.
wise_response: The Prophet said three times, "May his nose be in the dust," and explained: it is the one who has his parents in their old age and still enters the Fire.
why_it_worked: Aging parents are a ready door to the Garden. Missing it is a deep loss.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating elderly parents as a burden and letting the chance to care for them pass.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا خَالِدُ بْنُ مَخْلَدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ بِلاَلٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُهَيْلٌ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ رَغِمَ أَنْفُهُ، رَغِمَ أَنْفُهُ، رَغِمَ أَنْفُهُ، قَالُوا‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ مَنْ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ أَدْرَكَ وَالِدَيْهِ عِنْدَ الْكِبْرِ، أَوْ أَحَدَهُمَا، فَدَخَلَ النَّارَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: "May his nose be rubbed in dust, may his nose be rubbed in dust, may his nose be rubbed in dust." They said, "Who, Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Whoever reaches his parents in their old age, one or both of them, and then enters the Fire."

situation: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas's mother swore not to eat or drink until he left the Prophet.
wise_response: A verse came: do not obey parents who push you to associate others with Allah, yet keep company with them in this world with kindness.
why_it_worked: A child may refuse a parent's wrong demand and still owe the parent courtesy and good treatment.
tempting_wrong_answer: Either giving up one's conscience to please a parent, or cutting the parent off in anger.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِسْرَائِيلُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سِمَاكٌ، عَنْ مُصْعَبِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ سَعْدِ بْنِ أَبِي وَقَّاصٍ قَالَ‏:‏ نَزَلَتْ فِيَّ أَرْبَعُ آيَاتٍ مِنْ كِتَابِ اللهِ تَعَالَى‏:‏ كَانَتْ أُمِّي حَلَفَتْ أَنْ لاَ تَأْكُلَ وَلاَ تَشْرَبَ حَتَّى أُفَارِقَ مُحَمَّدًا صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ‏:‏ ‏{‏وَإِنْ جَاهَدَاكَ عَلَى أَنْ تُشْرِكَ بِي مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ فَلاَ تُطُعْهُمَا وَصَاحِبْهُمَا فِي الدُّنْيَا مَعْرُوفًا‏}‏‏.‏ وَالثَّانِيَةُ‏:‏ أَنِّي كُنْتُ أَخَذْتُ سَيْفًا أَعْجَبَنِي، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، هَبْ لِي هَذَا، فَنَزَلَتْ‏:‏ ‏{‏يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الأَنْفَالِ‏}‏‏.‏ وَالثَّالِثَةُ‏:‏ أَنِّي مَرِضْتُ فَأَتَانِي رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَقْسِمَ مَالِي، أَفَأُوصِي بِالنِّصْفِ‏؟‏ فَقَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ الثُّلُثُ‏؟‏ فَسَكَتَ، فَكَانَ الثُّلُثُ بَعْدَهُ جَائِزًا‏.‏ وَالرَّابِعَةُ‏:‏ إِنِّي شَرِبْتُ الْخَمْرَ مَعَ قَوْمٍ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ، فَضَرَبَ رَجُلٌ مِنْهُمْ أَنْفِي بِلَحْيِ جَمَلٍ، فَأَتَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَنْزَلَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ تَحْرِيمَ الْخَمْرِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Four verses of the Book of Allah came down about me. My mother had sworn she would not eat or drink until I left Muhammad, peace be upon him. So Allah revealed: {But if they strive to make you associate with Me what you have no knowledge of, do not obey them, and keep company with them in this world in kindness.} The second: I had taken a sword that pleased me and said, "Messenger of Allah, give me this," and there came down {They ask you about the spoils}. The third: I fell ill and the Messenger of Allah came to me, and I said, "Messenger of Allah, I want to divide my wealth. Shall I bequeath half?" He said, "No." I said, "A third?" He was silent, and after that a third was allowed. The fourth: I drank wine with some of the Ansar, and one of them struck my nose with a camel's jawbone. I came to the Prophet, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the prohibition of wine.

situation: Asma's mother, who did not share her faith, came to her hoping for help.
wise_response: Asma asked the Prophet whether she should keep ties with her. He said, "Yes."
why_it_worked: Kindness to a parent does not depend on agreeing about religion.
tempting_wrong_answer: Turning a parent away because of difference in belief.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا الْحُمَيْدِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامُ بْنُ عُرْوَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي أَبِي قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَتْنِي أَسْمَاءُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ قَالَتْ‏:‏ أَتَتْنِي أُمِّي رَاغِبَةً، فِي عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَسَأَلْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ أَصِلُهَا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ‏:‏ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِيهَا‏:‏ ‏{‏لاَ يَنْهَاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ‏}‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: My mother came to me, hoping for something, in the time of the Prophet, peace be upon him. I asked the Prophet, "Shall I keep ties with her?" He said, "Yes." Ibn 'Uyayna said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed about her: {Allah does not forbid you regarding those who did not fight you over religion}.

situation: 'Umar was given a silk robe he could not wear himself.
wise_response: The Prophet told him he could sell it or give it to clothe someone. 'Umar sent it to his brother in Makka who had not yet become Muslim.
why_it_worked: A gift one cannot use can still serve a relative, whatever his faith.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting something useful go to waste, or holding back from kin who believe differently.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ دِينَارٍ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عُمَرَ يَقُولُ‏:‏ رَأَى عُمَرُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ حُلَّةً سِيَرَاءَ تُبَاعُ فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، ابْتَعْ هَذِهِ، فَالْبَسْهَا يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ، وَإِذَا جَاءَكَ الْوُفُودُ، قَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّمَا يَلْبَسُ هَذِهِ مَنْ لاَ خَلاَقَ لَهُ، فَأُتِيَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْهَا بِحُلَلٍ، فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى عُمَرَ بِحُلَّةٍ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ كَيْفَ أَلْبَسُهَا وَقَدْ قُلْتَ فِيهَا مَا قُلْتَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ إِنِّي لَمْ أُعْطِكَهَا لِتَلْبَسَهَا، وَلَكِنْ تَبِيعَهَا أَوْ تَكْسُوَهَا، فَأَرْسَلَ بِهَا عُمَرُ إِلَى أَخٍ لَهُ مِنْ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُسْلِمَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: 'Umar saw a striped silk robe for sale and said, "Messenger of Allah, buy this and wear it on Friday and when delegations come to you." He said, "Only one who has no share [in the Hereafter] wears this." Then the Prophet was brought some such robes, and he sent one to 'Umar. 'Umar said, "How can I wear it when you said about it what you said?" He said, "I did not give it to you to wear, but to sell it or clothe someone with it." So 'Umar sent it to a brother of his among the people of Makka before he became Muslim.

situation: A man trades insults with others in a quarrel.
wise_response: The Prophet said reviling one's parents is a major sin. Asked how anyone would do that, he said: a man reviles another man's father and mother, and that man reviles his in return.
why_it_worked: Insults come back. Whoever abuses others' parents brings abuse onto his own.
tempting_wrong_answer: Cursing someone's family in anger without thinking of what will come back on one's own.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ كَثِيرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا سُفْيَانُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي سَعْدُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ حُمَيْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ مِنَ الْكَبَائِرِ أَنْ يَشْتِمَ الرَّجُلُ وَالِدَيْهِ، فَقَالُوا‏:‏ كَيْفَ يَشْتِمُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ يَشْتِمُ الرَّجُلَ، فَيَشْتُمُ أَبَاهُ وَأُمَّهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: "Among the major sins is that a man revile his parents." They said, "How would he revile them?" He said, "He reviles a man, and that man reviles his father and his mother."

situation: A person is tempted to oppress others or to cut off relatives.
wise_response: The Prophet said no sin is more deserving of swift punishment in this world, on top of what awaits in the next, than oppression and cutting kinship.
why_it_worked: These two wrongs damage the people nearest and weakest, and their harm returns quickly on the wrongdoer.
tempting_wrong_answer: Using power to crush others or walking away from family ties.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عُيَيْنَةُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ مَا مِنْ ذَنْبٍ أَجْدَرُ أَنْ يُعَجَّلَ لِصَاحِبِهِ الْعُقُوبَةُ مَعَ مَا يُدَّخَرُ لَهُ، مِنَ الْبَغِيِّ وَقَطِيعَةِ الرَّحِمِ.
translation.ai_translation: There is no sin more fitting to have its punishment hastened for its doer, along with what is stored up for him, than oppression and cutting the ties of kinship.

situation: Someone holds power over a weaker person, or over parents who depend on him.
wise_response: The Prophet said three prayers are answered without doubt: the prayer of the wronged, the prayer of the traveler, and the prayer of parents against their child.
why_it_worked: Those who are wronged, and parents who are grieved by a child, have a direct line to Allah. Wronging them invites their prayer against you.
tempting_wrong_answer: Mistreating the powerless, or giving parents such cause for grief that they pray against you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُعَاذُ بْنُ فَضَالَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامٌ، عَنْ يَحْيَى هُوَ ابْنُ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ يَقُولُ‏:‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ ثَلاَثُ دَعَوَاتٍ مُسْتَجَابَاتٌ لَهُنَّ، لاَ شَكَّ فِيهِنَّ‏:‏ دَعْوَةُ الْمَظْلُومِ، وَدَعْوَةُ الْمُسَافِرِ، وَدَعْوَةُ الْوَالِدِيْنِ عَلَى وَلَدِهِمَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Three prayers are answered, with no doubt about them: the prayer of the wronged, the prayer of the traveler, and the prayer of parents against their child.

situation: Jurayj, a monk, was praying in his hermitage when his mother called him three times. Each time he chose his prayer over answering her.
wise_response: His mother prayed that he would not die before looking into the faces of prostitutes. He was later falsely accused, his hermitage torn down. The infant spoke and cleared him. Offered a hermitage of gold, he asked only that it be rebuilt as it was, and said he smiled because "my mother's prayer reached me."
why_it_worked: A mother's call has a claim even on devotion. Ignoring her had a cost, though his honesty was later shown.
tempting_wrong_answer: Putting one's own pious routine above a parent who needs you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَيَّاشُ بْنُ الْوَلِيدِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الأَعْلَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ قُسَيْطٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ شُرَحْبِيلَ، أَخِي بَنِي عَبْدِ الدَّارِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ مَا تَكَلَّمَ مَوْلُودٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ فِي مَهْدٍ إِلاَّ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَصَاحِبُ جُرَيْجٍ، قِيلَ‏:‏ يَا نَبِيَّ اللهِ، وَمَا صَاحِبُ جُرَيْجٍ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ فَإِنَّ جُرَيْجًا كَانَ رَجُلاً رَاهِبًا فِي صَوْمَعَةٍ لَهُ، وَكَانَ رَاعِيَ بَقَرٍ يَأْوِي إِلَى أَسْفَلِ صَوْمَعَتِهِ، وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقَرْيَةِ تَخْتَلِفُ إِلَى الرَّاعِي، فَأَتَتْ أُمُّهُ يَوْمًا فَقَالَتْ‏:‏ يَا جُرَيْجُ، وَهُوَ يُصَلِّي، فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَهُوَ يُصَلِّي‏:‏ أُمِّي وَصَلاَتِي‏؟‏ فَرَأَى أَنْ يُؤْثِرَ صَلاَتَهُ، ثُمَّ صَرَخَتْ بِهِ الثَّانِيَةَ، فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ‏:‏ أُمِّي وَصَلاَتِي‏؟‏ فَرَأَى أَنْ يُؤْثِرَ صَلاَتَهُ، ثُمَّ صَرَخَتْ بِهِ الثَّالِثَةَ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ أُمِّي وَصَلاَتِي‏؟‏ فَرَأَى أَنْ يُؤْثِرَ صَلاَتَهُ، فَلَمَّا لَمْ يُجِبْهَا قَالَتْ‏:‏ لاَ أَمَاتَكَ اللَّهُ يَا جُرَيْجُ حَتَّى تَنْظُرَ فِي وَجْهِ الْمُومِسَاتِ، ثُمَّ انْصَرَفَتْ‏.‏ فَأُتِيَ الْمَلِكُ بِتِلْكَ الْمَرْأَةِ وَلَدَتْ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ مِمَّنْ‏؟‏ قَالَتْ‏:‏ مِنْ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَصَاحِبُ الصَّوْمَعَةِ‏؟‏ قَالَتْ‏:‏ نَعَمْ، قَالَ‏:‏ اهْدِمُوا صَوْمَعَتَهُ، وَأْتُونِي بِهِ، فَضَرَبُوا صَوْمَعَتَهُ بِالْفُئُوسِ حَتَّى وَقَعَتْ‏.‏ فَجَعَلُوا يَدَهُ إِلَى عُنُقِهِ بِحَبْلٍ، ثُمَّ انْطُلِقَ بِهِ، فَمَرَّ بِهِ عَلَى الْمُومِسَاتِ، فَرَآهُنَّ فَتَبَسَّمَ، وَهُنَّ يَنْظُرْنَ إِلَيْهِ فِي النَّاسِ، فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ‏:‏ مَا تَزْعُمُ هَذِهِ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ مَا تَزْعُمُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ تَزْعُمُ أَنَّ وَلَدَهَا مِنْكَ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَنْتِ تَزْعُمِينَ‏؟‏ قَالَتْ‏:‏ نَعَمْ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَيْنَ هَذَا الصَّغِيرُ‏؟‏ قَالُوا‏:‏ هَذا هُوَ فِي حِجْرِهَا، فَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ أَبُوكَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ رَاعِي الْبَقَرِ‏.‏ قَالَ الْمَلِكُ‏:‏ أَنَجْعَلُ صَوْمَعَتَكَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، قَالَ‏:‏ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَمَا نَجْعَلُهَا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ رُدُّوهَا كَمَا كَانَتْ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَمَا الَّذِي تَبَسَّمْتَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ أَمْرًا عَرَفْتُهُ، أَدْرَكَتْنِي دَعْوَةُ أُمِّي، ثُمَّ أَخْبَرَهُمْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: No child ever spoke in the cradle except 'Isa son of Maryam and the companion of Jurayj. Someone said, "Prophet of Allah, who is the companion of Jurayj?" He said: Jurayj was a monk in his hermitage. A cowherd used to shelter at the foot of the hermitage, and a woman from the village used to visit the cowherd. One day his mother came and said, "Jurayj!" while he was praying. He said to himself as he prayed, "My mother or my prayer?" and decided to keep to his prayer. She called him a second time, and he said to himself, "My mother or my prayer?" and decided to keep to his prayer. She called a third time, and he said, "My mother or my prayer?" and decided to keep to his prayer. When he did not answer her she said, "May Allah not let you die, Jurayj, until you look into the faces of prostitutes," and she went away. Then that woman was brought to the king after giving birth. He said, "From whom?" She said, "From Jurayj." He said, "The man of the hermitage?" She said, "Yes." He said, "Tear down his hermitage and bring him to me." They struck the hermitage with axes until it fell, tied his hand to his neck with a rope, and led him away. He was taken past the prostitutes. He saw them and smiled, while they watched him among the people. The king said, "What does this woman claim?" He said, "What does she claim?" He said, "She claims her child is from you." He said, "Do you claim that?" She said, "Yes." He said, "Where is the little one?" They said, "Here, in her lap." He turned to it and said, "Who is your father?" It said, "The cowherd." The king said, "Shall we make your hermitage of gold?" He said, "No." "Of silver?" He said, "No." "Then what shall we make it of?" He said, "Rebuild it as it was." He said, "Then why did you smile?" He said, "At something I recognized. My mother's prayer reached me." Then he told them.

situation: A man's parents have died and he asks whether any devotion to them is still possible.
wise_response: The Prophet said yes: pray for them, ask forgiveness for them, carry out their commitments, honor their friends, and keep the family ties that come to you only through them.
why_it_worked: Devotion to parents continues after death through how one treats the people and promises they left behind.
tempting_wrong_answer: Assuming the duty to parents ends at the grave and letting their friends and relatives drift away.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو نُعَيْمٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ الْغَسِيلِ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي أُسَيْدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا أُسَيْدٍ يُحَدِّثُ الْقَوْمَ قَالَ‏:‏ كُنَّا عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، هَلْ بَقِيَ مِنْ بِرِّ أَبَوَيَّ شَيْءٌ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِمَا أَبَرُّهُمَا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ نَعَمْ، خِصَالٌ أَرْبَعٌ‏:‏ الدُّعَاءُ لَهُمَا، وَالِاسْتِغْفَارُ لَهُمَا، وَإِنْفَاذُ عَهْدِهِمَا، وَإِكْرَامُ صَدِيقِهِمَا، وَصِلَةُ الرَّحِمِ الَّتِي لاَ رَحِمَ لَكَ إِلاَّ مِنْ قِبَلِهِمَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: We were with the Prophet, peace be upon him, when a man said, "Messenger of Allah, is there anything left of devotion to my parents that I can do for them after their death?" He said, "Yes, four things: praying for them, asking forgiveness for them, carrying out their pledges, honoring their friends, and keeping the ties of kinship that you have only through them."
