situation: On a journey Ibn 'Umar met a bedouin whose father had been a friend of 'Umar.
wise_response: Ibn 'Umar gave him the donkey he rode in turns and the turban from his own head. When a companion said two dirhams would have been enough, he quoted the Prophet: "Keep your father's friendships. Do not cut them off, or Allah will put out your light."
why_it_worked: Honoring the friends of one's father is part of honoring the father. Ibn 'Umar gave generously because the bond mattered more than the cost.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving the bare minimum to a family friend, or forgetting old friendships once a parent is gone.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي اللَّيْثُ، عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ‏:‏ مَرَّ أَعْرَابِيٌّ فِي سَفَرٍ، فَكَانَ أَبُو الأعْرَابِيِّ صَدِيقًا لِعُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، فَقَالَ لِلأَعْرَابِيِّ‏:‏ أَلَسْتَ ابْنَ فُلاَنٍ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ بَلَى، فَأَمَرَ لَهُ ابْنُ عُمَرَ بِحِمَارٍ كَانَ يَسْتَعْقِبُ، وَنَزَعَ عِمَامَتَهُ عَنْ رَأْسِهِ فَأَعْطَاهُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ بَعْضُ مَنْ مَعَهُ‏:‏ أَمَا يَكْفِيهِ دِرْهَمَانِ‏؟‏ فَقَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ احْفَظْ وُدَّ أَبِيكَ، لاَ تَقْطَعْهُ فَيُطْفِئَ اللَّهُ نُورَكَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A bedouin passed by on a journey. The bedouin's father had been a friend of 'Umar. He said to the bedouin, "Are you not the son of so-and-so?" He said, "Yes." Ibn 'Umar ordered that he be given a donkey that he used to ride in turns, and took the turban off his head and gave it to him. Someone with him said, "Would two dirhams not have been enough for him?" He said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said, "Keep the love of your father. Do not cut it off, or Allah will put out your light."

situation: Abu Hurayra saw a man walking with his father.
wise_response: He told him: "Do not call him by his name, do not walk in front of him, and do not sit down before he does."
why_it_worked: Respect for a parent shows in small courtesies of speech, walking and sitting.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating a father as an equal or a peer, with casual address and no deference.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الرَّبِيعِ، عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ زَكَرِيَّا، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامُ بْنُ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ ‏,‏ أَوْ غَيْرِهِ أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ أَبْصَرَ رَجُلَيْنِ، فَقَالَ لأَحَدِهِمَا‏:‏ مَا هَذَا مِنْكَ‏؟‏ فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَبِي، فَقَالَ‏:‏ لاَ تُسَمِّهِ بِاسْمِهِ، وَلاَ تَمْشِ أَمَامَهُ، وَلا تَجْلِسْ قَبْلَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayra saw two men and said to one of them, "What is this man to you?" He said, "My father." He said, "Do not call him by his name, do not walk in front of him, and do not sit before he sits."

situation: Hudhayfa was told that a certain man carried people's talk up to the caliph 'Uthman.
wise_response: Hudhayfa answered with what he had heard from the Prophet: a talebearer will not enter the Garden.
why_it_worked: Carrying words from one person to another to stir trouble breaks trust between people. The hadith treats it as grave enough to bar a person from Paradise.
tempting_wrong_answer: Passing on what you overheard to someone in power, to win favor or to harm the speaker.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو نُعَيْمٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ هَمَّامٍ‏:‏ كُنَّا مَعَ حُذَيْفَةَ، فَقِيلَ لَهُ‏:‏ إِنَّ رَجُلا يَرْفَعُ الْحَدِيثَ إِلَى عُثْمَانَ، فَقَالَ حُذَيْفَةُ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ لا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ قَتَّاتٌ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Hammam said: We were with Hudhayfa, and he was told that a man was carrying talk up to 'Uthman. Hudhayfa said: I heard the Prophet, peace be upon him, say, "A talebearer will not enter the Garden."

key_terms.قتات (qattat): talebearer, one who carries tales to cause harm

situation: The Prophet asked his companions if they wanted to know who were the best and the worst among them.
wise_response: He said the best are those whose presence reminds you of God. The worst are those who go about with gossip, split up people who love each other, and try to bring trouble on the innocent.
why_it_worked: People are judged by the effect they have on others. Someone who divides friends and harms the blameless does real damage to the community.
tempting_wrong_answer: Spreading gossip that drives friends apart or pulls innocent people into trouble.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ الْمُفَضَّلِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ خُثَيْمٍ، عَنْ شَهْرِ بْنِ حَوْشَبٍ، عَنْ أَسْمَاءَ بِنْتِ يَزِيدَ قَالَتْ‏:‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ أَلاَ أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِخِيَارِكُمْ‏؟‏ قَالُوا‏:‏ بَلَى، قَالَ‏:‏ الَّذِينَ إِذَا رُؤُوا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ، أَفَلاَ أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِشِرَارِكُمْ‏؟‏ قَالُوا‏:‏ بَلَى، قَالَ‏:‏ الْمَشَّاؤُونَ بِالنَّمِيمَةِ، الْمُفْسِدُونَ بَيْنَ الأَحِبَّةِ، الْبَاغُونَ الْبُرَآءَ الْعَنَتَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Asma' bint Yazid said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said, "Shall I not tell you who are the best of you?" They said, "Yes." He said, "Those who, when they are seen, God is remembered. Shall I not tell you who are the worst of you?" They said, "Yes." He said, "Those who walk about with slander, who spoil things between those who love one another, and who seek hardship for the innocent."

key_terms.النميمة (namima): talebearing, gossip that sets people against each other

situation: Someone says something indecent about another person, and others hear it and repeat it.
wise_response: 'Ali said that the one who says the indecent thing and the one who spreads it share the sin equally.
why_it_worked: Repeating a shameful report does as much harm as saying it first. Each retelling widens the damage.
tempting_wrong_answer: Telling yourself you only passed it on, so the fault lies with whoever said it first.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا وَهْبُ بْنُ جَرِيرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ يَحْيَى بْنَ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ أَبِي حَبِيبٍ، عَنْ مَرْثَدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللهِ، عَنْ حَسَّانَ بْنِ كُرَيْبٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ‏:‏ الْقَائِلُ الْفَاحِشَةَ، وَالَّذِي يُشِيعُ بِهَا، فِي الإِثْمِ سَوَاءٌ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: "The one who utters an indecency and the one who spreads it are equal in the sin."

situation: People are tempted to rush about spreading news and secrets in unsettled times.
wise_response: 'Ali told them not to be hasty, broadcasting and scattering talk, because hard trials and long, heavy troubles lay ahead.
why_it_worked: Loose talk feeds strife when times are tense. Holding your tongue protects people when trouble is coming.
tempting_wrong_answer: Rushing to repeat every rumor and secret you hear.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ ظَبْيَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي يَحْيَى حَكِيمِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ عَلِيًّا يَقُولُ‏:‏ لاَ تَكُونُوا عُجُلاً مَذَايِيعَ بُذُرًا، فَإِنْ مِنْ وَرَائِكُمْ بَلاَءً مُبَرِّحًا مُمْلِحًا، وَأُمُورًا مُتَمَاحِلَةً رُدُحًا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Hakim ibn Sa'd said: I heard 'Ali say, "Do not be hasty, people who broadcast and scatter talk. Behind you lies a painful, bitter trial, and long, heavy, drawn-out affairs."

situation: You feel the urge to talk about a friend's faults.
wise_response: Ibn 'Abbas said: when you want to mention your companion's faults, mention your own faults first.
why_it_worked: Remembering your own failings checks the impulse to judge others. It keeps you humble and fair.
tempting_wrong_answer: Listing a friend's faults while ignoring your own.

translation.ai_translation: Ibn 'Abbas said: "When you want to mention the faults of your companion, mention the faults of your own self."

situation: People within a community are tempted to find fault with and belittle one another.
wise_response: Ibn 'Abbas explained the verse "Do not find fault with yourselves" as meaning: do not attack one another.
why_it_worked: The verse says "yourselves" because people in a community are like one body. Wounding another is wounding your own.
tempting_wrong_answer: Sniping at and disparaging the people around you.

translation.ai_translation: Ibn 'Abbas said about the words of God, "And do not find fault with yourselves": "Let none of you attack another."

situation: When the Prophet came to the Banu Salima, nearly every man had two names, and one was often a nickname he disliked.
wise_response: The Prophet began calling men by a name, and people told him, "That angers him." The verse forbidding insulting nicknames came down about them.
why_it_worked: Calling someone by a name that hurts him is a small cruelty. People have a right to be addressed in a way that honors them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Using a mocking nickname because everyone else does, even when it angers the person.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا وُهَيْبٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا دَاوُدُ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو جَبِيرَةَ بْنُ الضَّحَّاكِ قَالَ‏:‏ فِينَا نَزَلَتْ، فِي بَنِي سَلِمَةَ‏:‏ ‏{‏وَلاَ تَنَابَزُوا بِالأَلْقَابِ‏}‏، قَالَ‏:‏ قَدِمَ عَلَيْنَا رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَلَيْسَ مِنَّا رَجُلٌ إِلاَّ لَهُ اسْمَانِ، فَجَعَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ يَا فُلاَنُ، فَيَقُولُونَ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، إِنَّهُ يَغْضَبُ مِنْهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Jabira ibn ad-Dahhak said: It was about us, the Banu Salima, that this came down: "And do not insult one another with nicknames." The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, came to us, and there was no man among us without two names. situation: At a meal, one of the guests called a slave girl who was serving them "harlot".
wise_response: Ibn 'Abbas (or his cousin) stopped him: if she does not take the punishment for slander from you in this world, she will take it in the next. When the man asked what if it were true, he said God does not love the foul and obscene.
why_it_worked: A servant has the same right not to be slandered as anyone. Even a true charge does not license vulgar speech.
tempting_wrong_answer: Insulting a person of low standing because she cannot answer back.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أخبرنا الْفَضْلُ بْنُ مُقَاتِلٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي حَكِيمٍ، عَنِ الْحَكَمِ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ عِكْرِمَةَ يَقُولُ‏:‏ لاَ أَدْرِي أَيُّهُمَا جَعَلَ لِصَاحِبِهِ طَعَامًا، ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ أَوِ ابْنُ عَمِّهِ، فَبَيْنَا الْجَارِيَةُ تَعْمَلُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ، إِذْ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمْ لَهَا‏:‏ يَا زَانِيَةُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ مَهْ، إِنْ لَمْ تَحُدَّكَ فِي الدُّنْيَا تَحُدُّكَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَفَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كَانَ كَذَاكَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يُحِبُّ الْفَاحِشَ الْمُتَفَحِّشَ‏.‏

situation: How a believer speaks about and to others.
wise_response: The Prophet said the believer does not defame, does not curse, is not obscene and is not foul-mouthed.
why_it_worked: Faith shows in the tongue. Harsh and abusive speech does not fit a believer.
tempting_wrong_answer: Cursing people, running them down and using crude language.

situation: A man was mentioned in front of the Prophet, and another man praised him highly.
wise_response: The Prophet said, "Woe to you, you have cut your companion's neck," several times. If you must praise someone, say "I think he is such-and-such" if you believe it, and leave his reckoning to God. Do not vouch for anyone over God.
why_it_worked: Lavish praise can make a person proud and ruin him. Measured praise stays honest about what you can know of another.
tempting_wrong_answer: Heaping certain, extravagant praise on someone as if you know his inner worth.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا آدَمُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ خَالِدٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ رَجُلاً ذُكِرَ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ رَجُلٌ خَيْرًا، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ وَيْحَكَ قَطَعْتَ عُنُقَ صَاحِبِكَ، يَقُولُهُ مِرَارًا، إِنْ كَانَ أَحَدُكُمْ مَادِحًا لاَ مَحَالَةَ فَلْيَقُلْ‏:‏ أَحْسَبُ كَذَا وَكَذَا، إِنْ كَانَ يَرَى أَنَّهُ كَذَلِكَ، وَحَسِيبُهُ اللَّهُ، وَلاَ يُزَكِّي عَلَى اللهِ أَحَدًا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Bakra reported that a man was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and a man praised him well. The Prophet said, "Woe to you, you have cut your companion's neck," saying it repeatedly. "If one of you must praise, let him say, 'I reckon him to be such and such,' if he sees him so, and God is his reckoner. And let him not declare anyone pure before God."

situation: The Prophet warned 'A'isha that a visitor was a bad member of his tribe, then received him warmly. He spoke well of a second visitor but was less effusive with him. 'A'isha asked why.
wise_response: He said, "'A'isha, among the worst of people is the one others are careful with for fear of his foul tongue."
why_it_worked: Courtesy toward a harsh man keeps the peace and denies him an excuse for abuse. The real fault lies with the person whose rudeness makes others tread carefully.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being so coarse that people treat you gently only to avoid your tongue.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ فُلَيْحٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَبِي يُونُسَ مَوْلَى عَائِشَةَ، أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ قَالَتِ‏:‏ اسْتَأْذَنَ رَجُلٌ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ بِئْسَ ابْنُ الْعَشِيرَةِ، فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ هَشَّ لَهُ وَانْبَسَطَ إِلَيْهِ، فَلَمَّا خَرَجَ الرَّجُلُ اسْتَأْذَنَ آخَرُ، قَالَ‏:‏ نِعْمَ ابْنُ الْعَشِيرَةِ، فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ لَمْ يَنْبَسِطْ إِلَيْهِ كَمَا انْبَسَطَ إِلَى الْآخَرِ، وَلَمْ يَهِشَّ إِلَيْهِ كَمَا هَشَّ لِلْآخَرِ، فَلَمَّا خَرَجَ قُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، قُلْتُ لِفُلاَنٍ مَا قُلْتَ ثُمَّ هَشَشْتَ إِلَيْهِ، وَقُلْتَ لِفُلاَنٍ مَا قُلْتَ وَلَمْ أَرَكَ صَنَعْتَ مِثْلَهُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ، إِنَّ مِنْ شَرِّ النَّاسِ مَنِ اتُّقِيَ لِفُحْشِهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: 'A'isha said: A man asked permission to come in to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. He said, "What a bad son of his clan." When he came in, he was cheerful and open with him. When the man left, another asked permission. He said, "What a good son of his clan." When he came in, he was not as open with him as he had been with the other, nor as cheerful. When he left, I said, "Messenger of God, you said what you said about that one and then were cheerful with him, and you said what you said about this one and I did not see you do the same." He said, "'A'isha, among the worst of people is one who is guarded against because of his foulness."

situation: A man stood up and began praising a governor.
wise_response: Al-Miqdad threw dust in his face and said the Messenger of God had told them to throw dust in the faces of flatterers.
why_it_worked: Flattering men in power corrupts both the flatterer and the ruler. The companions treated it as something to stop on the spot.
tempting_wrong_answer: Praising someone in authority to win favor.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ مَهْدِيٍّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ حَبِيبِ بْنِ أَبِي ثَابِتٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، عَنْ أَبِي مَعْمَرٍ قَالَ‏:‏ قَامَ رَجُلٌ يُثْنِي عَلَى أَمِيرٍ مِنَ الأُمَرَاءِ، فَجَعَلَ الْمِقْدَادُ يَحْثِي فِي وَجْهِهِ التُّرَابَ، وَقَالَ‏:‏ أَمَرَنَا رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ نَحْثِيَ فِي وُجُوهِ الْمَدَّاحِينَ التُّرَابَ‏.‏

situation: How to treat the young and the old in a community.
wise_response: The Prophet said that whoever does not show mercy to our young and recognize the right of our elders is not one of us.
why_it_worked: Children need gentleness and the old are owed respect. Both belong to how a community holds together.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being harsh with children and dismissive of the elderly.

translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayra reported that the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever does not have mercy on our young and know the right of our old is not of us."

situation: Whom should people honor?
wise_response: Al-Ash'ari said that honoring God includes honoring a grey-haired Muslim, one who carries the Qur'an without going to extremes or neglecting it, and a just ruler.
why_it_worked: Respect for the old, for balanced learning and for fair authority is part of reverence for God.
tempting_wrong_answer: Disregarding the elderly or giving honor to anyone regardless of justice.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا عَوْفٌ، عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ مِخْرَاقٍ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ أَبُو كِنَانَةَ، عَنِ الأَشْعَرِيِّ قَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّ مِنَ إِجْلاَلِ اللهِ إِكْرَامَ ذِي الشَّيْبَةِ الْمُسْلِمِ، وَحَامِلِ الْقُرْآنِ، غَيْرِ الْغَالِي فِيهِ، وَلاَ الْجَافِي عَنْهُ، وَإِكْرَامَ ذِي السُّلْطَانِ الْمُقْسِطِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Al-Ash'ari said: "Part of glorifying God is honoring the grey-haired Muslim, the bearer of the Qur'an who neither exaggerates in it nor turns away from it, and honoring the just holder of authority."

situation: After 'Abdullah ibn Sahl was killed at Khaybar, his relatives came to the Prophet. The youngest, 'Abd ar-Rahman, started speaking first.
wise_response: The Prophet told him, "Let the elder speak first." After hearing the case and finding no proof either way, he paid the blood money himself.
why_it_worked: Letting the elder speak honors age and experience. When no fair ruling could be reached, he bore the cost himself so the family was not left wronged.
tempting_wrong_answer: Pushing ahead of older relatives to speak, or leaving a grieving family with nothing because the case could not be proved.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ بُشَيْرِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ مَوْلَى الأَنْصَارِ، عَنْ رَافِعِ بْنِ خَدِيجٍ، وَسَهْلِ بْنِ أَبِي حَثْمَةَ، أَنَّهُمَا حَدَثَا، أَوْ حَدَّثَاهُ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللهِ بْنَ سَهْلٍ، وَمُحَيِّصَةَ بْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، أَتَيَا خَيْبَرَ فَتَفَرَّقَا فِي النَّخْلِ، فَقُتِلَ عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ سَهْلٍ، فَجَاءَ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ سَهْلٍ، وَحُوَيِّصَةُ وَمُحَيِّصَةُ ابْنَا مَسْعُودٍ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَتَكَلَّمُوا فِي أَمْرِ صَاحِبِهِمْ، فَبَدَأَ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ، وَكَانَ أَصْغَرَ الْقَوْمِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ كَبِّرِ الْكِبَرَ، قَالَ يَحْيَى‏:‏ لِيَلِيَ الْكَلاَمَ الأَكْبَرُ، فَتَكَلَّمُوا فِي أَمْرِ صَاحِبِهِمْ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ اسْتَحِقُّوا قَتِيلَكُمْ، أَوْ قَالَ‏:‏ صَاحِبَكُمْ، بِأَيْمَانِ خَمْسِينَ مِنْكُمْ، قَالُوا‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، أَمْرٌ لَمْ نَرَهُ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَتُبْرِئُكُمْ يَهُودُ بِأَيْمَانِ خَمْسِينَ مِنْهُمْ، قَالُوا‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، قَوْمٌ كُفَّارٌ‏.‏ فَفَدَاهُ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ قِبَلِهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Rafi' ibn Khadij and Sahl ibn Abi Hathma reported that 'Abdullah ibn Sahl and Muhayyisa ibn Mas'ud went to Khaybar and separated among the palms, and 'Abdullah ibn Sahl was killed. 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sahl and Huwayyisa and Muhayyisa, the sons of Mas'ud, came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and spoke about their companion. 'Abd ar-Rahman began, and he was the youngest of them. The Prophet said to him, "Let the elder go first," meaning let the eldest take the lead in speaking. They spoke about their companion, and the Prophet said, "Establish your right to your slain man by the oaths of fifty of you." They said, "Messenger of God, it is something we did not see." He said, "Then the Jews will clear themselves by the oaths of fifty of them." They said, "Messenger of God, they are unbelievers." So the Messenger of God paid his blood money from his own funds.

situation: In anger, a person wants to curse someone's face and the faces of those who look like him.
wise_response: Abu Hurayra said not to say "May God make your face ugly, and the face of anyone who resembles you," because God created Adam in his image.
why_it_worked: Every human face shares in the dignity given to Adam. An insult to one face insults all who resemble it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hurling curses at a person's appearance and family in a moment of anger.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَجْلاَنَ، عَنْ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ تَقُولَنَّ‏:‏ قَبَّحَ اللَّهُ وَجْهَكَ وَوَجْهَ مَنْ أَشْبَهَ وَجْهَكَ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ خَلَقَ آدَمَ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى صُورَتِهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Do not say: May God make your face ugly, and the face of whoever resembles your face. For God, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam in his image.

situation: The Prophet passed an animal that had been branded on the face, its nostrils still smoking.
wise_response: He said God curses whoever did this, and forbade anyone to brand or strike the face.
why_it_worked: Animals feel pain. Marking or hitting the face is needless cruelty to a creature that cannot protest.
tempting_wrong_answer: Branding an animal wherever is easiest without regard for its suffering.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا خَالِدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَبِي الزُّبَيْرِ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ قَالَ‏:‏ مَرَّ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِدَابَّةٍ قَدْ وُسِمَ يُدَخِّنُ مَنْخِرَاهُ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ فَعَلَ هَذَا، لاَ يَسِمَنَّ أَحَدٌ الْوَجْهَ وَلاَ يَضْرِبَنَّهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, peace be upon him, passed by an animal that had been branded, its nostrils smoking. The Prophet said: God has cursed whoever did this. Let no one brand the face, and let no one strike it.

situation: Mu'awiya ibn Suwayd slapped a freedman of his household, who ran off. His father called them both in.
wise_response: His father told the freedman to take his retaliation. Then he told how one of the seven sons of Muqarrin had slapped their only servant, and the Prophet ordered her freed. When told she was their only servant, he said to keep her until they could do without her and then let her go.
why_it_worked: A slap given in anger is a real wrong to the one under your hand. The father put justice for the weaker party above his son's pride.
tempting_wrong_answer: Shrugging off the slap because the one struck is of lower standing.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ سُفْيَانَ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي سَلَمَةُ بْنُ كُهَيْلٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ سُوَيْدِ بْنِ مُقَرِّنٍ قَالَ‏:‏ لَطَمْتُ مَوْلًى لَنَا فَفَرَّ، فَدَعَانِي أَبِي فَقَالَ لَهُ‏:‏ اقْتَصَّ، كُنَّا وَلَدَ مُقَرِّنٍ سَبْعَةً، لَنَا خَادِمٌ، فَلَطَمَهَا أَحَدُنَا، فَذُكِرَ ذَلِكَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ‏:‏ مُرْهُمْ فَلْيُعْتِقُوهَا، فَقِيلَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ خَادِمٌ غَيْرَهَا، قَالَ‏:‏ فَلْيَسْتَخْدِمُوهَا فَإِذَا اسْتَغْنَوْا خَلُّوا سَبِيلَهَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I slapped a freedman of ours and he ran away. My father called me and said to him: Take your retaliation. We, the sons of Muqarrin, were seven, and we had one servant. One of us slapped her. That was mentioned to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and he said: Tell them to free her. The Prophet was told: They have no servant but her. He said: Then let them keep her in service, and when they can do without her, let them set her free.

key_terms.اقتص (iqtass): take your retaliation, take your due

situation: Ibn Umar had beaten one of his servants. Later he called him over and looked at his back.
wise_response: He asked, "Does it hurt?" The servant said no, and Ibn Umar freed him anyway. He said he earned no reward for it, because the Prophet said that whoever beats a slave for an offence he did not commit, or slaps his face, must free him as expiation.
why_it_worked: He judged himself by the Prophet's standard and set the wrong right, even after the pain had passed.
tempting_wrong_answer: Deciding no amends are needed because the bruises have faded.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَوَانَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا فِرَاسٌ، عَنْ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ زَاذَانَ أَبِي عُمَرَ قَالَ‏:‏ كُنَّا عِنْدَ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، فَدَعَا بِغُلاَمٍ لَهُ كَانَ ضَرَبَهُ فَكَشَفَ عَنْ ظَهْرِهِ فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَيُوجِعُكَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ‏.‏ فَأَعْتَقَهُ، ثُمَّ رَفَعَ عُودًا مِنَ الأَرْضِ فَقَالَ‏:‏ مَالِي فِيهِ مِنَ الأَجْرِ مَا يَزِنُ هَذَا الْعُودَ، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، لِمَ تَقُولُ هَذَا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ أَوْ قَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ ضَرَبَ مَمْلُوكَهُ حَدًّا لَمْ يَأْتِهِ، أَوْ لَطَمَ وَجْهَهُ، فَكَفَّارَتُهُ أَنْ يُعْتِقَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: We were with Ibn Umar. He called for a servant of his whom he had beaten, uncovered his back and said: Does it hurt you? He said: No. So he freed him. Then he picked a stick up from the ground and said: I have no reward in this, not even the weight of this stick. I said: Abu Abd ar-Rahman, why do you say this? He said: I heard the Prophet, peace be upon him, say: Whoever beats his slave with a punishment for something he did not do, or slaps his face, his expiation is to free him.

situation: The strong often take from the weak and assume no one will hold them to account.
wise_response: The Prophet said every right will be returned to its owner, even to the hornless sheep against the horned one that butted it.
why_it_worked: No wrong is too small to be answered. That should restrain the strong now.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating small wrongs against the powerless as if they do not count.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الرَّبِيعِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الْعَلاَءُ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ لَتُؤَدُّنَّ الْحُقُوقَ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا، حَتَّى يُقَادَ لِلشَّاةِ الْجَمَّاءِ مِنَ الشَّاةِ الْقَرْنَاءِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: You will surely render rights to those they are owed, until retaliation is given to the hornless sheep from the horned sheep.

situation: The Prophet called a young servant girl and she was slow to come. Anger showed in his face. Umm Salama found the girl playing.
wise_response: Holding only a tooth-stick, he said to the girl, "Were it not for fear of retaliation on the Day of Resurrection, I would have hurt you with this tooth-stick." He did not strike her.
why_it_worked: Even justified anger did not license harm. Knowing he would answer for it, he held back.
tempting_wrong_answer: Striking a child or servant for being slow or distracted.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الْجُعْفِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أُسَامَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي دَاوُدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ مَوْلَى بَنِي هَاشِمٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَتْنِي جَدَّتِي، عَنْ أُمِّ سَلَمَةَ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ فِي بَيْتِهَا، فَدَعَا وَصِيفَةً لَهُ أَوْ لَهَا فَأَبْطَأَتْ، فَاسْتَبَانَ الْغَضَبُ فِي وَجْهِهِ، فَقَامَتْ أُمُّ سَلَمَةَ إِلَى الْحِجَابِ، فَوَجَدَتِ الْوَصِيفَةَ تَلْعَبُ، وَمَعَهُ سِوَاكٌ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ لَوْلاَ خَشْيَةُ الْقَوَدِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، لَأَوْجَعْتُكِ بِهَذَا السِّوَاكِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, peace be upon him, was in her house. He called a young servant girl of his, or of hers, and she was slow. Anger showed in his face. Umm Salama went to the curtain and found the girl playing. He had a tooth-stick with him and said: Were it not for fear of retaliation on the Day of Resurrection, I would have hurt you with this tooth-stick.

situation: A young man met Abu'l-Yasar and saw that he and his servant each wore one striped cloak and one plainer garment. He suggested they swap so each would have a matching set.
wise_response: Abu'l-Yasar blessed him and said he had heard the Prophet say, "Feed them from what you eat and clothe them from what you wear." He said giving his servant worldly goods was easier for him than losing his good deeds to him on the Day of Resurrection.
why_it_worked: He gave his servant the same as himself. Equal treatment mattered more to him than looking well dressed.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping the better clothes for oneself and dressing the servant in leftovers.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبَّادٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَاتِمُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ مُجَاهِدِ أَبِي حَزْرَةَ، عَنْ عُبَادَةَ بْنِ الْوَلِيدِ بْنِ عُبَادَةَ بْنِ الصَّامِتِ قَالَ‏:‏ خَرَجْتُ أَنَا وَأَبِي نَطْلُبُ الْعِلْمَ فِي هَذَا الْحَيِّ فِي الأَنْصَارِ، قَبْلَ أَنْ يَهْلِكُوا، فَكَانَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ لَقِينَا أَبُو الْيَسَرِ صَاحِبُ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَمَعَهُ غُلاَمٌ لَهُ، وَعَلَى أَبِي الْيَسَرِ بُرْدَةٌ وَمَعَافِرِيٌّ، وَعَلَى غُلاَمِهِ بُرْدَةٌ وَمَعَافِرِيٌّ، فَقُلْتُ لَهُ‏:‏ يَا عَمِّي، لَوْ أَخَذْتَ بُرْدَةَ غُلاَمِكَ وَأَعْطَيْتَهُ مَعَافِرِيَّكَ، أَوْ أَخَذْتَ مَعَافِرِيَّهُ وَأَعْطَيْتَهُ بُرْدَتَكَ، كَانَتْ عَلَيْكَ حُلَّةٌ أَوْ عَلَيْهِ حُلَّةٌ، فَمَسَحَ رَأْسِي وَقَالَ‏:‏ اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ فِيهِ، يَا ابْنَ أَخِي، بَصَرُ عَيْنَيَّ هَاتَيْنِ، وَسَمْعُ أُذُنَيَّ هَاتَيْنِ، وَوَعَاهُ قَلْبِي وَأَشَارَ إِلَى نِيَاطِ قَلْبِهِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ أَطْعِمُوهُمْ مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ، وَاكْسُوهُمْ مِمَّا تَلْبَسُونَ وَكَانَ أَنْ أُعْطِيَهُ مِنْ مَتَاعِ الدُّنْيَا أَهْوَنُ عَلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ مِنْ حَسَنَاتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: My father and I went out seeking knowledge among this clan of the Ansar before they passed away. The first we met was Abu'l-Yasar, Companion of the Prophet, peace be upon him, with a servant of his. Abu'l-Yasar wore a striped cloak and a Ma'afiri garment, and his servant wore a striped cloak and a Ma'afiri garment. I said to him: Uncle, if you took your servant's cloak and gave him your Ma'afiri garment, or took his Ma'afiri garment and gave him your cloak, you would have a full suit and he would have a full suit. He stroked my head and said: O God, bless him. Nephew, these two eyes of mine saw, and these two ears of mine heard, and this heart held it, and he pointed to his heart, the Prophet saying: Feed them from what you eat and clothe them from what you wear. That I give him of the goods of this world is easier for me than that he should take from my good deeds on the Day of Resurrection.

situation: Abu Dharr traded insults with a man and shamed him by mentioning his mother. The man complained to the Prophet.
wise_response: The Prophet asked, "Did you shame him through his mother?" and then said those under your hand are your brothers. Feed them what you eat, clothe them as you dress, do not overburden them, and if you do, help them. Abu Dharr afterwards dressed his servant as he dressed himself.
why_it_worked: Calling them brothers removed any ground for contempt. Abu Dharr took the correction to heart and changed how he lived.
tempting_wrong_answer: Mocking someone's lineage and treating those who serve you as lesser beings.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا آدَمُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا وَاصِلٌ الأَحْدَبُ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ الْمَعْرُورَ بْنَ سُوَيْدٍ يَقُولُ‏:‏ رَأَيْتُ أَبَا ذَرٍّ وَعَلَيْهِ حُلَّةٌ وَعَلَى غُلاَمِهِ حُلَّةٌ، فَسَأَلْنَاهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ إِنِّي سَابَبْتُ رَجُلاً فَشَكَانِي إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَ لِيَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ أَعَيَّرْتَهُ بِأُمِّهِ‏؟‏ قُلْتُ‏:‏ نَعَمْ، ثُمَّ قَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّ إِخْوَانَكُمْ خَوَلُكُمْ، جَعَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ تَحْتَ أَيْدِيكُمْ، فَمَنْ كَانَ أَخُوهُ تَحْتَ يَدَيْهِ فَلْيُطْعِمْهُ مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ، وَلْيُلْبِسْهُ مِمَّا يَلْبَسُ، وَلاَ تُكَلِّفُوهُمْ مَا يَغْلِبُهُمْ، فَإِنْ كَلَّفْتُمُوهُمْ مَا يَغْلِبُهُمْ فَأَعِينُوهُمْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I saw Abu Dharr wearing a robe and his servant wearing a robe, and we asked him about that. He said: I traded insults with a man and he complained about me to the Prophet, peace be upon him. The Prophet said to me: Did you shame him through his mother? I said: Yes. Then he said: Your brothers are your dependants. God has placed them under your hands. Whoever has his brother under his hand, let him feed him from what he eats and clothe him from what he wears. Do not burden them with what overwhelms them, and if you burden them with what overwhelms them, then help them.

situation: A person spends money feeding himself and his household and wonders whether that counts for anything.
wise_response: The Prophet said what you feed yourself is charity, and what you feed your child, your wife and your servant is charity.
why_it_worked: Providing for those who depend on you is itself a good deed.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being tight-fisted at home while thinking only gifts to outsiders count.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا بَقِيَّةُ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي بَحِيرُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ مَعْدَانَ، عَنِ الْمِقْدَامِ، سَمِعَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ مَا أَطْعَمْتَ نَفْسَكَ فَهُوَ صَدَقَةٌ، وَمَا أَطْعَمْتَ وَلَدَكَ وَزَوْجَتَكَ وَخَادِمَكَ فَهُوَ صَدَقَةٌ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: What you feed yourself is charity, and what you feed your child, your wife and your servant is charity.

situation: A person wants to give charity but has a family that depends on him.
wise_response: The Prophet said the best charity leaves you still self-sufficient, the giving hand is better than the taking hand, and you should begin with those you support. Your wife, your servant and your child all look to you.
why_it_worked: Duty starts at home. Giving away what your dependants need wrongs them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving lavishly to others for show while one's own family goes without.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ بَهْدَلَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ خَيْرُ الصَّدَقَةِ مَا بَقَّى غِنًى، وَالْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ السُّفْلَى، وَابْدَأْ بِمَنْ تَعُولُ، تَقُولُ امْرَأَتُكَ‏:‏ أَنْفِقْ عَلَيَّ أَوْ طَلِّقْنِي، وَيَقُولُ مَمْلُوكُكَ‏:‏ أَنْفِقْ عَلَيَّ أَوْ بِعْنِي، وَيَقُولُ وَلَدُكَ‏:‏ إِلَى مَنْ تَكِلُنَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The best charity is what leaves sufficiency behind. The upper hand is better than the lower hand. Begin with those you support. Your wife says: Spend on me or divorce me. Your slave says: Spend on me or sell me. Your child says: To whom will you leave us?

situation: A servant brings a meal he has prepared and sets it before his master.
wise_response: The Prophet said the master should sit the servant down to eat with him. If the servant will not, the master should hand him some of the food.
why_it_worked: The one who made the food deserves to share it. Eating together honours him.
tempting_wrong_answer: Eating in front of the servant who cooked and sending him away with nothing.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ أَبِي خَالِدٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ إِذَا جَاءَ أَحَدَكُمْ خَادِمُهُ بِطَعَامِهِ فَلْيُجْلِسْهُ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْبَلْ فَلْيُنَاوِلْهُ مِنْهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: When the servant of one of you brings him his food, let him seat him with him. If he will not accept, let him hand him some of it.

situation: The Prophet asked a riddle about a tree like a Muslim. The young Ibn 'Umar knew the answer, the palm, but kept quiet because Abu Bakr and 'Umar were present and had not spoken.
wise_response: He held back out of deference to his elders. Afterward his father 'Umar told him he would have loved for him to say it.
why_it_worked: The son showed respect by not jumping ahead of senior men. His father showed that elders should welcome a young person's right answer.
tempting_wrong_answer: Rushing to show off in front of elders, or an elder resenting a younger person who knows more.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللهِ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي نَافِعٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ أَخْبِرُونِي بِشَجَرَةٍ مَثَلُهَا مَثَلُ الْمُسْلِمِ، تُؤْتِي أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينٍ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهَا، لاَ تَحُتُّ وَرَقَهَا، فَوَقَعَ فِي نَفْسِي النَّخْلَةُ، فَكَرِهْتُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ، وَثَمَّ أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَعُمَرُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، فَلَمَّا لَمْ يَتَكَلَّمَا قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ هِيَ النَّخْلَةُ، فَلَمَّا خَرَجْتُ مَعَ أَبِي قُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا أَبَتِ، وَقَعَ فِي نَفْسِي النَّخْلَةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَنْ تَقُولَهَا‏؟‏ لَوْ كُنْتَ قُلْتَهَا كَانَ أَحَبَّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ كَذَا وَكَذَا، قَالَ‏:‏ مَا مَنَعَنِي إِلاَّ لَمْ أَرَكَ، وَلاَ أَبَا بَكْرٍ تَكَلَّمْتُمَا، فَكَرِهْتُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Ibn 'Umar said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said, "Tell me of a tree whose likeness is the likeness of the Muslim. It gives its fruit at every season by the leave of its Lord, and its leaves do not fall." The palm tree came to my mind, but I disliked speaking, since Abu Bakr and 'Umar were there. When they did not speak, the Prophet said, "It is the palm." When I went out with my father I said, "Father, the palm came to my mind." He said, "What stopped you from saying it? Had you said it, it would have been dearer to me than such and such." I said, "Nothing stopped me except that I did not see you or Abu Bakr speak, so I disliked to."

situation: Qays ibn 'Asim, dying, gave his sons his last advice.
wise_response: He told them to fear God and make the eldest their leader, to keep and manage their wealth well, to avoid begging from people, not to wail over him, and to bury him where an old enemy tribe he had raided would not find his grave.
why_it_worked: A family led by its eldest carries on the father's standing. Earning your own keep spares you from depending on mean people.
tempting_wrong_answer: Putting the youngest in charge, wasting wealth, or living off what others give.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ مَرْزُوقٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ مُطَرِّفًا، عَنْ حَكِيمِ بْنِ قَيْسِ بْنِ عَاصِمٍ، أَنَّ أَبَاهُ أَوْصَى عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ بَنِيهِ فَقَالَ‏:‏ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَسَوِّدُوا أَكْبَرُكُمْ، فَإِنَّ الْقَوْمَ إِذَا سَوَّدُوا أَكْبَرَهُمْ خَلَفُوا أَبَاهُمْ، وَإِذَا سَوَّدُوا أَصْغَرَهُمْ أَزْرَى بِهِمْ ذَلِكَ فِي أَكْفَائِهِمْ‏.‏ وَعَلَيْكُمْ بِالْمَالِ وَاصْطِنَاعِهِ، فَإِنَّهُ مَنْبَهَةٌ لِلْكَرِيمِ، وَيُسْتَغْنَى بِهِ عَنِ اللَّئِيمِ‏.‏ وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَمَسْأَلَةَ النَّاسِ، فَإِنَّهَا مِنْ آخِرِ كَسْبِ الرَّجُلِ‏.‏ وَإِذَا مُتُّ فَلاَ تَنُوحُوا، فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يُنَحْ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ وَإِذَا مُتُّ فَادْفِنُونِي بِأَرْضٍ لاَ يَشْعُرُ بِدَفْنِي بَكْرُ بْنُ وَائِلٍ، فَإِنِّي كُنْتُ أُغَافِلُهُمْ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Hakim ibn Qays ibn 'Asim reported that his father advised his sons at his death: "Fear God, and make your eldest your chief. When a people make their eldest their chief, they succeed their father; when they make their youngest their chief, it shames them before their peers. Hold to wealth and its good use, for it raises the noble and frees one from need of the base. Beware of asking people, for it is the last of a man's earnings. When I die, do not wail, for there was no wailing over the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. And when I die, bury me in a land where Bakr ibn Wa'il will not know of my burial, for I used to take them unawares in the Jahiliyya."

situation: When the first ripening dates of the season were brought to the Prophet.
wise_response: He prayed for blessing on the city and its measures, then handed a date to the youngest child near him.
why_it_worked: Giving the first fruit to the smallest child shows tenderness to children and lets them share in the joy.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping the first and best for the adults, or for yourself.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ، عَنْ سُهَيْلِ بْنِ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا أُتِيَ بِالزَّهْوِ قَالَ‏:‏ اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَنَا فِي مَدِينَتِنَا وَمُدِّنَا، وَصَاعِنَا، بَرَكَةً مَعَ بَرَكَةٍ، ثُمَّ نَاوَلَهُ أَصْغَرَ مَنْ يَلِيهِ مِنَ الْوِلْدَانِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayra said: When the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, was brought the first ripening dates, he would say, "O God, bless us in our city, our mudd and our sa', blessing upon blessing." Then he would hand it to the youngest of the children near him.

situation: On the way to a meal with his companions, the Prophet saw his grandson Husayn playing in the road.
wise_response: He hurried ahead of the others, opened his arms, and chased the boy this way and that, making him laugh until he caught him. Then he held him, kissed him and said, "Husayn is from me and I am from him."
why_it_worked: He put the child's joy ahead of his own dignity before others. Play and affection show love a child can feel.
tempting_wrong_answer: Walking past a child at play to keep up appearances in front of grown men.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، عَنْ رَاشِدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ يَعْلَى بْنِ مُرَّةَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ‏:‏ خَرَجْنَا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَدُعِينَا إِلَى طَعَامٍ فَإِذَا حُسَيْنٌ يَلْعَبُ فِي الطَّرِيقِ، فَأَسْرَعَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَمَامَ الْقَوْمِ، ثُمَّ بَسَطَ يَدَيْهِ، فَجَعَلَ يَمُرُّ مَرَّةً هَا هُنَا وَمَرَّةً هَا هُنَا، يُضَاحِكُهُ حَتَّى أَخَذَهُ، فَجَعَلَ إِحْدَى يَدَيْهِ فِي ذَقْنِهِ وَالأُخْرَى فِي رَأْسِهِ، ثُمَّ اعْتَنَقَهُ فَقَبَّلَهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ حُسَيْنٌ مِنِّي وَأَنَا مِنْهُ، أَحَبَّ اللَّهُ مَنْ أَحَبَّ الْحَسَنَ وَالْحُسَيْنَ، سَبِطَانِ مِنَ الأَسْبَاطِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Ya'la ibn Murra said: We went out with the Prophet, peace be upon him, invited to a meal, and there was Husayn playing in the road. The Prophet hurried ahead of the people and spread his arms, and the boy began running here and there while he made him laugh, until he caught him. He put one hand under his chin and the other on his head, then hugged and kissed him. Then the Prophet said, "Husayn is from me and I am from him. God loves whoever loves al-Hasan and al-Husayn. They are two grandsons among the grandsons."

situation: Young 'A'isha played with dolls in the Prophet's home, and her friends would hide when he came in.
wise_response: He would send her friends back in to her so they could keep playing.
why_it_worked: He let children be children and made sure his presence did not spoil their play.
tempting_wrong_answer: Expecting children to go silent and scatter whenever an adult enters.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَلامٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ خَازِمٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامُ بْنُ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ قَالَتْ‏:‏ كُنْتُ أَلْعَبُ بِالْبَنَاتِ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَكَانَ لِي صَوَاحِبُ يَلْعَبْنَ مَعِي، فَكَانَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا دَخَلَ يَنْقَمِعْنَ مِنْهُ، فَيُسَرِّبُهُنَّ إِلَيَّ، فَيَلْعَبْنَ مَعِي‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: 'A'isha said: I used to play with dolls in the presence of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and I had friends who played with me. When the Messenger of God came in, they would slip away from him, and he would send them back to me, and they would play with me.

situation: People who are hard toward others and still hope for God's kindness.
wise_response: The Prophet said: whoever does not have mercy on people, God will not have mercy on him.
why_it_worked: The mercy you hope to receive is tied to the mercy you give.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being harsh with others while counting on mercy for yourself.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ بْنُ حَفْصٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي زَيْدُ بْنُ وَهْبٍ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ جَرِيرًا، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ لاَ يَرْحَمِ النَّاسَ لاَ يَرْحَمْهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Jarir reported that the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever does not have mercy on people, God, mighty and majestic, will not have mercy on him."

situation: How a person who wants pardon should treat others.
wise_response: 'Umar said: whoever does not show mercy is not shown mercy, whoever does not forgive is not forgiven, whoever does not pardon is not pardoned, and whoever does not guard himself is not guarded.
why_it_worked: What you give others comes back to you in kind.
tempting_wrong_answer: Holding grudges while hoping others, and God, will let your faults go.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي عَبْدُ الْمَلِكِ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ قَبِيصَةَ بْنَ جَابِرٍ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ عُمَرَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ لاَ يَرْحَمُ لاَ يُرْحَمُ، وَلاَ يُغْفَرُ مَنْ لاَ يَغْفِرُ، وَلاَ يُعْفَ عَمَّنْ لَمْ يَعْفُ، وَلاَ يُوقَّ مَنْ لا يَتَوَقَّ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: 'Umar said: "Whoever does not show mercy is not shown mercy. Whoever does not forgive is not forgiven. Whoever does not pardon is not pardoned. And whoever does not guard himself is not guarded."

situation: Safwan brought Umar a large bowl of food. Umar called the poor and the slaves of those around him to eat with him.
wise_response: Umar condemned people who disdain to let their slaves eat with them. Safwan answered honestly that they did not disdain them but kept the good food for themselves because there was not enough to go round.
why_it_worked: Umar showed by his own table that rank does not decide who eats. Safwan named the real motive plainly.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping the best food for oneself and making excuses for leaving dependants out.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو يُونُسَ الْبَصْرِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي مُلَيْكَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ أَبُو مَحْذُورَةَ‏:‏ كُنْتُ جَالِسًا عِنْدَ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، إِذْ جَاءَ صَفْوَانُ بْنُ أُمَيَّةَ بِجَفْنَةٍ يَحْمِلُهَا نَفَرٌ فِي عَبَاءَةٍ، فَوَضَعُوهَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ عُمَرَ، فَدَعَا عُمَرُ نَاسًا مَسَاكِينَ وَأَرِقَّاءَ مِنْ أَرِقَّاءِ النَّاسِ حَوْلَهُ، فَأَكَلُوا مَعَهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ‏:‏ فَعَلَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ، أَوْ قَالَ‏:‏ لَحَا اللَّهُ قَوْمًا يَرْغَبُونَ عَنْ أَرِقَّائِهِمْ أَنْ يَأْكُلُوا مَعَهُمْ، فَقَالَ صَفْوَانُ‏:‏ أَمَا وَاللَّهِ، مَا نَرْغَبُ عَنْهُمْ، وَلَكِنَّا نَسْتَأْثِرُ عَلَيْهِمْ، لاَ نَجْدُ وَاللَّهِ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ الطِّيبِ مَا نَأْكُلُ وَنُطْعِمُهُمْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I was sitting with Umar when Safwan ibn Umayya came with a large bowl carried by a group of men in a cloak. They set it down before Umar. Umar called some poor people and some of the slaves of the people around him, and they ate with him. Then he said: May God deal with a people, or he said: May God shame a people, who disdain to have their slaves eat with them. Safwan said: By God, we do not disdain them, but we keep the best for ourselves. By God, we do not find enough good food to eat and to feed them too.

situation: A man told the Prophet that when he slaughters a sheep he feels mercy for it.
wise_response: The Prophet said, "And the sheep, if you have mercy on it, God will have mercy on you," twice.
why_it_worked: Kindness to an animal, even one you must kill for food, counts with God.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating an animal roughly because it is going to be slaughtered anyway.

situation: What it means when a person loses all tenderness for others.
wise_response: The Prophet said: mercy is taken away only from one who is wretched.
why_it_worked: A heart without mercy is a sign of ruin. Tenderness is something to guard.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting yourself grow hard and indifferent to others' suffering.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا آدَمُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ، سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عُثْمَانَ مَوْلَى الْمُغِيرَةِ بْنِ شُعْبَةَ يَقُولُ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ يَقُولُ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الصَّادِقَ الْمَصْدُوقَ أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ لاَ تُنْزَعُ الرَّحْمَةُ إِلا مِنْ شَقِيٍّ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayra said: I heard the Prophet, the truthful and the confirmed, Abu al-Qasim, peace be upon him, say: "Mercy is not taken away except from a wretched one."

situation: The Prophet's infant son Ibrahim was with a wet nurse whose husband was a blacksmith, in a house full of smoke.
wise_response: The Prophet would go there, and in the smoky house he would kiss the child and smell him.
why_it_worked: Anas called him the most merciful of people to his family. He showed it by going to the child in a humble, smoky home.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping your distance from your small children and leaving their care wholly to others.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا حَرَمِيُّ بْنُ حَفْصٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا وُهَيْبٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ قَالَ‏:‏ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَرْحَمَ النَّاسِ بِالْعِيَالِ، وَكَانَ لَهُ ابْنٌ مُسْتَرْضَعٌ فِي نَاحِيَةِ الْمَدِينَةِ، وَكَانَ ظِئْرُهُ قَيْنًا، وَكُنَّا نَأْتِيهِ، وَقَدْ دَخَنَ الْبَيْتُ بِإِذْخِرٍ، فَيُقَبِّلُهُ وَيَشُمُّهُ‏.‏

situation: A man came to the Prophet with a small boy and kept hugging him close.
wise_response: The Prophet asked, "Do you have mercy on him?" The man said yes. He said, "God is more merciful to you than you are to him, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful."
why_it_worked: The tender love a parent feels is a small sign of God's greater mercy. Affection for a child is good and natural.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hiding tenderness for a child as if it were weakness.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مَرْوَانُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ بْنُ كَيْسَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ أَتَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَجُلٌ وَمَعَهُ صَبِيٌّ، فَجَعَلَ يَضُمُّهُ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ أَتَرْحَمُهُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ نَعَمْ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَاللَّهُ أَرْحَمُ بِكَ مِنْكَ بِهِ، وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ‏.‏

situation: A thirsty traveler climbed down a well and drank. When he came up he saw a dog panting and licking the damp earth from thirst.
wise_response: He thought, "This dog is as thirsty as I was," went back down, filled his leather sock with water, held it in his teeth as he climbed, and gave the dog a drink. God thanked him and forgave him. Asked if there is reward for animals, the Prophet said, "In every living creature there is reward."
why_it_worked: He saw his own suffering in the dog and acted on it, even at real effort. Kindness to any living thing counts.
tempting_wrong_answer: Walking on once your own thirst is gone, since it is only a dog.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ سُمَيٍّ مَوْلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي صَالِحٍ السَّمَّانِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ بَيْنَمَا رَجُلٌ يَمْشِي بِطَرِيقٍ اشْتَدَّ بِهِ الْعَطَشُ، فَوَجَدَ بِئْرًا فَنَزَلَ فِيهَا، فَشَرِبَ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ، فَإِذَا كَلْبٌ يَلْهَثُ، يَأْكُلُ الثَّرَى مِنَ الْعَطَشِ، فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ‏:‏ لَقَدْ بَلَغَ هَذَا الْكَلْبَ مِنَ الْعَطَشِ مِثْلُ الَّذِي كَانَ بَلَغَنِي، فَنَزَلَ الْبِئْرَ فَمَلَأَ خُفَّاهُ، ثُمَّ أَمْسَكَهَا بِفِيهِ، فَسَقَى الْكَلْبَ، فَشَكَرَ اللَّهُ لَهُ، فَغَفَرَ لَهُ، قَالُوا‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، وَإِنَّ لَنَا فِي الْبَهَائِمِ أَجْرًا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ فِي كُلِّ ذَاتِ كَبِدٍ رَطْبَةٍ أَجْرٌ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayra reported that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "While a man was walking on a road, his thirst grew severe. He found a well, went down into it, drank, and came out. There was a dog panting, eating the damp earth from thirst. The man said, 'This dog has reached the thirst that I had reached.' He went down the well, filled his leather sock, held it in his mouth, and gave the dog water. God thanked him for it and forgave him." They said, "Messenger of God, is there reward for us in animals?" He said, "In every creature with a moist liver there is reward."

situation: A woman locked up a cat until it died of hunger.
wise_response: The Prophet said she was punished for it and entered the Fire. She neither fed it nor gave it water while she held it, nor let it go to eat the small creatures of the earth.
why_it_worked: If you take control of a creature, you owe it food and water or its freedom. Cruelty to an animal is a serious wrong.
tempting_wrong_answer: Confining an animal and neglecting it.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ عُذِّبَتِ امْرَأَةٌ فِي هِرَّةٍ حَبَسَتْهَا حَتَّى مَاتَتْ جُوعًا، فَدَخَلَتِ فِيهَا النَّارَ، يُقَالُ، وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ‏:‏ لاَ أَنْتِ أَطْعَمْتِيهَا، وَلاَ سَقِيتِيهَا حِينَ حَبَسْتِيهَا، وَلاَ أَنْتِ أَرْسَلْتِيهَا، فَأَكَلَتْ مِنْ خَشَاشِ الأَرْضِ‏.‏

situation: How people should treat one another's faults and needs.
wise_response: The Prophet said: show mercy and you will be shown mercy, forgive and God will forgive you. Woe to the funnels of speech, and woe to those who persist knowingly in what they have done.
why_it_worked: Mercy and forgiveness come back to the one who gives them. Taking in good words and letting them run out without acting, or holding on to a known wrong, brings ruin.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hearing good counsel without heeding it, and carrying on with a wrong you know is wrong.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عُقْبَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ الْقُرَشِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَرِيزٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حِبَّانُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ الشَّرْعَبِيُّ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ ارْحَمُوا تُرْحَمُوا، وَاغْفِرُوا يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ، وَيْلٌ لأَقْمَاعِ الْقَوْلِ، وَيْلٌ لِلْمُصِرِّينَ الَّذِينَ يُصِرُّونَ عَلَى مَا فَعَلُوا وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As reported that the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Have mercy and you will be shown mercy. Forgive and God will forgive you. Woe to the funnels of speech. Woe to the persistent, who persist in what they have done while they know."

situation: A person is tempted to cut off relatives.
wise_response: The Prophet related that kinship stood before Allah seeking refuge from being cut. Allah promised to stay connected to whoever keeps it and to cut off whoever cuts it.
why_it_worked: How one treats one's kin is tied to one's own standing with Allah.
tempting_wrong_answer: Severing family ties over grievances or convenience.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبِي أُوَيْسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ بِلاَلٍ، عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ أَبِي مُزَرِّدٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ الْخَلْقَ، فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْهُ قَامَتِ الرَّحِمُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ مَهْ، قَالَتْ‏:‏ هَذَا مَقَامُ الْعَائِذِ بِكَ مِنَ الْقَطِيعَةِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَلاَ تَرْضَيْنَ أَنْ أَصِلَ مَنْ وَصَلَكِ، وَأَقْطَعَ مَنْ قَطَعَكِ‏؟‏ قَالَتْ‏:‏ بَلَى يَا رَبِّ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَذَلِكَ لَكِ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ‏:‏ اقْرَؤُوا إِنْ شِئْتُمْ‏:‏ ‏{‏فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا فِي الأَرْضِ وَتُقَطِّعُوا أَرْحَامَكُمْ‏}‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the creation. When He had finished it, kinship stood up. He said, "What is it?" It said, "This is the place of one who seeks refuge with You from being cut off." He said, "Will you not be content that I keep connection with whoever keeps connection with you, and cut off whoever cuts you off?" It said, "Yes, my Lord." He said, "Then that is yours." Then Abu Hurayra said: Recite if you wish: {Would you then, if you turned away, cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship?}

key_terms.الرحم (ar-rahim): the womb; the bond of kinship

situation: A person is asked for help by relatives, the poor or travelers, sometimes when he has nothing to give.
wise_response: Ibn 'Abbas explained the verses: give kin, the poor and the traveler their due when you can. When you have nothing, speak to them with an easy, kind word and a hopeful promise. Do not be tight-fisted, and do not give away everything so you are left blamed and stripped bare.
why_it_worked: Generosity has a measure. A kind word honors those you cannot help now, and keeping something back lets you help those who come later.
tempting_wrong_answer: Turning people away harshly, hoarding, or giving everything in one burst and having nothing left.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا الْحُمَيْدِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعْدٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي مُوسَى، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ ‏{‏وَآتِ ذَا الْقُرْبَى حَقَّهُ وَالْمِسْكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ‏.‏‏.‏‏.‏‏}‏، قَالَ‏:‏ بَدَأَ فَأَمَرَهُ بِأَوْجَبِ الْحُقُوقِ، وَدَلَّهُ عَلَى أَفْضَلِ الأَعْمَالِ إِذَا كَانَ عِنْدَهُ شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ‏:‏ ‏{‏وَآتِ ذَا الْقُرْبَى حَقَّهُ وَالْمِسْكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ‏}‏، وَعَلَّمَهُ إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَهُ شَيْءٌ كَيْفَ يَقُولُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ ‏{‏وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ابْتِغَاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا فَقُلْ لَهُمْ قَوْلاً مَيْسُورًا‏}‏ عِدَّةً حَسَنَةً كَأَنَّهُ قَدْ كَانَ، وَلَعَلَّهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ، ‏{‏وَلاَ تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَى عُنُقِكَ‏}‏ لاَ تُعْطِي شَيْئًا، ‏{‏وَلاَ تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ‏}‏ تُعْطِي مَا عِنْدَكَ، ‏{‏فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًا‏}‏ يَلُومُكَ مَنْ يَأْتِيكَ بَعْدُ، وَلاَ يَجِدُ عِنْدَكَ شَيْئًا ‏{‏مَحْسُورًا‏}‏، قَالَ‏:‏ قَدْ حَسَّرَكَ مَنْ قَدْ أَعْطَيْتَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: About {Give the relative his due, and the poor and the traveler} he said: He began by commanding the most binding of rights and directed him to the best of deeds if he has something, saying {Give the relative his due, and the poor and the traveler}. And He taught him what to say if he has nothing: {And if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord that you hope for, then speak to them a gentle word}, a good promise, as if it had already happened, and perhaps it will be, if Allah wills. {And do not make your hand chained to your neck}, giving nothing, {nor stretch it out fully}, giving all you have, {so that you sit blamed}, blamed by whoever comes to you afterward and finds nothing with you, {and stripped bare}. He said: The one you gave everything to has left you stripped.

situation: A man told the Prophet his relatives cut him off, mistreat him, and act foolishly toward him, while he keeps ties, treats them well, and stays patient.
wise_response: The Prophet said that if it was as he said, it was as if he were feeding them hot ashes, and he would always have a helper from Allah against them as long as he kept on.
why_it_worked: Answering bad treatment with good shames the wrongdoer and keeps Allah's support with the one who persists.
tempting_wrong_answer: Paying relatives back in kind and dropping them because they dropped you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عُبَيْدِ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ أَتَى رَجُلٌ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، إِنَّ لِي قَرَابَةً أَصِلُهُمْ وَيَقْطَعُونَ، وَأُحْسِنُ إِلَيْهِمْ وَيُسِيئُونَ إِلَيَّ، وَيَجْهَلُونَ عَلَيَّ وَأَحْلُمُ عَنْهُمْ، قَالَ‏:‏ لَئِنْ كَانَ كَمَا تَقُولُ كَأَنَّمَا تُسِفُّهُمُ الْمَلَّ، وَلاَ يَزَالُ مَعَكَ مِنَ اللهِ ظَهِيرٌ عَلَيْهِمْ مَا دُمْتَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and said, "Messenger of Allah, I have relatives. I keep ties with them and they cut me off. I treat them well and they treat me badly. They are rash with me and I am patient with them." He said, "If it is as you say, it is as though you are making them swallow hot ashes, and you will not be without a helper from Allah against them as long as you keep to that."

situation: A person hopes for more livelihood and a longer life.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever wants his provision widened and his life lengthened should keep his ties of kinship.
why_it_worked: Family bonds bring support, goodwill and blessing in return.
tempting_wrong_answer: Neglecting relatives while chasing wealth and security alone.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي اللَّيْثُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي عَقِيلٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whoever would love to have his provision made wide for him and his life extended should keep his ties of kinship.

situation: Abu Hurayra asked anyone who had cut off a relative to leave his gathering. A young man who had not spoken to his aunt for two years went to her.
wise_response: She asked why he had come, then sent him back to ask Abu Hurayra why he said it. Abu Hurayra reported the Prophet's words that people's deeds are presented to Allah each Thursday evening, and the deeds of one who cuts kinship are not accepted.
why_it_worked: A public reminder moved the young man to go and repair the break himself.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting a family rift sit for years out of pride.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الْخَزْرَجُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ أَبُو الْخَطَّابِ السَّعْدِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو أَيُّوبَ سُلَيْمَانُ مَوْلَى عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَفَّانَ قَالَ‏:‏ جَاءَنَا أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ عَشِيَّةَ الْخَمِيسِ لَيْلَةَ الْجُمُعَةِ فَقَالَ‏:‏ أُحَرِّجُ عَلَى كُلِّ قَاطِعِ رَحِمٍ لَمَا قَامَ مِنْ عِنْدِنَا، فَلَمْ يَقُمْ أَحَدٌ حَتَّى قَالَ ثَلاَثًا، فَأَتَى فَتًى عَمَّةً لَهُ قَدْ صَرَمَهَا مُنْذُ سَنَتَيْنِ، فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا، فَقَالَتْ لَهُ‏:‏ يَا ابْنَ أَخِي، مَا جَاءَ بِكَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ يَقُولُ كَذَا وَكَذَا، قَالَتِ‏:‏ ارْجِعْ إِلَيْهِ فَسَلْهُ‏:‏ لِمَ قَالَ ذَاكَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ إِنَّ أَعْمَالَ بَنِي آدَمَ تُعْرَضُ عَلَى اللهِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى عَشِيَّةَ كُلِّ خَمِيسٍ لَيْلَةَ الْجُمُعَةِ، فَلاَ يَقْبَلُ عَمَلَ قَاطِعِ رَحِمٍ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayra came to us on Thursday evening, the eve of Friday, and said, "I urge everyone who has cut off a relative to get up and leave us." No one stood until he had said it three times. Then a young man went to an aunt of his whom he had cut off for two years and went in to her. She said to him, "Nephew, what has brought you?" He said, "I heard Abu Hurayra say such and such." She said, "Go back to him and ask him why he said that." [Abu Hurayra] said, "I heard the Prophet, peace be upon him, say: The deeds of the children of Adam are presented to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, every Thursday evening, the eve of Friday, and He does not accept the deed of one who cuts kinship."

situation: A man has money to spend and wonders where to begin.
wise_response: Ibn 'Umar said whatever a man spends on himself and his family hoping for reward is rewarded. Begin with those you support. If there is extra, give to the nearest relative, then the next. If there is still extra, give it away.
why_it_worked: Charity has an order. Meeting your own dependents' needs first is itself a good deed.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving lavishly to outsiders for praise while one's own family goes short.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ أَبِي لَيْلَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ بْنُ جَابِرٍ الْحَنَفِيُّ، عَنْ آدَمَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ‏:‏ مَا أَنْفَقَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَأَهْلِهِ يَحْتَسِبُهَا إِلاَّ آجَرَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِيهَا، وَابْدَأْ بِمَنْ تَعُولُ، فَإِنْ كَانَ فَضْلاً فَالأَقْرَبَ الأَقْرَبَ، وَإِنْ كَانَ فَضْلاً فَنَاوِلْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whatever a man spends on himself and his family, counting it for Allah, Allah the Exalted rewards him for it. Begin with those you support. If there is extra, then the nearest and the nearest. If there is still extra, then hand it out.

situation: A person's relatives cut him off.
wise_response: The Prophet said the one who truly keeps ties is not the one who returns like for like. It is the one who, when his kin cut him off, reconnects.
why_it_worked: Keeping family ties only when others do is just trade. Real loyalty reaches out when it is not returned.
tempting_wrong_answer: Visiting only those who visit you and dropping those who drop you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ كَثِيرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، وَالْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، وَفِطْرٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قَالَ سُفْيَانُ لَمْ يَرْفَعْهُ الأَعْمَشُ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَرَفَعَهُ الْحَسَنُ وَفِطْرٌ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ لَيْسَ الْوَاصِلُ بِالْمُكَافِئِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْوَاصِلَ الَّذِي إِذَا قُطِعَتْ رَحِمُهُ وَصَلَهَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The one who keeps ties is not the one who repays in kind. The one who keeps ties is the one who, when his kinship is cut, restores it.

key_terms.المكافئ (al-mukafi'): one who merely repays like with like

situation: A bedouin asked the Prophet for a deed that would bring him into the Garden.
wise_response: The Prophet told him to free a slave and to help pay toward another's freedom, to lend a good milking animal, and to be kind to relatives. If he could not, then urge good and forbid wrong. If he could not do that, then hold his tongue except from good.
why_it_worked: Every person can do some good at their own level, down to simply guarding the tongue.
tempting_wrong_answer: Doing nothing because the greatest deeds seem out of reach.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مَالِكُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عِيسَى بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ طَلْحَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَوْسَجَةَ، عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ قَالَ‏:‏ جَاءَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا نَبِيَّ اللهِ، عَلِّمْنِي عَمَلاً يُدْخِلُنِي الْجَنَّةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ لَئِنْ كُنْتَ أَقَصَرْتَ الْخُطْبَةَ لَقَدْ أَعْرَضْتَ الْمَسْأَلَةَ، أَعْتِقِ النَّسَمَةَ، وَفُكَّ الرَّقَبَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ أَوَ لَيْسَتَا وَاحِدًا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، عِتْقُ النَّسَمَةِ أَنْ تَعْتِقَ النَّسَمَةَ، وَفَكُّ الرَّقَبَةِ أَنْ تُعِينَ عَلَى الرَّقَبَةِ، وَالْمَنِيحَةُ الرَّغُوبُ، وَالْفَيْءُ عَلَى ذِي الرَّحِمِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تُطِقْ ذَلِكَ، فَأْمُرْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ، وَانْهَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تُطِقْ ذَلِكَ، فَكُفَّ لِسَانَكَ إِلاَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A bedouin came and said, "Prophet of Allah, teach me a deed that will bring me into the Garden." He said, "You have made the speech short, but you have made the question wide. Free a soul and release a neck." He said, "Are they not one thing?" He said, "No. Freeing a soul is to free it yourself. Releasing a neck is to help toward its freedom. And lend a milk animal with plenty of milk, and be kind to your kin. If you cannot manage that, command what is right and forbid what is wrong. If you cannot manage that, hold back your tongue except from good."

situation: Bad feeling arises between a man and a relative he barely knows is a relative.
wise_response: 'Umar told people from the pulpit to learn their lineages and keep their ties. If a man knew how close he was to the other, that knowledge would stop him from wronging him.
why_it_worked: Knowing who your kin are makes you slower to harm them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating distant relatives as strangers and quarreling with them freely.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ خَالِدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَتَّابُ بْنُ بَشِيرٍ، عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ مُطْعِمٍ، أَنَّ جُبَيْرَ بْنَ مُطْعِمٍ أَخْبَرَهُ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ يَقُولُ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ‏:‏ تَعَلَّمُوا أَنْسَابَكُمْ، ثُمَّ صِلُوا أَرْحَامَكُمْ، وَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لِيَكُونُ بَيْنَ الرَّجُلِ وَبَيْنَ أَخِيهِ الشَّيْءُ، وَلَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِي بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهُ مِنْ دَاخِلَةِ الرَّحِمِ، لَأَوْزَعَهُ ذَلِكَ عَنِ انْتِهَاكِهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Learn your lineages, then keep your ties of kinship. By Allah, there may be something between a man and his brother, and if he knew the closeness of kinship between them, it would restrain him from violating it.

situation: A man is raising daughters.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever has three daughters and shelters them, provides for them, and is merciful to them is assured the Garden. Asked "And two?" he said, "And two."
why_it_worked: Daughters were often seen as a burden. Caring for them gently is ranked among the highest deeds.
tempting_wrong_answer: Resenting daughters, providing grudgingly, or favoring sons.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو النُّعْمَانِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ زَيْدٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، أَنَّ جَابِرَ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللهِ حَدَّثَهُمْ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ مَنْ كَانَ لَهُ ثَلاَثُ بَنَاتٍ، يُؤْوِيهِنَّ، وَيَكْفِيهِنَّ، وَيَرْحَمُهُنَّ، فَقَدْ وَجَبَتْ لَهُ الْجَنَّةُ الْبَتَّةَ، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَعْضِ الْقَوْمِ‏:‏ وَثِنْتَيْنِ، يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ وَثِنْتَيْنِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whoever has three daughters, gives them shelter, provides for them, and shows them mercy, the Garden is surely his. A man among the people said, "And two, Messenger of Allah?" He said, "And two."

situation: A man's daughter comes back to live with him, with no one else to support her.
wise_response: The Prophet told Suraqa that one of the greatest charities is providing for a daughter returned to you who has no earner but you.
why_it_worked: Supporting a dependent daughter is counted as charity of the highest kind.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating a returned daughter as a drain and a disgrace.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مُوسَى بْنُ عَلِيٍّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ لِسُرَاقَةَ بْنِ جُعْشُمٍ‏:‏ أَلاَ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى أَعْظَمِ الصَّدَقَةِ، أَوْ مِنْ أَعْظَمِ الصَّدَقَةِ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ ابْنَتُكَ مَرْدُودَةٌ إِلَيْكَ، لَيْسَ لَهَا كَاسِبٌ غَيْرُكَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: "Shall I not show you the greatest charity, or one of the greatest?" He said, "Yes, Messenger of Allah." He said, "Your daughter sent back to you, who has no one to earn for her but you."

situation: A person wonders whether everyday spending on family counts for anything.
wise_response: The Prophet said what you feed yourself, your child, your wife and your servant is all charity for you.
why_it_worked: Ordinary provision for those in your care is a good deed. It includes the servant as well as the family.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking only public giving counts, or feeding a servant poorly.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا حَيْوَةُ بْنُ شُرَيْحٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا بَقِيَّةُ، عَنْ بَحِيرٍ، عَنْ خَالِدٍ، عَنِ الْمِقْدَامِ بْنِ مَعْدِي كَرِبَ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ مَا أَطْعَمْتَ نَفْسَكَ فَهُوَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ، وَمَا أَطْعَمْتَ وَلَدَكَ فَهُوَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ، وَمَا أَطْعَمْتَ زَوْجَكَ فَهُوَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ، وَمَا أَطْعَمْتَ خَادِمَكَ فَهُوَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: What you feed yourself is charity for you. What you feed your child is charity for you. What you feed your wife is charity for you. What you feed your servant is charity for you.

situation: A man sitting with Ibn 'Umar wished his daughters would die.
wise_response: Ibn 'Umar became angry and said: "Is it you who provides for them?"
why_it_worked: Provision comes from Allah. Seeing daughters as a burden to be rid of is arrogance and cruelty.
tempting_wrong_answer: Resenting one's children as mouths to feed.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ مَهْدِيٍّ، عَنْ سُفْيَانَ، عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ أَبِي الرَّوَّاعِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ‏:‏ أَنَّ رَجُلاً كَانَ عِنْدَهُ، وَلَهُ بَنَاتٌ فَتَمَنَّى مَوْتَهُنَّ، فَغَضِبَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَنْتَ تَرْزُقُهُنَّ‏؟‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man was with him who had daughters and wished they would die. Ibn 'Umar became angry and said, "Are you the one who provides for them?"

situation: A person in service to another must decide how faithfully to do his work.
wise_response: The Prophet said the servant who worships his Lord well and gives his master the obedience and sincere counsel he owes has two rewards.
why_it_worked: Faithful, honest service is counted as worth in itself, whatever one's station.
tempting_wrong_answer: Doing the job carelessly or deceiving the one you work for.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْعَلاَءِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أُسَامَةَ، عَنْ بُرَيْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللهِ، عَنْ أَبِي بُرْدَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي مُوسَى قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ الْمَمْلُوكُ الَّذِي يُحْسِنُ عِبَادَةَ رَبِّهِ، وَيُؤَدِّي إِلَى سَيِّدِهِ الَّذِي فُرِضَ، الطَّاعَةُ وَالنَّصِيحَةُ، لَهُ أَجْرَانِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The slave who worships his Lord well, and renders to his master what is due to him of obedience and sincere counsel, has two rewards.

situation: A man from Iraq asked Ibn 'Umar whether the blood of a gnat was impure, soon after Iraqis had killed the Prophet's grandson.
wise_response: Ibn 'Umar said: "Look at this man. He asks me about the blood of a gnat, and they killed the son of the Prophet." He recalled the Prophet saying of his grandsons, "They are my two sweet basils in this world."
why_it_worked: Fussing over tiny points of purity while ignoring the shedding of innocent blood turns religion upside down.
tempting_wrong_answer: Scrupulous attention to small rules alongside indifference to grave wrongs.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مَهْدِيُّ بْنُ مَيْمُونٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ أَبِي يَعْقُوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي نُعْمٍ قَالَ‏:‏ كُنْتُ شَاهِدًا ابْنَ عُمَرَ إِذْ سَأَلَهُ رَجُلٌ عَنْ دَمِ الْبَعُوضَةِ‏؟‏ فَقَالَ‏:‏ مِمَّنْ أَنْتَ‏؟‏ فَقَالَ‏:‏ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ انْظُرُوا إِلَى هَذَا، يَسْأَلُنِي عَنْ دَمِ الْبَعُوضَةِ، وَقَدْ قَتَلُوا ابْنَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ هُمَا رَيْحَانَيَّ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I was present with Ibn 'Umar when a man asked him about the blood of a gnat. He said, "Where are you from?" He said, "From the people of Iraq." He said, "Look at this one. He asks me about the blood of a gnat, and they killed the son of the Prophet, peace be upon him. I heard the Prophet say: They are my two sweet basils from this world."

situation: A poor woman came to 'A'isha with her two children and was given three dates.
wise_response: She gave each child a date and kept one. When they finished and looked at her, she split her own date and gave each half. The Prophet said Allah had shown her mercy because of her mercy to her children.
why_it_worked: Her mercy cost her the last of her food. That self-giving is what earns Allah's mercy.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping one's own share while the children are still hungry.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسْلِمُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ فَضَالَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا بَكْرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ الْمُزَنِيُّ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ‏:‏ جَاءَتِ امْرَأَةٌ إِلَى عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا، فَأَعْطَتْهَا عَائِشَةُ ثَلاَثَ تَمَرَاتٍ، فَأَعْطَتْ كُلَّ صَبِيٍّ لَهَا تَمْرَةً، وَأَمْسَكَتْ لِنَفْسِهَا تَمْرَةً، فَأَكَلَ الصِّبْيَانُ التَّمْرَتَيْنِ وَنَظَرَا إِلَى أُمِّهِمَا، فَعَمَدَتْ إِلَى التَّمْرَةِ فَشَقَّتْهَا، فَأَعْطَتْ كُلَّ صَبِيٍّ نِصْفَ تَمْرَةٍ، فَجَاءَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَخْبَرَتْهُ عَائِشَةُ فَقَالَ‏:‏ وَمَا يُعْجِبُكِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ‏؟‏ لَقَدْ رَحِمَهَا اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَتِهَا صَبِيَّيْهَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A woman came to 'A'isha, and 'A'isha gave her three dates. She gave each of her children a date and kept one for herself. The children ate the two dates and looked at their mother. She took the date, split it, and gave each child half a date. The Prophet, peace be upon him, came and 'A'isha told him. He said, "What surprises you about that? Allah has shown her mercy for her mercy to her two children."

situation: The Prophet kissed his grandson Hasan. Al-Aqra' ibn Habis said he had ten children and had never kissed one.
wise_response: The Prophet looked at him and said: "Whoever does not show mercy is not shown mercy."
why_it_worked: Open tenderness toward children is mercy, and mercy given is mercy received.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating affection toward children as weakness.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْيَمَانِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا شُعَيْبٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو سَلَمَةَ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ قَبَّلَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَسَنَ بْنَ عَلِيٍّ وَعِنْدَهُ الأَقْرَعُ بْنُ حَابِسٍ التَّمِيمِيُّ جَالِسٌ، فَقَالَ الأَقْرَعُ‏:‏ إِنَّ لِي عَشَرَةً مِنَ الْوَلَدِ مَا قَبَّلْتُ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدًا، فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ قَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ لا يَرْحَمُ لا يُرْحَمُ‏.‏

situation: Bashir wanted the Prophet to witness a gift he had given to one son, an-Nu'man, and not to his other children.
wise_response: The Prophet asked if he had given the same to all his children. When he said no, the Prophet said, "Then call someone other than me as witness." He asked, "Would it not please you that they be equally good to you?" Bashir said yes. He said, "Then no."
why_it_worked: Favoring one child breeds resentment among siblings and toward the parent. Fairness keeps them all close.
tempting_wrong_answer: Showering gifts on a favorite child.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَلاَمٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الأَعْلَى بْنُ عَبْدِ الأَعْلَى الْقُرَشِيُّ، عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ أَبِي هِنْدَ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، أَنَّ النُّعْمَانَ بْنَ بَشِيرٍ حَدَّثَهُ، أَنَّ أَبَاهُ انْطَلَقَ بِهِ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَحْمِلُهُ فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، إِنِّي أُشْهِدُكَ أَنِّي قَدْ نَحَلْتُ النُّعْمَانَ كَذَا وَكَذَا، فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَكُلَّ وَلَدَكَ نَحَلْتَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَأَشْهِدْ غَيْرِي، ثُمَّ قَالَ‏:‏ أَلَيْسَ يَسُرُّكَ أَنْ يَكُونُوا فِي الْبِرِّ سَوَاءً‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ بَلَى، قَالَ‏:‏ فَلاَ إِذًا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: His father brought him, carrying him, to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and said, "Messenger of Allah, I call you to witness that I have given an-Nu'man such and such." situation: A parent focuses on what his children owe him.
wise_response: Ibn 'Umar said Allah called the righteous "the dutiful" because they were dutiful to parents and children alike. "As your parent has a right over you, your child has a right over you."
