translation.ai_translation: Allah only called them the righteous (al-abrar) because they were dutiful to their fathers and their sons. Just as your parent has a right over you, so your child has a right over you.

situation: A person sees animals caring for their young.
wise_response: The Prophet said Allah divided mercy into a hundred parts, kept ninety-nine, and sent one to earth. From that one part creatures show mercy to one another, so that a mare lifts her hoof away from her foal for fear of hurting it.
why_it_worked: All tenderness on earth is a small share of Allah's mercy. Showing it is to take part in that mercy.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating mercy as optional or weak.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا الْحَكَمُ بْنُ نَافِعٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا شُعَيْبٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ الْمُسَيِّبِ، أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ الرَّحْمَةَ مِئَةَ جُزْءٍ، فَأَمْسَكَ عِنْدَهُ تِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ، وَأَنْزَلَ فِي الأَرْضِ جُزْءًا وَاحِدًا، فَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْجُزْءِ يَتَرَاحَمُ الْخَلْقُ، حَتَّى تَرْفَعَ الْفَرَسُ حَافِرَهَا عَنْ وَلَدِهَا، خَشْيَةَ أَنْ تُصِيبَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made mercy into a hundred parts. He kept ninety-nine with Himself and sent down one part to the earth. From that one part creatures show mercy to each other, so that a mare lifts her hoof away from her foal for fear of striking it.

situation: Daily life with neighbors, guests and conversation.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should be good to his neighbor, honor his guest, and say what is good or keep silent.
why_it_worked: Faith shows in how one treats the people nearby and how one uses one's tongue.
tempting_wrong_answer: Ignoring neighbors, neglecting guests, and speaking carelessly or cruelly.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا صَدَقَةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنْ نَافِعِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي شُرَيْحٍ الْخُزَاعِيِّ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُحْسِنْ إِلَى جَارِهِ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ ضَيْفَهُ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him be good to his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say good or keep silent.

situation: The companions agreed adultery and theft were forbidden.
wise_response: The Prophet said a man committing adultery with ten women is lighter than with his neighbor's wife, and stealing from ten houses is lighter than stealing from his neighbor's house.
why_it_worked: Neighbors live on trust. Betraying them is worse than the same wrong done elsewhere.
tempting_wrong_answer: Exploiting a neighbor's trust and closeness.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ فُضَيْلٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا ظَبْيَةَ الْكَلاَعِيَّ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ الْمِقْدَادَ بْنَ الأَسْوَدِ يَقُولُ‏:‏ سَأَلَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَصْحَابَهُ عَنِ الزِّنَا‏؟‏ قَالُوا‏:‏ حَرَامٌ، حَرَّمَهُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ لأَنْ يَزْنِيَ الرَّجُلُ بِعَشْرِ نِسْوَةٍ، أَيْسَرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَنْ يَزْنِيَ بِامْرَأَةِ جَارِهِ، وَسَأَلَهُمْ عَنِ السَّرِقَةِ‏؟‏ قَالُوا‏:‏ حَرَامٌ، حَرَّمَهَا اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَرَسُولُهُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ لأَنْ يَسْرِقَ مِنْ عَشَرَةِ أَهْلِ أَبْيَاتٍ، أَيْسَرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَنْ يَسْرِقَ مِنْ بَيْتِ جَارِهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of Allah asked his companions about adultery. They said, "Forbidden. Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it." He said, "For a man to commit adultery with ten women is lighter for him than to commit adultery with his neighbor's wife." He asked them about theft. They said, "Forbidden. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger have forbidden it." He said, "For him to steal from ten households is lighter for him than to steal from his neighbor's house."

situation: People hold different kinds of responsibility: rulers over subjects, men over households, workers over what they are trusted with.
wise_response: The Prophet said each of you is a shepherd and each of you will be asked about his flock.
why_it_worked: Everyone has someone or something in his care. Responsibility comes with being trusted.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating authority as privilege and neglecting those in one's charge.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبِي أُوَيْسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ، وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْؤولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ، فَالأَمِيرُ الَّذِي عَلَى النَّاسِ رَاعٍ، وَهُوَ مَسْؤولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ، وَالرَّجُلُ رَاعٍ عَلَى أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ، وَهُوَ مَسْؤُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ، وَعَبْدُ الرَّجُلِ رَاعٍ عَلَى مَالِ سَيِّدِهِ، وَهُوَ مَسْؤُولٌ عَنْهُ، أَلاَ كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ، وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْؤُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ‏.‏

situation: A master refers to the people who serve him.
wise_response: The Prophet said not to say "my slave" or "my slave-woman," since all are slaves of God. Say "my lad" or "my girl" instead.
why_it_worked: Words that claim ownership over a person feed arrogance. Gentler words keep in mind that master and servant stand equal before God.
tempting_wrong_answer: Speaking of servants in terms that stress their lowliness and one's own ownership.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عُبَيْدِ اللهِ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ يَقُلْ أَحَدُكُمْ‏:‏ عَبْدِي، أَمَتِي، كُلُّكُمْ عَبِيدُ اللهِ، وَكُلُّ نِسَائِكُمْ إِمَاءُ اللهِ، وَلْيَقُلْ‏:‏ غُلاَمِي، جَارِيَتِي، وَفَتَايَ، وَفَتَاتِي‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Let none of you say: my slave, my slave-woman. All of you are slaves of God, and all your women are handmaids of God. Let him say: my boy, my girl, my young man, my young woman.

situation: A delegation of the Banu Amir came to the Prophet and praised him as their master and the best and most generous of them.
wise_response: He said, "The Master is God," and then, "Say what you have to say, but do not let Satan draw you on."
why_it_worked: He would not take titles that belong to God, and he warned them against praise that grows into excess.
tempting_wrong_answer: Accepting flattery and letting admirers raise one ever higher.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ الْفَضْلِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مَسْلَمَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي نَضْرَةَ، عَنْ مُطَرِّفٍ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ أَبِي‏:‏ انْطَلَقْتُ فِي وَفْدِ بَنِي عَامِرٍ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالُوا‏:‏ أَنْتَ سَيِّدُنَا، قَالَ‏:‏ السَّيِّدُ اللَّهُ، قَالُوا‏:‏ وَأَفْضَلُنَا فَضْلاً، وَأَعْظَمُنَا طَوْلاً، قَالَ‏:‏ فَقَالَ‏:‏ قُولُوا بِقَوْلِكُمْ، وَلاَ يَسْتَجْرِيَنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I went with the delegation of the Banu Amir to the Prophet, peace be upon him. They said: You are our master. He said: The Master is God. They said: And the most excellent of us in merit and the greatest of us in bounty. He said: Say what you have to say, but do not let Satan carry you away.

situation: A group of young men stayed with the Prophet for twenty nights to learn. He sensed they missed their families.
wise_response: He asked who they had left at home. Then, being gentle and merciful, he sent them back to teach and guide their families.
why_it_worked: He noticed what they did not say and put their families' need and their own longing ahead of keeping them near him.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping students on out of zeal while their families wait and they quietly suffer.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلاَبَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي سُلَيْمَانَ مَالِكِ بْنِ الْحُوَيْرِثِ قَالَ‏:‏ أَتَيْنَا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَنَحْنُ شَبَبَةٌ مُتَقَارِبُونَ، فَأَقَمْنَا عِنْدَهُ عِشْرِينَ لَيْلَةً، فَظَنَّ أَنَّا اشْتَهَيْنَا أَهْلِينَا، فَسَأَلْنَا عَنْ مَنْ تَرَكْنَا فِي أَهْلِينَا‏؟‏ فَأَخْبَرْنَاهُ، وَكَانَ رَفِيقًا رَحِيمًا، فَقَالَ‏:‏ ارْجِعُوا إِلَى أَهْلِيكُمْ فَعَلِّمُوهُمْ وَمُرُوهُمْ، وَصَلُّوا كَمَا رَأَيْتُمُونِي أُصَلِّي، فَإِذَا حَضَرَتِ الصَّلاَةُ، فَلْيُؤَذِّنْ لَكُمْ أَحَدُكُمْ، وَلْيَؤُمَّكُمْ أَكْبَرُكُمْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: We came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, young men close in age, and stayed with him twenty nights. He thought we were longing for our families and asked us about those we had left behind among them, and we told him. He was gentle and merciful, and he said: Go back to your families, teach them and instruct them, and pray as you have seen me pray. When the prayer is due, let one of you give the call for you, and let the eldest of you lead you.

situation: Someone does you a favour and you have nothing to repay it with.
wise_response: The Prophet said to repay a kindness. If you cannot, praise the one who did it, for praise is thanks. Hiding it is ingratitude.
why_it_worked: Gratitude can always be shown, even by the poor. Silence about a kindness treats it as nothing.
tempting_wrong_answer: Saying nothing about a favour because one cannot pay it back.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ عُفَيْرٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ غَزِيَّةَ، عَنْ شُرَحْبِيلَ مَوْلَى الأَنْصَارِ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللهِ الأَنْصَارِيِّ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ مَنْ صُنِعَ إِلَيْهِ مَعْرُوفٌ فَلْيُجْزِئْهُ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ مَا يُجْزِئُهُ فَلْيُثْنِ عَلَيْهِ، فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا أَثْنَى فَقَدْ شَكَرَهُ، وَإِنْ كَتَمَهُ فَقَدْ كَفَرَهُ، وَمَنْ تَحَلَّى بِمَا لَمْ يُعْطَ، فَكَأَنَّمَا لَبِسَ ثَوْبَيْ زُورٍ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whoever has a kindness done to him, let him repay it. If he finds nothing to repay it with, let him praise the doer, for if he praises him he has thanked him, and if he hides it he has been ungrateful to him. And whoever adorns himself with what he was not given is like one wearing two garments of falsehood.

situation: The emigrants to Madina had been housed and supported by the Ansar. They felt the Ansar had earned all the reward and they could never match it.
wise_response: The Prophet said no, not as long as they prayed for the Ansar and praised them for what they did.
why_it_worked: When you cannot repay in kind, sincere thanks and prayer are a real return.
tempting_wrong_answer: Feeling only indebted or resentful, and saying nothing to honour the benefactors.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، أَنَّ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ قَالُوا‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، ذَهَبَ الأَنْصَارُ بِالأَجْرِ كُلِّهِ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، مَا دَعَوْتُمُ اللَّهَ لَهُمْ، وَأَثْنَيْتُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ بِهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Emigrants said: Messenger of God, have the Ansar taken all the reward? He said: No, as long as you pray to God for them and praise them for it.

situation: People help us every day, and it is easy to take that for granted.
wise_response: The Prophet said, "Whoever does not thank people does not thank God."
why_it_worked: Thanks owed to God show up in how we thank the people through whom good reaches us.
tempting_wrong_answer: Claiming to be grateful to God while never thanking the people who help you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الرَّبِيعُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ يَشْكُرُ اللَّهَ مَنْ لاَ يَشْكُرُ النَّاسَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whoever does not thank people does not thank God.

situation: Abu Dharr asked what good he could do if he lacked the strength for the greatest deeds.
wise_response: The Prophet said to help someone in need or work for someone unskilled. If he was too weak even for that, he should keep his harm away from people, which is a charity he gives himself.
why_it_worked: There is always some good within reach. At the least, refraining from harm counts.
tempting_wrong_answer: Deciding that since one cannot do great things, nothing one does matters.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أُوَيْسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي مُرَاوِحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، قِيلَ‏:‏ أَيُّ الأَعْمَالِ خَيْرٌ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ إِيمَانٌ بِاللَّهِ، وَجِهَادٌ فِي سَبِيلِهِ، قِيلَ‏:‏ فَأَيُّ الرِّقَابِ أَفْضَلُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ أَغْلاَهَا ثَمَنًا، وَأَنْفَسُهَا عِنْدَ أَهْلِهَا، قَالَ‏:‏ أَفَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ لَمْ أَسْتَطِعْ بَعْضَ الْعَمَلِ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ فَتُعِينُ ضَائِعًا، أَوْ تَصْنَعُ لأَخْرَقَ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَفَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ ضَعُفْتُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ تَدَعُ النَّاسَ مِنَ الشَّرِّ، فَإِنَّهَا صَدَقَةٌ تَصَدَّقُ بِهَا عَلَى نَفْسِكَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: It was asked: Which deeds are best? He said: Faith in God and striving in His path. It was asked: Which slaves are best to free? He said: The most costly and the most precious to their owners. He said: What if I cannot do some of these deeds? He said: Then help someone in need, or work for someone unskilled. He said: What if I am too weak? He said: Keep people safe from your harm, for that is a charity you give to yourself.

situation: Harmala came back twice to ask the Prophet what he should do.
wise_response: The Prophet said: do what is good and avoid what is wrong. Do whatever you would love people to say of you after you leave them, and avoid whatever you would hate them to say. Harmala found these left nothing out.
why_it_worked: Imagining what people say of you once you have gone gives a simple, honest test for any act.
tempting_wrong_answer: Behaving one way in company and another once out of sight.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ حَسَّانَ الْعَنْبَرِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حِبَّانُ بْنُ عَاصِمٍ، وَكَانَ حَرْمَلَةُ أَبَا أُمِّهِ، فَحَدَّثَتْنِي صَفِيَّةُ ابْنَةُ عُلَيْبَةَ، وَدُحَيْبَةُ ابْنَةُ عُلَيْبَةَ، وَكَانَ جَدَّهُمَا حَرْمَلَةُ أَبَا أَبِيهِمَا، أَنَّهُ أَخْبَرَهُمْ، عَنْ حَرْمَلَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللهِ، أَنَّهُ خَرَجَ حَتَّى أَتَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَكَانَ عِنْدَهُ حَتَّى عَرَفَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَلَمَّا ارْتَحَلَ قُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي‏:‏ وَاللَّهِ لَآتِيَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى أَزْدَادَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ، فَجِئْتُ أَمْشِي حَتَّى قُمْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ مَا تَأْمُرُنِي أَعْمَلُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ يَا حَرْمَلَةُ، ائْتِ الْمَعْرُوفَ، وَاجْتَنَبِ الْمُنْكَرَ، ثُمَّ رَجَعْتُ، حَتَّى جِئْتُ الرَّاحِلَةَ، ثُمَّ أَقْبَلْتُ حَتَّى قُمْتُ مَقَامِي قَرِيبًا مِنْهُ، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، مَا تَأْمُرُنِي أَعْمَلُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ يَا حَرْمَلَةُ، ائْتِ الْمَعْرُوفَ، وَاجْتَنَبِ الْمُنْكَرَ، وَانْظُرْ مَا يُعْجِبُ أُذُنَكَ أَنْ يَقُولَ لَكَ الْقَوْمُ إِذَا قُمْتَ مِنْ عِنْدِهِمْ فَأْتِهِ، وَانْظُرِ الَّذِي تَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَقُولَ لَكَ الْقَوْمُ إِذَا قُمْتَ مِنْ عِنْدِهِمْ فَاجْتَنِبْهُ، فَلَمَّا رَجَعْتُ تَفَكَّرْتُ، فَإِذَا هُمَا لَمْ يَدَعَا شَيْئًا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: He went out until he came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and stayed with him until the Prophet knew him. When he set off, I said to myself: By God, I will go back to the Prophet to gain more knowledge. I came walking until I stood before him and said: What do you command me to do? He said: Harmala, do what is good and avoid what is wrong. Then I went back to my mount, and came again until I stood in my place near him and said: Messenger of God, what do you command me to do? He said: Harmala, do what is good and avoid what is wrong. Look at what you would love people to say of you when you get up and leave them, and do it. And look at what you would hate them to say of you when you get up and leave them, and avoid it. When I went back I thought it over, and these two had left nothing out.

situation: The Prophet's party stopped at a camp, and a man took the eggs of a small bird. The mother bird came and fluttered over the Prophet's head.
wise_response: He asked, "Which of you has distressed this bird over its eggs?" A man said he had taken them. The Prophet said, "Return them, out of mercy for her."
why_it_worked: He noticed the distress of a small creature and set it right. Mercy reaches even a bird.
tempting_wrong_answer: Ignoring an animal's distress because it is small and the eggs are easy food.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا طَلْقُ بْنُ غَنَّامٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الْمَسْعُودِيُّ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللهِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَزَلَ مَنْزِلاً فَأَخَذَ رَجُلٌ بَيْضَ حُمَّرَةٍ، فَجَاءَتْ تَرِفُّ عَلَى رَأْسِ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَيُّكُمْ فَجَعَ هَذِهِ بِبَيْضَتِهَا‏؟‏ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، أَنَا أَخَذْتُ بَيْضَتَهَا، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ ارْدُدْ، رَحْمَةً لَهَا‏.‏

It came beating its wings over the head of the Messenger of God. He said, "Which of you has pained this one over her eggs?" A man said, "Messenger of God, I took her eggs." The Prophet said, "Give them back, out of mercy for her."

situation: The Prophet visited the house of Abu Talha and saw his small son Abu 'Umayr, who had a little bird he played with.
wise_response: He spoke to the boy by his nickname and asked about his pet: "Abu 'Umayr, what happened to the little bird?"
why_it_worked: He took a child's small world seriously and gave him warm attention.
tempting_wrong_answer: Ignoring children or treating their concerns as beneath notice.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ الْمُغِيرَةِ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ دَخَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَرَأَى ابْنًا لأَبِي طَلْحَةَ يُقَالُ لَهُ‏:‏ أَبُو عُمَيْرٍ، وَكَانَ لَهُ نُغَيْرٌ يَلْعَبُ بِهِ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا أَبَا عُمَيْرٍ، مَا فَعَلَ أَوْ، أَيْنَ، النُّغَيْرُ‏؟‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Anas said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, came in and saw a son of Abu Talha called Abu 'Umayr, who had a little bird he used to play with. He said, "Abu 'Umayr, what did the little bird do?" or "Where is the little bird?"

situation: Two people are at odds, and someone wants to bring them back together.
wise_response: The Prophet said the one who makes peace between people by saying good things or passing on good words is not a liar. Umm Kulthum added that she heard him allow this kind of speech only in three cases: making peace between people, a husband speaking to his wife, and a wife speaking to her husband.
why_it_worked: Repairing a broken bond is worth more than strict literal accounting of every word. The allowance is narrow and serves peace.
tempting_wrong_answer: Passing on every harsh word each side said, which keeps the quarrel alive.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي اللَّيْثُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي يُونُسُ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي حُمَيْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَنَّ أُمَّهَ أُمَّ كُلْثُومِ ابْنَةَ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ أَبِي مُعَيْطٍ أَخْبَرَتْهُ، أَنَّهَا سَمِعَتْ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ لَيْسَ الْكَذَّابُ الَّذِي يُصْلِحُ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ، فَيَقُولُ خَيْرًا، أَوْ يَنْمِي خَيْرًا، قَالَتْ‏:‏ وَلَمْ أَسْمَعْهُ يُرَخِّصُ فِي شَيْءٍ مِمَّا يَقُولُ النَّاسُ مِنَ الْكَذِبِ إِلاَّ فِي ثَلاَثٍ‏:‏ الإِصْلاَحِ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ، وَحَدِيثِ الرَّجُلِ امْرَأَتَهُ، وَحَدِيثِ الْمَرْأَةِ زَوْجَهَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt reported that she heard the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, say: "He is not a liar who sets things right between people and says good or passes on good." She said: I did not hear him allow anything of what people call lying except in three: setting things right between people, a man's talk to his wife, and a woman's talk to her husband.

situation: Whether to hold to the truth when a lie would be easier.
wise_response: The Prophet said: hold to truthfulness. It leads to goodness, and goodness leads to the Garden. A man keeps telling the truth until he is written with God as truthful. Beware of lying. It leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man keeps lying until he is written with God as a liar.
why_it_worked: Honesty and lying are habits. Each small choice moves a person toward who he will become.
tempting_wrong_answer: Telling small lies on the theory that they do not matter.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ دَاوُدَ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ أَبِي وَائِلٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالصِّدْقِ، فَإِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ، وَإِنَّ الْبِرَّ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، وَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ يَصْدُقُ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللهِ صِدِّيقًا، وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ، فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ، وَالْفُجُورَ يَهْدِي إِلَى النَّارِ، وَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَكْذِبُ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللهِ كَذَّابًا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: 'Abdullah reported that the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Hold to truthfulness, for truthfulness guides to righteousness, and righteousness guides to the Garden. A man keeps being truthful until he is written with God as a truthful one. And beware of lying, for lying guides to wickedness, and wickedness guides to the Fire. A man keeps lying until he is written with God as a liar."

situation: A parent tells a child he will get something, with no intention of giving it.
wise_response: 'Abdullah said lying is not right in earnest or in jest, and none of you should promise his child something and then not give it.
why_it_worked: Children learn honesty from how adults keep their word to them. A joke or a casual promise is still a promise.
tempting_wrong_answer: Making empty promises to a child to quiet him, or lying for a laugh.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا قُتَيْبَةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا جَرِيرٌ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، عَنْ أَبِي مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ يَصْلُحُ الْكَذِبُ فِي جِدٍّ وَلاَ هَزْلٍ، وَلاَ أَنْ يَعِدَ أَحَدُكُمْ وَلَدَهُ شَيْئًا ثُمَّ لاَ يُنْجِزُ لَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: 'Abdullah said: "Lying is not fitting, in earnest or in jest. Nor is it fitting that one of you promise his child something and then not fulfil it for him."

situation: Living among people means putting up with their irritations and slights.
wise_response: The Prophet said the believer who mixes with people and bears their harm patiently is better than one who keeps away from people and does not bear their harm.
why_it_worked: Goodness is tested and practiced among others. Withdrawing to avoid annoyance gives up that good.
tempting_wrong_answer: Pulling away from people to avoid being hurt.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا آدَمُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ وَثَّابٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ الْمُؤْمِنُ الَّذِي يُخَالِطُ النَّاسَ، وَيَصْبِرُ عَلَى أَذَاهُمْ، خَيْرٌ مِنَ الَّذِي لاَ يُخَالِطُ النَّاسَ، وَلاَ يَصْبِرُ عَلَى أَذَاهُمْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Ibn 'Umar reported that the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The believer who mixes with people and is patient with the harm they do is better than the one who does not mix with people and is not patient with their harm."

situation: After the Prophet divided some goods, a man of the Ansar said the division was not made for God's sake. Ibn Mas'ud told the Prophet privately.
wise_response: The Prophet was hurt and his face changed with anger. Then he said, "Musa was hurt with more than this, and he was patient."
why_it_worked: He felt the insult and let it go by recalling someone who bore worse. Ibn Mas'ud also learned that passing on a hurtful remark can cause pain.
tempting_wrong_answer: Striking back at the critic, or carrying a hurtful remark to the person it was about.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ بْنُ حَفْصٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ شَقِيقًا يَقُولُ‏:‏ قَالَ عَبْدُ اللهِ‏:‏ قَسَمَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قِسْمَةً، كَبَعْضِ مَا كَانَ يَقْسِمُ، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ‏:‏ وَاللَّهِ، إِنَّهَا لَقِسْمَةٌ مَا أُرِيدَ بِهَا وَجْهَ اللهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، قُلْتُ أَنَا‏:‏ لَأَقُولَنَّ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَأَتَيْتُهُ، وَهُوَ فِي أَصْحَابِهِ، فَسَارَرْتُهُ، فَشَقَّ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَتَغَيَّرَ وَجْهُهُ، وَغَضِبَ، حَتَّى وَدِدْتُ أَنِّي لَمْ أَكُنْ أَخْبَرَتْهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ‏:‏ قَدْ أُوذِيَ مُوسَى بِأَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَصَبَرَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: 'Abdullah said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, made a distribution like some he used to make. A man of the Ansar said, "By God, this is a distribution by which God's face was not sought." I said, "I will tell the Prophet." I went to him while he was among his companions and told him privately. It weighed on him, his face changed and he grew angry, until I wished I had not told him. Then he said, "Musa was harmed with more than this, and he was patient."

situation: People wonder which good deeds count most.
wise_response: The Prophet asked if they wanted to know of a rank higher than prayer, fasting and charity. It is setting right relations between people. Spoiled relations between people are the razor.
why_it_worked: Reconciling people protects a whole community. Discord strips away good the way a razor strips hair.
tempting_wrong_answer: Leaving quarrels to fester, or stirring them, while relying on private worship.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا صَدَقَةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ مُرَّةَ، عَنْ سَالِمِ بْنِ أَبِي الْجَعْدِ، عَنْ أُمِّ الدَّرْدَاءِ، عَنْ أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ أَلاَ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِدَرَجَةٍ أَفْضَلَ مِنَ الصَّلاَةِ وَالصِّيَامِ وَالصَّدَقَةِ‏؟‏ قَالُوا‏:‏ بَلَى، قَالَ‏:‏ صَلاَحُ ذَاتِ الْبَيْنِ، وَفَسَادُ ذَاتِ الْبَيْنِ هِيَ الْحَالِقَةُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu ad-Darda' reported that the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Shall I not tell you of a rank better than prayer, fasting and charity?" They said, "Yes." He said, "Setting right what is between people. And corruption of what is between people is the razor."

key_terms.الحالقة (al-haliqa): the razor, that which shaves away

situation: Someone trusts you and believes what you tell him.
wise_response: The Prophet said: it is a great betrayal to tell your brother something he believes from you while you are lying to him.
why_it_worked: The greater the trust, the worse the lie. Lying to someone who trusts you betrays him.
tempting_wrong_answer: Using someone's trust to get a lie past him.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا حَيْوَةُ بْنُ شُرَيْحٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا بَقِيَّةُ، عَنْ ضُبَارَةَ بْنِ مَالِكٍ الْحَضْرَمِيِّ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ نُفَيْرٍ، أَنَّ أَبَاهُ حَدَّثَهُ، أَنَّ سُفْيَانَ بْنَ أُسَيْدٍ الْحَضْرَمِيَّ حَدَّثَهُ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ كَبُرَتْ خِيَانَةً أَنْ تُحَدِّثَ أَخَاكَ حَدِيثًا هُوَ لَكَ مُصَدِّقٌ، وَأَنْتَ لَهُ كَاذِبٌ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Sufyan ibn Usayd al-Hadrami reported that he heard the Prophet, peace be upon him, say: "It is a great betrayal that you tell your brother something in which he believes you, while you are lying to him."

situation: Dealings with a friend or brother.
wise_response: The Prophet said: do not argue with your brother, do not mock him, and do not make him a promise and then break it.
why_it_worked: Quarrels, ridicule and broken promises each wear down a friendship.
tempting_wrong_answer: Arguing to win, joking at a friend's expense, and making promises you will not keep.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الْمُحَارِبِيُّ، عَنْ لَيْثٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ لاَ تُمَارِ أَخَاكَ، وَلاَ تُمَازِحْهُ، وَلاَ تَعِدْهُ مَوْعِدًا فَتُخْلِفَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Ibn 'Abbas reported that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "Do not dispute with your brother, do not make fun of him, and do not promise him something and then break your promise."

situation: A man's own people are in the wrong and expect him to back them.
wise_response: Fusayla's father asked the Prophet if it was tribal partisanship for a man to help his people in wrongdoing. The Prophet said yes.
why_it_worked: Loyalty to your own people does not extend to helping them do wrong. Justice comes first.
tempting_wrong_answer: Siding with your family or group in an injustice because they are your own.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا زَكَرِيَّا، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الْحَكَمُ بْنُ الْمُبَارَكِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا زِيَادُ بْنُ الرَّبِيعِ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي عَبَّادٌ الرَّمْلِيُّ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَتْنِي امْرَأَةٌ يُقَالُ لَهَا‏:‏ فُسَيْلَةُ، قَالَتْ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَبِي يَقُولُ‏:‏ قُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، أَمِنَ الْعَصَبِيَّةِ أَنْ يُعِينَ الرَّجُلُ قَوْمَهُ عَلَى ظُلْمٍ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ نَعَمْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A woman named Fusayla said she heard her father say: I said, "Messenger of God, is it partisanship for a man to help his people in wrongdoing?" He said, "Yes."

situation: 'A'isha heard that her nephew 'Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr had threatened to restrict her giving. She vowed never to speak to him again and refused all who interceded.
wise_response: Two men brought Ibn az-Zubayr in with them. He embraced her and wept, and they reminded her that the Prophet forbade cutting off a brother for more than three nights. She spoke to him again, freed forty slaves to make up for her vow, and later wept at the memory.
why_it_worked: She let the Prophet's teaching on keeping ties outweigh her hurt pride and a vow made in anger. She paid the cost of breaking the vow.
tempting_wrong_answer: Holding to a vow made in anger and cutting off a relative for good.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي اللَّيْثُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ خَالِدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ عَوْفِ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ الطُّفَيْلِ، وَهُوَ ابْنُ أَخِي عَائِشَةَ لِأُمِّهَا، أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا حُدِّثَتْ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللهِ بْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ قَالَ فِي بَيْعٍ، أَوْ عَطَاءٍ، أَعْطَتْهُ عَائِشَةُ‏:‏ وَاللَّهِ لَتَنْتَهِيَنَّ عَائِشَةُ أَوْ لَأَحْجُرَنَّ عَلَيْهَا، فَقَالَتْ‏:‏ أَهُوَ قَالَ هَذَا‏؟‏ قَالُوا‏:‏ نَعَمْ، قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ‏:‏ فَهُوَ لِلَّهِ نَذْرٌ أَنْ لاَ أُكَلِّمَ ابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ كَلِمَةً أَبَدًا، فَاسْتَشْفَعَ ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ بِالْمُهَاجِرِينَ حِينَ طَالَتْ هِجْرَتُهَا إِيَّاهُ، فَقَالَتْ‏:‏ وَاللَّهِ، لاَ أُشَفِّعُ فِيهِ أَحَدًا أَبَدًا، وَلاَ أُحَنِّثُ نَذْرِي الَّذِي نَذَرْتُ أَبَدًا‏.‏ فَلَمَّا طَالَ عَلَى ابْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ كَلَّمَ الْمِسْوَرَ بْنَ مَخْرَمَةَ وَعَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ الأَسْوَدِ بْنِ يَغُوثَ، وَهُمَا مِنْ بَنِي زُهْرَةَ، فَقَالَ لَهُمَا‏:‏ أَنْشُدُكُمَا بِاللَّهِ إِلاَّ أَدْخَلْتُمَانِي عَلَى عَائِشَةَ، فَإِنَّهَا لاَ يَحِلُّ لَهَا أَنْ تَنْذِرَ قَطِيعَتِي، فَأَقْبَلَ بِهِ الْمِسْوَرُ وَعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ مُشْتَمِلَيْنِ عَلَيْهِ بِأَرْدِيَتِهِمَا، حَتَّى اسْتَأْذَنَا عَلَى عَائِشَةَ فَقَالاَ‏:‏ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكِ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، أَنَدْخُلُ‏؟‏ فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ‏:‏ ادْخُلُوا، قَالاَ‏:‏ كُلُّنَا يَا أُمَّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ‏؟‏ قَالَتْ‏:‏ نَعَمْ، ادْخُلُوا كُلُّكُمْ‏.‏ وَلاَ تَعْلَمُ عَائِشَةُ أَنَّ مَعَهُمَا ابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ، فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا دَخَلَ ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ فِي الْحِجَابِ، وَاعْتَنَقَ عَائِشَةَ وَطَفِقَ يُنَاشِدُهَا يَبْكِي، وَطَفِقَ الْمِسْوَرُ وَعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ يُنَاشِدَانِ عَائِشَةَ إِلاَّ كَلَّمَتْهُ وَقَبِلَتْ مِنْهُ، وَيَقُولاَنِ‏:‏ قَدْ عَلِمْتِ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَهَى عَمَّا قَدْ عَلِمْتِ مِنَ الْهِجْرَةِ، وَأَنَّهُ لاَ يَحِلُّ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَهْجُرَ أَخَاهُ فَوْقَ ثَلاَثِ لَيَالٍ‏.‏ قَالَ‏:‏ فَلَمَّا أَكْثَرُوا التَّذْكِيرَ وَالتَّحْرِيجَ طَفِقَتْ تُذَكِّرُهُمْ وَتَبْكِي وَتَقُولُ‏:‏ إِنِّي قَدْ نَذَرْتُ وَالنَّذْرُ شَدِيدٌ، فَلَمْ يَزَالُوا بِهَا حَتَّى كَلَّمَتِ ابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ، ثُمَّ أَعْتَقَتْ بِنَذْرِهَا أَرْبَعِينَ رَقَبَةً، ثُمَّ كَانَتْ تَذْكُرُ بَعْدَ مَا أَعْتَقَتْ أَرْبَعِينَ رَقَبَةً فَتَبْكِي حَتَّى تَبُلَّ دُمُوعُهَا خِمَارَهَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: 'Awf ibn al-Harith ibn at-Tufayl, the son of 'A'isha's brother through her mother, reported that 'A'isha was told that 'Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr had said, about a sale or gift she made: "By God, 'A'isha will stop or I will put her under restriction." She said, "Did he say this?" They said, "Yes." 'A'isha said, "Then I vow to God that I will never speak a word to Ibn az-Zubayr." When her shunning of him went on long, Ibn az-Zubayr sought the intercession of the Muhajirun. She said, "By God, I will never accept anyone's intercession for him, and I will never break the vow I made." When it went on long for Ibn az-Zubayr, he spoke to al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth, both of Banu Zuhra, and said to them, "I adjure you by God to bring me in to 'A'isha, for it is not lawful for her to vow to cut me off." Al-Miswar and 'Abd ar-Rahman came with him wrapped in their cloaks and asked leave of 'A'isha: "Peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of God. May we come in?" 'A'isha said, "Come in." They said, "All of us, Mother of the Believers?" She said, "Yes, come in, all of you," not knowing Ibn az-Zubayr was with them. When they entered, Ibn az-Zubayr went behind the screen, embraced 'A'isha, and began imploring her and weeping. Al-Miswar and 'Abd ar-Rahman began imploring her to speak to him and accept him, saying, "You know that the Messenger of God forbade the shunning you know of, and that it is not lawful for a man to shun his brother beyond three nights." When they pressed the reminder hard, she began reminding them and weeping, saying, "I made a vow, and a vow is a serious thing." They kept on until she spoke to Ibn az-Zubayr. Then she freed forty slaves for her vow. Afterward, when she remembered it, she would weep until her tears soaked her head-covering.

situation: Rivalry, resentment and grudges arise between people.
wise_response: The Prophet said: do not hate one another, do not envy one another, do not turn your backs on one another. Be servants of God, brothers. It is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three nights.
why_it_worked: Hatred, envy and coldness pull people apart. Treating others as brothers and setting a short limit on shunning keeps rifts from hardening.
tempting_wrong_answer: Nursing envy or a grudge and freezing someone out indefinitely.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ تَبَاغَضُوا، وَلاَ تَحَاسَدُوا، وَلاَ تَدَابَرُوا، وَكُونُوا عِبَادَ اللهِ إِخْوَانًا، وَلاَ يَحِلُّ لِمُسْلِمٍ أَنْ يَهْجُرَ أَخَاهُ فَوْقَ ثَلاَثِ لَيَالٍ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Anas ibn Malik reported that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "Do not hate one another, do not envy one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and be servants of God, brothers. It is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother beyond three nights."

situation: Two people have fallen out and turn away from each other when they meet.
wise_response: The Prophet said it is not lawful to shun a brother beyond three nights, each turning away when they meet. The better of the two is the one who greets first.
why_it_worked: Ending the silence takes humility. The one who speaks first is counted the better.
tempting_wrong_answer: Waiting for the other person to make the first move.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي اللَّيْثُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي يُونُسُ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ اللَّيْثِيِّ ثُمَّ الْجُنْدَعِيِّ، أَنَّ أَبَا أَيُّوبَ صَاحِبَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ يَحِلُّ لأَحَدٍ أَنْ يَهْجُرَ أَخَاهُ فَوْقَ ثَلاَثِ لَيَالٍ، يَلْتَقِيَانِ فَيَصُدُّ هَذَا وَيَصُدُّ هَذَا، وَخَيْرُهُمَا الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ بِالسَّلامِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Ayyub, the companion of the Messenger of God, reported that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "It is not lawful for anyone to shun his brother beyond three nights, so that they meet and this one turns away and that one turns away. The better of them is the one who begins with the greeting of peace."

situation: Two friends whose bond was built on faith drift apart.
wise_response: The Prophet said two people who love each other for God's sake, or in Islam, are not parted except by a sin one of them commits.
why_it_worked: A real friendship founded on God breaks only when one side does wrong. A rift is a cue to look at your own conduct.
tempting_wrong_answer: Blaming the other person for a split without asking what you did.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ وَهْبٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي عَمْرٌو، عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ أَبِي حَبِيبٍ، عَنْ سِنَانِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ مَا تَوَادَّ اثْنَانِ فِي اللهِ جَلَّ وَعَزَّ أَوْ فِي الإِسْلاَمِ، فَيُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَهُمَا إِلاَّ بِذَنْبٍ يُحْدِثُهُ أَحَدُهُمَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Anas reported that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "No two people love each other for the sake of God, mighty and majestic, or in Islam, and then are parted, except through a sin that one of them commits."

situation: Two Muslims have stopped speaking to each other.
wise_response: The Prophet said it is not lawful to cut off a Muslim beyond three days. While they keep it up, both have turned from the truth. The first to come back has that as expiation. If one greets and the other refuses, an angel answers the greeter and Satan answers the refuser.
why_it_worked: Coming back first is rewarded. Refusing an offered greeting puts a person on the wrong side.
tempting_wrong_answer: Refusing someone's attempt at reconciliation.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مَعْمَرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَتْ مُعَاذَةَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ هِشَامَ بْنَ عَامِرٍ الأَنْصَارِيَّ، ابْنَ عَمِّ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، وَكَانَ قُتِلَ أَبُوهُ يَوْمَ أُحُدٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ يَحِلُّ لِمُسْلِمٍ أَنْ يُصَارِمَ مُسْلِمًا فَوْقَ ثَلاَثٍ، فَإِنَّهُمَا نَاكِبَانِ عَنِ الْحَقِّ مَا دَامَا عَلَى صِرَامِهِمَا، وَإِنَّ أَوَّلَهُمَا فَيْئًا يَكُونُ كَفَّارَةً عَنْهُ سَبْقُهُ بِالْفَيْءِ، وَإِنْ مَاتَا عَلَى صِرَامِهِمَا لَمْ يَدْخُلاَ الْجَنَّةَ جَمِيعًا أَبَدًا، وَإِنْ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ فَأَبَى أَنْ يَقْبَلَ تَسْلِيمَهُ وَسَلاَمَهُ، رَدَّ عَلَيْهِ الْمَلَكُ، وَرَدَّ عَلَى الْآخَرِ الشَّيْطَانُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Hisham ibn 'Amir al-Ansari, cousin of Anas ibn Malik, whose father was killed at Uhud, heard the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, say: "It is not lawful for a Muslim to cut off a Muslim beyond three. They are both turning away from the truth as long as they persist in cutting each other off. The first of them to return, his being first to return is an expiation for him. If they die while cut off, they will never both enter the Garden. If one greets the other and he refuses to accept his greeting and his peace, the angel answers the one, and Satan answers the other."

situation: A person has no money to give and thinks he cannot do charity.

tempting_wrong_answer: Doing nothing for others because one has nothing to give in cash.

translation.ai_translation: Every kindness is charity.

situation: A man walking along a road came across thorns that could hurt the next traveller.
wise_response: He said, "I will clear these thorns so they do not hurt anyone," and moved them. The Prophet said he was forgiven for it.
why_it_worked: A small act to protect strangers he would never meet carried great weight.
tempting_wrong_answer: Stepping around the hazard and leaving it for someone else to deal with.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا وُهَيْبٌ، عَنْ سُهَيْلٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ مَرَّ رَجُلٌ مُسْلِمٌ بِشَوْكٍ فِي الطَّرِيقِ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ لَأُمِيطَنَّ هَذَا الشَّوْكَ، لاَ يَضُرُّ رَجُلاً مُسْلِمًا، فَغُفِرَ لَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A Muslim man passed by thorns in the road and said: I will surely remove these thorns so they do not harm a Muslim man. And he was forgiven.

situation: After Khadija died, the Prophet still received gifts and had to decide where to send them.
wise_response: He would say, "Take it to so-and-so, for she was a friend of Khadija. Take it to the house of so-and-so, for she loved Khadija."
why_it_worked: He kept faith with his late wife by honouring the people she loved, long after she was gone.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting the dead and their friends fade from one's care once the loss has passed.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُبَارَكٌ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا أُتِيَ بِالشَّيْءِ يَقُولُ‏:‏ اذْهَبُوا بِهِ إِلَى فُلاَنَةٍ، فَإِنَّهَا كَانَتْ صَدِيقَةَ خَدِيجَةَ‏.‏ اذْهَبُوا بِهِ إِلَى بَيْتِ فُلاَنَةٍ، فَإِنَّهَا كَانَتْ تُحِبُّ خَدِيجَةَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: When something was brought to the Prophet, peace be upon him, he would say: Take it to so-and-so, for she was a friend of Khadija. Take it to the house of so-and-so, for she loved Khadija.

situation: Hudhayfa was repeating harsh things the Prophet had said in anger about certain groups. People asked Salman to confirm them.
wise_response: Salman would only say, "Hudhayfa knows best what he says," because he did not want grudges to grow between people. He recalled that the Prophet had prayed that any curse he spoke in anger against someone who did not deserve it be turned into a blessing.
why_it_worked: Words spoken in a heated moment can stir lasting hatred. Salman chose not to spread them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Passing on every harsh remark one has heard and fanning resentment between groups.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ مَخْلَدٍ، عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ أُسَامَةَ، عَنْ مِسْعَرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ أَبِي قُرَّةَ الْكِنْدِيِّ قَالَ‏:‏ عَرَضَ أَبِي عَلَى سَلْمَانَ أُخْتَهُ، فَأَبَى وَتَزَوَّجَ مَوْلاَةً لَهُ، يُقَالُ لَهَا‏:‏ بُقَيْرَةُ، فَبَلَغَ أَبَا قُرَّةَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ بَيْنَ حُذَيْفَةَ وَسَلْمَانَ شَيْءٌ، فَأَتَاهُ يَطْلُبُهُ، فَأَخْبَرَ أَنَّهُ فِي مَبْقَلَةٍ لَهُ، فَتَوَجَّهَ إِلَيْهِ، فَلَقِيَهُ مَعَهُ زَبِيلٌ فِيهِ بَقْلٌ، قَدْ أَدْخَلَ عَصَاهُ فِي عُرْوَةِ الزَّبِيلِ، وَهُوَ عَلَى عَاتِقِهِ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ اللهِ، مَا كَانَ بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ حُذَيْفَةَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ يَقُولُ سَلْمَانُ‏:‏ ‏{‏وَكَانَ الإِنْسَانُ عَجُولاً‏}‏، فَانْطَلَقَا حَتَّى أَتَيَا دَارَ سَلْمَانَ، فَدَخَلَ سَلْمَانُ الدَّارَ فَقَالَ‏:‏ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ، ثُمَّ أَذِنَ لأَبِي قُرَّةَ، فَدَخَلَ، فَإِذَا نَمَطٌ مَوْضُوعٌ عَلَى بَابٍ، وَعِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ لَبِنَاتٌ، وَإِذَا قُرْطَاطٌ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ اجْلِسْ عَلَى فِرَاشِ مَوْلاَتِكَ الَّتِي تُمَهِّدُ لِنَفْسِهَا، ثُمَّ أَنْشَأَ يُحَدِّثُهُ فَقَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّ حُذَيْفَةَ كَانَ يُحَدِّثُ بِأَشْيَاءَ، كَانَ يَقُولُهَا رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي غَضَبِهِ لأَقْوَامٍ، فَأُوتَى فَأُسْأَلُ عَنْهَا‏؟‏ فَأَقُولُ‏:‏ حُذَيْفَةُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُ، وَأَكْرَهُ أَنْ تَكُونَ ضَغَائِنُ بَيْنَ أَقْوَامٍ، فَأُتِيَ حُذَيْفَةُ، فَقِيلَ لَهُ‏:‏ إِنَّ سَلْمَانَ لاَ يُصَدِّقُكَ وَلاَ يُكَذِّبُكَ بِمَا تَقُولُ، فَجَاءَنِي حُذَيْفَةُ فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا سَلْمَانُ ابْنَ أُمِّ سَلْمَانَ، فَقُلْتُ يَا حُذَيْفَةُ ابْنَ أُمِّ حُذَيْفَةَ، لَتَنْتَهِيَنَّ، أَوْ لَأَكْتُبَنَّ فِيكَ إِلَى عُمَرَ، فَلَمَّا خَوَّفْتُهُ بِعُمَرَ تَرَكَنِي، وَقَدْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ مِنْ وَلَدِ آدَمَ أَنَا، فَأَيُّمَا عَبْدٌ مِنْ أُمَّتِي لَعَنْتُهُ لَعْنَةً، أَوْ سَبَبْتُهُ سَبَّةً، فِي غَيْرِ كُنْهِهِ، فَاجْعَلْهَا عَلَيْهِ صَلاةً‏
translation.ai_translation: My father offered Salman his sister in marriage, but he declined and married a freedwoman of his named Buqayra. Abu Qurra heard that there was something between Hudhayfa and Salman, so he went looking for him. He was told he was in a vegetable plot of his, so he went there and met him with a basket of greens, his staff pushed through the basket's handle and resting on his shoulder. He said: Abu Abdullah, what was it between you and Hudhayfa? Salman said: "Man is ever hasty." They went on until they came to Salman's house. Salman went in and said: Peace be upon you. Then he gave Abu Qurra leave, and he went in. There was a rug laid on a door, with some bricks at its head, and a saddle cloth. He said: Sit on your freedwoman's bed, which she spreads for herself. Then he began to tell him: Hudhayfa used to relate things the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said in anger about certain people. People would come to me and ask me about them, and I would say: Hudhayfa knows best what he says. I disliked that there should be grudges between peoples. Then Hudhayfa was told: Salman neither confirms nor denies what you say. So Hudhayfa came to me and said: Salman, son of Salman's mother! I said: Hudhayfa, son of Hudhayfa's mother, you will stop, or I will write to Umar about you. When I made him fear Umar, he left me alone. And the Messenger of God said: I am one of the children of Adam. So any servant from my community whom I have cursed with a curse or insulted with an insult that he did not deserve, make it a blessing upon him.

situation: Ibn Mas'ud climbed a tree at the Prophet's request. The companions saw his very thin legs and laughed.
wise_response: The Prophet said, "What are you laughing at? Abdullah's leg is heavier in the Balance than the mountain of Uhud."
why_it_worked: A person's worth lies in character and deeds, not in how the body looks. Mocking it is foolish.
tempting_wrong_answer: Laughing at someone's body or appearance.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَلامٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ غَزْوَانَ، عَنْ مُغِيرَةَ، عَنْ أُمِّ مُوسَى قَالَتْ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ عَلِيًّا صَلَوَاتُ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ يَقُولُ‏:‏ أَمَرَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَبْدَ اللهِ بْنَ مَسْعُودٍ أَنْ يَصْعَدَ شَجَرَةً فَيَأْتِيَهُ مِنْهَا بِشَيْءٍ، فَنَظَرَ أَصْحَابُهُ إِلَى سَاقِ عَبْدِ اللهِ فَضَحِكُوا مِنْ حُمُوشَةِ سَاقَيْهِ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ مَا تَضْحَكُونَ‏؟‏ لَرِجْلُ عَبْدِ اللهِ أَثْقَلُ فِي الْمِيزَانِ مِنْ أُحُدٍ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, peace be upon him, ordered Abdullah ibn Mas'ud to climb a tree and bring him something from it. His companions looked at Abdullah's shins and laughed at how thin they were. The Messenger of God said: What are you laughing at? Abdullah's leg is heavier in the Balance than Uhud.

situation: A person sees a friend's faults and knows the friend's interests are at risk when he is not around.
wise_response: The Prophet said the believer is his brother's mirror. He guards him against loss and protects him behind his back.
why_it_worked: A true friend shows you yourself honestly and looks after you when you cannot look after yourself.
tempting_wrong_answer: Flattering a friend to his face and letting him be harmed or slandered in his absence.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ حَمْزَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنْ كَثِيرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، عَنِ الْوَلِيدِ بْنِ رَبَاحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ الْمُؤْمِنُ مَرْآةُ أَخِيهِ، وَالْمُؤْمِنُ أَخُو الْمُؤْمِنِ، يَكُفُّ عَلَيْهِ ضَيْعَتَهُ، وَيَحُوطُهُ مِنْ وَرَائِهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The believer is his brother's mirror. The believer is the brother of the believer: he keeps loss away from him and guards him from behind.

situation: Someone can gain a meal, clothing or standing by running down a fellow Muslim to others.
wise_response: The Prophet warned that whoever eats a meal or wears a garment gained at a Muslim's expense will be given the like from Hell, and whoever shows himself off at another's expense will be put on show on the Day of Resurrection.
why_it_worked: Profit or fame bought by damaging someone's honour is a wrong that returns on the one who does it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Selling gossip or slander about others for favour, gifts or status.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عَاصِمٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي حَيْوَةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا بَقِيَّةُ، عَنِ ابْنِ ثَوْبَانَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ مَكْحُولٍ، عَنْ وَقَّاصِ بْنِ رَبِيعَةَ، عَنِ الْمُسْتَوْرِدِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ أَكَلَ بِمُسْلِمٍ أُكْلَةً، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُطْعِمُهُ مِثْلَهَا مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ، وَمَنْ كُسِيَ بِرَجُلٍ مُسْلِمٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَكْسُوهُ مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ، وَمَنْ قَامَ بِرَجُلٍ مَقَامَ رِيَاءٍ وَسُمْعَةٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُومُ بِهِ مَقَامَ رِيَاءٍ وَسُمْعَةٍ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whoever eats a meal at the expense of a Muslim, God will feed him the like of it from Hell. Whoever is clothed at the expense of a Muslim man, God, Mighty and Majestic, will clothe him from Hell. And whoever takes a stand of show and fame at another man's expense, God will make him stand in a place of show and fame on the Day of Resurrection.

situation: Friends play pranks by taking each other's belongings.
wise_response: The Prophet said not to take a companion's things, in play or in earnest. If you take his staff, give it back.
why_it_worked: A joke that takes another's property still causes worry and loss. Respect for what belongs to others holds even in fun.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hiding or keeping a friend's things and calling it a joke.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَاصِمُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ أَبِي ذِئْبٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ السَّائِبِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، يَعْنِي، يَقُولُ‏:‏ لاَ يَأْخُذُ أَحَدُكُمْ مَتَاعَ صَاحِبِهِ لاَعِبًا وَلاَ جَادًّا، فَإِذَا أَخَذَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَصَا صَاحِبِهِ فَلْيَرُدَّهَا إِلَيْهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Let none of you take his companion's belongings, in play or in earnest. If one of you takes his companion's staff, let him give it back to him.

situation: A man's mount broke down on his journey and he asked the Prophet for another. The Prophet had none to give.
wise_response: He sent him to a man who might help, and that man gave him a mount. The Prophet said, "Whoever points the way to good has the like of the reward of the one who does it."
why_it_worked: When you cannot help directly, connecting a person with someone who can is real help.
tempting_wrong_answer: Saying "I have nothing" and leaving it there.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ كَثِيرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ أَبِي عَمْرٍو الشَّيْبَانِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي مَسْعُودٍ الأَنْصَارِيِّ قَالَ‏:‏ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ‏:‏ إِنِّي أُبْدِعَ بِي فَاحْمِلْنِي، قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ أَجِدُ، وَلَكِنِ ائْتِ فُلاَنًا، فَلَعَلَّهُ أَنْ يَحْمِلَكَ، فَأَتَاهُ فَحَمَلَهُ، فَأَتَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَخْبَرَهُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and said: My mount has broken down, so give me a mount. He said: I have none, but go to so-and-so; perhaps he will give you a mount. He went to him and he gave him a mount. Then he came to the Prophet and told him, and he said: Whoever points the way to good has the like of the reward of the one who does it.

situation: A woman served the Prophet a poisoned sheep and he ate from it. She was brought before him and his companions asked whether to kill her.
wise_response: He said, "No." Anas said the effect of the poison stayed visible in the Prophet's mouth for years after.
why_it_worked: He chose mercy toward someone who tried to harm him personally, though the harm lasted.
tempting_wrong_answer: Taking revenge on the spot for an attempt on one's own life.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْوَهَّابِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا خَالِدُ بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، أَنَّ يَهُودِيَّةً أَتَتِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِشَاةٍ مَسْمُومَةٍ، فَأَكَلَ مِنْهَا، فَجِيءَ بِهَا، فَقِيلَ‏:‏ أَلاَ نَقْتُلُهَا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَمَا زِلْتُ أَعْرِفُهَا فِي لَهَوَاتِ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A Jewish woman brought the Prophet, peace be upon him, a poisoned sheep, and he ate from it. She was brought, and it was said: Shall we not kill her? He said: No. Anas said: I kept recognising it in the palate of the Messenger of God.

situation: Ibn az-Zubayr spoke from the pulpit about the verse "Take what is freely given, command what is right, and turn away from the ignorant."
wise_response: He said it means to accept from people's characters what comes easily, and swore he would do so as long as he lived among them.
why_it_worked: Expecting perfection from people leads to constant friction. Taking them as they are keeps peace.
tempting_wrong_answer: Demanding more of people than they can give and quarrelling over every flaw.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَلامٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامٌ، عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ عَبْدَ اللهِ بْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ يَقُولُ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ‏:‏ ‏{‏خُذِ الْعَفْوَ‏}‏ وَأْمُرْ بِالْعُرْفِ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْجَاهِلِينَ، قَالَ‏:‏ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَمَرَ بِهَا أَنْ تُؤْخَذَ إِلاَّ مِنْ أَخْلاَقِ النَّاسِ، وَاللَّهِ لَآخُذَنَّهَا مِنْهُمْ مَا صَحِبْتُهُمْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: "Take what is freely given, command what is right, and turn away from the ignorant." He said: By God, He commanded only that it be taken from people's characters. By God, I will take it from them for as long as I keep company with them.

key_terms.العفو (al-'afw): what is freely given, pardon, the easy part

situation: A teacher or leader must guide others, and anger sometimes rises in the moment.
wise_response: The Prophet said: teach, make things easy and do not make them hard. When one of you is angry, let him be silent.
why_it_worked: Ease draws people in and harshness drives them off. Silence in anger prevents words one would regret.
tempting_wrong_answer: Making rules burdensome and speaking while angry.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَلامٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ فُضَيْلِ بْنِ غَزْوَانَ، عَنْ لَيْثٍ، عَنْ طَاوُسٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ عَلِّمُوا وَيَسِّرُوا وَلاَ تُعَسِّرُوا، وَإِذَا غَضِبَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَسْكُتْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Teach, make things easy and do not make them hard. And when one of you becomes angry, let him keep silent.

situation: Ata asked Abdullah ibn Amr how the Prophet was described in the Torah.
wise_response: Abdullah said he is described as neither harsh nor coarse, not loud in the markets, one who does not repay a bad deed with a bad deed but pardons and forgives.
why_it_worked: Gentleness and forgiveness are named as marks of the best character.
tempting_wrong_answer: Answering rudeness with rudeness and harm with harm.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا فُلَيْحُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا هِلاَلُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ قَالَ‏:‏ لَقِيتُ عَبْدَ اللهِ بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ أَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ صِفَةِ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي التَّوْرَاةِ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَجَلْ وَاللَّهِ، إِنَّهُ لَمَوْصُوفٌ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ بِبَعْضِ صِفَتِهِ فِي الْقُرْآنِ‏:‏ ‏{‏يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِدًا وَمُبَشِّرًا وَنَذِيرًا‏}‏، وَحِرْزًا لِلأُمِّيِّينَ، أَنْتَ عَبْدِي وَرَسُولِي، سَمَّيْتُكَ الْمُتَوَكِّلَ، لَيْسَ بِفَظٍّ وَلاَ غَلِيظٍ، وَلاَ صَخَّابٍ فِي الأَسْوَاقِ، وَلاَ يَدْفَعُ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ، وَلَكِنْ يَعْفُو وَيَغْفِرُ، وَلَنْ يَقْبِضَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى حَتَّى يُقِيمَ بِهِ الْمِلَّةَ الْعَوْجَاءَ، بِأَنْ يَقُولُوا‏:‏ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ، وَيَفْتَحُوا بِهَا أَعْيُنًا عُمْيًا، وَآذَانًا صُمًّا، وَقُلُوبًا غُلْفًا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I met Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As and said: Tell me about the description of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, in the Torah. He said: Yes, by God, he is described in the Torah with some of his description in the Qur'an: "O Prophet, We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good news and a warner," and a safeguard for the unlettered. You are My servant and My messenger. I have named you the one who trusts. He is not harsh or coarse, nor loud in the markets. He does not repay a bad deed with a bad deed, but pardons and forgives. God the Exalted will not take him until He has straightened the crooked creed through him, so that they say: There is no god but God, and through it open blind eyes, deaf ears and covered hearts.

situation: A ruler or manager is tempted to watch people closely and act on every suspicion.
wise_response: Mu'awiya recalled the Prophet saying that if you chase after suspicions about people, you will corrupt them. So he did not.
why_it_worked: Constant suspicion breeds the very behaviour it fears. Trust gives people room to be decent.
tempting_wrong_answer: Spying on people and treating every doubt as proof.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ الْعَلاَءِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ الْحَارِثِ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ سَالِمٍ الأَشْعَرِيُّ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ هُوَ ابْنُ الْوَلِيدِ الزُّبَيْدِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ جَابِرٍ وَهُوَ يَحْيَى بْنُ جَابِرٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ نُفَيْرٍ حَدَّثَهُ، أَنَّ أَبَاهُ حَدَّثَهُ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ مُعَاوِيَةَ يَقُولُ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ مِنَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَلاَمًا نَفَعَنِي اللَّهُ بِهِ، سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ، أَوْ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ إِنَّكَ إِذَا اتَّبَعْتَ الرِّيبَةَ فِي النَّاسِ أَفْسَدْتَهُمْ فَإِنِّي لاَ أَتَّبِعُ الرِّيبَةَ فِيهِمْ فَأُفْسِدَهُمْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I heard words from the Prophet, peace be upon him, by which God benefited me. I heard him say: If you follow up suspicion about people, you will corrupt them. So I do not follow up suspicion about them and so corrupt them.

situation: The Prophet was with his small grandson al-Hasan or al-Husayn.
wise_response: He held the boy's hands, let him climb up his legs until his feet were on his chest, kissed him, and prayed, "O God, love him, for I love him."
why_it_worked: Open, playful affection shows a child he is loved and safe.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping children at a distance out of dignity or busyness.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عُبَيْدِ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَاتِمٌ، عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ أَبِي مُزَرِّدٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ يَقُولُ‏:‏ سَمِعَ أُذُنَايَ هَاتَانِ، وَبَصُرَ عَيْنَايَ هَاتَانِ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَخَذَ بِيَدَيْهِ جَمِيعًا بِكَفَّيِّ الْحَسَنِ، أَوِ الْحُسَيْنِ صَلَوَاتُ اللهِ عَلَيْهِمَا وَقَدَمَيهِ عَلَى قَدَمِ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَرَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ ارْقَهْ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَرَقِيَ الْغُلاَمُ حَتَّى وَضَعَ قَدَمَيْهِ عَلَى صَدْرِ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، ثُمَّ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ افْتَحْ فَاكَ، ثُمَّ قَبَّلَهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ‏:‏ اللَّهُمَّ أَحِبَّهُ، فَإِنِّي أُحِبُّهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: These two ears of mine heard and these two eyes of mine saw the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, take hold of the palms of al-Hasan, or al-Husayn, with both hands, his feet on the feet of the Messenger of God, while the Messenger of God said: Climb up. The boy climbed until he put his feet on the chest of the Messenger of God. Then the Messenger of God said: Open your mouth. Then he kissed him and said: O God, love him, for I love him.

situation: A person feels strongly about someone, either drawn to them or set against them. Strong feeling pulls toward excess in both directions.
wise_response: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: keep your love from turning into doting, and keep your dislike from turning into ruin. Asked what he meant, he said that in love people dote like a child, and in dislike they come to want their companion destroyed.
why_it_worked: Love and dislike both stay sound when they are held in measure. Love without restraint loses judgment, and dislike without restraint becomes a wish to harm.
tempting_wrong_answer: To fall into childish infatuation with someone you love, or to let dislike grow until you want the other person to come to ruin.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي مَرْيَمَ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا زَيْدُ بْنُ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ يَكُنْ حُبُّكَ كَلَفًا، وَلاَ بُغْضُكَ تَلَفًا، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ كَيْفَ ذَاكَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ إِذَا أَحْبَبْتَ كَلِفْتَ كَلَفَ الصَّبِيِّ، وَإِذَا أَبْغَضْتَ أَحْبَبْتَ لِصَاحِبِكَ التَّلَف‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "Do not let your love be doting, and do not let your hatred be ruin." I asked, "How is that?" He said, "When you love, you dote the way a child dotes. When you hate, you want your companion to be ruined."

situation: Jarir became Muslim and met the Prophet often afterwards.
wise_response: Jarir said the Prophet never once saw him without smiling at him.
why_it_worked: A steady, warm welcome made Jarir feel valued every time.
tempting_wrong_answer: Greeting people with a cold or indifferent face.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنِا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنْ قَيْسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ جَرِيرًا يَقُولُ‏:‏ مَا رَآنِي رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مُنْذُ أَسْلَمْتُ إِلاَّ تَبَسَّمَ فِي وَجْهِي، وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ يَدْخُلُ مِنْ هَذَا الْبَابِ رَجُلٌ مِنْ خَيْرِ ذِي يَمَنٍ، عَلَى وَجْهِهِ مَسْحَةُ مَلَكٍ، فَدَخَلَ جَرِيرٌ‏.‏

situation: A person spends much of his time in jokes and laughter.
wise_response: The Prophet said to laugh less, for much laughter deadens the heart.
why_it_worked: Constant levity dulls a person to what matters. Moderation keeps the heart awake.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating everything as a joke.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ أَبُو الرَّبِيعِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ زَكَرِيَّا، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو رَجَاءٍ، عَنْ بُرْدٍ، عَنْ مَكْحُولٍ، عَنْ وَاثِلَةَ بْنِ الأَسْقَعِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ أَقِلَّ الضَّحِكَ، فَإِنَّ كَثْرَةَ الضَّحِكِ تُمِيتُ الْقَلْبَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Laugh less, for much laughter deadens the heart.

situation: The Prophet found his companions laughing and warned that if they knew what he knew, they would laugh little and weep much. They were left weeping.
wise_response: He was told not to make people despair. He went back and said, "Rejoice, keep to the right course, and come as near to it as you can."
why_it_worked: A warning that crushes hope does harm. He corrected himself and gave them encouragement with the guidance.
tempting_wrong_answer: Frightening people into despair and leaving them there.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الرَّبِيعُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ خَرَجَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى رَهْطٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ يَضْحَكُونَ وَيَتَحَدَّثُونَ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ مَا أَعْلَمُ لَضَحِكْتُمْ قَلِيلاً، وَلَبَكَيْتُمْ كَثِيرًا، ثُمَّ انْصَرَفَ وَأَبْكَى الْقَوْمَ، وَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِلَيْهِ‏:‏ يَا مُحَمَّدُ، لِمَ تُقَنِّطُ عِبَادِي‏؟‏، فَرَجَعَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَبْشِرُوا، وَسَدِّدُوا، وَقَارِبُوا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, peace be upon him, came out to a group of his companions who were laughing and talking. He said: By the One in whose hand my soul is, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much. Then he left, and the people wept. God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: Muhammad, why do you make My servants despair? So the Prophet went back and said: Rejoice, aim aright, and come as close as you can.

situation: Abu'l-Haytham was to receive a servant and asked the Prophet to choose for him.
wise_response: The Prophet said, "The one who is consulted is entrusted," chose a man he had seen praying, and told him to treat him well. Abu'l-Haytham's wife said he could only fulfil that by freeing him, so he freed him.
why_it_worked: Advice is a trust and must be given in the other's true interest. Abu'l-Haytham listened to his wife's counsel and did more than the minimum.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving careless or self-serving advice, or ignoring good counsel from those close to you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا آدَمُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شَيْبَانُ أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْمَلِكِ بْنُ عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لأَبِي الْهَيْثَمِ‏:‏ هَلْ لَكَ خَادِمٌ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَإِذَا أَتَانَا سَبْيٌ فَأْتِنَا فَأُتِيَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِرَأْسَيْنِ لَيْسَ مَعَهُمَا ثَالِثٌ، فَأَتَاهُ أَبُو الْهَيْثَمِ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ اخْتَرْ مِنْهُمَا، قَالَ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، اخْتَرْ لِي، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ إِنَّ الْمُسْتَشَارَ مُؤْتَمَنٌ، خُذْ هَذَا، فَإِنِّي رَأَيْتُهُ يُصَلِّي، وَاسْتَوْصِ بِهِ خَيْرًا، فَقَالَتِ امْرَأَتُهُ‏:‏ مَا أَنْتَ بِبَالِغٍ مَا قَالَ فِيهِ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلاَّ أَنْ تُعْتِقَهُ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَهُوَ عَتِيقٌ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يَبْعَثْ نَبِيًّا وَلاَ خَلِيفَةً، إِلاَّ وَلَهُ بِطَانَتَانِ‏:‏ بِطَانَةٌ تَأْمُرُهُ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَتَنْهَاهُ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ، وَبِطَانَةٌ لاَ تَأْلُوهُ خَبَالاً، وَمَنْ يُوقَ بِطَانَةَ السُّوءِ فَقَدْ وُقِيَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said to Abu'l-Haytham: Do you have a servant? He said: No. He said: When captives come to us, come to us. Two captives were brought to the Prophet, with no third. Abu'l-Haytham came to him, and the Prophet said: Choose between them. He said: Messenger of God, choose for me. The Prophet said: The one who is consulted is entrusted. Take this one, for I have seen him praying, and treat him well. His wife said: You will not reach what the Prophet said about him unless you free him. He said: Then he is free. The Prophet said: God has not sent a prophet or a successor but that he has two inner circles: a circle that bids him to what is right and forbids him what is wrong, and a circle that spares no effort to ruin him. Whoever is protected from the bad circle has been protected.

situation: A group faces a decision and could leave it to one person's judgment.
wise_response: Al-Hasan said no people ever consulted one another without being guided to the best course open to them, and recited, "Their affairs are by consultation among them."
why_it_worked: Many minds together see more than one. Consulting others leads to better choices.
tempting_wrong_answer: Deciding alone out of pride or haste.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا آدَمُ بْنُ أَبِي إِيَاسٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، عَنِ السَّرِيِّ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ قَالَ‏:‏ وَاللَّهِ مَا اسْتَشَارَ قَوْمٌ قَطُّ إِلاَّ هُدُوا لأَفْضَلِ مَا بِحَضْرَتِهِمْ، ثُمَّ تَلاَ‏:‏ ‏{‏وَأَمْرُهُمْ شُورَى بَيْنَهُمْ‏}‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: By God, no people ever took counsel together but they were guided to the best of what was before them. Then he recited: "And their affair is by consultation among them."

situation: A friend asks for your advice. You could give it carelessly or bend it to suit yourself.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever is asked for advice by his brother and points him to what is not right has betrayed him.
why_it_worked: Someone who asks for counsel trusts you. Bad advice breaks that trust.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving advice that serves one's own interest, or answering without knowing.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ يَزِيدَ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي بَكْرُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو، عَنْ أَبِي عُثْمَانَ مُسْلِمِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ مَنْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيَّ مَا لَمْ أَقُلْ، فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ وَمَنِ اسْتَشَارَهُ أَخُوهُ الْمُسْلِمُ، فَأَشَارَ عَلَيْهِ بِغَيْرِ رُشْدٍ فَقَدْ خَانَهُ وَمَنْ أُفْتِيَ فُتْيَا بِغَيْرِ ثَبْتٍ، فَإِثْمُهُ عَلَى مَنْ أَفْتَاهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whoever attributes to me what I did not say, let him take his seat in the Fire. Whoever is asked for counsel by his Muslim brother and advises him to what is not right has betrayed him. And whoever is given a ruling without a firm basis, its sin is on the one who gave it.

situation: People in a community drift apart and resentment builds.
wise_response: The Prophet said you will not truly submit until you love one another, and told them to spread greetings of peace. He warned that hatred is a razor that shaves away religion.
why_it_worked: Simple greetings build love, and hatred destroys faith from within.
tempting_wrong_answer: Passing people without greeting them and letting hatred settle in.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبِي أُوَيْسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي أَخِي، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ بِلاَلٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي أُسَيْدٍ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، لاَ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى تُسْلِمُوا، وَلاَ تُسْلِمُوا حَتَّى تَحَابُّوا، وَأَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ تَحَابُّوا، وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَالْبُغْضَةَ، فَإِنَّهَا هِيَ الْحَالِقَةُ، لاَ أَقُولُ لَكُمْ‏:‏ تَحْلِقُ الشَّعْرَ، وَلَكِنْ تَحْلِقُ الدِّينَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: By the One in whose hand my soul is, you will not enter the Garden until you submit, and you will not submit until you love one another. Spread the greeting of peace and you will love one another. And beware of hatred, for it is the shaver. I do not say to you that it shaves hair, but it shaves religion.

key_terms.الحالقة (al-haliqa): the shaver, that which strips away

situation: Ibn Abbas reflected on what holds people together.
wise_response: He said favours are met with ingratitude and family ties are cut, but he had seen nothing like the closeness of hearts.
why_it_worked: Gifts and kinship can fail. A bond of genuine affection outlasts them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Relying on favours or family obligation alone and neglecting real friendship.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَيْسَرَةَ، عَنْ طَاوُسٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ النِّعَمُ تُكْفَرُ، وَالرَّحِمُ تُقْطَعُ، وَلَمْ نَرَ مِثْلَ تَقَارُبِ الْقُلُوبِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Blessings are denied, ties of kinship are cut, and we have seen nothing like the drawing together of hearts.

situation: Anjasha, a camel driver, was driving the camels carrying some of the Prophet's wives and Umm Sulaym, and pushing them fast.
wise_response: The Prophet said, "Anjasha, gently! Go slowly with the glass vessels."
why_it_worked: He looked out for the comfort of those in someone else's charge and asked for gentleness.
tempting_wrong_answer: Rushing ahead without regard for the people who must bear the ride.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلاَبَةَ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أَتَى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى بَعْضِ نِسَائِهِ وَمَعَهُنَّ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا أَنْجَشَةُ، رُوَيْدًا سَوْقَكَ بِالْقَوَارِيرِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, peace be upon him, came upon some of his wives, with Umm Sulaym among them, and said: Anjasha, gently, drive the glass vessels slowly.

situation: The companions noticed that the Prophet joked with them and asked him about it.

translation.ai_translation: They said: Messenger of God, you joke with us? He said: I say nothing but the truth.

situation: A man asked the Prophet for a mount. The Prophet said he would give him a she-camel's young, and the man protested he could not ride a calf.
wise_response: The Prophet said, "Are camels born of anything but she-camels?"
why_it_worked: He joked kindly and the joke was still true. Every camel is some she-camel's young.
tempting_wrong_answer: Teasing with a falsehood, or being so stern one never puts people at ease.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الصَّبَّاحِ حَدَّثَنَا خَالِدٌ هُوَ ابْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ، عَنْ حُمَيْدٍ الطَّوِيلِ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ قَالَ‏:‏ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَسْتَحْمِلُهُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَنَا حَامِلُكَ عَلَى وَلَدِ نَاقَةٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، وَمَا أَصْنَعُ بِوَلَدِ نَاقَةٍ‏؟‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ وَهَلْ تَلِدُ الإِبِلَ إِلاَّ النُّوقُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, asking him for a mount. He said: I will mount you on a she-camel's young. He said: Messenger of God, what will I do with a she-camel's young? The Messenger of God said: And do camels give birth to anything but she-camels?

wise_response: The Prophet mixed with the family so freely that he would ask the boy, "Abu Umayr, what happened to the little bird?"
why_it_worked: He took a child's small world seriously and spoke to him with warmth.
tempting_wrong_answer: Ignoring children's concerns as beneath notice.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا آدَمُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو التَّيَّاحِ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ يَقُولُ‏:‏ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَيُخَالِطُنَا، حَتَّى يَقُولَ لأَخٍ لِي صَغِيرٍ‏:‏ يَا أَبَا عُمَيْرٍ، مَا فَعَلَ النُّغَيْرُ‏؟‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, peace be upon him, used to mingle with us so much that he would say to a little brother of mine: Abu Umayr, what has the little bird done?

wise_response: He was never obscene and never tried to be. He used to say, "The best of you are those with the best character."

tempting_wrong_answer: Using crude or abusive language.

translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, peace be upon him, was neither obscene nor one who affected obscenity, and he used to say: The best of you are the best of you in character.

situation: The Prophet told 'A'isha he could tell when she was pleased or angry with him.

situation: A quarrel turns into a long estrangement.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever shuns his brother for a year is like one who sheds his blood.

tempting_wrong_answer: Letting a grudge stretch into months and years.

situation: Someone moves between two groups who are at odds.
wise_response: The Prophet said that among the worst people with God on the Day of Resurrection is the two-faced, who comes to these with one face and to those with another.

tempting_wrong_answer: Telling each group what it wants to hear.

situation: You start to assume the worst about other people.
wise_response: The Prophet said: beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of talk. Do not bid up prices to trick buyers, do not envy, do not hate, do not compete for worldly things, do not turn your backs on one another. Be servants of God, brothers.
why_it_worked: Suspicion feels like knowledge and often is false. Trickery, envy and coldness all poison brotherhood.
tempting_wrong_answer: Acting on suspicion, or using small tricks to gain at another's expense.

situation: Two people hold a grudge against each other.
wise_response: The Prophet said the gates of the Garden open on Mondays and Thursdays and everyone who does not associate partners with God is forgiven, except a man with enmity between him and his brother. It is said: hold these two back until they make peace.
why_it_worked: Forgiveness from God waits on making peace with each other. A grudge blocks the way.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping a feud going and assuming it does not matter to God.

situation: A person carries rancor toward someone.
wise_response: The Prophet named among those whom God may forgive: one who died without associating partners with God, was not a sorcerer, and bore no rancor toward his brother.
why_it_worked: A heart free of resentment toward others is named with the most basic conditions for forgiveness.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping a private store of resentment toward a brother.

situation: Three days have passed since a falling-out.
wise_response: The Prophet said that after three days a person should go to the other and greet him. If he answers, they share the reward. If he does not, the one who greeted is cleared of the sin of shunning.
why_it_worked: You are responsible for your own step toward peace. Once you offer it, the burden moves to the one who refuses.
tempting_wrong_answer: Waiting it out, or giving up on peace because the other might rebuff you.

tempting_wrong_answer: Crowding together until small irritations turn into a family rift.

situation: One man cursed another in front of the Prophet. The second man said nothing, then finally answered back.
wise_response: The Prophet sat while the man was silent and got up when he retorted. He explained that while the man was silent the angels were answering for him. When he answered, the angels left, and he left with them.
why_it_worked: Silence under insult keeps a person in the right with the angels on his side. Answering back drags him into the quarrel.
tempting_wrong_answer: Trading insult for insult.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أُمَيَّةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عِيسَى بْنُ مُوسَى، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ اسْتَبَّ رَجُلاَنِ عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَسَبَّ أَحَدُهُمَا وَالْآخَرُ سَاكِتٌ، وَالنَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَالِسٌ، ثُمَّ رَدَّ الْآخَرُ‏.‏ فَنَهَضَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقِيلَ‏:‏ نَهَضْتَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ نَهَضَتِ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ فَنَهَضْتُ مَعَهُمْ، إِنَّ هَذَا مَا كَانَ سَاكِتًا رَدَّتِ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ عَلَى الَّذِي سَبَّهُ، فَلَمَّا رَدَّ نَهَضَتِ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Ibn 'Abbas said: Two men reviled each other in the time of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. One reviled while the other was silent, and the Prophet was sitting. Then the other answered back, and the Prophet got up. It was said, "You got up?" He said, "The angels got up, so I got up with them. While this one was silent, the angels were answering the one who reviled him. When he answered, the angels got up."
