situation: A man told Umm ad-Darda' that someone had spoken badly of her before the caliph 'Abd al-Malik.
wise_response: She said, "If we are blamed for what is not in us, how often we have been praised for what is not in us."
why_it_worked: She weighed the unfair blame against the unearned praise she had received. That kept her calm and humble.
tempting_wrong_answer: Rushing to defend yourself or striking back at the one who spoke against you.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا رُدَيْحُ بْنُ عَطِيَّةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْلَةَ، عَنْ أُمِّ الدَّرْدَاءِ أَنَّ رَجُلاً أَتَاهَا فَقَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّ رَجُلاً نَالَ مِنْكِ عِنْدَ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ، فَقَالَتْ‏:‏ إِنْ نُؤْبَنَ بِمَا لَيْسَ فِينَا، فَطَالَمَا زُكِّينَا بِمَا لَيْسَ فِينَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Abla reported from Umm ad-Darda' that a man came to her and said, "A man spoke ill of you before 'Abd al-Malik." She said, "If we are faulted for what is not in us, how long we have been praised for what is not in us."

situation: A person wonders how he can give charity every day.
wise_response: Ibn 'Abbas said each of the 360 joints of the body owes charity every day. Every good word is charity. Helping your brother is charity. A drink of water you give is charity. Removing something harmful from the road is charity.
why_it_worked: Small, ordinary kindnesses are a way of giving thanks for your own body.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking charity means only money, and so doing nothing.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَاحِدِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا لَيْثٌ، عَنْ طَاوُسٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، أَظُنُّهُ رَفَعَهُ، شَكَّ لَيْثٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ فِي ابْنِ آدَمَ سِتُّونَ وَثَلاَثُمِئَةِ سُلاَمَى، أَوْ عَظْمٍ، أَوْ مَفْصِلٍ، عَلَى كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ صَدَقَةٌ، كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ طَيْبَةٍ صَدَقَةٌ، وَعَوْنُ الرَّجُلِ أَخَاهُ صَدَقَةٌ، وَالشَّرْبَةُ مِنَ الْمَاءِ يَسْقِيهَا صَدَقَةٌ، وَإِمَاطَةُ الأَذَى عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ صَدَقَةٌ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Ibn 'Abbas said, and Layth thought he traced it to the Prophet: "In the son of Adam are three hundred and sixty joints, or bones, or joints of the limbs. On each one, every day, is a charity. Every good word is charity. A man's help to his brother is charity. A drink of water he gives is charity. Removing harm from the road is charity."

situation: Two people are trading insults.
wise_response: The Prophet said that what two people say in reviling each other falls on the one who started it, as long as the wronged one does not go beyond what was said.
why_it_worked: The one who starts the abuse carries the blame. The one who answers stays clear only if he does not exceed what he received.
tempting_wrong_answer: Starting the insults, or answering an insult with worse.

translation.ai_translation: Abu Hurayra reported that the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Two who revile each other: what they say is on the one who began, as long as the wronged one does not transgress."

situation: 'Iyad ibn Himar asked the Prophet about a man who insulted him.
wise_response: The Prophet said two who revile each other are two devils who trade abuse and lies.

translation.ai_translation: 'Iyad ibn Himar said: I said, "Messenger of God, a man reviles me?" The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Two who revile each other are two devils, babbling at each other and calling each other liars."

situation: How to rebuke someone who has done wrong.
wise_response: Anas said the Prophet was never coarse, never cursed and never reviled. When he wanted to reproach someone, he said, "What is the matter with him? May his forehead be dusty."
why_it_worked: Correction can be firm without being abusive. His mildest phrase did the work.
tempting_wrong_answer: Reproaching people with curses and insults.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا فُلَيْحُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا هِلاَلُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ لَمْ يَكُنْ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَاحِشًا، وَلاَ لَعَّانًا، وَلاَ سَبَّابًا، كَانَ يَقُولُ عِنْدَ الْمَعْتَبَةِ‏:‏ مَا لَهُ تَرِبَ جَبِينُهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Anas said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, was not foul-spoken, nor a curser, nor a reviler. When he reproached someone he would say, "What is wrong with him, may his forehead be dusty."

situation: 'Ali, then the Commander of the Believers, bought a dirham's worth of dates and carried them home wrapped in his cloak. Someone offered to carry them for him.
wise_response: 'Ali refused. He said the father of the family has the most right to carry it.
why_it_worked: Carrying his own household's food kept 'Ali close to ordinary work. High rank did not put him above serving his family.
tempting_wrong_answer: A man in power lets others carry his load and treats small chores as beneath him.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ بَحْرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ هَاشِمِ بْنِ الْبَرِيدِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا صَالِحٌ بَيَّاعُ الأَكْسِيَةِ، عَنْ جَدَّتِهِ قَالَتْ‏:‏ رَأَيْتُ عَلِيًّا رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ اشْتَرَى تَمْرًا بِدِرْهَمٍ، فَحَمَلَهُ فِي مِلْحَفَتِهِ، فَقُلْتُ لَهُ، أَوْ قَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ‏:‏ أَحْمِلُ عَنْكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، أَبُو الْعِيَالِ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يَحْمِلَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I saw 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, buy dates for a dirham and carry them in his wrap. I said to him, or a man said to him: "Let me carry it for you, Commander of the Believers." He said: "No. The father of the household has more right to carry it."

key_terms.أبو العيال (abu al-'iyal): father of the household, the one who provides for dependents

situation: A person grows proud of their power and standing and acts as if greatness belongs to them.
wise_response: The Prophet reported that God said: might is His lower garment and grandeur His cloak, and whoever contends with Him for either will be punished.
why_it_worked: Greatness belongs to God alone. A person who claims it reaches for something that is not theirs.
tempting_wrong_answer: Carrying oneself with arrogance and claiming a grandeur over others that no human owns.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ أَبِي مُسْلِمٍ الأَغَرِّ حَدَّثَهُ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ، وَأَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ الْعِزُّ إِزَارِي، وَالْكِبْرِيَاءُ رِدَائِي، فَمَنْ نَازَعَنِي بِشَيْءٍ مِنْهُمَا عَذَّبْتُهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Might is My lower garment and grandeur is My cloak. Whoever contends with Me over anything of them, I will punish him."

key_terms.الكبرياء (al-kibriya'): grandeur, pride; here the greatness that belongs only to God

situation: An-Nu'man ibn Bashir warned the people from the pulpit about the traps that lead people astray.
wise_response: He named them: to be reckless and ungrateful with God's blessings, to boast about what God has given, to act proud toward God's servants, and to follow desire for something other than God.
why_it_worked: Each trap turns a gift into a source of vanity. Gratitude and humility keep blessings from becoming snares.
tempting_wrong_answer: Showing off one's wealth or gifts and looking down on other people because of them.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ حُجْرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو رَوَاحَةَ يَزِيدُ بْنُ أَيْهَمَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ الطَّائِيِّ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ النُّعْمَانَ بْنَ بَشِيرٍ يَقُولُ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ، قَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّ لِلشَّيْطَانِ مَصَالِيًا وَفُخُوخًا، وَإِنَّ مَصَالِيَ الشَّيْطَانِ وَفُخُوخَهُ‏:‏ الْبَطَرُ بِأَنْعُمِ اللهِ، وَالْفَخْرُ بِعَطَاءِ اللهِ، وَالْكِبْرِيَاءُ عَلَى عِبَادِ اللهِ، وَاتِّبَاعُ الْهَوَى فِي غَيْرِ ذَاتِ اللهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Satan has snares and traps. Among Satan's snares and traps are: reckless ingratitude for God's blessings, boasting of God's gifts, arrogance toward God's servants, and following desire for other than God's sake.

key_terms.البطر (al-batar): insolent ingratitude, exulting recklessly in a blessing

situation: A handsome man who loved fine things asked the Prophet whether wanting no one to outdo him, even in a sandal strap, was pride.
wise_response: The Prophet said no. Pride is to reject the truth and to look down on people.
why_it_worked: Loving beauty is not the fault. The fault is refusing what is true and holding others in contempt.
tempting_wrong_answer: Dismissing a truth because it came from someone you think beneath you, and treating people as worthless.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَهَّابِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامٌ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَجُلاً أَتَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَكَانَ جَمِيلاً، فَقَالَ‏:‏ حُبِّبَ إِلَيَّ الْجَمَالُ، وَأُعْطِيتُ مَا تَرَى، حَتَّى مَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ يَفُوقَنِي أَحَدٌ، إِمَّا قَالَ‏:‏ بِشِرَاكِ نَعْلٍ، وَإِمَّا قَالَ‏:‏ بِشِسْعٍ أَحْمَرَ، الْكِبْرُ ذَاكَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، وَلَكِنَّ الْكِبْرَ مَنْ بَطَرَ الْحَقَّ، وَغَمَطَ النَّاسَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man came to the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace. He was handsome, and he said: "Beauty has been made dear to me, and I have been given what you see, so that I do not like anyone to surpass me, even by a sandal strap" (or he said, "by a red sandal thong"). "Is that pride?" He said: "No. Pride is to spurn the truth and to belittle people."

key_terms.غمط الناس (ghamt al-nas): belittling people, holding them in contempt

situation: The Ansar of Madina offered to split their palm groves with the emigrants from Mecca, who had arrived with nothing.
wise_response: The Prophet declined the split. Instead the emigrants would do the work of tending the trees and share in the fruit. The Ansar agreed: "We hear and obey."
why_it_worked: The arrangement let the newcomers earn their share with labor. The owners kept their land and both sides were provided for.
tempting_wrong_answer: Either giving nothing to people in need, or handing over property in a way that leaves the newcomers dependent and the givers stripped.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْيَمَانِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعَيْبُ بْنُ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الزِّنَادِ، عَنِ الأَعْرَجِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ الأَنْصَارَ قَالَتْ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ اقْسِمْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَانِنَا النَّخِيلَ، قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ، فَقَالُوا‏:‏ تَكْفُونَا الْمَؤُونَةَ، وَنُشْرِكُكُمْ فِي الثَّمَرَةِ‏؟‏ قَالُوا‏:‏ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Ansar said to the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace: "Divide the palm trees between us and our brothers." He said: "No." They said: "Then you take on the labor for us and we will share the fruit with you?" They said: "We hear and obey."

situation: In the Year of the Drought, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab had sent camels, wheat and oil to the Bedouins until the farmland was exhausted. Then he prayed for rain, and it came.
wise_response: 'Umar said that if relief had not come, he would have placed in every Muslim household that had means as many poor people as its own members. Two people do not perish on food that keeps one alive.
why_it_worked: Shared food stretches. A ruler who plans to make the comfortable carry the hungry in their own homes takes the duty of care seriously.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting those with plenty keep their surplus while the poor starve.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَصْبَغُ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ وَهْبٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي يُونُسُ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، أَنَّ سَالِمًا أَخْبَرَهُ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ أَخْبَرَهُ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ عَامَ الرَّمَادَةِ، وَكَانَتْ سَنَةً شَدِيدَةً مُلِمَّةً، بَعْدَ مَا اجْتَهَدَ عُمَرُ فِي إِمْدَادِ الأعْرَابِ بِالإِبِلِ وَالْقَمْحِ وَالزَّيْتِ مِنَ الأَرْيَافِ كُلِّهَا، حَتَّى بَلَحَتِ الأَرْيَافُ كُلُّهَا مِمَّا جَهَدَهَا ذَلِكَ، فَقَامَ عُمَرُ يَدْعُو فَقَالَ‏:‏ اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ رِزْقَهُمْ عَلَى رُءُوسِ الْجِبَالِ، فَاسْتَجَابَ اللَّهُ لَهُ وَلِلْمُسْلِمِينَ، فَقَالَ حِينَ نَزَلَ بِهِ الْغَيْثُ‏:‏ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، فَوَاللَّهِ لَوْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يُفْرِجْهَا مَا تَرَكْتُ بِأَهْلِ بَيْتٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ لَهُمْ سَعَةٌ إِلاَّ أَدْخَلْتُ مَعَهُمْ أَعْدَادَهُمْ مِنَ الْفُقَرَاءِ، فَلَمْ يَكُنِ اثْنَانِ يَهْلِكَانِ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ عَلَى مَا يُقِيمُ وَاحِدًا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: In the Year of Ashes, a hard and grievous year, after 'Umar had striven to supply the Bedouins with camels, wheat and oil from all the farmlands until the farmlands were worn out by the effort, 'Umar stood and prayed: "O God, place their provision on the mountaintops." God answered him and the Muslims. When the rain came down he said: "Praise be to God. By God, had God not relieved it, I would not have left a single Muslim household with means without putting in with them their own number of the poor. Two people do not perish on food that sustains one."

key_terms.عام الرمادة ('am al-ramada): the Year of Ashes, the great famine in 'Umar's rule

situation: One year the Prophet told people not to keep any sacrificial meat in their homes past three days. The next year they asked whether the rule still held.
wise_response: He told them to eat and store it. That earlier year people had been in hardship, and he had wanted them to help.
why_it_worked: The rule existed so the meat would reach the hungry. When the need passed, the rule eased.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hoarding food in a hard year while neighbors go without.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَاصِمٍ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ أَبِي عُبَيْدٍ، عَنْ سَلَمَةَ بْنِ الأَكْوَعِ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ ضَحَايَاكُمْ، لاَ يُصْبِحُ أَحَدُكُمْ بَعْدَ ثَالِثَةٍ، وَفِي بَيْتِهِ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْعَامُ الْمُقْبِلُ قَالُوا‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، نَفْعَلُ كَمَا فَعَلْنَا الْعَامَ الْمَاضِيَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ كُلُوا وَادَّخِرُوا، فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ الْعَامَ كَانُوا فِي جَهْدٍ فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ تُعِينُوا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Your sacrifices: let none of you wake after the third day with any of it still in his house." When the next year came they said: "Messenger of God, shall we do as we did last year?" He said: "Eat and store. That year the people were in hardship, and I wanted you to help them."

situation: People want to be patient and wise without having been through anything hard.
wise_response: Abu Sa'id said no one is forbearing who has not stumbled, and no one is wise who has not been tested.
why_it_worked: Forbearance grows from knowing your own failures. Wisdom grows from experience.
tempting_wrong_answer: Judging others harshly because you have never fallen yourself, or claiming wisdom you have not earned.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ عُفَيْرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ زَحْرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ حَلِيمَ إِلاَّ ذُو عَثْرَةٍ، وَلاَ حَكِيمَ إِلاَّ ذُو تَجْرِبَةٍ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: No one is forbearing except one who has stumbled, and no one is wise except one who has experience.

situation: 'Ali weighed two good deeds: feeding friends and freeing a slave.
wise_response: He said he would rather gather a group of his brothers around a measure or two of food than go to the market and free a slave.
why_it_worked: Sharing a meal builds love among people. 'Ali held that bond in very high regard.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping one's food to oneself and neglecting the company of friends.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ أَبُو الرَّبِيعِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا جَرِيرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ، عَنْ لَيْثٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ نَشْرٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَنَفِيَّةِ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ قَالَ‏:‏ لأَنْ أَجْمَعَ نَفَرًا مِنْ إِخْوَانِي عَلَى صَاعٍ أَوْ صَاعَيْنِ مِنْ طَعَامٍ، أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ أَخْرُجَ إِلَى سُوقِكُمْ فَأُعْتِقَ رَقَبَةً‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: That I gather a few of my brothers over a sa' or two of food is dearer to me than going out to your market and freeing a slave.

situation: Before his mission, the Prophet had joined his uncles in the Alliance of the Perfumed, a pact among Meccan clans.
wise_response: He said he would not want to break it even in exchange for the finest red camels.
why_it_worked: A pledge made for a good purpose stays binding. No price is worth breaking one's word.
tempting_wrong_answer: Dropping an old agreement when it becomes inconvenient or when a profit is offered.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ عُلَيَّةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ مُطْعِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَوْفٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ شَهِدْتُ مَعَ عُمُومَتِي حِلْفَ الْمُطَيَّبِينَ، فَمَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَنْكُثَهُ، وَأَنَّ لِي حُمْرَ النَّعَمِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, said: "I witnessed the Alliance of the Perfumed with my uncles, and I would not want to break it even if I were given red camels."

key_terms.حمر النعم (humr al-na'am): red camels, the most prized wealth of the Arabs

situation: The Prophet was lying on 'A'isha's bed in her wrap. He received Abu Bakr and 'Umar as he was. When 'Uthman asked to enter, he sat up and asked 'A'isha to gather her clothes.
wise_response: When 'A'isha asked why, he said 'Uthman was a very shy man, and he feared that if he received him in that state, 'Uthman would not bring up what he needed.
why_it_worked: He adjusted to the temperament of the person in front of him so that person could speak freely.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating everyone the same way regardless of their nature and leaving a shy person unable to ask for help.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ صَالِحٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْعَاصِ، أَنَّ سَعِيدَ بْنَ الْعَاصِ أَخْبَرَهُ، أَنَّ عُثْمَانَ وَعَائِشَةَ، حَدَّثَاهُ، أَنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ اسْتَأْذَنَ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَهُوَ مُضْطَجِعٌ عَلَى فِرَاشِ عَائِشَةَ لاَبِسًا مِرْطَ عَائِشَةَ، فَأَذِنَ لأَبِي بَكْرٍ وَهُوَ كَذَلِكَ، فَقَضَى إِلَيْهِ حَاجَتَهُ، ثُمَّ انْصَرَفَ‏.‏ ثُمَّ اسْتَأْذَنَ عُمَرُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، فَأَذِنَ لَهُ وَهُوَ كَذَلِكَ، فَقَضَى إِلَيْهِ حَاجَتَهُ، ثُمَّ انْصَرَفَ‏.‏ قَالَ عُثْمَانُ‏:‏ ثُمَّ اسْتَأْذَنْتُ عَلَيْهِ، فَجَلَسَ وَقَالَ لِعَائِشَةَ‏:‏ اجْمَعِي إِلَيْكِ ثِيَابَكِ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَقَضَيْتُ إِلَيْهِ حَاجَتِي، ثُمَّ انْصَرَفْتُ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، لَمْ أَرَكَ فَزِعْتَ لأَبِي بَكْرٍ وَعُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا كَمَا فَزِعْتَ لِعُثْمَانَ‏؟‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ إِنَّ عُثْمَانَ رَجُلٌ حَيِيٌّ، وَإِنِّي خَشِيتُ إِنْ أَذِنْتُ لَهُ، وَأَنَا عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالِ، أَنْ لاَ يَبْلُغَ إِلَيَّ فِي حَاجَتِهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Abu Bakr asked permission to enter on the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, while he was lying on 'A'isha's bed wearing 'A'isha's wrap. He let Abu Bakr in while he was like that, and Abu Bakr took care of his need with him and left. Then 'Umar asked permission, and he let him in while he was like that, and he took care of his need and left. 'Uthman said: Then I asked permission, and he sat up and said to 'A'isha: "Gather your clothes about you." I took care of my need with him and left. 'A'isha said: "Messenger of God, I did not see you stir for Abu Bakr and 'Umar as you did for 'Uthman." The Messenger of God said: "'Uthman is a shy man, and I feared that if I let him in while I was in that state, he would not get to his need with me."

situation: Guests from Madina rode up to Abu Hurayra's land. He sent to his mother for food, and she sent three barley loaves with oil and salt.
wise_response: Abu Hurayra praised God for filling them with bread after a time when they had only dates and water. After the guests left he told Humayd to treat his sheep well, wipe their noses clean, keep their pen pleasant, and pray near them.
why_it_worked: He served guests what he had and remembered how little he once had. The same care extended to his animals.
tempting_wrong_answer: Being ashamed of simple food and forgetting past hardship, or neglecting the animals in one's care.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ حَلْحَلَةَ، عَنْ حُمَيْدِ بْنِ مَالِكِ بْنِ خُثَيْمٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ‏:‏ كُنْتُ جَالِسًا مَعَ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ بِأَرْضِهِ بِالْعَقِيقِ، فَأَتَاهُ قَوْمٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ عَلَى دَوَابَّ، فَنَزَلُوا، قَالَ حُمَيْدٌ‏:‏ فَقَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ‏:‏ اذْهَبْ إِلَى أُمِّي وَقُلْ لَهَا‏:‏ إِنَّ ابْنَكِ يُقْرِئُكِ السَّلاَمَ وَيَقُولُ‏:‏ أَطْعِمِينَا شَيْئًا، قَالَ‏:‏ فَوَضَعَتْ ثَلاَثَةَ أَقْرَاصٍ مِنْ شَعِيرٍ، وَشَيْئًا مِنْ زَيْتٍ وَمِلْحٍ فِي صَحْفَةٍ، فَوَضَعْتُهَا عَلَى رَأْسِي، فَحَمَلْتُهَا إِلَيْهِمْ، فَلَمَّا وَضَعْتُهُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ، كَبَّرَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ وَقَالَ‏:‏ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَشْبَعَنَا مِنَ الْخُبْزِ بَعْدَ أَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ طَعَامُنَا إِلاَّ الأَسْوَدَانِ‏:‏ التَّمْرُ وَالْمَاءُ، فَلَمْ يُصِبِ الْقَوْمُ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ شَيْئًا، فَلَمَّا انْصَرَفُوا قَالَ‏:‏ يَا ابْنَ أَخِي، أَحْسِنْ إِلَى غَنَمِكَ، وَامْسَحْ الرُّغَامَ عَنْهَا، وَأَطِبْ مُرَاحَهَا، وَصَلِّ فِي نَاحِيَتِهَا، فَإِنَّهَا مِنْ دَوَابِّ الْجَنَّةِ، وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لَيُوشِكُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ عَلَى النَّاسِ زَمَانٌ تَكُونُ الثُّلَّةُ مِنَ الْغَنَمِ أَحَبَّ إِلَى صَاحِبِهَا مِنْ دَارِ مَرْوَانَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I was sitting with Abu Hurayra on his land at al-'Aqiq when some people of Madina came to him on riding animals and dismounted. Abu Hurayra said: "Go to my mother and tell her: your son sends you greetings and says, feed us something." She put three barley loaves and some oil and salt in a dish. I set it on my head and carried it to them. When I put it before them, Abu Hurayra said "God is greatest" and said: "Praise be to God who has filled us with bread after our only food was the two black things, dates and water." The people did not take any of the food. When they had gone he said: "Son of my brother, be good to your sheep. Wipe the mucus from them, keep their resting place clean, and pray in a corner of it, for they are among the animals of Paradise. situation: Camel owners and sheep owners were boasting to each other about whose way of life was nobler.
wise_response: The Prophet said Moses was sent while a shepherd, David was sent while a shepherd, and he himself was sent while herding sheep for his family at Ajyad.
why_it_worked: Humble work carries no shame. Prophets came from it, so boasting about status is empty.
tempting_wrong_answer: Taking pride in one's trade or herd and looking down on others for theirs.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَشَّارٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، سَمِعْتُ أَبَا إِسْحَاقَ، سَمِعْتُ عَبْدَةَ بْنَ حَزْنٍ يَقُولُ‏:‏ تَفَاخَرَ أَهْلُ الإِبِلِ وَأَصْحَابُ الشَّاءِ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ بُعِثَ مُوسَى وَهُوَ رَاعِي غَنَمٍ، وَبُعِثَ دَاوُدُ وَهُوَ رَاعٍ، وَبُعِثْتُ أَنَا وَأَنَا أَرْعَى غَنَمًا لأَهْلِي بِأَجْيَادِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The people of camels and the owners of sheep boasted against each other. The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Moses was sent, and he was a shepherd of sheep. David was sent, and he was a shepherd. And I was sent while I was herding sheep for my family at Ajyad."

situation: A young man, before setting off home from his studies, asked a scholar for a lesson. The scholar told him: fear God, be patient, and do not rush. At home he found a man asleep in the house near his sleeping wife.
wise_response: Three times he went to his mount for his sword, and three times he remembered the words and turned back. Then the man woke, leapt up, embraced and kissed him, and asked what he had gained while away. He answered that he had walked between the sword and the man's head three times, and what he had learned kept him from killing him.
why_it_worked: Holding back gave the truth time to appear. One lesson of patience saved an innocent life and his own soul.
tempting_wrong_answer: Acting on the first jealous impulse and striking before knowing the facts.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو هِلاَلٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الْحَسَنُ، أَنَّ رَجُلاً تُوُفِّيَ وَتَرَكَ ابْنًا لَهُ وَمَوْلًى لَهُ، فَأَوْصَى مَوْلاَهُ بِابْنِهِ، فَلَمْ يَأْلُوهُ حَتَّى أَدْرَكَ وَزَوَّجَهُ، فَقَالَ لَهُ‏:‏ جَهَّزْنِي أَطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ، فَجَهَّزَهُ، فَأَتَى عَالِمًا فَسَأَلَهُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَنْطَلِقَ فَقُلْ لِي أُعَلِّمْكَ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ حَضَرَ مِنِّي الْخُرُوجُ فَعَلِّمْنِي، فَقَالَ‏:‏ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ وَاصْبِرْ، وَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلْ‏.‏ قَالَ الْحَسَنُ‏:‏ فِي هَذَا الْخَيْرُ كُلُّهُ، فَجَاءَ وَلاَ يَكَادُ يَنْسَاهُنَّ، إِنَّمَا هُنَّ ثَلاَثٌ، فَلَمَّا جَاءَ أَهْلَهُ نَزَلَ عَنْ رَاحِلَتِهِ، فَلَمَّا نَزَلَ الدَّارَ إِذَا هُوَ بِرَجُلٍ نَائِمٍ مُتَرَاخٍ عَنِ الْمَرْأَةِ، وَإِذَا امْرَأَتُهُ نَائِمَةٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ وَاللَّهِ مَا أُرِيدُ مَا أَنْتَظِرُ بِهَذَا‏؟‏ فَرَجَعَ إِلَى رَاحِلَتِهِ، فَلَمَّا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ السَّيْفَ قَالَ‏:‏ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ وَاصْبِرْ، وَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلْ‏.‏ فَرَجَعَ، فَلَمَّا قَامَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ قَالَ‏:‏ مَا أَنْتَظِرُ بِهَذَا شَيْئًا، فَرَجَعَ إِلَى رَاحِلَتِهِ، فَلَمَّا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ سَيْفَهُ ذَكَرَهُ، فَرَجَعَ إِلَيْهِ، فَلَمَّا قَامَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ اسْتَيْقَظَ الرَّجُلُ، فَلَمَّا رَآهُ وَثَبَ إِلَيْهِ فَعَانَقَهُ وَقَبَّلَهُ، وَسَاءَلَهُ قَالَ‏:‏ مَا أَصَبْتَ بَعْدِي‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ أَصَبْتُ وَاللَّهِ بَعْدَكَ خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا، أَصَبْتُ وَاللَّهِ بَعْدَكَ‏:‏ أَنِّي مَشَيْتُ اللَّيْلَةَ بَيْنَ السَّيْفِ وَبَيْنَ رَأْسِكَ ثَلاَثَ مِرَارٍ، فَحَجَزَنِي مَا أَصَبْتُ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ عَنْ قَتْلِكَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man died and left a son and a freedman. He entrusted his son to the freedman, who spared no effort for him until he came of age, and then he married him off. The son said: "Equip me so I can seek knowledge." He equipped him. He came to a scholar and asked him. The scholar said: "When you want to leave, tell me and I will teach you." He said: "My departure has come, so teach me." He said: "Fear God, be patient, and do not hurry." Al-Hasan said: In this is all good. He came home hardly able to forget them; they were only three. When he reached his family he got down from his mount. When he entered the house, there was a man asleep, lying apart from the woman, and his wife was asleep. He said: "By God, I want nothing else; what am I waiting for with this one?" He went back to his mount, and when he went to take the sword he said: "Fear God, be patient, and do not hurry." He went back. When he stood over the man's head he said: "I am waiting for nothing with this one." He went back to his mount, and when he went to take his sword he remembered it, and went back to him. When he stood over his head, the man woke. When he saw him he jumped up to him, embraced him, kissed him and questioned him. He said: "What did you gain after leaving me?" He said: "By God, after you I gained much good. By God, after you I gained this: tonight I walked between the sword and your head three times, and the knowledge I gained held me back from killing you."

key_terms.لا تستعجل (la tasta'jil): do not rush, do not act in haste

situation: Ashajj of 'Abd al-Qays came to the Prophet with his tribe's delegation.
wise_response: The Prophet told him he had two traits God loves: forbearance and modesty. Ashajj asked whether they were old or new in him, and on hearing they were long-standing, he thanked God who had formed him with them.
why_it_worked: Forbearance and modesty keep a person calm and decent with others. Ashajj answered praise with thanks rather than pride.
tempting_wrong_answer: Reacting in haste and anger, or taking praise as a reason for vanity.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مَعْمَرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا يُونُسُ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرَةَ، عَنْ أَشَجِّ عَبْدِ الْقَيْسِ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ لِيَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ إِنَّ فِيكَ لَخُلُقَيْنِ يُحِبُّهُمَا اللَّهُ، قُلْتُ‏:‏ وَمَا هُمَا يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ الْحِلْمُ وَالْحَيَاءُ، قُلْتُ‏:‏ قَدِيمًا كَانَ أَوْ حَدِيثًا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ قَدِيمًا، قُلْتُ‏:‏ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي جَبَلَنِي عَلَى خُلُقَيْنِ أَحَبَّهُمَا اللَّهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: "There are in you two traits that God loves." I said: "What are they, Messenger of God?" He said: "Forbearance and modesty." I said: "Have they been in me long or are they new?" He said: "Long." I said: "Praise be to God who formed me with two traits that God loves."

key_terms.الحياء (al-haya'): modesty, a sense of shame that holds one back from wrong

situation: People wrong others, disobey their parents, or cut off their relatives, and assume any reckoning is far off.
wise_response: The Prophet said God delays what He wills of sins until the Day of Resurrection, except oppression, mistreating parents, and cutting ties of kinship. For these the punishment comes in this world, before death.
why_it_worked: These wrongs injure the people closest to us and the weak. Their harm comes back on the wrongdoer quickly.
tempting_wrong_answer: Abusing others or neglecting parents and relatives, thinking there is no cost.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا حَامِدُ بْنُ عُمَرَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا بَكَّارُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ كُلُّ ذُنُوبٍ يُؤَخِّرُ اللَّهُ مِنْهَا مَا شَاءَ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ، إِلاَّ الْبَغْيَ، وَعُقُوقَ الْوَالِدَيْنِ، أَوْ قَطِيعَةَ الرَّحِمِ، يُعَجِّلُ لِصَاحِبِهَا فِي الدُّنْيَا قَبْلَ الْمَوْتِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Of all sins, God postpones what He wills until the Day of Resurrection, except oppression, disobedience to parents, and cutting off kin. For those He hastens it to the one who does them in this world, before death."

situation: A person is quick to notice small faults in others.
wise_response: Abu Hurayra said one of you sees the speck in his brother's eye and forgets the log in his own.

situation: Mu'awiya ibn Qurra saw Ma'qil al-Muzani clear something harmful off the road, and then cleared another thing himself.
wise_response: Ma'qil asked why he did it. When he said he had copied him, Ma'qil praised him and told him the Prophet said whoever removes harm from the Muslims' road has a good deed written for him, and whoever has a good deed accepted enters Paradise.
why_it_worked: A small act that protects passersby counts. Good example spreads, and Ma'qil encouraged it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Walking past an obstacle in the road because someone else will deal with it.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الْخَلِيلُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الْمُسْتَنِيرُ بْنُ أَخْضَرَ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ قُرَّةَ قَالَ‏:‏ كُنْتُ مَعَ مَعْقِلٍ الْمُزَنِيِّ، فَأَمَاطَ أَذًى عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ، فَرَأَيْتُ شَيْئًا فَبَادَرْتُهُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ مَا حَمَلَكَ عَلَى مَا صَنَعْتَ يَا ابْنَ أَخِي‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ رَأَيْتُكَ تَصْنَعُ شَيْئًا فَصَنَعْتُهُ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَحْسَنْتَ يَا ابْنَ أَخِي، سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ‏:‏ مَنْ أَمَاطَ أَذًى عَنْ طَرِيقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كُتِبَ لَهُ حَسَنَةٌ، وَمَنْ تُقُبِّلَتْ لَهُ حَسَنَةٌ دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ‏.‏

situation: A person chooses between speaking and acting with modesty or with crudeness.
wise_response: The Prophet said modesty never enters anything without making it beautiful, and obscenity never enters anything without making it ugly.
why_it_worked: Restraint and decency improve whatever they touch. Coarseness spoils even good things.
tempting_wrong_answer: Using crude, shameless speech and behavior because it seems bold or funny.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ الْبُنَانِيِّ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ مَا كَانَ الْحَيَاءُ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلاَّ زَانَهُ، وَلاَ كَانَ الْفُحْشُ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلا شَانَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Modesty was never in anything except that it adorned it, and obscenity was never in anything except that it disfigured it.

key_terms.الفحش (al-fuhsh): obscenity, coarse and indecent speech or conduct

situation: The Prophet passed a man scolding his brother for being too shy, as if his modesty was hurting him.
wise_response: The Prophet told him: leave him alone, for modesty is part of faith.
why_it_worked: Shyness that keeps a person from wrong is a strength. It should not be shamed out of someone.
tempting_wrong_answer: Pushing a modest person to be brash and treating their restraint as weakness.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ سَالِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَرَّ بِرَجُلٍ يَعِظُ أَخَاهُ فِي الْحَيَاءِ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ دَعْهُ، فَإِنَّ الْحَيَاءَ مِنَ الإيمَانِ‏.‏- حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ سَالِمٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ‏:‏ مَرَّ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى رَجُلٍ يُعَاتِبُ أَخَاهُ فِي الْحَيَاءِ، كَأَنَّهُ يَقُولُ‏:‏ أَضَرَّ بِكَ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ دَعْهُ، فَإِنَّ الْحَيَاءَ مِنَ الإِيمَانِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, passed a man who was admonishing his brother about modesty, as if saying, "It has harmed you." He said: "Leave him. Modesty is part of faith."

situation: Families of the early generations lived side by side behind cane walls. When a guest came to one of them, the host might take a neighbor's cooking pot off the fire to feed the guest.
wise_response: When the pot's owner asked who had taken it, the host said they took it for their guest. The owner answered, "May God bless it for you." They did the same with fresh bread.
why_it_worked: Neighbors treated feeding a guest as a shared duty. The owner gave up his meal gladly rather than complain.
tempting_wrong_answer: Guarding one's own food and resenting a neighbor who used it to honor a guest.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدَةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا بَقِيَّةُ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أَدْرَكْتُ السَّلَفَ، وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَكُونُونَ فِي الْمَنْزِلِ الْوَاحِدِ بِأَهَالِيهِمْ، فَرُبَّمَا نَزَلَ عَلَى بَعْضِهُمُ الضَّيْفُ، وَقِدْرُ أَحَدِهِمْ عَلَى النَّارِ، فَيَأْخُذُهَا صَاحِبُ الضَّيْفِ لِضَيْفِهِ، فَيَفْقِدُ الْقِدْرَ صَاحِبُهَا فَيَقُولُ‏:‏ مَنْ أَخَذَ الْقِدْرَ‏؟‏ فَيَقُولُ صَاحِبُ الضَّيْفِ‏:‏ نَحْنُ أَخَذْنَاهَا لِضَيْفِنَا، فَيَقُولُ صَاحِبُ الْقِدْرِ‏:‏ بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ فِيهَا، أَوْ كَلِمَةً نَحْوَهَا قَالَ بَقِيَّةُ‏:‏ وَقَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ‏:‏ وَالْخُبْزُ إِذَا خَبَزُوا مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ، وَلَيْسَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِلاَّ جُدُرُ الْقَصَبِ‏.‏ قَالَ بَقِيَّةُ‏:‏ وَأَدْرَكْتُ أَنَا ذَلِكَ‏:‏ مُحَمَّدَ بْنَ زِيَادٍ وَأَصْحَابَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I knew the early generation. They would live in a single dwelling with their families. Sometimes a guest would come to one of them while another's pot was on the fire, and the guest's host would take it for his guest. The owner would miss his pot and say, "Who took the pot?" The guest's host would say, "We took it for our guest." The owner of the pot would say, "May God bless it for you," or words like that. Muhammad said: and bread too when they baked, the same. There was nothing between them but walls of cane. Baqiyya said: I too saw that, Muhammad ibn Ziyad and his companions.

situation: A hungry man came to the Prophet, whose own households had only water. An Ansari man offered to host him, but at home his wife said they had only enough food for their children.
wise_response: He told her to prepare the food, put the children to sleep, and put out the lamp as if fixing it. In the dark the couple pretended to eat so the guest would eat his fill, and they went to bed hungry. The next morning the Prophet told him God was delighted with what they had done.
why_it_worked: They put the guest's need above their own and hid their sacrifice so he would not feel he was taking from them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Turning the guest away, or feeding him grudgingly so he knows what it cost.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ دَاوُدَ، عَنْ فُضَيْلِ بْنِ غَزْوَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَجُلاً أَتَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَبَعَثَ إِلَى نِسَائِهِ، فَقُلْنَ‏:‏ مَا مَعَنَا إِلاَّ الْمَاءُ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ مَنْ يَضُمُّ، أَوْ يُضِيفُ، هَذَا‏؟‏ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ‏:‏ أَنَا‏.‏ فَانْطَلَقَ بِهِ إِلَى امْرَأَتِهِ فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَكْرِمِي ضَيْفَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَتْ‏:‏ مَا عِنْدَنَا إِلاَّ قُوتٌ لِلصِّبْيَانِ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ هَيِّئِي طَعَامَكِ، وَأَصْلِحِي سِرَاجَكِ، وَنَوِّمِي صِبْيَانَكِ إِذَا أَرَادُوا عَشَاءً، فَهَيَّأَتْ طَعَامَهَا، وَأَصْلَحَتْ سِرَاجَهَا، وَنَوَّمَتْ صِبْيَانَهَا، ثُمَّ قَامَتْ كَأَنَّهَا تُصْلِحُ سِرَاجَهَا فَأَطْفَأَتْهُ، وَجَعَلاَ يُرِيَانِهِ أَنَّهُمَا يَأْكُلاَنِ، وَبَاتَا طَاوِيَيْنِ، فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ غَدَا إِلَى رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ لَقَدْ ضَحِكَ اللَّهُ، أَوْ‏:‏ عَجِبَ، مِنْ فَعَالِكُمَا، وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ‏:‏ ‏{‏وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَلَوْ كَانَ بِهِمْ خَصَاصَةٌ وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ‏}‏‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man came to the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, and he sent to his wives. They said: "We have nothing but water." The Messenger of God said: "Who will take in, or host, this man?" A man of the Ansar said: "I will." He took him to his wife and said: "Honor the guest of the Messenger of God." She said: "We have nothing but the children's food." He said: "Get your food ready, fix your lamp, and put your children to sleep when they want supper." She got her food ready, fixed her lamp and put her children to sleep. Then she got up as if to fix the lamp and put it out. The two of them made him think they were eating, and they spent the night hungry. In the morning he went to the Messenger of God, who said: "God laughed, or marveled, at what you two did." And God revealed: "They prefer others above themselves even when they are in need. Whoever is saved from the greed of his own soul, those are the successful."

situation: People wonder what they owe their neighbors and guests, and how to use their tongue.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever believes in God and the Last Day should honor his neighbor, honor his guest with his due of a special day and night, and either say something good or stay silent. Hospitality lasts three days, and beyond that it is charity.
why_it_worked: Faith shows in how one treats the people nearby and in what one says. Honoring neighbors and guests and guarding speech are its daily signs.
tempting_wrong_answer: Neglecting neighbors, hosting guests stingily, and talking without restraint.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا اللَّيْثُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي سَعِيدٌ الْمَقْبُرِيُّ، عَنْ أَبِي شُرَيْحٍ الْعَدَوِيِّ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعَتْ أُذُنَايَ، وَأَبْصَرَتْ عَيْنَايَ، حِينَ تَكَلَّمَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ جَارَهُ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ ضَيْفَهُ جَائِزَتَهُ، قَالَ‏:‏ وَمَا جَائِزَتُهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ يَوْمٌ وَلَيْلَةٌ، وَالضِّيَافَةُ ثَلاَثَةُ أَيَّامٍ، فَمَا كَانَ وَرَاءَ ذَلِكَ فَهُوَ صَدَقَةٌ عَلَيْهِ‏.‏ وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: My ears heard and my eyes saw when the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, spoke and said: "Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor. Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honor his guest with his due." He was asked: "What is his due, Messenger of God?" He said: "A day and a night. Hospitality is three days, and whatever is beyond that is charity to him. And whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep silent."

key_terms.جائزة (ja'iza): the guest's due, a special first day and night of generous hosting

situation: A guest is enjoying a host's hospitality and is tempted to stay on.
wise_response: The Prophet set out the host's duty: honor the guest a full day and night, host him for three days, and what follows is charity. He added that it is not lawful for the guest to stay until he puts his host in hardship.
why_it_worked: Hospitality runs both ways. The host gives freely, and the guest does not exploit that generosity.
tempting_wrong_answer: Overstaying one's welcome and burdening a host who is too polite to say so.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ سَعِيدٍ الْمَقْبُرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي شُرَيْحٍ الْكَعْبِيِّ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ ضَيْفَهُ جَائِزَتَهُ يَوْمٌ وَلَيْلَةٌ‏.‏ وَالضِّيَافَةُ ثَلاَثَةُ أَيَّامٍ، فَمَا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَهُوَ صَدَقَةٌ، وَلاَ يَحِلُّ لَهُ أَنْ يَثْوِيَ عِنْدَهُ حَتَّى يُحْرِجَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep silent. Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honor his guest; his due is a day and a night. Hospitality is three days, and whatever comes after that is charity. It is not lawful for him to stay with him until he causes him hardship.

key_terms.يحرجه (yuhrijahu): puts him in difficulty, burdens him

situation: Nu'aym ibn Qa'nab came to Abu Dharr carrying an old guilt. Before Islam he had buried a daughter alive, and he dreaded hearing there was no way back for him.
wise_response: Abu Dharr asked if it had happened before Islam. When Nu'aym said yes, he told him, "God has pardoned what is past." He then had his wife serve the guest a meal.
why_it_worked: He met a repentant man with hope, not condemnation. That opened a way for Nu'aym to move forward.
tempting_wrong_answer: Telling a remorseful person their past makes them beyond forgiveness.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مَعْمَرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي الْجُرَيْرِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْعَلاَءِ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ، عَنْ نُعَيْمِ بْنِ قَعْنَبٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أَتَيْتُ أَبَا ذَرٍّ فَلَمْ أُوَافِقْهُ، فَقُلْتُ لِامْرَأَتِهِ‏:‏ أَيْنَ أَبُو ذَرٍّ‏؟‏ قَالَتْ‏:‏ يَمْتَهِنُ، سَيَأْتِيكَ الْآنَ، فَجَلَسْتُ لَهُ، فَجَاءَ وَمَعَهُ بَعِيرَانِ، قَدْ قَطَرَ أَحَدَهُمَا بِعَجُزِ الْآخَرِ، فِي عُنُقِ كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا قِرْبَةٌ، فَوَضَعَهُمَا ثُمَّ جَاءَ، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ، مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ كُنْتُ أَلْقَاهُ كَانَ أَحَبَّ إِلَيَّ لُقْيًا مِنْكَ، وَلاَ أَبْغَضَ إِلَيَّ لُقْيًا مِنْكَ، قَالَ‏:‏ لِلَّهِ أَبُوكَ، وَمَا جَمَعَ هَذَا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ إِنِّي كُنْتُ وَأَدْتُ مَوْءُودَةً فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ أَرْهَبُ إِنْ لَقِيتُكَ أَنْ تَقُولَ‏:‏ لاَ تَوْبَةَ لَكَ، لاَ مَخْرَجَ لَكَ، وَكُنْتُ أَرْجُو أَنْ تَقُولَ‏:‏ لَكَ تَوْبَةٌ وَمَخْرَجٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَفِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ أَصَبْتَ‏؟‏ قُلْتُ‏:‏ نَعَمْ، قَالَ‏:‏ عَفَا اللَّهُ عَمَّا سَلَفَ‏.‏ وَقَالَ لِامْرَأَتِهِ‏:‏ آتِينَا بِطَعَامٍ، فَأَبَتَ، ثُمَّ أَمَرَهَا فَأَبَتَ، حَتَّى ارْتَفَعَتْ أَصْوَاتُهُمَا، قَالَ‏:‏ إِيهِ، فَإِنَّكُنَّ لاَ تَعْدُونَ مَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، قُلْتُ‏:‏ وَمَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ فِيهِنَّ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ خُلِقَتْ مِنْ ضِلَعٍ، وَإِنَّكَ إِنْ تُرِدْ أَنْ تُقِيمَهَا تَكْسِرُهَا، وَإِنْ تُدَارِهَا فَإِنَّ فِيهَا أَوَدًا وَبُلْغَةً، فَوَلَّتْ فَجَاءَتْ بِثَرِيدَةٍ كَأَنَّهَا قَطَاةٌ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ كُلْ وَلاَ أَهُولَنَّكَ فَإِنِّي صَائِمٌ، ثُمَّ قَامَ يُصَلِّي، فَجَعَلَ يُهَذِّبُ الرُّكُوعَ، ثُمَّ انْفَتَلَ فَأَكَلَ، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ، مَا كُنْتُ أَخَافُ أَنْ تَكْذِبَنِي، قَالَ‏:‏ لِلَّهِ أَبُوكَ، مَا كَذَبْتُ مُنْذُ لَقِيتَنِي، قُلْتُ‏:‏ أَلَمْ تُخْبِرْنِي أَنَّكَ صَائِمٌ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ بَلَى، إِنِّي صُمْتُ مِنْ هَذَا الشَّهْرِ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ فَكُتِبَ لِي أَجْرُهُ، وَحَلَّ لِيَ الطَّعَامُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I came to Abu Dharr but did not find him, so I said to his wife: "Where is Abu Dharr?" She said: "He is doing work; he will come to you soon." I sat waiting for him. He came with two camels, one tied behind the other, each with a waterskin on its neck. He set them down and came over. I said: "Abu Dharr, there was no man I could meet whom I wanted more to meet than you, nor whom I dreaded more to meet than you." He said: "God bless your father, how can those two go together?" I said: "I had buried a girl alive in the time of ignorance. I feared that if I met you, you would say: there is no repentance for you, no way out for you. And I hoped you would say: there is repentance for you and a way out." He said: "Was it in the time of ignorance that you did it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "God has pardoned what is past." He said to his wife: "Bring us food." She refused. He told her again and she refused, until their voices rose. He said: "Enough. You women do not go beyond what the Messenger of God said." I said: "What did the Messenger of God say about them?" He said: "Woman was created from a rib. If you try to straighten her you will break her, and if you bear with her, there is crookedness in her and yet enough to live on." She turned away and came back with a bowl of tharid like a sandgrouse. He said: "Eat, and do not let me worry you, for I am fasting." Then he stood and prayed, hurrying his bowing, then turned and ate. I said: "We belong to God. I never feared you would lie to me." He said: "God bless your father, I have not lied since I met you." I said: "Did you not tell me you were fasting?" He said: "Yes. I fasted three days of this month, so its reward is written for me, and food is lawful for me."

situation: A person decides where their money does the most good.
wise_response: The Prophet said among the best dinars a man spends is the one he spends on his dependents, then the one spent on his companions in God's cause, and the one spent on his mount in God's cause.
why_it_worked: Providing for the people who depend on you comes first and counts as a high form of giving.
tempting_wrong_answer: Giving lavishly to outsiders for show while one's own family goes short.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلاَبَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي أَسْمَاءَ، عَنْ ثَوْبَانَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّ مِنْ أَفْضَلِ دِينَارٍ أَنْفَقَهُ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى عِيَالِهِ، وَدِينَارٌ أَنْفَقَهُ عَلَى أَصْحَابِهِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ، وَدِينَارٌ أَنْفَقَهُ عَلَى دَابَّتِهِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Among the best dinars a man spends is a dinar he spends on his dependents, a dinar he spends on his companions in the cause of God, and a dinar he spends on his mount in the cause of God.

key_terms.عياله ('iyaluhu): his dependents, the household he supports

situation: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas wondered whether ordinary spending on his household carried any merit.
wise_response: The Prophet told him that anything he spends seeking God's pleasure is rewarded, even the morsel he puts in his wife's mouth.
why_it_worked: Small daily kindnesses at home count. Care for a spouse is good conduct when done with a sincere heart.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating care for one's family as a chore of no worth and saving kindness for public deeds.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْيَمَانِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شُعَيْبٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي عَامِرُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ أَبِي وَقَّاصٍ أَنَّهُ أَخْبَرَهُ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ لِسَعْدٍ‏:‏ إِنَّكَ لَنْ تُنْفِقَ نَفَقَةً تَبْتَغِي بِهَا وَجْهَ اللهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِلاَّ أُجِرْتَ بِهَا، حَتَّى مَا تَجْعَلُ فِي فَمِ امْرَأَتِكَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, said to Sa'd: "You will not spend anything seeking by it the face of God, Mighty and Majestic, except that you are rewarded for it, even what you put in your wife's mouth."

situation: On a night march, Abu Ruhm kept pulling his camel back from the Prophet's. He dozed off, his camel pushed into the Prophet's, and it struck the Prophet's foot in the stirrup. The Prophet cried out in pain.
wise_response: Abu Ruhm begged him to ask forgiveness for him. The Prophet simply said, "Ride on," and went on talking with him and asking after people of his tribe.
why_it_worked: The hurt was an accident. The Prophet let it go at once and kept the conversation warm so Abu Ruhm would not be crushed by shame.
tempting_wrong_answer: Scolding someone for an accidental injury and leaving them to stew in embarrassment.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ أَخِي أَبِي رُهْمٍ كُلْثُومُ بْنُ الْحُصَيْنِ الْغِفَارِيُّ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا رُهْمٍ، وَكَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الَّذِينَ بَايَعُوهُ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ، يَقُولُ‏:‏ غَزَوْتُ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم غَزْوَةَ تَبُوكَ، فنُمْتُ لَيْلَةً بِالأَخْضَرِ، فَصِرْتُ قَرِيبًا مِنْهُ، فَأُلْقِيَ عَلَيْنَا النُّعَاسُ، فَطَفِقْتُ أَسْتَيْقِظُ وَقَدْ دَنَتْ رَاحِلَتِي مِنْ رَاحِلَتِهِ، فَيُفْزِعُنِي دُنُوُّهَا خَشْيَةَ أَنْ تُصِيبَ رِجْلَهُ فِي الْغَرْزِ، فَطَفِقْتُ أُؤَخِّرُ رَاحِلَتِي حَتَّى غَلَبَتْنِي عَيْنِي بَعْضَ اللَّيْلِ، فَزَاحَمَتْ رَاحِلَتِي رَاحِلَةَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَرِجْلُهُ فِي الْغَرْزِ، فَأَصَبْتُ رِجْلَهُ، فَلَمْ أَسْتَيْقِظْ إِلاَّ بِقَوْلِهِ‏:‏ حَسِّ، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، اسْتَغْفِرْ لِي، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ سِرْ‏.‏ فَطَفِقَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَسْأَلُنِي عَنْ مَنْ تَخَلَّفَ مِنْ بَنِي غِفَارٍ فَأُخْبِرُهُ، فَقَالَ، وَهُوَ يَسْأَلُنِي‏:‏ مَا فَعَلَ النَّفْرُ الْحُمُرُ الطِّوَالُ الثِّطَاطُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ فَحَدَّثْتُهُ بِتَخَلُّفِهِمْ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَمَا فَعَلَ السُّودُ الْجِعَادُ الْقِصَارُ الَّذِينَ لَهُمْ نَعَمٌ بِشَبَكَةِ شَرَخٍ‏؟‏ فَتَذَكَّرْتُهُمْ فِي بَنِي غِفَارٍ، فَلَمْ أَذْكُرْهُمْ حَتَّى ذَكَرْتُ أَنَّهُمْ رَهْطٌ مِنْ أَسْلَمَ، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، أُولَئِكَ مِنْ أَسْلَمَ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَمَا يَمْنَعُ أَحَدَ أُولَئِكَ، حِينَ يَتَخَلَّفُ، أَنْ يَحْمِلَ عَلَى بَعِيرٍ مِنْ إِبِلِهِ امْرَءًا نَشِيطًا فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ‏؟‏ فَإِنَّ أَعَزَّ أَهْلِي عَلَيَّ أَنْ يَتَخَلَّفَ عَنِّي الْمُهَاجِرُونَ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ وَالأَنْصَارُ، وَغِفَارٌ وَأَسْلَمُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I went with the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, on the campaign of Tabuk. One night at al-Akhdar I was close to him, and drowsiness fell on us. I kept waking to find my mount had come near his, and its nearness alarmed me for fear it would hit his foot in the stirrup. So I kept holding my mount back, until sleep overcame me part of the night and my mount pressed against the mount of the Messenger of God while his foot was in the stirrup. I hit his foot, and I did not wake until he said, "Ouch!" I said: "Messenger of God, ask forgiveness for me." The Messenger of God said: "Ride on." Then he began asking me about those of Banu Ghifar who had stayed behind, and I told him. While asking he said: "What did the tall, red, thin-bearded ones do?" I told him they had stayed behind. He said: "And what of the short, dark, curly-haired ones who have herds at Shabakat Sharkh?" I tried to recall them among Banu Ghifar and could not, until I remembered they were a clan of Aslam. I said: "Messenger of God, those are from Aslam." He said: "What stops one of them, when he stays behind, from mounting an eager man on one of his camels for the cause of God? The hardest thing for me is that the Emigrants of Quraysh, the Ansar, Ghifar and Aslam stay behind from me."

situation: A man known for bad conduct asked to see the Prophet. Beforehand the Prophet said he was a bad member of his tribe, yet when the man came in, he was friendly and open with him.
wise_response: When 'A'isha asked about it, the Prophet said God does not love the one who is obscene and deliberately crude.
why_it_worked: Courtesy does not depend on the other person deserving it. Meeting a difficult man with harshness would have made the Prophet coarse himself.
tempting_wrong_answer: Answering a rude person with rudeness and insults.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا قَالَتِ‏:‏ اسْتَأْذَنَ رَجُلٌ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ‏:‏ بِئْسَ أَخُو الْعَشِيرَةِ، فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ انْبَسَطَ إِلَيْهِ، فَقُلْتُ لَهُ‏؟‏ فَقَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يُحِبُّ الْفَاحِشَ الْمُتَفَحِّشَ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man asked permission to see the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: "What a bad brother of the clan he is." When the man came in, he was easy and open with him. I asked him about it, and he said: "God does not love the obscene, the one who makes a habit of obscenity."

key_terms.الفاحش المتفحش (al-fahish al-mutafahhish: the coarse person who deliberately speaks obscenely

situation: While dividing goods after Hunayn, the Prophet was mobbed by people pressing in on him for their share.
wise_response: He told of an earlier prophet whose people rejected him and struck his head. Wiping the blood from his forehead, that prophet prayed, "O God, forgive my people, for they do not know."
why_it_worked: Even when hurt, the prophet saw that his attackers acted from ignorance and asked mercy for them. The Prophet held this up while being crowded himself.
tempting_wrong_answer: Lashing out at people who mistreat you and wishing harm on them.

situation: Some people told 'Uqba ibn 'Amir that their neighbors drank and misbehaved, and asked whether to report them to the ruler.
wise_response: 'Uqba said no. He told them the Prophet said whoever sees a Muslim's shameful fault and covers it is like one who brings a buried girl back to life from her grave.
why_it_worked: Exposing a neighbor's private failing can ruin him. Covering it leaves room for him to recover his dignity and change.
tempting_wrong_answer: Running to the authorities to expose a neighbor's private sins.

situation: Someone hears people praising them.
wise_response: When one of the Prophet's companions was praised, he would pray: "O God, do not hold me to account for what they say, and forgive me what they do not know."
why_it_worked: He knew his own hidden faults better than his admirers did. Praise turned him toward humility.
tempting_wrong_answer: Believing the praise and growing proud.

translation.ai_translation: When a man among the companions of the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, was praised, he would say: "O God, do not take me to task for what they say, and forgive me what they do not know."

situation: People pass on hearsay with "they claim" and speak harshly of believers.
wise_response: Abu Mas'ud reported the Prophet said "they claim" is a bad mount for a man, and that cursing a believer is like killing him.
why_it_worked: Spreading what you have not checked carries you into falsehood. Cursing a person wounds them gravely.
tempting_wrong_answer: Repeating rumors as fact and cursing people in anger.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ بْنُ يُونُسَ الْيَمَامِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلاَبَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي الْمُهَلَّبِ أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللهِ بْنَ عَامِرٍ قَالَ‏:‏ يَا أَبَا مَسْعُودٍ، مَا سَمِعْتَ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ فِي زَعَمُوا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ‏:‏ بِئْسَ مَطِيَّةُ الرَّجُلِ، وَسَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ‏:‏ لَعْنُ الْمُؤْمِنِ كَقَتْلِهِ‏.‏

situation: A person is unsure of something but wants to sound certain.
wise_response: Ibn 'Abbas said no one should say "God knows it" about something he does not know, when God knows otherwise. That is to claim to inform God of what He does not know, and it is grave.
why_it_worked: Swearing God as witness to a guess is a lie with heavy weight. Honesty means admitting what you do not know.
tempting_wrong_answer: Calling on God to back up a claim one is not sure of.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ قَالَ‏:‏ قَالَ عَمْرٌو‏:‏ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ‏:‏ لاَ يَقُولَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ لِشَيْءٍ لاَ يَعْلَمُهُ‏:‏ اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُهُ ؛ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ، فَيُعَلِّمَ اللَّهَ مَا لاَ يَعْلَمُ، فَذَاكَ عِنْدَ اللهِ عَظِيمٌ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: None of you should say about something he does not know, "God knows it," when God knows something other than that, so that he informs God of what He does not know. That is grave in God's sight.

situation: A person is curious about a companion's movements.
wise_response: Mujahid said it is disliked for a man to stare hard at his brother, to follow him with his eyes as he walks away, or to ask him where he came from and where he is going.
why_it_worked: People are owed privacy. Prying stares and questions make them uneasy.
tempting_wrong_answer: Watching and questioning others about their comings and goings.

translation.ai_translation: It is disliked for a man to fix a sharp gaze on his brother, or to follow him with his eyes when he turns away, or to ask him, "Where have you come from, and where are you going?"

situation: A man asked the Prophet which charity brings the greatest reward.
wise_response: The Prophet said it is to give while you are healthy and tight-fisted, afraid of poverty and hoping for wealth. Do not wait until death is at your throat and then say, "This much for so-and-so," when it already belongs to them.
why_it_worked: Giving costs most when you still need what you give. Bequests at death give away what is no longer yours to keep.
tempting_wrong_answer: Holding on to everything through life and planning to be generous only on one's deathbed.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَلامٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ فُضَيْلِ بْنِ غَزْوَانَ، عَنْ عُمَارَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي زُرْعَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ‏:‏ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، أَيُّ الصَّدَقَةِ أَفْضَلُ أَجْرًا‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ أَمَا وَأَبِيكَ لَتُنَبَّأَنَّهُ‏:‏ أَنْ تَصَدَّقَ وَأَنْتَ صَحِيحٌ شَحِيحٌ تَخْشَى الْفَقْرَ، وَتَأْمُلُ الْغِنَى، وَلاَ تُمْهِلْ حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ قُلْتَ‏:‏ لِفُلاَنٍ كَذَا، وَلِفُلاَنٍ كَذَا، وَقَدْ كَانَ لِفلانٍ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: A man came to the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, and said: "Messenger of God, which charity has the greatest reward?" He said: "By your father, you will be told it: that you give charity while you are healthy and stingy, fearing poverty and hoping for riches. And do not delay until, when it reaches the throat, you say: so much for so-and-so and so much for so-and-so, when it already belonged to so-and-so."

situation: A person wants something from a friend and is tempted to flatter him to get it.
wise_response: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: seek what you need with a light touch, for you will have only what is decreed for you. Do not go to your companion and praise him, so that you break his back.
why_it_worked: Flattery harms the one praised by feeding his pride. Asking simply keeps both people honest.
tempting_wrong_answer: Heaping praise on someone to win a favor.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو نُعَيْمٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي الأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ أَبِي الأَحْوَصِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ قَالَ‏:‏ إِذَا طَلَبَ أَحَدُكُمُ الْحَاجَةَ فَلْيَطْلُبْهَا طَلَبًا يَسِيرًا، فَإِنَّمَا لَهُ مَا قُدِّرَ لَهُ، وَلاَ يَأْتِي أَحَدُكُمْ صَاحِبَهُ فَيَمْدَحَهُ، فَيَقْطَعَ ظَهْرَهُ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: When one of you seeks something he needs, let him seek it gently, for he will have only what has been decreed for him. And let none of you come to his companion and praise him, and so break his back.

tempting_wrong_answer: Quarreling with or mistreating a person one must live or work alongside.

situation: Abu Dharr walked with the Prophet toward al-Baqi' and Uhud, and the Prophet spoke to him about wealth.
wise_response: He said those with much will have little on the Day of Resurrection, except those who give it out this way and that for what is right. He said it would not please him if Uhud turned to gold for his family and a single dinar of it stayed with them by nightfall.
why_it_worked: Wealth counts only for what it does for others. He would rather give it away at once than keep it overnight.
tempting_wrong_answer: Piling up wealth and keeping it while needs around you go unmet.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُعَاذُ بْنُ فَضَالَةَ، عَنْ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ وَهْبٍ، عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ قَالَ‏:‏ فَانْطَلَقَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَحْوَ الْبَقِيعِ، وَانْطَلَقْتُ أَتْلُوهُ، فَالْتَفَتَ فَرَآنِي فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ لَبَّيْكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، وَسَعْدَيْكَ، وَأَنَا فِدَاؤُكَ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّ الْمُكْثِرِينَ هُمُ الْمُقِلُّونَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، إِلاَّ مَنْ قَالَ هَكَذَا وَهَكَذَا فِي حَقٍّ، قُلْتُ‏:‏ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ، فَقَالَ‏:‏ هَكَذَا ثَلاَثًا، ثُمَّ عَرَضَ لَنَا أُحُدٌ فَقَالَ‏:‏ يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ لَبَّيْكَ رَسُولَ اللهِ وَسَعْدَيْكَ، وَأَنَا فِدَاؤُكَ، قَالَ‏:‏ مَا يَسُرُّنِي أَنَّ أُحُدًا لِآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ ذَهَبًا، فَيُمْسِي عِنْدَهُمْ دِينَارٌ، أَوْ قَالَ‏:‏ مِثْقَالٌ، ثُمَّ عَرَضَ لَنَا وَادٍ، فَاسْتَنْتَلَ فَظَنَنْتُ أَنَّ لَهُ حَاجَةً، فَجَلَسْتُ عَلَى شَفِيرٍ، وَأَبْطَأَ عَلَيَّ‏.‏ قَالَ‏:‏ فَخَشِيتُ عَلَيْهِ، ثُمَّ سَمِعْتُهُ كَأَنَّهُ يُنَاجِي رَجُلاً، ثُمَّ خَرَجَ إِلَيَّ وَحْدَهُ، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، مَنِ الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي كُنْتَ تُنَاجِي‏؟‏ فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَوَ سَمِعْتَهُ‏؟‏ قُلْتُ‏:‏ نَعَمْ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَإِنَّهُ جِبْرِيلُ أَتَانِي، فَبَشَّرَنِي أَنَّهُ مَنْ مَاتَ مِنْ أُمَّتِي لاَ يُشْرِكُ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ، قُلْتُ‏:‏ وَإِنْ زَنَى وَإِنْ سَرَقَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ نَعَمْ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, set off toward al-Baqi', and I went following him. He turned, saw me and said: "Abu Dharr." I said: "At your service, Messenger of God, and at your call, and may I be your ransom." He said: "Those who have much are those who have little on the Day of Resurrection, except whoever says this way and this way with it, in what is right." I said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said it that way three times. Then Uhud came into view and he said: "Abu Dharr." I said: "At your service, Messenger of God, and at your call, and may I be your ransom." He said: "It would not please me that Uhud were gold for the family of Muhammad and a dinar of it, or he said a mithqal, remained with them at nightfall." Then a valley came into view and he went ahead. I thought he had a need, so I sat at the edge. He was long in coming and I feared for him. Then I heard him as if he were talking privately with a man. Then he came out to me alone. I said: "Messenger of God, who was the man you were talking with?" He said: "Did you hear him?" I said: "Yes." He said: "That was Gabriel. He came to me and gave me the good news that whoever of my community dies without associating anything with God will enter Paradise." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said: "Yes."

situation: A young man came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who greeted him as "nephew." When the young man gave his lineage, 'Umar learned that his father had died before Islam.
wise_response: 'Umar began calling him "my son, my son."
why_it_worked: He saw the young man lacked a father in the faith and drew him closer with tenderness.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating the son of an unbeliever coldly or holding his father's past against him.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ الْحَكَمِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مَحْبُوبُ بْنُ مُحْرِزٍ الْكُوفِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الصَّعْبُ بْنُ حَكِيمٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ قَالَ‏:‏ أَتَيْتُ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، فَجَعَلَ يَقُولُ‏:‏ يَا ابْنَ أَخِي، ثُمَّ سَأَلَنِي‏؟‏ فَانْتَسَبْتُ لَهُ، فَعَرَفَ أَنَّ أَبِي لَمْ يُدْرِكِ الإِسْلاَمَ، فَجَعَلَ يَقُولُ‏:‏ يَا بُنَيَّ يَا بُنَيَّ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and he began saying: "Son of my brother." Then he asked me, and I told him my lineage, and he knew that my father had not lived to see Islam. So he began saying: "My son, my son."

situation: A man from Bali visited the Prophet with his father. Afterward he asked his father what the Prophet had told him privately.
wise_response: The Prophet's advice was: when you want to do something, go slowly and deliberately until God shows you a way out of it, or makes a way out for you.
why_it_worked: Taking one's time lets the right path become clear. Rushing closes options.
tempting_wrong_answer: Plunging into a decision before thinking it through.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا سَعْدُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ الأَنْصَارِيُّ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ مِنْ بَلِيٍّ قَالَ‏:‏ أَتَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَعَ أَبِي، فَنَاجَى أَبِي دُونِي، قَالَ‏:‏ فَقُلْتُ لأَبِي‏:‏ مَا قَالَ لَكَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَمْرًا فَعَلَيْكَ بِالتُّؤَدَةِ حَتَّى يُرِيَكَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ الْمَخْرَجَ، أَوْ حَتَّى يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكَ مَخْرَجًا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: I came to the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, with my father, and he spoke privately with my father apart from me. I said to my father: "What did he say to you?" He said: "When you intend a matter, hold to deliberateness until God shows you the way out of it, or until God makes a way out for you."

situation: Someone has a milk animal or knowledge of the way, and a neighbor or traveler needs it.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever lends a milk animal, or guides someone down a lane or road, has the equal of freeing a slave.
why_it_worked: Small, practical help carries great worth. Lending what you have and showing the way can change someone's day.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keeping one's animal to oneself and ignoring a lost person.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَلامٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا الْفَزَارِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا قِنَانُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَوْسَجَةَ، عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ بْنِ عَازِبٍ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ مَنْ مَنَحَ مَنِيحَةً أَوْ هَدَّى زُقَاقًا، أَوْ قَالَ‏:‏ طَرِيقًا، كَانَ لَهُ عَدْلُ عِتَاقِ نَسَمَةٍ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Whoever lends a milk animal, or guides someone down an alley, or he said a road, has the equal of freeing a soul.

key_terms.منيحة (maniha): an animal lent so the borrower can use its milk

situation: A person thinks charity means money they do not have.
wise_response: Abu Dharr reported that pouring from your bucket into your brother's bucket is charity. So is telling people to do good and stop wrong, smiling in your brother's face, clearing stones, thorns and bones from the road, and guiding a man in a place where he is lost.
why_it_worked: Charity is any act that eases another's life. Everyone can give it every day.
tempting_wrong_answer: Thinking only big gifts count and so doing nothing for others.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ رَجَاءٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا عِكْرِمَةُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ، عَنْ أَبِي زُمَيْلٍ، عَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ مَرْثَدٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ، يَرْفَعْهُ، قَالَ‏:‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ‏:‏ لاَ أَعْلَمُهُ إِلاَّ رَفَعَهُ، قَالَ‏:‏ إِفْرَاغُكَ مِنْ دَلْوِكَ فِي دَلْوِ أَخِيكَ صَدَقَةٌ، وَأَمْرُكَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَنَهْيُكَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ صَدَقَةٌ، وَتَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ صَدَقَةٌ، وَإِمَاطَتُكَ الْحَجَرَ وَالشَّوْكَ وَالْعَظْمَ عَنْ طَرِيقِ النَّاسِ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ، وَهِدَايَتُكَ الرَّجُلَ فِي أَرْضِ الضَّالَّةِ صَدَقَةٌ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: Pouring from your bucket into your brother's bucket is charity. Your enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is charity. Your smiling in your brother's face is charity. Your removing stones, thorns and bones from people's road is charity for you. And your guiding a man in a land where people go astray is charity.

situation: Someone has the chance to mislead a blind person for a cruel joke.
wise_response: The Prophet said God curses whoever leads a blind man astray from the road.
why_it_worked: Exploiting the vulnerable is a grave wrong. A person who cannot see depends on others' honesty.
tempting_wrong_answer: Making sport of a disabled person or misdirecting them.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبِي أُوَيْسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ أَبِي عَمْرٍو، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ كَمَّهَ أَعْمَى عَنِ السَّبِيلِ‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: God curses whoever leads a blind man astray from the way.

situation: In Mecca, 'Uthman ibn Maz'un smiled at the Prophet as he passed, and the Prophet invited him to sit. As they talked, the Prophet told him of a verse that had just come to him.
wise_response: The verse said: God commands justice, doing good, and giving to relatives, and forbids indecency, wrongdoing and oppression. 'Uthman said that was when faith settled in his heart and he came to love Muhammad.
why_it_worked: A plain call to justice and kindness won 'Uthman over. It names the core of good conduct toward people.
tempting_wrong_answer: Ignoring relatives, acting indecently, and oppressing others.

translation.original_text: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبَانَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْحَمِيدِ بْنُ بَهْرَامَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا شَهْرٌ قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ‏:‏ بَيْنَمَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِفِنَاءِ بَيْتِهِ بِمَكَّةَ جَالِسٌ، إِذْ مَرَّ بِهِ عُثْمَانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ، فَكَشَرَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ أَلاَ تَجْلِسُ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ بَلَى، فَجَلَسَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مُسْتَقْبِلَهُ، فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ يُحَدِّثُهُ إِذْ شَخَصَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَصَرَهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَقَالَ‏:‏ أَتَانِي رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم آنِفًا، وَأَنْتَ جَالِسٌ، قَالَ‏:‏ فَمَا قَالَ لَكَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ ‏{‏إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالإِحْسَانِ وَإِيتَاءِ ذِي الْقُرْبَى وَيَنْهَى عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ وَالْبَغْيِ يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ‏}‏ قَالَ عُثْمَانُ‏:‏ وَذَلِكَ حِينَ اسْتَقَرَّ الإِيمَانُ فِي قَلْبِي وَأَحْبَبْتُ مُحَمَّدًا‏.‏
translation.ai_translation: While the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting in the courtyard of his house in Mecca, 'Uthman ibn Maz'un passed by and smiled at the Prophet. The Prophet said to him: "Won't you sit?" He said: "Yes." So the Prophet sat facing him. While he was talking with him, the Prophet fixed his gaze on the sky and said: "A messenger of God came to me just now while you were sitting." He said: "What did he say to you?" He said: "God commands justice, excellence, and giving to kin, and He forbids indecency, wrongdoing and oppression. He admonishes you so that you may take heed." 'Uthman said: That was when faith settled in my heart and I loved Muhammad.

source.title: The Forty Hadith of an-Nawawi
source.author: Imam Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi
source.date_or_era: 13th century CE
source.citation: Arabic text via AhmedBaset/hadith-json; English translation cited, not stored

situation: Some things are plainly right and some plainly wrong, but many sit in a grey area that most people cannot judge. A person has to decide how close to the line to walk.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever avoids doubtful matters keeps his faith and his honor clear, and whoever falls into them falls into the forbidden, like a shepherd grazing near a private pasture who will soon stray into it. He added that the heart is the part that makes the whole body sound or corrupt.
why_it_worked: Staying back from the edge protects your integrity and your name. Small compromises lead to large ones, and conduct follows the state of the heart.
tempting_wrong_answer: Grazing right up to the boundary because it is not yet clearly forbidden, until one day you are over it.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ النُّعْمَانِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، قَالَ: سَمِعْت رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَقُولُ: "إنَّ الْحَلَالَ بَيِّنٌ، وَإِنَّ الْحَرَامَ بَيِّنٌ، وَبَيْنَهُمَا أُمُورٌ مُشْتَبِهَاتٌ لَا يَعْلَمُهُنَّ كَثِيرٌ مِنْ النَّاسِ، فَمَنْ اتَّقَى الشُّبُهَاتِ فَقْد اسْتَبْرَأَ لِدِينِهِ وَعِرْضِهِ، وَمَنْ وَقَعَ فِي الشُّبُهَاتِ وَقَعَ فِي الْحَرَامِ، كَالرَّاعِي يَرْعَى حَوْلَ الْحِمَى يُوشِكُ أَنْ يَرْتَعَ فِيهِ، أَلَا وَإِنَّ لِكُلِّ مَلِكٍ حِمًى، أَلَا وَإِنَّ حِمَى اللَّهِ مَحَارِمُهُ، أَلَا وَإِنَّ فِي الْجَسَدِ مُضْغَةً إذَا صَلَحَتْ صَلَحَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، وَإذَا فَسَدَتْ فَسَدَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، أَلَا وَهِيَ الْقَلْبُ". 
 
.
translation.ai_translation: The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know. Whoever guards against the doubtful has kept his religion and his honor free of blame, and whoever falls into the doubtful falls into the forbidden, like a shepherd grazing around a protected pasture who is about to graze in it. Every king has a protected pasture, and God's protected pasture is what He has forbidden. In the body there is a piece of flesh; when it is sound the whole body is sound, and when it is corrupt the whole body is corrupt. It is the heart.

situation: A person sets out to do something that looks good, such as leaving home for a better life. The same outward act can be driven by very different motives.
wise_response: The Prophet said deeds are judged by intentions, and each person gets what he intended. One who migrated for God and His Messenger has that migration; one who migrated for worldly gain or to marry a woman has only what he went for.
why_it_worked: The worth of an act sits in the motive behind it. Being honest with yourself about why you act is the first step of good conduct.
tempting_wrong_answer: Doing good things for show or gain while presenting them as noble, and trusting the outward act to cover the motive.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَبِي حَفْصٍ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ: " إنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى، فَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ إلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَهِجْرَتُهُ إلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، وَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ لِدُنْيَا يُصِيبُهَا أَوْ امْرَأَةٍ يَنْكِحُهَا فَهِجْرَتُهُ إلَى مَا هَاجَرَ إلَيْهِ". 
رَوَاهُ إِمَامَا الْمُحَدِّثِينَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللهِ مُحَمَّدُ بنُ إِسْمَاعِيل بن إِبْرَاهِيم بن الْمُغِيرَة بن بَرْدِزبَه الْبُخَارِيُّ الْجُعْفِيُّ  رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُمَا فِي "صَحِيحَيْهِمَا" اللذَينِ هُمَا أَصَحُّ الْكُتُبِ الْمُصَنَّفَةِ.
translation.ai_translation: Actions are only by intentions, and each person has only what he intended. So whoever's emigration was to God and His Messenger, his emigration is to God and His Messenger. And whoever's emigration was for some worldly thing he would gain, or a woman he would marry, his emigration is to that for which he emigrated.

key_terms.نية (niyya): intention, the purpose behind an act

situation: A man asked the Prophet for advice. He kept asking again, as if hoping for something more.
wise_response: The Prophet said, 'Do not become angry.' Each time the man repeated his request, he gave the same answer.
why_it_worked: Much harm to others and to oneself starts with anger. Mastering it is advice enough.
tempting_wrong_answer: Letting anger run, and looking for grander advice while ignoring the simple one.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ رَجُلًا قَالَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم أَوْصِنِي. قَالَ: لَا تَغْضَبْ، فَرَدَّدَ مِرَارًا، قَالَ: لَا تَغْضَبْ" .   
 .
translation.ai_translation: A man said to the Prophet: Advise me. He said: Do not become angry. The man repeated this several times, and he said: Do not become angry.

situation: The companions asked what religion comes down to in practice.
wise_response: The Prophet said, 'Religion is sincere counsel.' Asked to whom, he said to God, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims and their ordinary people.
why_it_worked: Sincerity means wanting good for others and telling them the truth for their benefit, whether they are rulers or common people.
tempting_wrong_answer: Flattering leaders, deceiving ordinary people, or keeping quiet when honest advice would help someone.

translation.original_text: عَنْ أَبِي رُقَيَّةَ تَمِيمِ بْنِ أَوْسٍ الدَّارِيِّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: "الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ." قُلْنَا: لِمَنْ؟ قَالَ: "لِلَّهِ، وَلِكِتَابِهِ، وَلِرَسُولِهِ، وَلِأَئِمَّةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَعَامَّتِهِمْ."
translation.ai_translation: Religion is sincere goodwill. We said: To whom? He said: To God, to His Book, to His Messenger, to the leaders of the Muslims and to their common people.

situation: A man travels far, dusty and disheveled, and raises his hands to the sky calling 'My Lord, my Lord'. But his food, drink and clothing were all gained unlawfully.
wise_response: The Prophet said God is good and accepts only what is good, and asked how such a man's prayer could be answered.
why_it_worked: Outward devotion does not wash clean what was taken wrongly. How you earn your living is part of your character.
tempting_wrong_answer: Earning by unlawful means and expecting showy piety to make up for it.

translation.original_text: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم "إنَّ اللَّهَ طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إلَّا طَيِّبًا، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ أَمَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِمَا أَمَرَ بِهِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ فَقَالَ تَعَالَى: "يَا أَيُّهَا الرُّسُلُ كُلُوا مِنْ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَاعْمَلُوا صَالِحًا"، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: "يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ" ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ الرَّجُلَ يُطِيلُ السَّفَرَ أَشْعَثَ أَغْبَرَ يَمُدُّ يَدَيْهِ إلَى السَّمَاءِ: يَا رَبِّ! يَا رَبِّ! وَمَطْعَمُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَمَشْرَبُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَمَلْبَسُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَغُذِّيَ بِالْحَرَامِ، فَأَنَّى يُسْتَجَابُ لَهُ؟".
translation.ai_translation: God is good and accepts only what is good. God commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers. He said: 'O messengers, eat of good things and do righteous work.' And He said: 'O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided you.' Then he mentioned a man who travels long, disheveled and dusty, stretching his hands to the sky: 'My Lord! My Lord!' while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished on the unlawful. How then can he be answered?
