situation: People are drawn to others' business: gossip, idle questions, matters that are none of theirs.
wise_response: The Prophet said part of a person's good practice of Islam is leaving alone what does not concern him.
why_it_worked: Minding your own affairs spares others intrusion and spares you wasted effort and harm.
tempting_wrong_answer: Prying into other people's lives and talking about matters that are not yours.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم "مِنْ حُسْنِ إسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ". 
حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ، رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ .
translation.ai_translation: Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him.

situation: A person wants good things for himself and has to decide how he regards the good fortune of others.
wise_response: The Prophet said none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
why_it_worked: Faith is measured by wanting for others what you want for yourself. It rules out envy and selfishness.
tempting_wrong_answer: Wanting the best only for yourself and feeling threatened when others have it.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ خَادِمِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: "لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ". 
رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ .  
 
،
translation.ai_translation: None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.

situation: Daily life brings chances to speak carelessly, and to treat neighbors and guests well or badly.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever believes in God and the Last Day should speak good or stay silent, honor his neighbor, and honor his guest.
why_it_worked: Faith shows in the tongue and in how you treat those near you and those who come to your door.
tempting_wrong_answer: Saying whatever comes to mind, ignoring or troubling the neighbor, and treating a guest as a burden.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: "مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاَللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاَللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ جَارَهُ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاَللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ ضَيْفَهُ".   
 
،
translation.ai_translation: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep silent. Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor. Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honor his guest.

situation: Even when an animal must be slaughtered, the person doing it chooses how much it suffers.
wise_response: The Prophet said God has prescribed excellence in everything. When you slaughter, do it well: sharpen your blade and spare the animal distress.
why_it_worked: Care is owed in every act, including hard ones. Doing a necessary thing well means doing it with the least pain.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating the animal carelessly, with a dull blade and no thought for its suffering.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي يَعْلَى شَدَّادِ بْنِ أَوْسٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: "إنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ الْإِحْسَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، فَإِذَا قَتَلْتُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا الْقِتْلَةَ، وَإِذَا ذَبَحْتُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا الذِّبْحَةَ، وَلْيُحِدَّ أَحَدُكُمْ شَفْرَتَهُ، وَلْيُرِحْ ذَبِيحَتَهُ". 
.
translation.ai_translation: God has prescribed excellence in everything. So when you kill, kill well, and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Let each of you sharpen his blade and give ease to the animal he slaughters.

key_terms.الإحسان (al-ihsan): excellence, doing a thing well and kindly

situation: Everyone does wrong at times and deals with other people every day.
wise_response: The Prophet said: be mindful of God wherever you are, follow a bad deed with a good one and it will erase it, and treat people with good character.
why_it_worked: A mistake is answered by setting to work on good. Good character with people is part of the same duty.
tempting_wrong_answer: Despairing after a wrong, or excusing it and carrying on, and treating people roughly.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ جُنْدَبِ بْنِ جُنَادَةَ، وَأَبِي عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ مُعَاذِ بْنِ جَبَلٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: "اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْت، وَأَتْبِعْ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقْ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ" . 
رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ  وَقَالَ: حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ، وَفِي بَعْضِ النُّسَخِ: حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ.
translation.ai_translation: Be mindful of God wherever you are. Follow the bad deed with a good deed and it will wipe it out. And deal with people with good character.

situation: The Prophet spoke to the young Ibn Abbas, who was riding behind him. A young person can easily fear what others can do to him.
wise_response: He told him to keep God's limits and God would keep him, to ask of God and seek help from God, and to know that if the whole community gathered to help or harm him, they could do only what God had written. In another version he added that victory comes with patience, relief with distress, and ease with hardship.
why_it_worked: Knowing that people's power over you is limited frees you from fear and flattery. Patience in hard times is rewarded with relief.
tempting_wrong_answer: Living in fear of people's power, bending to them, and losing heart when hardship comes.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: "كُنْت خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَوْمًا، فَقَالَ: يَا غُلَامِ! إنِّي أُعَلِّمُك كَلِمَاتٍ: احْفَظْ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْك، احْفَظْ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَك، إذَا سَأَلْت فَاسْأَلْ اللَّهَ، وَإِذَا اسْتَعَنْت فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاَللَّهِ، وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْأُمَّةَ لَوْ اجْتَمَعَتْ عَلَى أَنْ يَنْفَعُوك بِشَيْءٍ لَمْ يَنْفَعُوك إلَّا بِشَيْءٍ قَدْ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ لَك، وَإِنْ اجْتَمَعُوا عَلَى أَنْ يَضُرُّوك بِشَيْءٍ لَمْ يَضُرُّوك إلَّا بِشَيْءٍ قَدْ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْك؛ رُفِعَتْ الْأَقْلَامُ، وَجَفَّتْ الصُّحُفُ" . رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ  وَقَالَ: حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ. 
وَفِي رِوَايَةِ غَيْرِ التِّرْمِذِيِّ: "احْفَظْ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ أمامك، تَعَرَّفْ إلَى اللَّهِ فِي الرَّخَاءِ يَعْرِفُك فِي الشِّدَّةِ، وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ مَا أَخْطَأَك لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُصِيبَك، وَمَا أَصَابَك لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُخْطِئَك، وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ النَّصْرَ مَعَ الصَّبْرِ، وَأَنْ الْفَرَجَ مَعَ الْكَرْبِ، وَأَنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا".
translation.ai_translation: I was behind the Messenger of God one day and he said: Young man, I will teach you some words. Guard God and He will guard you. Guard God and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask God. When you seek help, seek help from God. Know that if the community gathered to benefit you with something, they would benefit you only with what God has written for you. And if they gathered to harm you with something, they would harm you only with what God has written against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried. In another version: Know God in ease and He will know you in hardship. Know that what missed you was never going to reach you, and what reached you was never going to miss you. Know that victory comes with patience, relief with distress, and with hardship comes ease.

situation: A person is about to do something shameful. Only his own sense of shame stands in the way.
wise_response: The Prophet quoted a saying from the earliest prophets: 'If you feel no shame, then do as you wish.'
why_it_worked: A sense of shame is what holds a person back from wrong. Once it is gone, nothing else restrains him.
tempting_wrong_answer: Silencing your sense of shame and treating every desire as permitted.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي مَسْعُودٍ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ عَمْرٍو الْأَنْصَارِيِّ الْبَدْرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم "إنَّ مِمَّا أَدْرَكَ النَّاسُ مِنْ كَلَامِ النُّبُوَّةِ الْأُولَى: إذَا لَمْ تَسْتَحِ فَاصْنَعْ مَا شِئْت" . 
 .
translation.ai_translation: Among what people have received from the words of the first prophecy is: If you have no shame, then do whatever you wish.

key_terms.الحياء (al-haya'): modesty, a sense of shame that restrains from wrong

situation: Sufyan ibn Abdullah asked the Prophet for one saying about Islam so complete that he would not need to ask anyone else.
wise_response: The Prophet said, 'Say: I believe in God, and then stand firm.'
why_it_worked: Belief has to be followed by staying on course day after day. Consistency is the whole of the practice.
tempting_wrong_answer: Professing belief and then drifting, or chasing ever more complicated teachings instead of keeping to the simple one.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي عَمْرٍو وَقِيلَ: أَبِي عَمْرَةَ سُفْيَانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: "قُلْت: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ! قُلْ لِي فِي الْإِسْلَامِ قَوْلًا لَا أَسْأَلُ عَنْهُ أَحَدًا غَيْرَك؛ قَالَ: قُلْ: آمَنْت بِاَللَّهِ ثُمَّ اسْتَقِمْ" . 
.
translation.ai_translation: I said: Messenger of God, tell me something about Islam that I will not need to ask anyone but you. He said: Say, I believe in God, then be upright.

key_terms.استقم (istaqim): be upright, stay on a straight course

source.author: Imam Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi
source.date_or_era: 13th century CE

situation: People have power over one another and are tempted to use it unjustly. They also face the results of their own deeds.
wise_response: In this hadith God says He has forbidden oppression for Himself and made it forbidden among people, so they must not wrong one another. It ends: whoever finds good should praise God, and whoever finds otherwise should blame no one but himself.
why_it_worked: Injustice is forbidden at the highest level, so no one may excuse it. Each person owns the results of his own conduct.
tempting_wrong_answer: Wronging those weaker than you, and blaming others for what your own deeds produced.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ الْغِفَارِيِّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم فِيمَا يَرْوِيهِ عَنْ رَبِّهِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: "يَا عِبَادِي: إنِّي حَرَّمْت الظُّلْمَ عَلَى نَفْسِي، وَجَعَلْته بَيْنَكُمْ مُحَرَّمًا؛ فَلَا تَظَالَمُوا. يَا عِبَادِي! كُلُّكُمْ ضَالٌّ إلَّا مَنْ هَدَيْته، فَاسْتَهْدُونِي أَهْدِكُمْ. يَا عِبَادِي! كُلُّكُمْ جَائِعٌ إلَّا مَنْ أَطْعَمْته، فَاسْتَطْعِمُونِي أُطْعِمْكُمْ. يَا عِبَادِي! كُلُّكُمْ عَارٍ إلَّا مَنْ كَسَوْته، فَاسْتَكْسُونِي أَكْسُكُمْ. يَا عِبَادِي! إنَّكُمْ تُخْطِئُونَ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ، وَأَنَا أَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا؛ فَاسْتَغْفِرُونِي أَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ. يَا عِبَادِي! إنَّكُمْ لَنْ تَبْلُغُوا ضُرِّي فَتَضُرُّونِي، وَلَنْ تَبْلُغُوا نَفْعِي فَتَنْفَعُونِي. يَا عِبَادِي! لَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ كَانُوا عَلَى أَتْقَى قَلْبِ رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ مِنْكُمْ، مَا زَادَ ذَلِكَ فِي مُلْكِي شَيْئًا. يَا عِبَادِي! لَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ كَانُوا عَلَى أَفْجَرِ قَلْبِ رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ مِنْكُمْ، مَا نَقَصَ ذَلِكَ مِنْ مُلْكِي شَيْئًا. يَا عِبَادِي! لَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ قَامُوا فِي صَعِيدٍ وَاحِدٍ، فَسَأَلُونِي، فَأَعْطَيْت كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ مَسْأَلَته، مَا نَقَصَ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا عِنْدِي إلَّا كَمَا يَنْقُصُ الْمِخْيَطُ إذَا أُدْخِلَ الْبَحْرَ. يَا عِبَادِي! إنَّمَا هِيَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ أُحْصِيهَا لَكُمْ، ثُمَّ أُوَفِّيكُمْ إيَّاهَا؛ فَمَنْ وَجَدَ خَيْرًا فَلْيَحْمَدْ اللَّهَ، وَمَنْ وَجَدَ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ فَلَا يَلُومَن إلَّا نَفْسَهُ". 
.
translation.ai_translation: My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. My servants, all of you are astray except whom I guide, so ask Me for guidance and I will guide you. All of you are hungry except whom I feed, so ask Me for food and I will feed you. All of you are naked except whom I clothe, so ask Me for clothing and I will clothe you. You err by night and by day and I forgive all sins, so ask My forgiveness and I will forgive you. You cannot reach harming Me so as to harm Me, nor reach benefiting Me so as to benefit Me. If the first and last of you, men and jinn, had the heart of the most God-fearing man among you, that would add nothing to My kingdom. If they had the heart of the most wicked man among you, that would take nothing from My kingdom. If they all stood on one plain and asked of Me, and I gave each what he asked, that would reduce what I have only as a needle reduces the sea when it is dipped in. My servants, it is only your deeds that I count for you and then repay you in full. Whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame only himself.

situation: Poorer companions complained that the wealthy were taking all the reward. The rich prayed and fasted as they did, and also gave their surplus wealth in charity.
wise_response: The Prophet told them they had their own charity: every praise of God, every call to what is right and every check on what is wrong is charity, and even a man's lawful relations with his wife carry reward.
why_it_worked: Goodness is open to everyone, rich or poor. Words, right conduct and ordinary life lived well all count.
tempting_wrong_answer: Resenting the wealthy and assuming that without money you have nothing good to give.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَيْضًا، "أَنَّ نَاسًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالُوا لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ذَهَبَ أَهْلُ الدُّثُورِ بِالْأُجُورِ؛ يُصَلُّونَ كَمَا نُصَلِّي، وَيَصُومُونَ كَمَا نَصُومُ، وَيَتَصَدَّقُونَ بِفُضُولِ أَمْوَالِهِمْ. قَالَ: أَوَلَيْسَ قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ مَا تَصَّدَّقُونَ؟ إنَّ بِكُلِّ تَسْبِيحَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَكُلِّ تَكْبِيرَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَكُلِّ تَحْمِيدَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَكُلِّ تَهْلِيلَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَأَمْرٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ صَدَقَةٌ، وَنَهْيٌ عَنْ مُنْكَرٍ صَدَقَةٌ، وَفِي بُضْعِ أَحَدِكُمْ صَدَقَةٌ. قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَيَأْتِي أَحَدُنَا شَهْوَتَهُ وَيَكُونُ لَهُ فِيهَا أَجْرٌ؟ قَالَ: أَرَأَيْتُمْ لَوْ وَضَعَهَا فِي حَرَامٍ أَكَانَ عَلَيْهِ وِزْرٌ؟ فَكَذَلِكَ إذَا وَضَعَهَا فِي الْحَلَالِ، كَانَ لَهُ أَجْرٌ". 
.
translation.ai_translation: Some of the companions said to the Prophet: Messenger of God, the wealthy have taken the rewards. They pray as we pray, fast as we fast, and give charity from their surplus wealth. He said: Has God not given you something to give in charity? Every glorification of God is charity, every declaration of His greatness is charity, every praise is charity, every 'there is no god but God' is charity, commanding good is charity, forbidding evil is charity, and in a man's intimacy with his wife there is charity. They said: Messenger of God, one of us fulfills his desire and gets reward for it? He said: Do you not see that if he put it in something unlawful he would bear a sin? So likewise when he puts it in the lawful, he has a reward.

situation: People think of charity as giving money. Ordinary days are full of smaller chances to do good.
wise_response: The Prophet said every joint of a person owes charity each day: judging fairly between two people, helping a man onto his mount or lifting his load onto it, a good word, each step to prayer, and removing something harmful from the road.
why_it_worked: Each day of health is a gift owed back in small acts of help and fairness that anyone can do.
tempting_wrong_answer: Passing by someone struggling with a load, or a hazard in the road, because it is not your job.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم "كُلُّ سُلَامَى مِنْ النَّاسِ عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةٌ، كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَطْلُعُ فِيهِ الشَّمْسُ تَعْدِلُ بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ صَدَقَةٌ، وَتُعِينُ الرَّجُلَ فِي دَابَّتِهِ فَتَحْمِلُهُ عَلَيْهَا أَوْ تَرْفَعُ لَهُ عَلَيْهَا مَتَاعَهُ صَدَقَةٌ، وَالْكَلِمَةُ الطَّيِّبَةُ صَدَقَةٌ، وَبِكُلِّ خُطْوَةٍ تَمْشِيهَا إلَى الصَّلَاةِ صَدَقَةٌ، وَتُمِيطُ الْأَذَى عَنْ الطَّرِيقِ صَدَقَةٌ". 
 
، .
translation.ai_translation: Every joint of a person owes charity every day the sun rises. Judging fairly between two people is charity. Helping a man with his mount, lifting him onto it or raising his goods onto it, is charity. A good word is charity. Every step you walk to prayer is charity. Removing harm from the road is charity.

situation: Wabisa ibn Ma'bad came to ask how to tell right from wrong, especially when others tell you something is allowed.
wise_response: The Prophet said righteousness is good character, and sin is what unsettles your chest and you would hate people to see. To Wabisa he said: consult your heart; righteousness is what the soul and heart rest easy with, and sin is what nags at the soul, even if people keep giving you rulings that it is fine.
why_it_worked: An honest conscience knows when something is wrong. Wanting to hide an act is a sign of it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Overriding your own unease by finding someone who will tell you it is permitted.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ النَّوَّاسِ بْنِ سَمْعَانَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: "الْبِرُّ حُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ، وَالْإِثْمُ مَا حَاكَ فِي صَدْرِك، وَكَرِهْت أَنْ يَطَّلِعَ عَلَيْهِ النَّاسُ" رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ . وَعَنْ وَابِصَةَ بْنِ مَعْبَدٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: أَتَيْت رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم فَقَالَ: "جِئْتَ تَسْأَلُ عَنْ الْبِرِّ؟ قُلْت: نَعَمْ. فقَالَ: استفت قلبك، الْبِرُّ مَا اطْمَأَنَّتْ إلَيْهِ النَّفْسُ، وَاطْمَأَنَّ إلَيْهِ الْقَلْبُ، وَالْإِثْمُ مَا حَاكَ فِي النَّفْسِ وَتَرَدَّدَ فِي الصَّدْرِ، وَإِنْ أَفْتَاك النَّاسُ وَأَفْتَوْك" . 
حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ، رَوَيْنَاهُ في مُسْنَدَي الْإِمَامَيْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ حَنْبَلٍ  بِإِسْنَادٍ حَسَنٍ.
translation.ai_translation: Righteousness is good character, and sin is what wavers in your chest and you dislike people seeing it. And from Wabisa: I came to the Messenger of God and he said: You have come to ask about righteousness? I said yes. He said: Ask your heart for a ruling. Righteousness is what the soul is at peace with and the heart is at peace with. Sin is what wavers in the soul and goes back and forth in the chest, even if people give you rulings, and give you rulings again.

situation: Mu'adh ibn Jabal asked for a deed that would bring him to Paradise. After listing the pillars and other good works, the Prophet offered to tell him what holds it all together.
wise_response: The Prophet took hold of his own tongue and said, 'Restrain this.' When Mu'adh asked whether people are held to account for what they say, he answered that nothing throws people on their faces into the Fire more than the harvest of their tongues.
why_it_worked: Speech does great damage to others and to oneself. Guarding the tongue protects everything else a person builds.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treating words as weightless and saying whatever one likes.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ مُعَاذِ بْنِ جَبَلٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قُلْت يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ! أَخْبِرْنِي بِعَمَلٍ يُدْخِلُنِي الْجَنَّةَ وَيُبَاعِدْنِي مِنْ النَّارِ، قَالَ: "لَقَدْ سَأَلْت عَنْ عَظِيمٍ، وَإِنَّهُ لَيَسِيرٌ عَلَى مَنْ يَسَّرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: تَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِهِ شَيْئًا، وَتُقِيمُ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِي الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصُومُ رَمَضَانَ، وَتَحُجُّ الْبَيْتَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَلَا أَدُلُّك عَلَى أَبْوَابِ الْخَيْرِ؟ الصَّوْمُ جُنَّةٌ، وَالصَّدَقَةُ تُطْفِئُ الْخَطِيئَةَ كَمَا يُطْفِئُ الْمَاءُ النَّارَ، وَصَلَاةُ الرَّجُلِ فِي جَوْفِ اللَّيْلِ، ثُمَّ تَلَا: " تَتَجَافَى جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ " حَتَّى بَلَغَ "يَعْمَلُونَ"، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَلَا أُخْبِرُك بِرَأْسِ الْأَمْرِ وَعَمُودِهِ وَذُرْوَةِ سَنَامِهِ؟ قُلْت: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ. قَالَ: رَأْسُ الْأَمْرِ الْإِسْلَامُ، وَعَمُودُهُ الصَّلَاةُ، وَذُرْوَةُ سَنَامِهِ الْجِهَادُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَلَا أُخْبِرُك بِمَلَاكِ ذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ؟ فقُلْت: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ! فَأَخَذَ بِلِسَانِهِ وَقَالَ: كُفَّ عَلَيْك هَذَا. قُلْت: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ وَإِنَّا لَمُؤَاخَذُونَ بِمَا نَتَكَلَّمُ بِهِ؟ فَقَالَ: ثَكِلَتْك أُمُّك وَهَلْ يَكُبُّ النَّاسَ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ -أَوْ قَالَ عَلَى مَنَاخِرِهِمْ- إلَّا حَصَائِدُ أَلْسِنَتِهِمْ؟!" . 
رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ  وَقَالَ: حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ.
translation.ai_translation: I said: Messenger of God, tell me of a deed that will bring me into Paradise and keep me far from the Fire. He said: You have asked about something great, yet it is easy for whom God makes it easy. Worship God without associating anything with Him, establish prayer, give zakat, fast Ramadan, and make pilgrimage to the House. Then he said: Shall I not guide you to the doors of good? Fasting is a shield, charity puts out sin as water puts out fire, and a man's prayer in the depth of night. Then he recited the verse. Then he said: Shall I not tell you of the head of the matter, its pillar and its peak? I said yes. He said: The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is prayer, and its peak is striving. Then he said: Shall I not tell you what holds all of this? I said yes, Messenger of God. He took hold of his tongue and said: Restrain this. I said: Prophet of God, will we be held to account for what we say? He said: May your mother lose you! Does anything topple people on their faces, or on their noses, into the Fire except the harvests of their tongues?

situation: A man asked for a deed that would make God love him and make people love him.
wise_response: The Prophet said, 'Do without the world and God will love you. Do without what people have and people will love you.'
why_it_worked: People are drawn to someone who does not covet what they own. Not grasping frees you and puts others at ease.
tempting_wrong_answer: Eyeing what others have, asking and angling for it, and wondering why people keep their distance.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي الْعَبَّاسِ سَهْلِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ السَّاعِدِيّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ! دُلَّنِي عَلَى عَمَلٍ إذَا عَمِلْتُهُ أَحَبَّنِي اللهُ وَأَحَبَّنِي النَّاسُ؛ فَقَالَ: "ازْهَدْ فِي الدُّنْيَا يُحِبَّك اللهُ، وَازْهَدْ فِيمَا عِنْدَ النَّاسِ يُحِبَّك النَّاسُ" . 
حديث حسن، رَوَاهُ ابْنُ مَاجَهْ ، وَغَيْرُهُ بِأَسَانِيدَ حَسَنَةٍ.
translation.ai_translation: A man came to the Prophet and said: Messenger of God, guide me to a deed which, if I do it, God will love me and people will love me. He said: Be detached from the world and God will love you, and be detached from what people have and people will love you.

situation: A person is harmed, or is tempted to harm someone for his own benefit.
wise_response: The Prophet said, 'There is to be no harming and no returning harm.'
why_it_worked: Harm, and harm paid back with harm, both feed injustice. The rule protects everyone.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hurting others when it suits you, or answering one harm with another.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ سَعْدِ بْنِ مَالِكِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ الْخُدْرِيّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: " لَا ضَرَرَ وَلَا ضِرَارَ" . 
حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ، رَوَاهُ ابْنُ مَاجَهْ  فِي "الْمُوَطَّإِ" عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم مُرْسَلًا، فَأَسْقَطَ أَبَا سَعِيدٍ، وَلَهُ طُرُقٌ يُقَوِّي بَعْضُهَا بَعْضًا.
translation.ai_translation: No harm and no harming in return.

situation: In a dispute, one party makes a claim against another's property or life.
wise_response: The Prophet said that if people were given whatever they claimed, men would claim others' wealth and blood. So proof falls on the one who claims, and the oath on the one who denies.
why_it_worked: A claim alone is not enough to take from someone. Fair judgment needs evidence and protects the accused.
tempting_wrong_answer: Taking someone's word as proof against another, or pressing a claim you cannot back up.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: "لَوْ يُعْطَى النَّاسُ بِدَعْوَاهُمْ لَادَّعَى رِجَالٌ أَمْوَالَ قَوْمٍ وَدِمَاءَهُمْ، لَكِنَّ الْبَيِّنَةَ عَلَى الْمُدَّعِي، وَالْيَمِينَ عَلَى مَنْ أَنْكَرَ" . 
حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ، رَوَاهُ الْبَيْهَقِيّ ، وَغَيْرُهُ هَكَذَا، وَبَعْضُهُ فِي "الصَّحِيحَيْنِ".
translation.ai_translation: If people were given according to their claims, men would claim the wealth and the blood of others. But the evidence is on the claimant, and the oath is on the one who denies.

situation: A person sees something wrong being done.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever sees a wrong should change it with his hand; if he cannot, with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.
why_it_worked: Each person acts against wrong as far as his ability reaches. At the very least he must not accept it inwardly.
tempting_wrong_answer: Looking away from a wrong you could stop or speak against, and growing comfortable with it.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ سَمِعْت رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَقُولُ: "مَنْ رَأَى مِنْكُمْ مُنْكَرًا فَلْيُغَيِّرْهُ بِيَدِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِلِسَانِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِقَلْبِهِ، وَذَلِكَ أَضْعَفُ الْإِيمَانِ" . 
.
translation.ai_translation: Whoever of you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand. If he cannot, then with his tongue. If he cannot, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.

situation: Neighbors, traders and peers are tempted to envy one another, outbid or undercut each other, nurse hatred, and turn their backs.
wise_response: The Prophet forbade envy, price rigging, hatred, turning away and undercutting another's sale, and said: be brothers. A Muslim does not wrong his brother, abandon him, lie to him or look down on him. Pointing to his chest three times, he said God-consciousness is here, and it is evil enough to despise your brother.
why_it_worked: Real worth is in the heart. No one can see it, so no one has grounds for contempt. Each person's blood, property and honor are sacred.
tempting_wrong_answer: Looking down on others, undercutting them in business, or cutting them off out of envy.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم " لَا تَحَاسَدُوا، وَلَا تَنَاجَشُوا، وَلَا تَبَاغَضُوا، وَلَا تَدَابَرُوا، وَلَا يَبِعْ بَعْضُكُمْ عَلَى بَيْعِ بَعْضٍ، وَكُونُوا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ إخْوَانًا، الْمُسْلِمُ أَخُو الْمُسْلِمِ، لَا يَظْلِمُهُ، وَلَا يَخْذُلُهُ، وَلَا يَكْذِبُهُ، وَلَا يَحْقِرُهُ، التَّقْوَى هَاهُنَا، وَيُشِيرُ إلَى صَدْرِهِ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، بِحَسْبِ امْرِئٍ مِنْ الشَّرِّ أَنْ يَحْقِرَ أَخَاهُ الْمُسْلِمَ، كُلُّ الْمُسْلِمِ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِ حَرَامٌ: دَمُهُ وَمَالُهُ وَعِرْضُهُ" . 
.
translation.ai_translation: Do not envy one another, do not bid up prices against one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and do not sell over one another's sale. Be servants of God, brothers. A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim. He does not wrong him, abandon him, lie to him or despise him. God-consciousness is here, and he pointed to his chest three times. It is enough evil for a man to despise his Muslim brother. All of a Muslim is sacred to another Muslim: his blood, his property and his honor.

key_terms.يحقره (yahqiruhu): looks down on him, holds him in contempt

situation: Someone near you is in distress, in debt, or has a fault you know about.
wise_response: The Prophet said whoever relieves a believer's hardship, God will relieve his hardship on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever eases things for someone in difficulty, God eases things for him. Whoever covers a Muslim's fault, God covers his. God helps a servant as long as he helps his brother.
why_it_worked: Help given is returned in kind. Covering someone's faults protects their dignity.
tempting_wrong_answer: Pressing a struggling debtor, ignoring someone in trouble, or exposing a person's faults.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالَ: "مَنْ نَفَّسَ عَنْ مُؤْمِنٍ كُرْبَةً مِنْ كُرَبِ الدُّنْيَا نَفَّسَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ كُرْبَةً مِنْ كُرَبِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَمَنْ يَسَّرَ عَلَى مُعْسِرٍ، يَسَّرَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، وَمَنْ سَتَرَ مُسْلِما سَتَرَهُ اللهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ ، وَاَللَّهُ فِي عَوْنِ الْعَبْدِ مَا كَانَ الْعَبْدُ فِي عَوْنِ أَخِيهِ، وَمَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إلَى الْجَنَّةِ، وَمَا اجْتَمَعَ قَوْمٌ فِي بَيْتٍ مِنْ بُيُوتِ اللَّهِ يَتْلُونَ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ، وَيَتَدَارَسُونَهُ فِيمَا بَيْنَهُمْ؛ إلَّا نَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ السَّكِينَةُ، وَغَشِيَتْهُمْ الرَّحْمَةُ، وَ حَفَّتهُمُ المَلاَئِكَة، وَذَكَرَهُمْ اللَّهُ فِيمَنْ عِنْدَهُ، وَمَنْ أَبَطْأَ بِهِ عَمَلُهُ لَمْ يُسْرِعْ بِهِ نَسَبُهُ". 
 بهذا اللفظ.
translation.ai_translation: Whoever relieves a believer of one of the hardships of this world, God will relieve him of one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection. Whoever makes things easy for someone in difficulty, God will make things easy for him in this world and the next. Whoever covers a Muslim, God will cover him in this world and the next. God is in the help of His servant as long as the servant is in the help of his brother. Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, God makes easy for him a path to Paradise. No people gather in a house of God, reciting the Book of God and studying it together, except that tranquility descends on them, mercy covers them, the angels surround them, and God mentions them among those with Him. Whoever is held back by his deeds will not be hurried forward by his lineage.

situation: The Prophet took Ibn Umar by the shoulder. People tend to settle into the world as if it were permanent and put off what matters.
wise_response: He said, 'Be in the world as if you were a stranger or a traveler passing through.' Ibn Umar used to say: in the evening do not wait for morning, in the morning do not wait for evening, and take from your health for your sickness and from your life for your death.
why_it_worked: Holding the world lightly keeps you from greed and delay. Using health and time while you have them is plain sense.
tempting_wrong_answer: Living as if you will stay forever, piling up things and putting off good work until later.

translation.original_text:
عَنْ ابْن عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: أَخَذَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم بِمَنْكِبِي، وَقَالَ: "كُنْ فِي الدُّنْيَا كَأَنَّك غَرِيبٌ أَوْ عَابِرُ سَبِيلٍ". وَكَانَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا يَقُولُ: إذَا أَمْسَيْتَ فَلَا تَنْتَظِرْ الصَّبَاحَ، وَإِذَا أَصْبَحْتَ فَلَا تَنْتَظِرْ الْمَسَاءَ، وَخُذْ مِنْ صِحَّتِك لِمَرَضِك، وَمِنْ حَيَاتِك لِمَوْتِك. 
 .
translation.ai_translation: The Messenger of God took me by the shoulder and said: Be in the world as though you were a stranger or a passer-by on the road. And Ibn Umar used to say: When evening comes, do not wait for morning, and when morning comes, do not wait for evening. Take from your health for your illness, and from your life for your death.

situation: Amos speaks to the powerful men of Israel who run the town court at the gate. They hate anyone who calls them out, squeeze grain from the poor, take bribes and push the needy out of court.
wise_response: Welcome the person who rebukes you in public and the one who speaks plainly. Give the poor a fair hearing at the gate. Amos names the wrong directly: "you harass the innocent, take hush money, and push the needy aside at the gate."
why_it_worked: A community stays honest only if its critics are heard and its weakest members can get justice. Wealth taken from the poor does not last; Amos says they will not live in the stone houses they built.
tempting_wrong_answer: Silence the critic, resent honest speech, and use power over the court to profit from people who cannot fight back.

translation.original_text: שָׂנְא֥וּ בַשַּׁ֖עַר מוֹכִ֑יחַ וְדֹבֵ֥ר תָּמִ֖ים יְתָעֵֽבוּ׃ לָ֠כֵ֠ן יַ֣עַן בּוֹשַׁסְכֶ֞ם עַל־דָּ֗ל וּמַשְׂאַת־בַּר֙ תִּקְח֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ בָּתֵּ֥י גָזִ֛ית בְּנִיתֶ֖ם וְלֹא־תֵ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֑ם כַּרְמֵי־חֶ֣מֶד נְטַעְתֶּ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁתּ֖וּ אֶת־יֵינָֽם׃ כִּ֤י יָדַ֙עְתִּי֙ רַבִּ֣ים פִּשְׁעֵיכֶ֔ם וַעֲצֻמִ֖ים חַטֹּאתֵיכֶ֑ם צֹרְרֵ֤י צַדִּיק֙ לֹ֣קְחֵי כֹ֔פֶר וְאֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים בַּשַּׁ֥עַר הִטּֽוּ׃
translation.scholarly_translation: They hate him that reproveth in the gate, And they abhor him that speaketh uprightly. Therefore, because ye trample upon the poor, And take from him exactions of wheat; Ye have built houses of hewn stone, But ye shall not dwell in them, Ye have planted pleasant vineyards, But ye shall not drink wine thereof. For I know how manifold are your transgressions, And how mighty are your sins; Ye that afflict the just, that take a ransom, And that turn aside the needy in the gate.
translation.scholarly_source: The Holy Scriptures: A New Translation (JPS 1917) (Public Domain); Hebrew: Miqra according to the Masorah (CC-BY-SA)
translation.ai_translation: They hate the one who rebukes at the gate, and they loathe the one who speaks with integrity. So, because you trample the poor and take levies of grain from him, you have built houses of cut stone, but you will not live in them; you have planted lovely vineyards, but you will not drink their wine. For I know how many your crimes are and how great your sins: you harass the innocent, you take hush money, and you push the needy aside at the gate.

situation: The people say God is with them, while their courts are corrupt. Amos tells them what would make that claim true.
wise_response: Choose good over evil in practice, and set fair judgment firmly in the court. "Hate evil and love good, and set justice firmly in the gate."
why_it_worked: Belonging to a people or a faith does not make anyone good; conduct does. Amos offers only a "perhaps," so the good is to be done for its own sake.
tempting_wrong_answer: Assume you are on the right side because of who you are, and keep the corrupt court running.

translation.original_text: דִּרְשׁוּ־ט֥וֹב וְאַל־רָ֖ע לְמַ֣עַן תִּֽחְי֑וּ וִיהִי־כֵ֞ן יְהֹוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֛וֹת אִתְּכֶ֖ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲמַרְתֶּֽם׃ שִׂנְאוּ־רָע֙ וְאֶ֣הֱבוּ ט֔וֹב וְהַצִּ֥יגוּ בַשַּׁ֖עַר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט אוּלַ֗י יֶחֱנַ֛ן יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יוֹסֵֽף׃ {ס}
translation.scholarly_translation: Seek good, and not evil, that ye may live; And so the LORD, the God of hosts, will be with you, as ye say. Hate the evil, and love the good, And establish justice in the gate; It may be that the LORD, the God of hosts, Will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph.

translation.ai_translation: Seek good and not evil, so that you may live; then the LORD, God of hosts, will truly be with you, as you claim. Hate evil and love good, and set justice firmly in the gate. Perhaps the LORD, God of hosts, will show favor to the remnant of Joseph.

situation: Israel keeps lavish festivals, offerings and temple music while injustice goes on. Amos says God rejects all of it.
wise_response: Put justice before display. "Let justice roll on like water, and righteousness like a stream that never dries."
why_it_worked: Worship and ceremony do not cover for cheating and oppression. Justice has to run steadily through ordinary life, like a stream that flows in every season.
tempting_wrong_answer: Spend on public piety and loud ritual to feel righteous, while leaving unfair dealing in place.

translation.original_text: שָׂנֵ֥אתִי מָאַ֖סְתִּי חַגֵּיכֶ֑ם וְלֹ֥א אָרִ֖יחַ בְּעַצְּרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃ כִּ֣י אִם־תַּעֲלוּ־לִ֥י עֹל֛וֹת וּמִנְחֹתֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֣א אֶרְצֶ֑ה וְשֶׁ֥לֶם מְרִיאֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֥א אַבִּֽיט׃ הָסֵ֥ר מֵעָלַ֖י הֲמ֣וֹן שִׁרֶ֑יךָ וְזִמְרַ֥ת נְבָלֶ֖יךָ לֹ֥א אֶשְׁמָֽע׃ וְיִגַּ֥ל כַּמַּ֖יִם מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה כְּנַ֥חַל אֵיתָֽן׃
translation.scholarly_translation: I hate, I despise your feasts, And I will take no delight in your solemn assemblies. Yea, though ye offer me burnt-offerings and your meal-offerings, I will not accept them; Neither will I regard the peace-offerings of your fat beasts. Take thou away from Me the noise of thy songs; And let Me not hear the melody of thy psalteries. But let justice well up as waters, And righteousness as a mighty stream.
translation.scholarly_source: The Holy Scriptures: A New Translation (JPS 1917) (Public Domain); Hebrew: Miqra according to the Masorah (CC-BY-SA)
translation.ai_translation: I hate, I reject your festivals; I take no pleasure in your solemn gatherings. Even if you bring me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them; I will not look at the peace offerings of your fattened cattle. Take the noise of your songs away from me; I will not listen to the music of your harps. Instead, let justice roll on like water, and righteousness like a stream that never dries.

situation: Moses has just recalled how the people broke faith with the golden calf and how he had to carve the tablets again. He tells them what has to change inside them.
wise_response: Open the heart and stop resisting correction. "Circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and do not stiffen your neck any longer."
why_it_worked: Wrong conduct starts with a closed heart and a stubborn will. Willingness to be corrected is the beginning of change.
tempting_wrong_answer: Stay stubborn, refuse to bend, and repeat the same failure.

translation.scholarly_translation: Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.

situation: Moses describes the God Israel serves: one who plays no favorites, takes no bribes, and protects those with no one to stand for them. Then he draws the duty from it.
wise_response: Love the stranger and provide for them, as God gives the stranger bread and clothing. "You shall love the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt."
why_it_worked: People who remember being outsiders owe care to the outsiders among them. Justice for the orphan, the widow and the immigrant is how God is described, so it is what God's people are asked to do.
tempting_wrong_answer: Favor the powerful and well-connected, and treat the foreigner living among you as someone else's problem.

translation.original_text: כִּ֚י יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם ה֚וּא אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַאֲדֹנֵ֖י הָאֲדֹנִ֑ים הָאֵ֨ל הַגָּדֹ֤ל הַגִּבֹּר֙ וְהַנּוֹרָ֔א אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹא־יִשָּׂ֣א פָנִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יִקַּ֖ח שֹֽׁחַד׃ עֹשֶׂ֛ה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט יָת֖וֹם וְאַלְמָנָ֑ה וְאֹהֵ֣ב גֵּ֔ר לָ֥תֶת ל֖וֹ לֶ֥חֶם וְשִׂמְלָֽה׃ וַאֲהַבְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־הַגֵּ֑ר כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

He doth execute justice for the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment. Love ye therefore the stranger; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

situation: Neighbors fall into debt and cannot climb out. The law sets a fixed year when lenders must let the debts go.
wise_response: Every seventh year, cancel what your neighbor owes you and stop pressing for payment, because "a release for the LORD has been proclaimed."
why_it_worked: Debt that never ends turns a neighbor into a permanent underclass. A set release gives people a fresh start and keeps lenders from owning their neighbors' lives.
tempting_wrong_answer: Collect every debt to the last coin, however long it takes and whatever it does to the borrower.

translation.original_text: מִקֵּ֥ץ שֶֽׁבַע־שָׁנִ֖ים תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה שְׁמִטָּֽה׃ וְזֶה֮ דְּבַ֣ר הַשְּׁמִטָּה֒ שָׁמ֗וֹט כׇּל־בַּ֙עַל֙ מַשֵּׁ֣ה יָד֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַשֶּׁ֖ה בְּרֵעֵ֑הוּ לֹֽא־יִגֹּ֤שׂ אֶת־רֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ וְאֶת־אָחִ֔יו כִּֽי־קָרָ֥א שְׁמִטָּ֖ה לַיהֹוָֽה׃
translation.scholarly_translation: At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release. And this is the manner of the release: every creditor shall release that which he hath lent unto his neighbour; he shall not exact it of his neighbour and his brother; because the LORD’S release hath been proclaimed.
translation.scholarly_source: The Holy Scriptures: A New Translation (JPS 1917) (Public Domain); Hebrew: Miqra according to the Masorah (CC-BY-SA)
translation.ai_translation: At the end of every seven years you shall make a release. This is how the release works: every creditor shall let go of what he lent to his neighbor. He shall not press his neighbor, his kinsman, for payment, because a release for the LORD has been proclaimed.

key_terms.שְׁמִטָּה (shemitah): release; letting something drop from the hand

situation: A poor neighbor asks for a loan as the seventh year approaches. The lender knows the debt will be cancelled soon and he will likely never be repaid.
wise_response: Lend anyway, enough for what he lacks, and give without resentment. "Open your hand wide to him," and "do not let your heart begrudge it when you give."
why_it_worked: Need does not go away, so the duty to help does not go away. The law names the hidden calculation, the grudging eye, and calls it sin.
tempting_wrong_answer: Do the math, see the release year coming, and refuse the loan with a cold eye.

translation.original_text: כִּֽי־יִהְיֶה֩ בְךָ֨ אֶבְי֜וֹן מֵאַחַ֤ד אַחֶ֙יךָ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד שְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ בְּאַ֨רְצְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁר־יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֣ן לָ֑ךְ לֹ֧א תְאַמֵּ֣ץ אֶת־לְבָבְךָ֗ וְלֹ֤א תִקְפֹּץ֙ אֶת־יָ֣דְךָ֔ מֵאָחִ֖יךָ הָאֶבְיֽוֹן׃ כִּֽי־פָתֹ֧חַ תִּפְתַּ֛ח אֶת־יָדְךָ֖ ל֑וֹ וְהַעֲבֵט֙ תַּעֲבִיטֶ֔נּוּ דֵּ֚י מַחְסֹר֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֶחְסַ֖ר לֽוֹ׃ הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֡ פֶּן־יִהְיֶ֣ה דָבָר֩ עִם־לְבָבְךָ֨ בְלִיַּ֜עַל לֵאמֹ֗ר קָֽרְבָ֣ה שְׁנַֽת־הַשֶּׁ֘בַע֮ שְׁנַ֣ת הַשְּׁמִטָּה֒ וְרָעָ֣ה עֵֽינְךָ֗ בְּאָחִ֙יךָ֙ הָֽאֶבְי֔וֹן וְלֹ֥א תִתֵּ֖ן ל֑וֹ וְקָרָ֤א עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ אֶל־יְהֹוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה בְךָ֖ חֵֽטְא׃ נָת֤וֹן תִּתֵּן֙ ל֔וֹ וְלֹא־יֵרַ֥ע לְבָבְךָ֖ בְּתִתְּךָ֣ ל֑וֹ כִּ֞י בִּגְלַ֣ל ׀ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה יְבָרֶכְךָ֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכׇֽל־מַעֲשֶׂ֔ךָ וּבְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁלַ֥ח יָדֶֽךָ׃ כִּ֛י לֹא־יֶחְדַּ֥ל אֶבְי֖וֹן מִקֶּ֣רֶב הָאָ֑רֶץ עַל־כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר פָּ֠תֹ֠חַ תִּפְתַּ֨ח אֶת־יָדְךָ֜ לְאָחִ֧יךָ לַעֲנִיֶּ֛ךָ וּלְאֶבְיֹנְךָ֖ בְּאַרְצֶֽךָ׃ {ס}
translation.scholarly_translation: If there be among you a needy man, one of thy brethren, within any of thy gates, in thy land which the LORD thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thy heart, nor shut thy hand from thy needy brother; but thou shalt surely open thy hand unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need in that which he wanteth. Beware that there be not a base thought in thy heart, saying: ‘The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand’; and thine eye be evil against thy needy brother, and thou give him nought; and he cry unto the LORD against thee, and it be sin in thee. Thou shalt surely give him, and thy heart shall not be grieved when thou givest unto him; because that for this thing the LORD thy God will bless thee in all thy work, and in all that thou puttest thy hand unto. For the poor shall never cease out of the land; therefore I command thee, saying: ‘Thou shalt surely open thy hand unto thy poor and needy brother, in thy land.’
translation.scholarly_source: The Holy Scriptures: A New Translation (JPS 1917) (Public Domain); Hebrew: Miqra according to the Masorah (CC-BY-SA)
translation.ai_translation: If there is a poor man among you, one of your kin, in any of your towns in the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not harden your heart and do not close your hand against your poor kinsman. Rather, open your hand wide to him, and lend him enough for whatever he lacks. Watch yourself, so that no base thought enters your heart: "The seventh year, the year of release, is close," and you look on your poor kinsman with a grudging eye and give him nothing. He will cry out to the LORD against you, and it will be counted as sin in you. Give to him freely, and do not let your heart begrudge it when you give, for because of this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you set your hand to. For the poor will never disappear from the land. That is why I command you: open your hand wide to your kinsman, to the poor and needy in your land.

situation: A fellow Israelite sold into service for debt finishes six years of work. The master must now let him go.
wise_response: Send him off free and with a real start: load him generously from the flock, the threshing floor and the winepress. "Do not send him away empty-handed."
why_it_worked: A person leaving years of service should not walk out with nothing. The master is told to remember that he too was once a slave and was set free.
tempting_wrong_answer: Release him with nothing in his hands, so that he is likely to fall back into debt and servitude.

translation.original_text: כִּֽי־יִמָּכֵ֨ר לְךָ֜ אָחִ֣יךָ הָֽעִבְרִ֗י א֚וֹ הָֽעִבְרִיָּ֔ה וַעֲבָֽדְךָ֖ שֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים וּבַשָּׁנָה֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔ת תְּשַׁלְּחֶ֥נּוּ חׇפְשִׁ֖י מֵעִמָּֽךְ׃ וְכִֽי־תְשַׁלְּחֶ֥נּוּ חׇפְשִׁ֖י מֵֽעִמָּ֑ךְ לֹ֥א תְשַׁלְּחֶ֖נּוּ רֵיקָֽם׃ הַעֲנֵ֤יק תַּעֲנִיק֙ ל֔וֹ מִצֹּ֣אנְךָ֔ וּמִֽגׇּרְנְךָ֖ וּמִיִּקְבֶ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר בֵּרַכְךָ֛ יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ תִּתֶּן־לֽוֹ׃ וְזָכַרְתָּ֗ כִּ֣י עֶ֤בֶד הָיִ֙יתָ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַֽיִּפְדְּךָ֖ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ עַל־כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֧י מְצַוְּךָ֛ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה הַיּֽוֹם׃
translation.scholarly_translation: If thy brother, a Hebrew man, or a Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee, he shall serve thee six years; and in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free from thee. And when thou lettest him go free from thee, thou shalt not let him go empty; thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, and out of thy threshing-floor, and out of thy winepress; of that wherewith the LORD thy God hath blessed thee thou shalt give unto him. And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the LORD thy God redeemed thee; therefore I command thee this thing to-day.
translation.scholarly_source: The Holy Scriptures: A New Translation (JPS 1917) (Public Domain); Hebrew: Miqra according to the Masorah (CC-BY-SA)
translation.ai_translation: If your kinsman, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold to you, he shall serve you six years, and in the seventh year you shall send him away free. And when you send him away free, do not send him away empty-handed. Load him generously from your flock, your threshing floor and your winepress; give him from what the LORD your God has blessed you with. Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you. That is why I give you this command today.

situation: At the harvest Feast of Weeks, a farmer celebrates his good year. The law names who must be at the table.
wise_response: Bring everyone into the joy: son and daughter, male and female servants, the Levite, the stranger, the orphan and the widow. "Remember that you were a slave in Egypt."
why_it_worked: A celebration that leaves out the poor and the outsider is incomplete. Memory of one's own hard past opens the door to others.
tempting_wrong_answer: Celebrate the harvest with your own family and leave the servant, the widow and the stranger outside.

translation.original_text: וְשָׂמַחְתָּ֞ לִפְנֵ֣י ׀ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ אַתָּ֨ה וּבִנְךָ֣ וּבִתֶּ֘ךָ֮ וְעַבְדְּךָ֣ וַאֲמָתֶ֒ךָ֒ וְהַלֵּוִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ וְהַגֵּ֛ר וְהַיָּת֥וֹם וְהָאַלְמָנָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבֶּ֑ךָ בַּמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִבְחַר֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לְשַׁכֵּ֥ן שְׁמ֖וֹ שָֽׁם׃ וְזָ֣כַרְתָּ֔ כִּי־עֶ֥בֶד הָיִ֖יתָ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֣ וְעָשִׂ֔יתָ אֶת־הַֽחֻקִּ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃ {פ}
translation.scholarly_translation: And thou shalt rejoice before the LORD thy God, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, and thy man-servant, and thy maid-servant, and the Levite that is within they gates, and the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, that are in the midst of thee, in the place which the LORD thy God shall choose to cause His name to dwell there. And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt; and thou shalt observe and do these statutes.

translation.ai_translation: And rejoice before the LORD your God, you, your son and your daughter, your male and female servants, the Levite in your towns, and the stranger, the orphan and the widow among you, at the place the LORD your God chooses to make his name dwell. Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and keep and do these statutes.

situation: The people are told to set up judges and officers in every town. The law spells out how those judges must act.
wise_response: Judge fairly. Do not bend the ruling, do not favor anyone, and take no gift from a party. "Justice, justice you shall pursue."
why_it_worked: A bribe corrupts even good and wise people, because it changes what they can see. Justice has to be chased actively.
tempting_wrong_answer: Accept a gift, lean toward the important party, and tell yourself it will not affect the ruling.

translation.original_text: שֹׁפְטִ֣ים וְשֹֽׁטְרִ֗ים תִּֽתֶּן־לְךָ֙ בְּכׇל־שְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְהֹוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ לִשְׁבָטֶ֑יךָ וְשָׁפְט֥וּ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם מִשְׁפַּט־צֶֽדֶק׃ לֹא־תַטֶּ֣ה מִשְׁפָּ֔ט לֹ֥א תַכִּ֖יר פָּנִ֑ים וְלֹא־תִקַּ֣ח שֹׁ֔חַד כִּ֣י הַשֹּׁ֗חַד יְעַוֵּר֙ עֵינֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֔ים וִֽיסַלֵּ֖ף דִּבְרֵ֥י צַדִּיקִֽם׃ צֶ֥דֶק צֶ֖דֶק תִּרְדֹּ֑ף לְמַ֤עַן תִּֽחְיֶה֙ וְיָרַשְׁתָּ֣ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃ {ס}
translation.scholarly_translation: Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the LORD thy God giveth thee, tribe by tribe; and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment. Thou shalt not wrest judgment; thou shalt not respect persons; neither shalt thou take a gift; for a gift doth blind the eyes of the wise, and pervert the words of the righteous. Justice, justice shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live, and inherit the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.
translation.scholarly_source: The Holy Scriptures: A New Translation (JPS 1917) (Public Domain); Hebrew: Miqra according to the Masorah (CC-BY-SA)
translation.ai_translation: Appoint judges and officers for yourself in all your towns that the LORD your God is giving you, tribe by tribe, and they shall judge the people with right judgment. Do not bend justice. Do not show favoritism. Do not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous. Justice, justice you shall pursue, so that you may live and possess the land the LORD your God is giving you.

key_terms.שֹׁחַד (shochad): bribe, a gift to sway a judgment

situation: You see a neighbor's ox or sheep wandering loose, or find something he lost. Nobody would know if you ignored it or kept it.
wise_response: Bring it back. If the owner is far away or unknown, take it home and look after it until he comes for it. "You may not hide your eyes."
why_it_worked: Honesty includes not looking away. Someone else's loss becomes your responsibility once you have seen it.
tempting_wrong_answer: Pretend not to notice, or quietly keep what you found.

translation.original_text: לֹֽא־תִרְאֶה֩ אֶת־שׁ֨וֹר אָחִ֜יךָ א֤וֹ אֶת־שֵׂיוֹ֙ נִדָּחִ֔ים וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ֖ מֵהֶ֑ם הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֵ֖ם לְאָחִֽיךָ׃ וְאִם־לֹ֨א קָר֥וֹב אָחִ֛יךָ אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְלֹ֣א יְדַעְתּ֑וֹ וַאֲסַפְתּוֹ֙ אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ בֵּיתֶ֔ךָ וְהָיָ֣ה עִמְּךָ֗ עַ֣ד דְּרֹ֤שׁ אָחִ֙יךָ֙ אֹת֔וֹ וַהֲשֵׁבֹת֖וֹ לֽוֹ׃ וְכֵ֧ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה לַחֲמֹר֗וֹ וְכֵ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂה֮ לְשִׂמְלָתוֹ֒ וְכֵ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֗ה לְכׇל־אֲבֵדַ֥ת אָחִ֛יךָ אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאבַ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נּוּ וּמְצָאתָ֑הּ לֹ֥א תוּכַ֖ל לְהִתְעַלֵּֽם׃ {ס}
translation.scholarly_translation: Thou shalt not see thy brother’s ox or his sheep driven away, and hide thyself from them; thou shalt surely bring them back unto thy brother. And if thy brother be not nigh unto thee, and thou know him not, then thou shalt bring it home to thy house, and it shall be with thee until thy brother require it, and thou shalt restore it to him. And so shalt thou do with his ass; and so shalt thou do with his garment; and so shalt thou do with every lost thing of thy brother’s, which he hath lost, and thou hast found; thou mayest not hide thyself.
translation.scholarly_source: The Holy Scriptures: A New Translation (JPS 1917) (Public Domain); Hebrew: Miqra according to the Masorah (CC-BY-SA)
translation.ai_translation: If you see your kinsman's ox or sheep straying, do not look away from them; you must bring them back to him. If he does not live near you, or you do not know who he is, take it into your house and keep it with you until your kinsman comes looking for it, then give it back to him. Do the same with his donkey, with his cloak, and with anything your kinsman loses and you find. You may not hide your eyes.
translation.translation_notes: AI draft. Hebrew original stored; AI translation made from the Hebrew. Public or openly licensed English translation stored alongside for comparison. אָח (ach), "brother," here means a fellow member of the community, not only a blood relative.

situation: A neighbor's donkey or ox has collapsed on the road under its load. You are passing by.
wise_response: Stop and help him get it up. "You must help him lift them up": the work is done together with the owner.
why_it_worked: A person struggling on the road should not be left alone with the problem. Helping alongside him respects both his need and his own effort.
tempting_wrong_answer: Walk past and leave him to manage.

translation.original_text: לֹא־תִרְאֶה֩ אֶת־חֲמ֨וֹר אָחִ֜יךָ א֤וֹ שׁוֹרוֹ֙ נֹפְלִ֣ים בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ֖ מֵהֶ֑ם הָקֵ֥ם תָּקִ֖ים עִמּֽוֹ׃ {ס}
translation.scholarly_translation: Thou shalt not see thy brother’s ass or his ox fallen down by the way, and hide thyself from them; thou shalt surely help him to lift them up again.
translation.scholarly_source: The Holy Scriptures: A New Translation (JPS 1917) (Public Domain); Hebrew: Miqra according to the Masorah (CC-BY-SA)
translation.ai_translation: If you see your kinsman's donkey or ox fallen on the road, do not look away from them; you must help him lift them up.

key_terms.הָקֵם תָּקִים עִמּוֹ (hakem takim imo): you must raise them up with him: help alongside the owner

situation: A traveler finds a bird's nest with the mother sitting on her eggs or chicks. He could take them all.
wise_response: Take the young if you need them, but let the mother go. "Send the mother away."
why_it_worked: Even when taking food, there is a limit. Sparing the mother shows restraint toward a creature at its most exposed and keeps the source of life going.
tempting_wrong_answer: Take everything, the mother and the young, because they are within easy reach.

translation.original_text: כִּ֣י יִקָּרֵ֣א *(בספרי תימן קַן בקו״ף גדולה)קַן־צִפּ֣וֹר ׀ לְפָנֶ֡יךָ בַּדֶּ֜רֶךְ בְּכׇל־עֵ֣ץ ׀ א֣וֹ עַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶפְרֹחִים֙ א֣וֹ בֵיצִ֔ים וְהָאֵ֤ם רֹבֶ֙צֶת֙ עַל־הָֽאֶפְרֹחִ֔ים א֖וֹ עַל־הַבֵּיצִ֑ים לֹא־תִקַּ֥ח הָאֵ֖ם עַל־הַבָּנִֽים׃ שַׁלֵּ֤חַ תְּשַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־הָאֵ֔ם וְאֶת־הַבָּנִ֖ים תִּֽקַּֽח־לָ֑ךְ לְמַ֙עַן֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ וְהַאֲרַכְתָּ֖ יָמִֽים׃ {ס}
translation.scholarly_translation: If a bird’s nest chance to be before thee in the way, in any tree or on the ground, with young ones or eggs, and the dam sitting upon the young, or upon the eggs, thou shalt not take the dam with the young; thou shalt in any wise let the dam go, but the young thou mayest take unto thyself; that it may be well with thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days.
translation.scholarly_source: The Holy Scriptures: A New Translation (JPS 1917) (Public Domain); Hebrew: Miqra according to the Masorah (CC-BY-SA)
translation.ai_translation: If you come upon a bird's nest along the road, in any tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs, and the mother sitting on the chicks or the eggs, do not take the mother along with the young. Send the mother away and take the young for yourself, so that it may go well with you and you may live long.

situation: A man builds a new house with a flat roof where people will walk. A fall could kill someone.
wise_response: Build a railing around the roof before anyone is hurt.
why_it_worked: You are responsible for dangers you create for others. Preventing harm ahead of time is part of right conduct.
tempting_wrong_answer: Skip the railing to save effort and money, and call it bad luck if someone falls.

translation.original_text: כִּ֤י תִבְנֶה֙ בַּ֣יִת חָדָ֔שׁ וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מַעֲקֶ֖ה לְגַגֶּ֑ךָ וְלֹֽא־תָשִׂ֤ים דָּמִים֙ בְּבֵיתֶ֔ךָ כִּֽי־יִפֹּ֥ל הַנֹּפֵ֖ל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
translation.scholarly_translation: When thou buildest a new house, then thou shalt make a parapet for thy roof, that thou bring not blood upon thy house, if any man fall from thence.
translation.scholarly_source: The Holy Scriptures: A New Translation (JPS 1917) (Public Domain); Hebrew: Miqra according to the Masorah (CC-BY-SA)
translation.ai_translation: When you build a new house, make a railing for your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if someone falls from it.

key_terms.דָּמִים (damim): blood; bloodguilt for a death one could have prevented

situation: People who are causing harm are told to stop spreading corruption in the land. They answer that they are only setting things right.
wise_response: Hear the warning and check your own conduct. The verse says the harm-doers "do not perceive it", so the wise person does not assume good intentions prove good results.
why_it_worked: People can do damage while sincerely calling it reform. Honest self-examination is the guard against that.
tempting_wrong_answer: Insist on your own good motives and wave the warning away, as the people in the verse did.

translation.original_text: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ قَالُوا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَشْعُرُونَ
translation.scholarly_translation: And when it is said unto them: Make not mischief in the earth, they say: We are peacemakers only. Are not they indeed the mischief-makers? But they perceive not.
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: When they are told, "Do not spread corruption in the land," they say, "We are only setting things right." No. They are the ones spreading corruption, but they do not see it.

key_terms.مُصْلِحُون (muslihun): those who set things right, reformers
key_terms.مُفْسِدُون (mufsidun): those who corrupt, spoil or ruin

situation: People make a solemn pledge and are bound by ties they are told to keep joined. Breaking them would serve their interest.
wise_response: Keep the pledge once it is made firm and keep the ties joined. The verse names those who "break the pledge after it is made firm" and "cut what was commanded to be joined" as the losers.
why_it_worked: Trust and family bonds hold a community together. Breaking them damages the one who breaks them as well as others.
tempting_wrong_answer: Drop a pledge or cut off kin when it becomes inconvenient.

translation.original_text: الَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ مِيثَاقِهِ وَيَقْطَعُونَ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ
translation.scholarly_translation: Those who break the covenant of Allah after ratifying it, and sever that which Allah ordered to be joined, and (who) make mischief in the earth: Those are they who are the losers.
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: Those who break God's pledge after it has been made firm, who cut what God commanded to be joined, and who spread corruption in the land: they are the losers.

key_terms.يُوصَل (yusal): to be joined, connected; often read as ties of kinship

situation: People who know the truth find it useful to blur it or keep it hidden.
wise_response: Keep truth and falsehood apart and speak what you know. In the verse's words: "Do not dress the truth in falsehood."
why_it_worked: Mixing a lie into the truth or hiding what you know both mislead others. Honesty requires clear speech and disclosure.
tempting_wrong_answer: Shade the truth with half-lies, or stay silent about what you know when speaking would cost you.

translation.original_text: وَلَا تَلْبِسُوا الْحَقَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُوا الْحَقَّ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
translation.scholarly_translation: Confound not truth with falsehood, nor knowingly conceal the truth.

translation.ai_translation: Do not dress the truth in falsehood, and do not hide the truth while you know it.

situation: People who read scripture urge others to do good, but neglect to do it themselves.
wise_response: Apply the teaching to yourself first. The verse asks: "Do you order people to do good and forget yourselves?"
why_it_worked: Advice carries weight only when the adviser lives it. Self-correction comes before correcting others.
tempting_wrong_answer: Preach goodness to others while excusing yourself.

translation.original_text: أَتَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبِرِّ وَتَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
translation.scholarly_translation: Enjoin ye righteousness upon mankind while ye yourselves forget (to practise it)? And ye are readers of the Scripture! Have ye then no sense?
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: Do you order people to do good and forget yourselves, while you recite the Book? Will you not use your reason?

situation: A people make a solemn pledge that sets out how they must treat others: parents, relatives, orphans, the poor and people at large. Most later turn away from it.
wise_response: Do good to parents, kin, orphans and the poor, and "speak well to people." Keep these duties alongside worship.
why_it_worked: Goodness starts at home and reaches out to the weak, and it includes how you speak to everyone. The pledge ties all of this together.
tempting_wrong_answer: Accept the pledge and then drift from it, as most of the people in the verse did.

translation.original_text: وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ لَا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَامَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْنًا وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّنكُمْ وَأَنتُم مُّعْرِضُونَ
translation.scholarly_translation: And (remember) when We made a covenant with the Children of Israel, (saying): Worship none save Allah (only), and be good to parents and to kindred and to orphans and the needy, and speak kindly to mankind; and establish worship and pay the poor-due. Then, after that, ye slid back, save a few of you, being averse.
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: And remember when We took a pledge from the Children of Israel: worship none but God; do good to parents, to relatives, to orphans and to the poor; speak well to people; keep up the prayer and give the alms. Then you turned away, all but a few of you, and you still turn aside.

situation: People lean on the merit of famous ancestors and argue over who they belonged to.
wise_response: Answer for your own deeds. The verse says of the earlier generation: "It has what it earned, and you have what you earned."
why_it_worked: Each person is judged on their own conduct. Ancestors' virtue cannot cover yours, and their failings are not yours to carry.
tempting_wrong_answer: Rest on your forebears' reputation, or blame the past for your own choices.

translation.original_text: تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَلَكُم مَّا كَسَبْتُمْ وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ
translation.scholarly_translation: Those are a people who have passed away. Theirs is that which they earned, and yours is that which ye earn. And ye will not be asked of what they used to do.
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: That was a community that has passed on. It has what it earned, and you have what you earned. You will not be asked about what they used to do.

situation: Communities face different directions in worship and dispute over whose direction is right.
wise_response: Stop competing over direction and compete in doing good. The verse says: "Race one another to good deeds."
why_it_worked: Rivalry turned toward good works makes everyone better. The final sorting of differences is left to God, who "will bring you all together."
tempting_wrong_answer: Spend your energy proving your side right and the others wrong.

translation.original_text: وَلِكُلٍّ وِجْهَةٌ هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَا فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ أَيْنَ مَا تَكُونُوا يَأْتِ بِكُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
translation.scholarly_translation: And each one hath a goal toward which he turneth; so vie with one another in good works. Wheresoever ye may be, Allah will bring you all together. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things.

situation: People are struck by fear, hunger, and loss of wealth, lives and harvests.
wise_response: Bear the loss with patience and say: "We belong to God, and to Him we return."
why_it_worked: Seeing your life and possessions as entrusted, not owned, lets you grieve without despair. Patience keeps you steady enough to go on.
tempting_wrong_answer: Rage against the loss, give up, or decide that hardship means you have been abandoned.

translation.original_text: وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُم بِشَيْءٍ مِّنَ الْخَوْفِ وَالْجُوعِ وَنَقْصٍ مِّنَ الْأَمْوَالِ وَالْأَنفُسِ وَالثَّمَرَاتِ وَبَشِّرِ الصَّابِرِينَ الَّذِينَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُم مُّصِيبَةٌ قَالُوا إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ أُولَٰئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ

situation: People are called to follow guidance, and they answer that they will follow only what they found their fathers doing.
wise_response: Weigh a practice by sense and guidance, not only by inheritance. The verse asks: "Even if their fathers understood nothing?"
why_it_worked: Custom earns respect but does not prove itself right. A thinking person tests what was handed down.
tempting_wrong_answer: Refuse to examine anything because "this is what our fathers did."

translation.original_text: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا أَوَلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ
translation.scholarly_translation: And when it is said unto them: Follow that which Allah hath revealed, they say: We follow that wherein we found our fathers. What! Even though their fathers were wholly unintelligent and had no guidance?

situation: People argue over which direction to face in prayer, as if that were the heart of goodness.
wise_response: Righteousness is faith shown in conduct: giving wealth you love to relatives, orphans, the poor, travelers, those who ask, and to free captives; keeping promises; and being patient in hardship and danger.
why_it_worked: Outward form matters less than character. Goodness is measured by what you give up for others, the word you keep, and how you hold up under strain.
tempting_wrong_answer: Treat correct ritual form as the whole of virtue while ignoring the needy.

translation.original_text: لَّيْسَ الْبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ قِبَلَ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ وَلَٰكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالْكِتَابِ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ ذَوِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَامَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ وَالسَّائِلِينَ وَفِي الرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَى الزَّكَاةَ وَالْمُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِهِمْ إِذَا عَاهَدُوا وَالصَّابِرِينَ فِي الْبَأْسَاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ وَحِينَ الْبَأْسِ أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُونَ
translation.scholarly_translation: It is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West; but righteous is he who believeth in Allah and the Last Day and the angels and the Scripture and the prophets; and giveth wealth, for love of Him, to kinsfolk and to orphans and the needy and the wayfarer and to those who ask, and to set slaves free; and observeth proper worship and payeth the poor-due. And those who keep their treaty when they make one, and the patient in tribulation and adversity and time of stress. Such are they who are sincere. Such are the Allah-fearing.
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west. Righteousness is to believe in God, the Last Day, the angels, the Book and the prophets; to give wealth, though you love it, to relatives, orphans, the poor, the traveler, those who ask, and for freeing those in bondage; to keep up the prayer and give the alms; to keep your promises when you make them; and to be patient in poverty, in suffering, and in times of danger. These are the ones who are true, and these are the ones who are mindful of God.

situation: A person near death leaves wealth and must make a bequest. Others will later hear the will, and some may want to change it.
wise_response: Make a fair bequest to parents and close relatives. Do not alter a will once heard. If the will is unjust, make peace between the parties rather than enforce the wrong.
why_it_worked: A fair will protects family bonds after death. Honoring it is a trust, and setting right a clear injustice through reconciliation serves the same aim.
tempting_wrong_answer: Write a lopsided will, or change someone's last wishes for your own gain.

translation.original_text: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا الْوَصِيَّةُ لِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ حَقًّا عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ فَمَن بَدَّلَهُ بَعْدَ مَا سَمِعَهُ فَإِنَّمَا إِثْمُهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ فَمَنْ خَافَ مِن مُّوصٍ جَنَفًا أَوْ إِثْمًا فَأَصْلَحَ بَيْنَهُمْ فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
translation.scholarly_translation: It is prescribed for you, when death approacheth one of you, if he leave wealth, that he bequeath unto parents and near relatives in kindness. (This is) a duty for all those who ward off (evil). And whoso changeth (the will) after he hath heard it - the sin thereof is only upon those who change it. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower. But he who feareth from a testator some unjust or sinful clause, and maketh peace between the parties, (it shall be) no sin for him. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: It is prescribed for you, when death comes near one of you and he leaves wealth, to make a fair bequest to parents and close relatives. This is a duty on those mindful of God. Whoever alters it after hearing it, the sin falls only on those who alter it. God hears and knows. But whoever fears that the testator leaned toward injustice or sin, and makes peace between them, there is no sin on him. God is forgiving and merciful.

situation: Someone can take another's property by fraud, or by bringing a case before judges with a bribe or a false claim.
wise_response: Do not consume others' wealth wrongfully, and do not use the courts to take what you know is not yours.
why_it_worked: A legal win does not make a wrongful taking right. Justice depends on the honesty of those who come to court.
tempting_wrong_answer: Bribe the judge or work the system to take property you know belongs to someone else.

translation.original_text: وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُم بَيْنَكُم بِالْبَاطِلِ وَتُدْلُوا بِهَا إِلَى الْحُكَّامِ لِتَأْكُلُوا فَرِيقًا مِّنْ أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ بِالْإِثْمِ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
translation.scholarly_translation: And eat not up your property among yourselves in vanity, nor seek by it to gain the hearing of the judges that ye may knowingly devour a portion of the property of others wrongfully.

translation.ai_translation: Do not consume one another's wealth wrongfully, and do not offer it to the judges so that you may knowingly devour part of other people's wealth through sin.

situation: A man speaks impressively and swears God knows his heart, yet he is a bitter opponent and works ruin when out of sight. When told to be mindful of God, he grows proud.
wise_response: Judge people by their deeds, not their fine words. And when you are told to take care, accept the correction.
why_it_worked: Pride that refuses correction locks a person into wrongdoing. Words prove nothing when the deeds destroy.
tempting_wrong_answer: Answer a rebuke with injured pride and carry on, as this man does; or trust a smooth talker on his oath alone.

translation.original_text: وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَيُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِي قَلْبِهِ وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ الْخِصَامِ وَإِذَا تَوَلَّىٰ سَعَىٰ فِي الْأَرْضِ لِيُفْسِدَ فِيهَا وَيُهْلِكَ الْحَرْثَ وَالنَّسْلَ وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْفَسَادَ وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ الْعِزَّةُ بِالْإِثْمِ فَحَسْبُهُ جَهَنَّمُ وَلَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ

situation: People ask about wine and gambling, and about how much they should give away.
wise_response: Weigh harm against benefit: "their sin is greater than their benefit." And give "what is beyond your needs."
why_it_worked: Something can bring some benefit and still do more harm than good. Giving from your surplus is generous without ruining yourself.
tempting_wrong_answer: Point to the small benefits of a harmful habit to excuse it; or give nothing, or give so recklessly that you become a burden.

translation.original_text: يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ قُلْ فِيهِمَا إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَإِثْمُهُمَا أَكْبَرُ مِن نَّفْعِهِمَا وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنفِقُونَ قُلِ الْعَفْوَ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ
translation.scholarly_translation: They question thee about strong drink and games of chance. Say: In both is great sin, and (some) utility for men; but the sin of them is greater than their usefulness. And they ask thee what they ought to spend. Say: that which is superfluous. Thus Allah maketh plain to you (His) revelations, that haply ye may reflect.

situation: Guardians of orphans worry about mixing the orphans' food and property with their own.
wise_response: Do what is best for the orphans. If you share household and affairs with them, treat them as family: "they are your brothers."
why_it_worked: Care for orphans means improving their lot, not keeping them at a distance. God knows who spoils and who sets right.
tempting_wrong_answer: Exploit the orphan's property, or keep the orphan apart out of fear and neglect.

translation.original_text: فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْيَتَامَىٰ قُلْ إِصْلَاحٌ لَّهُمْ خَيْرٌ وَإِن تُخَالِطُوهُمْ فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْمُفْسِدَ مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَأَعْنَتَكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ

And if ye mingle your affairs with theirs, then (they are) your brothers. Allah knoweth him who spoileth from him who improveth. Had Allah willed He could have overburdened you. Allah is Mighty, Wise.

situation: A person swears an oath by God not to do some good thing, then holds to the oath as a reason not to help or make peace.
wise_response: Do not make God's name an excuse in your oaths against doing good, being mindful, and making peace between people.
why_it_worked: An oath should not lock a person into withholding kindness. Doing good and reconciling people outweigh a vow made against them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hide behind a hasty oath to avoid helping someone or mending a quarrel.

translation.original_text: وَلَا تَجْعَلُوا اللَّهَ عُرْضَةً لِّأَيْمَانِكُمْ أَن تَبَرُّوا وَتَتَّقُوا وَتُصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
translation.scholarly_translation: And make not Allah, by your oaths, a hindrance to your being righteous and observing your duty unto Him and making peace among mankind. Allah is Hearer, Knower.
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: Do not make God, through your oaths, a barrier against doing good, being mindful, and making peace between people. God hears and knows.

situation: A husband has divorced his wife and her waiting term is ending. He can take her back only to keep her from others, and her family can block her from remarrying.
wise_response: Keep her fairly or release her fairly. Do not hold her to harm her, and do not stand in the way when a couple agree fairly to marry.
why_it_worked: Power within a marriage or family must not be used to trap someone. Fairness at the end of a marriage protects the weaker party.
tempting_wrong_answer: Take a wife back only to hurt her, or block a woman's remarriage out of pride or spite.

translation.original_text: وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ وَلَا تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ ضِرَارًا لِّتَعْتَدُوا وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوا آيَاتِ اللَّهِ هُزُوًا وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَا أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ الْكِتَابِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ يَعِظُكُم بِهِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ وَإِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ أَن يَنكِحْنَ أَزْوَاجَهُنَّ إِذَا تَرَاضَوْا بَيْنَهُم بِالْمَعْرُوفِ ذَٰلِكَ يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَن كَانَ مِنكُمْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَزْكَىٰ لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
translation.scholarly_translation: When ye have divorced women, and they have reached their term, then retain them in kindness or release them in kindness. Retain them not to their hurt so that ye transgress (the limits). He who doeth that hath wronged his soul. Make not the revelations of Allah a laughing-stock (by your behaviour), but remember Allah's grace upon you and that which He hath revealed unto you of the Scripture and of wisdom, whereby He doth exhort you. Observe your duty to Allah and know that Allah is Aware of all things. And when ye have divorced women and they reach their term, place not difficulties in the way of their marrying their husbands if it is agreed between them in kindness. This is an admonition for him among you who believeth in Allah and the Last Day. That is more virtuous for you, and cleaner. Allah knoweth; ye know not.
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: When you divorce women and they reach the end of their term, either keep them in a fair way or let them go in a fair way. Do not keep them in order to harm them and wrong them. Whoever does that wrongs himself. Do not make a joke of God's signs. Remember God's favor to you, and what He sent down to you of the Book and wisdom to instruct you. Be mindful of God, and know that God knows all things. And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they agree between themselves in a fair way. This is the counsel for whoever among you believes in God and the Last Day. It is more upright and purer for you. God knows, and you do not.

"Their husbands" in 2:232 is read as their former husbands or the men they now wish to marry; the ones addressed are often taken to be the woman's guardians.
