situation: Parents, married or separated, must decide how to feed and care for a nursing child and how to share the cost.
wise_response: The father provides fairly for the mother; neither parent is to be harmed through the child; weaning is decided "by mutual consent and consultation." No one is burdened beyond capacity.
why_it_worked: A child's welfare is best served when parents share the load fairly and decide together. Using a child as leverage harms everyone.
tempting_wrong_answer: Use the child to punish the other parent, or push the whole burden onto one side.

translation.original_text: وَالْوَالِدَاتُ يُرْضِعْنَ أَوْلَادَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ كَامِلَيْنِ لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يُتِمَّ الرَّضَاعَةَ وَعَلَى الْمَوْلُودِ لَهُ رِزْقُهُنَّ وَكِسْوَتُهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ لَا تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا لَا تُضَارَّ وَالِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِهَا وَلَا مَوْلُودٌ لَّهُ بِوَلَدِهِ وَعَلَى الْوَارِثِ مِثْلُ ذَٰلِكَ فَإِنْ أَرَادَا فِصَالًا عَن تَرَاضٍ مِّنْهُمَا وَتَشَاوُرٍ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا وَإِنْ أَرَدتُّمْ أَن تَسْتَرْضِعُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا سَلَّمْتُم مَّا آتَيْتُم بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
translation.scholarly_translation: Mothers shall suckle their children for two whole years; (that is) for those who wish to complete the suckling. The duty of feeding and clothing nursing mothers in a seemly manner is upon the father of the child. No-one should be charged beyond his capacity. A mother should not be made to suffer because of her child, nor should he to whom the child is born (be made to suffer) because of his child. And on the (father's) heir is incumbent the like of that (which was incumbent on the father). If they desire to wean the child by mutual consent and (after) consultation, it is no sin for them; and if ye wish to give your children out to nurse, it is no sin for you, provide that ye pay what is due from you in kindness. Observe your duty to Allah, and know that Allah is Seer of what ye do.
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: Mothers may nurse their children two full years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing. The father must provide their food and clothing in a fair way. No soul is charged beyond its capacity. No mother shall be harmed because of her child, nor any father because of his child. The same duty falls on the heir. If both wish to wean by mutual consent and consultation, there is no blame on them. And if you wish to have your children nursed by another woman, there is no blame on you, as long as you pay what you agreed in a fair way. Be mindful of God, and know that God sees what you do.

situation: A marriage ends before it is consummated, after a dower was set. Half the dower is due, and either side could insist on every coin.
wise_response: Pay what is due, and be ready to waive more. "To forgo is closer to mindfulness of God. And do not forget generosity between you."
why_it_worked: Even at a painful parting, graciousness keeps both people decent. Giving up a strict right can be the better act.
tempting_wrong_answer: Haggle over every amount and part as enemies.

translation.original_text: وَإِن طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً فَنِصْفُ مَا فَرَضْتُمْ إِلَّا أَن يَعْفُونَ أَوْ يَعْفُوَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ النِّكَاحِ وَأَن تَعْفُوا أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ وَلَا تَنسَوُا الْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
translation.scholarly_translation: If ye divorce them before ye have touched them and ye have appointed unto them a portion, then (pay the) half of that which ye appointed, unless they (the women) agree to forgo it, or he agreeth to forgo it in whose hand is the marriage tie. To forgo is nearer to piety. And forget not kindness among yourselves. Allah is Seer of what ye do.
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: If you divorce them before you have touched them but after you have set a dower for them, then half of what you set is due, unless they waive it, or the one who holds the marriage tie waives it. To waive is closer to mindfulness of God. And do not forget generosity between you. God sees what you do.

key_terms.الفَضْل (al-fadl): graciousness, generosity beyond what is owed

situation: A man is dying and will leave a wife behind, who could be turned out of the home by his heirs.
wise_response: Leave her a year's provision and do not let her be turned out. If she chooses to leave, let her decide for herself.
why_it_worked: A widow should not lose her home and support at the moment of loss. Her own choices afterward are hers to make.
tempting_wrong_answer: Let the heirs evict the widow and divide everything at once.

translation.original_text: وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجًا وَصِيَّةً لِّأَزْوَاجِهِم مَّتَاعًا إِلَى الْحَوْلِ غَيْرَ إِخْرَاجٍ فَإِنْ خَرَجْنَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي مَا فَعَلْنَ فِي أَنفُسِهِنَّ مِن مَّعْرُوفٍ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
translation.scholarly_translation: (In the case of) those of you who are about to die and leave behind them wives, they should bequeath unto their wives a provision for the year without turning them out, but if they go out (of their own accord) there is no sin for you in that which they do of themselves within their rights. Allah is Mighty, Wise.
translation.scholarly_source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain in the US
translation.ai_translation: Those of you who die and leave wives should leave a bequest for their wives: provision for a year without their being turned out. But if they leave, there is no blame on you for what they do with themselves in a fair way. God is mighty and wise.

Many scholars hold this verse was superseded by 2:234 and the inheritance shares; others keep it as a recommended provision.

source.citation: Seven Samurai (1954), dir. Akira Kurosawa, Toho

story_title: The village that hired its defenders
situation: A poor farming village is raided every harvest by bandits. The villagers have no weapons and no fighters, and can offer only food.
wise_response: Kambei, a veteran samurai, takes the task because it is right rather than because it pays, and recruits others on the same terms. The samurai train the villagers, fortify the village, and fight beside them instead of in their place.
why_it_worked: They treated the villagers as partners rather than clients. Teaching people to defend themselves spread courage through the village, so the defence did not depend on a handful of hired swords.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hire mercenaries and let them do the fighting while the village watches, or promise payment the village cannot keep.

situation: A boy loses his sister's only pair of shoes. The family is poor, new shoes mean a debt they cannot carry, and telling their father risks punishment.
wise_response: The brother and sister share his sneakers in secret — she wears them in the morning, he in the afternoon — and he enters a race hoping to win third prize, a new pair of shoes.
why_it_worked: They carried the cost themselves instead of passing it to their parents, and kept their promise to each other even when it was humiliating and inconvenient.
tempting_wrong_answer: Blame each other, steal a pair, or hide the loss until it grows into a crisis the whole family pays for.

story_title: The granddaughter who claimed the canoe
situation: A Maori community's leader expects a male heir. His granddaughter Pai is a natural leader, but he refuses to train her because tradition says the line passes to a son.
wise_response: Pai learns the old ways in secret, and when the community's canoe is lost and the whales strand, she rides the whale back to sea and returns — claiming her place without humiliating her grandfather.
why_it_worked: She neither fought the tradition nor abandoned it. She fulfilled it better than the rule allowed, so the community could recognize her without having to admit the rule was wrong.
tempting_wrong_answer: Obey and disappear, or break with the elders and take leadership by force.

story_title: The letter writer and the boy
situation: A retired teacher writes letters for illiterate strangers at a train station. A woman is killed by a bus, leaving her young son with nowhere to go.
wise_response: Dora, cynical and poor, first sells the boy to an adoption ring. Then she takes him back and travels across Brazil to find a father she does not know and may not exist.
why_it_worked: She acted before she felt ready, and kept acting after the easy part was over. The boy's trust came from her staying, not from anything she said.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hand him to an institution, or keep the money and tell herself it was for the best.

situation: A martial arts master loses his wealth in the war and takes factory work. A rival challenges him publicly to prove which school is superior.
wise_response: Ip Man accepts the fight but holds back, refuses to humiliate the challenger, and keeps teaching that kung fu is for restraint rather than display.
why_it_worked: He won without making an enemy. The restraint cost him face and preserved the community he had to live in.
tempting_wrong_answer: Win decisively and publicly to build his reputation while he has nothing else left.

story_title: The applicant who did not want the job
situation: A wealthy quadriplegic, Philippe, is interviewing caretakers. Driss, a young man from the projects, applies only to get a signature proving he was rejected for benefits.
wise_response: Philippe hires him anyway — not out of charity, but because Driss treats him as a man rather than a patient. Driss, in turn, refuses to indulge Philippe's self-pity and pushes him back into life.
why_it_worked: Each gave the other what the other could not ask for. Philippe gave trust and a chance; Driss gave honesty and refused pity.
tempting_wrong_answer: Hire the most qualified applicant and manage the relationship as a service.

source.title: Abebe Bikila, Rome and Tokyo marathons
source.citation: 1960 Rome and 1964 Tokyo Olympic marathons; coached by Onni Niskanen

situation: An unknown Ethiopian runner arrives at the 1960 Rome Olympics and finds that the shoes he trained in have worn out. Nothing in the sponsor's kit fits him properly.
wise_response: He runs the 26 miles barefoot over Roman roads and wins, becoming the first Black African Olympic champion. Four years later, six weeks after an appendectomy, he wins again in Tokyo, this time with shoes.
why_it_worked: He had trained for years at altitude under a Swedish coach who treated him as an athlete rather than a curiosity. Equipment and circumstance set the conditions, not the ceiling.
tempting_wrong_answer: Withdraw because the equipment isn't right, or run hurt in bad shoes to protect appearances.

story_title: The leg brace and the three golds
situation: Born premature, one of twenty-two children in segregated Tennessee, she had polio and wore a leg brace until she was nine.
wise_response: Her mother took her to a Black hospital fifty miles away twice a week for years, and her siblings took turns massaging her leg every day. She became the fastest woman in the world and won three golds in Rome.
why_it_worked: The family treated her recovery as a shared job rather than her private burden. The discipline came from being expected at practice, not from being inspired.
tempting_wrong_answer: Accept the brace as the end of the story, or leave a child to carry the work alone.

story_title: The team that was not supposed to win
situation: A newly promoted English football club, priced at 5,000-1, with a squad of players other clubs had discarded.
wise_response: The manager gave each player one job, the team defended as a unit, and the same eleven started most of the season. Nobody was asked to be a star.
why_it_worked: The system made each player's role small enough to master and important enough to keep. Cooperation beat talent because talent was not the constraint.

why_it_worked: She used the one thing she had trained for, in the moment it was needed, and did not wait for permission or a plan.

situation: A Canadian teenager loses a leg to cancer and decides to run across the country on a prosthetic leg to raise money for cancer research.
wise_response: He runs a marathon a day for 143 days, through weather and pain, until the cancer reaches his lungs. He stops, and says he will continue if he can.
why_it_worked: He asked for money for other people rather than sympathy for himself, which is why the country kept giving after he stopped.

situation: Rural Kenyan women watch streams dry up and firewood disappear as forests are cleared. The government treats the land as a resource to be sold.
wise_response: She pays women a small wage to plant indigenous trees, village by village, and keeps planting when the government arrests her and the work is dismissed as women's business.
why_it_worked: The trees were the argument. Each surviving seedling proved the claim without a speech, and the wage made conservation a livelihood rather than a sacrifice.

source.title: Milkha Singh, 1960 Rome 400m
source.citation: 1960 Rome Olympics; later Asian and Commonwealth Games

situation: An Indian runner orphaned in the Partition violence runs the 400m final in Rome, leads until the last stretch, and finishes fourth, missing a medal by a fraction.
wise_response: He does not dispute the result or blame the lane. He goes home, trains, wins gold at the Asian and Commonwealth Games, and spends decades coaching young Indian athletes.
why_it_worked: He treated the loss as information rather than an identity, and turned the near-miss into a standard for the people who came after him.

story_title: Two hundred and forty miles on a lawnmower
situation: Alvin Straight, seventy-three, lives in Iowa and learns that his estranged brother has had a stroke two hundred and forty miles away. He cannot drive, and he will not fly.
wise_response: He buys a riding lawnmower and drives it for six weeks, camping along the way, to reach his brother and make peace.
why_it_worked: The slowness was the point. It gave him time to arrive as someone ready to reconcile, and it asked nothing of his brother except presence.
tempting_wrong_answer: Send a message, or wait for the brother to reach out first.

situation: Hirayama cleans public toilets in Tokyo. He lives alone in a small flat, with cassette tapes and paperback books.
wise_response: He does the work carefully, photographs the trees on his lunch break, and keeps his life small enough to attend to.
why_it_worked: He is not waiting for a bigger life. Attention rather than ambition is what makes the days good.

story_title: The escape that was planned for months
situation: A Resistance fighter is imprisoned by the Gestapo in Lyon and awaits execution.
wise_response: He studies the cell, the guards' routines and the hinges for months, makes tools from what is at hand, and escapes on the night he judges right, taking a young prisoner with him.
why_it_worked: He never mistook hope for a plan. Every step was tested before it was used, and he waited until the odds were his.
tempting_wrong_answer: Rush an escape while the guards are alert, or trust a stranger with the plan.

source.title: Dead Man Walking
source.author: Tim Robbins
source.citation: Dead Man Walking (1995), dir. Tim Robbins

situation: A nun is asked to counsel a man on death row who has been convicted of murder and denies the worst of it.
wise_response: She visits him for years, listens without excusing him, and stays through the execution, while also sitting with the victims' families.
why_it_worked: She separated the person from the act without pretending the act was smaller than it was. Mercy held because it was honest.
tempting_wrong_answer: Either condemn him and stay away, or become his advocate and forget the victims.

source.author: Colm Bairead
source.citation: The Quiet Girl (2022), dir. Colm Bairead

situation: A neglected nine-year-old is sent to spend the summer with distant relatives on a farm while her mother has another child.
wise_response: The couple feed her, teach her chores, and let her be useful without making her earn affection. When she has to leave, she runs after the car.
why_it_worked: They gave her ordinary care — food, work, attention — instead of pity. Being treated as capable is what let her trust them.
tempting_wrong_answer: Shower her with treats, or keep her at arm's length because she is only temporary.

source.author: Ritesh Batra
source.citation: The Lunchbox (2013), dir. Ritesh Batra

situation: A Mumbai office worker's lunch is delivered by mistake to a stranger, an aging accountant. She writes a note the next day.
wise_response: They exchange notes in the lunchbox — small, honest, increasingly personal — without meeting, and each begins to change how he lives.
why_it_worked: The exchange was low-stakes enough to be honest, and reciprocal: each gave something and each received something, so neither became the other's project.
tempting_wrong_answer: Meet immediately and turn it into a romance, or stop writing once it got real.

story_title: Turning back within sight of the summit
situation: A mountaineer is high on Annapurna, close enough to the summit to see it, and the conditions are turning.
wise_response: He turns around. He returns years later and finishes the climb on a day the mountain allows it.
why_it_worked: He had decided in advance that the summit was optional and the descent was not, so the decision was already made when it got hard. He was not choosing between courage and fear; he was keeping a promise to himself.
tempting_wrong_answer: Push for the top because the summit is right there and the effort is already spent.

story_title: A country that gave up its army
situation: After a civil war, Costa Rica's provisional leader holds the army that won. The country is poor and the region is full of military governments.
wise_response: He abolishes the army and writes the decision into the constitution. The money goes to schools, clinics and roads instead.
why_it_worked: It removed the instrument that had produced the war, rather than promising to use it better. The saving was visible within a generation.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keep the army to protect the new government, and promise reform later.

source.date_or_era: 2003 onward
source.citation: Kamikatsu, Tokushima Prefecture; zero-waste declaration 2003

situation: A small mountain town loses its landfill and incinerator. The cheapest option is to truck waste out of the valley and forget it.
wise_response: The town declares a zero-waste goal and asks every household to sort rubbish into forty-five categories, wash it, and bring it to a single collection point. They keep doing it for twenty years.
why_it_worked: The task was small enough for each household to do and visible enough that everyone could see whether their neighbours did it. Patience became a civic habit rather than a policy.
tempting_wrong_answer: Pay to export the waste and keep the inconvenience out of sight.

source.title: The Copiapo miners, 2010
source.citation: Copiapo mining accident, 2010; 33 men, 69 days underground

situation: Thirty-three miners are trapped 700 metres underground after a collapse. Nobody above ground knows whether they are alive.
wise_response: Underground, they ration food, organize shifts, keep a daily routine and assign one man to keep morale. Above ground, the rescue team keeps drilling holes that miss.
why_it_worked: They made the group the unit of survival. Rationing and routine replaced individual endurance, so the weakest did not set the pace and nobody had to be a hero alone.
tempting_wrong_answer: Let the strongest take what they need and hope the drilling finds you.

source.title: Bhutan and Gross National Happiness
source.date_or_era: 1972 onward
source.citation: Bhutan, Gross National Happiness, declared 1972; constitutional principle 2008

story_title: Measuring the wrong thing on purpose
situation: A small Himalayan kingdom opens to the world and has to choose what development means before it has much of it.
wise_response: The king declares that Gross National Happiness matters more than Gross National Product, and the country builds its policy around that claim, including forest cover, culture and time use.
why_it_worked: It changed the scoreboard before the incentives hardened. What counted as success was decided publicly, so later governments had to argue against a stated standard rather than quietly ignore one.
tempting_wrong_answer: Maximize growth first and worry about wellbeing once the country is rich.

source.title: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission
source.citation: Truth and Reconciliation Commission, 1996-1998, chaired by Desmond Tutu

situation: After apartheid, the new government has to decide what to do with thousands of perpetrators and a country full of unresolved crimes.
wise_response: The commission offers amnesty to those who confess fully and can show a political motive, and it hears victims in public. Those who do not confess remain liable.
why_it_worked: It traded punishment for information without trading away the truth. Mercy was conditional and public, so it did not require anyone to pretend nothing had happened.

situation: After Kristallnacht, Jewish children in Germany and occupied territory are in danger, and few countries will take them.
wise_response: British families, churches and charities arrange visas, foster homes and guarantees, and bring roughly ten thousand children out without their parents.
why_it_worked: It was organized as a hundred small household decisions rather than one national one, so it could proceed while governments hesitated.
tempting_wrong_answer: Wait for an international agreement, or take only the children who are easiest to place.

story_title: A factory where the workers own the pay gap
situation: A Basque priest arrives in a poor industrial town after the civil war and finds workers with no capital and no say in the factories that employ them.
wise_response: He starts a technical school, then a cooperative in which workers own the firm, elect the managers and set their own pay ratios. The model is copied into dozens of businesses.
why_it_worked: Ownership made reciprocity structural rather than aspirational. Because the pay ratio was voted on, restraint was a decision the members made together, not a favour granted by an owner.
tempting_wrong_answer: Attract an outside investor and accept whatever terms keep the factory open.

situation: Villagers in Bangladesh borrow from moneylenders at rates that keep them poor. Banks will not lend to them because they have no collateral.
wise_response: The bank lends small sums to groups of women who guarantee each other, with repayment scheduled weekly and no collateral.
why_it_worked: The group replaced the collateral. Reciprocity did the work that assets usually do, and the weekly meeting made repayment a shared obligation rather than a private risk.

source.title: The Balinese subak
source.date_or_era: c. 9th century onward
source.citation: Subak irrigation system, Bali; UNESCO World Heritage, 2012

story_title: Water shared by a temple, not a landlord
situation: Rice terraces on volcanic slopes need water in sequence. One farmer upstream can take everything; downstream farmers can do nothing about it.
wise_response: Farmers who share a water source form a subak, which allocates water by rule, maintains the channels together, and settles disputes at a temple rather than in a court.
why_it_worked: The water was treated as a shared obligation rather than a property right, and the temple gave the rule an authority no single farmer could claim. Patience and turn-taking were enforceable because everyone could see the schedule.
tempting_wrong_answer: Take as much water as the upstream position allows and sell the surplus.

wise_response: The verse says to check anger like a charioteer pulling a lurching chariot; that is what makes someone a driver rather than a passenger.
why_it_worked: It puts the test in the first second, where he still has a choice, instead of after the words are out.

story_title: Defeat each fault with its opposite
situation: A man is being lied about and belittled by someone who is behaving worse than he is.
wise_response: The verse says to defeat anger with kindness, villainy with virtue, stinginess with giving, and lies with truth.
why_it_worked: It answers each fault with its opposite rather than its equal, so the exchange cannot continue on the other person's terms.
tempting_wrong_answer: Answer each attack in kind and call it standing up for himself.
